**The interpretation of His words, ﴿They ask you about the spoils. Say: The spoils belong to God and the Messenger﴾**

Abu Ja'far said: The exegetes (ahl al-ta'wil) differed about the meaning of "al-anfal" (the spoils) mentioned by God in this passage.

Some of them said: They are the booty (al-ghanaim). They said: the meaning of the statement is: Your companions ask you, O Muhammad, about the booty that you and your companions seized on the day of Badr, to whom does it belong? So say: It belongs to God and His Messenger.

Mention of those who said this:

15628. Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, saying: Suwayd ibn 'Amr narrated to us, from Hammad ibn Zayd, from 'Ikrimah, regarding ﴿They ask you about the spoils﴾, he said: "Al-anfal" are the booty.

15629. Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿They ask you about the spoils﴾, he said: "Al-anfal" are the booty.

15630. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Mujahid, who said: "Al-anfal" is the spoils (al-maghnam).

15631. Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Abu Khalid al-Ahmar narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, regarding ﴿They ask you about the spoils﴾, he said: the booty.

15632. It was narrated to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say, regarding His words "al-anfal", he said: it means the booty.

15633. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talha, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words ﴿They ask you about the spoils﴾, he said: "Al-anfal" are the booty.

15634. Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿They ask you about the spoils﴾, "al-anfal" are the booty.

15635. Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His words ﴿They ask you about the spoils﴾, he said: "Al-anfal" are the booty.

15636. Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: "Al-anfal" are the booty.

15637. Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from 'Ata', regarding ﴿They ask you about the spoils﴾, he said: the booty.

* *

Others said: They are the spoils of the raiding detachments (anfal al-saraya).

Mention of those who said this:

15638. Al-Harith narrated to me, saying: 'Abd al-'Aziz narrated to us, saying: 'Ali ibn Salih ibn Hayy narrated to us, saying: It reached me regarding His words ﴿They ask you about the spoils﴾, he said: the raiding detachments (al-saraya).

* *

Others said: "Al-anfal" is what strayed from the polytheists to the Muslims, whether a slave or an animal, and what is similar to that.

Mention of those who said this:

15639. Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Jabir ibn Nuh narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Malik, from 'Ata', regarding His words ﴿They ask you about the spoils. Say: The spoils belong to God and the Messenger﴾, he said: It is what strayed from the polytheists to the Muslims without fighting: an animal, or a slave, or goods. That belongs to the Prophet ﷺ, who does with it as he wills.

15640. Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Ibn Numayr narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Malik, from 'Ata': ﴿They ask you about the spoils﴾, he said: It is what strayed from the polytheists to the Muslims without fighting, a slave, a female slave, goods, or baggage [[In the printed and manuscript texts: "or nafl", and the correct reading is what I have recorded. "Al-thiql" (with two fatha vowels) is the traveller's goods and dependants.]], so it belongs to the Prophet ﷺ, who does with it as he wills.

15641. ... narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri: that Ibn 'Abbas was asked about "al-anfal", and he said: the spoils (salab) and the horse.

15642. Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas: It is also said that "al-anfal" is what is taken of the goods that fell away after the booty has been divided; so it is a nafl (gift) to God and His Messenger.

15643. Al-Qasim narrated to me, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: al-Hajjaj narrated to me, saying: Ibn Jurayj said: 'Uthman ibn Abi Sulayman informed me, from Muhammad ibn Shihab, that a man said to Ibn 'Abbas: What are "al-anfal"? He said: The horse, the armour, and the spear. [[The report 15643: 'Uthman ibn Abi Sulayman ibn Jubayr ibn Mut'im al-Nawfali is trustworthy (thiqa), and was a judge in Mecca. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, Ibn Sa'd 5:357, and Ibn Abi Hatim 3/1/152. This report was also transmitted by Abu 'Ubayd al-Qasim ibn Sallam in Kitab al-Amwal, p. 304, no. 757, at greater length.]]

15644. Al-Harith narrated to me, saying: 'Abd al-'Aziz narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Warith ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Ibn Jurayj said: 'Ata' said: "Al-anfal": the strayed horse, the armour, and the garment.

15645. Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Prophet would give a man the salab of another man and his horse as a nafl. [[In the printed and manuscript texts: "the horse of the man and his salab", but in the manuscript, above "horse" and "salab" there is the letter "m", indicating reversal of order, so I did that.]]

15646. Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Malik ibn Anas informed me, from Ibn Shihab, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, who said: I heard a man ask Ibn 'Abbas about "al-anfal", and Ibn 'Abbas said: The horse is of the nafl, and the salab is of the nafl. Then the man returned to his question, and Ibn 'Abbas said the same again. Then the man said: "Al-anfal" which God mentioned in His Book, what are they? Al-Qasim said: He kept asking him until he nearly embarrassed him, and Ibn 'Abbas said: Do you know what the likeness of this is? It is the likeness of Subay' whom 'Umar ibn al-Khattab struck, may God be pleased with him? [[The report 15646: Malik narrated it in al-Muwatta', p. 455, in this same wording. "Subay'" is Subay' ibn 'Isl ibn Sahl al-Hanzali, whose biography Ibn Hajar gives in al-Isaba in the third section. Subay' came to 'Umar in Medina and began asking about the ambiguous (mutashabih) verses of the Qur'an. 'Umar struck him until his head bled, and he said: Enough, O Commander of the Faithful, what I was finding in my head has gone! 'Umar exiled him to Basra and wrote to them not to sit with him, so Subay' remained lowly among his people after having been their leader.]]

15647. Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, who said: Ibn 'Abbas said: When 'Umar, may God be pleased with him, was asked about something, he would say: "I do not command you, nor forbid you." Then Ibn 'Abbas said: By God, God did not send His Prophet, peace be upon him, except as one who commands and forbids, who makes lawful and unlawful. Al-Qasim said: A man was set upon Ibn 'Abbas to ask him about "al-anfal", and Ibn 'Abbas said: The man would give the horse of a man and his weapon as a nafl. The man repeated it to him, and he said the same to him. Then he repeated it to him until he angered him, and Ibn 'Abbas said: Do you know what the likeness of this is? It is the likeness of Subay' whom 'Umar struck until the blood flowed down his heels, or his legs. The man said: As for you, God has avenged 'Umar on you.

15647 (second). Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Malik, from 'Ata', regarding ﴿They ask you about the spoils﴾, he said: They ask you about what strayed from the polytheists to the Muslims without fighting, from an animal or [a slave] [[What is between the brackets is in the printed text alone; in the manuscript its place is blank.]], so it is a nafl for the Prophet ﷺ.

* *

Others said: "The nafl" is the fifth (al-khums) that God assigned to the people of the fifth.

Mention of those who said this:

15648. Al-Harith narrated to me, saying: 'Abd al-'Aziz narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Warith ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿They ask you about the spoils﴾, he said: It is the fifth. The emigrants (muhajirun) said: Why is this fifth not lifted from us? Why is it not taken from us? God said: It belongs to God and the Messenger. [[In the manuscript: "lam yurfa' huna" (not lifted here), and the correct reading is what is in the printed text.]]

15649. Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: 'Abbad ibn al-'Awwam narrated to us, from al-Hajjaj, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: that they asked the Prophet ﷺ about the fifth after the four-fifths, and ﴿They ask you about the spoils﴾ was revealed.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of these opinions regarding the meaning of "al-anfal" is the statement of the one who said: They are increments that the leader (imam) adds for some of the army or all of them, either from his own share over their rights in the division, [[In the printed text: "from his spoils over their rights", and in the manuscript: "from his share over their rights", and the reading of the manuscript is what I have recorded. The printed text makes no sense.]] or from what he obtained as a nafl, or by some of its causes, as an incentive for him and as encouragement for those with him in his army toward what is good for them and for the Muslims, or for the benefit of one of the two parties. It may include what Ibn 'Abbas said, that it is the horse, the armour, and similar things. It may include what 'Ata' said, that it is what came back from the polytheists to the Muslims, a slave or a horse, because that matter is for the leader, when what they obtained was not by overpowering and subjugation [[In the printed and manuscript texts: "li-ghalaba" (for the sake of overpowering), and the correct reading is "bi-ghalaba" (by overpowering).]]: he does what is good for the people of Islam. It may also include what the army overpowered by force.

* *

We only said that this is the most correct opinion because "nafl" in the speech of the Arabs means an addition to something. From it one says: "nafalltuka kadha" and "anfaltuka" when I added to you.

"Al-anfal" is the plural of "nafl". From it is the saying of Labid ibn Rabi'a:

Indeed, the fear of our Lord is the best nafl,
and by God's leave, delay and haste [[Diwan 2:11; Majaz al-Qur'an of Abu 'Ubayda 1:240; al-Lisan (n-f-l); and many others. It is the opening of a long poem of his.]]

Since its meaning is what we have mentioned, then whatever is added to the fighters of the army over their share of the booty, if that is for a trial he endured or for a service he rendered to the Muslims, by the governor's granting of it as a nafl to him, its ruling for him becomes like the spoils that the slayer takes. So that which is added from this is a nafl, because the addition is a nafl. [[The printed text reads: "because the addition is a nafl" (with "wa-l-nafl" in brackets), and this is an editorial addition.]] Even if he deserves it in some circumstances as a right, it is not from the booty in which the division takes place. [[This sentence in the printed text was: "because the addition, although deserved in some circumstances as a right, is not from the booty in which the division takes place." The manuscript differs entirely. The sentence in the manuscript begins: "because the addition is more excellent, although it is deserved," unpointed and poorly written. It is clear that its correct form is what I have recorded, with the addition I placed between the brackets.]] Likewise, whatever is given as a reward to one who has no share in the booty is a "nafl", [[" 'Rada'a lahu min al-mal" means he gave him a modest gift, that is, a small one.]] because although it is overpowered, it is not what the division applies to.

So the distinction, since the matter is as we have described, between "ghanima" (booty) and "nafl" is that the booty is what God bestows upon the Muslims from the property of the polytheists by overpowering and subjugation, whether a nafl is given from it or not. The "nafl" is what a man is given for a trial or a service rendered to the army, outside of the division. [[In the printed text: "What a man is given"; I have recorded what is in the manuscript.]]

* *

Since that is the meaning of "nafl", the interpretation of the statement is: Your companions ask you, O Muhammad, about the surplus of property in which division takes place from the booty of the unbelievers of Quraysh who were killed at Badr, to whom does it belong? Say to them, O Muhammad: It belongs to God and His Messenger, not to you; He places it wherever He wills.

* *

Differences arose concerning the cause for which this verse was revealed.

Some of them said: It was revealed concerning the booty of Badr, because the Prophet ﷺ had given a nafl to some people for a trial they endured. Some of them endured trials, and others remained behind with the Messenger of God ﷺ. They differed about it after the war was over, so God revealed this verse to His Messenger, informing them that what the Messenger of God ﷺ did regarding it was right and binding.

Mention of those who said this:

15650. Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, saying: I heard Dawud ibn Abi Hind narrate, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, that the Prophet ﷺ said: "Whoever goes to such-and-such a place, he will have such-and-such; or whoever does such-and-such, he will have such-and-such." The young men hastened to it, and the elders remained by the banners. When God granted them victory, they came seeking what the Prophet ﷺ had designated for them. The elders said to them: Do not take it away without us! So God revealed the verse: ﴿So fear God and set right what is between you﴾. [[The report 15650: This report of Ibn 'Abbas is transmitted by Abu Ja'far through four chains, from no. 15650 to 15653, except the last of them, which is not traced back to Ibn 'Abbas. It is a report with a sound chain. The first chain is "Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman from Dawud...", which al-Hakim transmitted in al-Mustadrak 2:326 and said: "This is a hadith with a sound chain, though they (Bukhari and Muslim) did not include it," and al-Dhahabi agreed. Al-Bayhaqi transmitted it in al-Sunan al-Kubra 6:315, and in both there is an addition after "do not take it away without us": "For we were a support (ridf) for you." It was also cited by Ibn Kathir in his Tafsir 4:6, and by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur 3:159.]]

15651. Al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us [and Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us], saying: Dawud narrated to us, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: When the Day of Badr came, the Messenger of God ﷺ said: "Whoever does such-and-such, he will have such-and-such." He said: The young men of the men hastened to that, and the elders remained under the banners. When it came to the booty, they came seeking what had been designated for them. The elders said: Do not take preference over us, for we were a support (ridf) for you, and we were under the banners; if you had been routed, you would have retreated to us! They disputed, so God revealed: ﴿They ask you about the spoils. Say: The spoils belong to God and the Messenger. So fear God and set right what is between you, and obey God and His Messenger, if you are believers.﴾ [[The report 15651: This is the second chain of the report of Ibn 'Abbas mentioned above. "'Abd al-A'la" is 'Abd al-A'la ibn 'Abd al-A'la al-Qurashi al-Sulami, trustworthy, whom the whole group (of compilers) transmitted from. It passed as no. 4751 and 8282.]]

15652. Ishaq ibn Shahin narrated to me, saying: Khalid ibn 'Abd Allah narrated to us, from Dawud, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: When the Day of Badr came, the Messenger of God ﷺ said: "Whoever does such-and-such, he will have such-and-such as a nafl." He said: The youths advanced, and the elders kept to the banners and did not leave them. When victory was granted to them, the elders said: We were a support for you, so if you had been routed, you would have withdrawn to us. Do not take the booty away without us! The youths refused and said: The Messenger of God ﷺ gave it to us! So God revealed: ﴿They ask you about the spoils. Say: The spoils belong to God and the Messenger.﴾ He said: That was better for them, and likewise, obey me, for I know better. [[The report 15652: "Ishaq ibn Shahin al-Wasiti", a teacher of al-Tabari, has passed many times, the last at no. 11504. "Khalid ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Wasiti al-Tahhan" has also passed many times, the last at no. 11504. This report with this chain was transmitted by Abu Dawud in his Sunan 3:102, no. 2737, with slight differences in its wording. Its end there is: "So likewise, obey me, for I know better the outcome of this from you." It was transmitted by al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan 6:291, 292. It was also transmitted by al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak 2:131, 132, who said: "This is a sound hadith, for al-Bukhari relied on 'Ikrimah, and Muslim relied on Dawud ibn Abi Hind, though they did not include it," and al-Dhahabi said: "Sound; I say it meets the condition of al-Bukhari." The addition in it is as in the Sunan of Abu Dawud. Ibn Kathir cited it in his Tafsir 4:6, and added its attribution to al-Nasa'i, and Ibn Mardawayh (whose wording is there), and Ibn Hibban.]]

15653. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us, saying: Dawud narrated to us, from 'Ikrimah, regarding this verse: ﴿They ask you about the spoils. Say: The spoils belong to God and the Messenger﴾, he said: When the Day of Badr came, the Prophet ﷺ said: "Whoever does such-and-such, he will have such-and-such as a nafl!" Youths of the men went out and began to do it. When it came to the division, the elders said: We are the people of the banners, and we were a support for you! So God revealed concerning that: ﴿Say: The spoils belong to God and the Messenger. So fear God and set right what is between you, and obey God and His Messenger, if you are believers.﴾ [[The report 15653: See the comment on the preceding reports.]]

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 8, verse 1 (part 2 of 4):**

156654. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Ya'qub al-Zuhri narrated to us, saying: al-Mughira ibn Abd al-Rahman narrated to me, from his father, from Sulayman ibn Musa, from Makhul, client of the Hudhayl, from Abu Sallam, from Abu Umama al-Bahili, from Ubada ibn al-Samit, who said: "When the people disputed over the spoils on the day of Badr, Allah revealed: ﴿They ask you about the spoils﴾ up to His words ﴿if you are believers﴾." So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) divided them among them, *'an bawa'* (equally).

[[The report: 15654. This is the report of Ubada ibn al-Samit, transmitted here by two routes; this is the first of them. "Ishaq" is Ishaq ibn al-Hajjaj al-Tahhan, previously mentioned under nos. 230, 1614, 10314. "Ya'qub al-Zuhri" is Ya'qub ibn Muhammad ibn Isa al-Zuhri. He is disputed, but is trustworthy, God willing; previously mentioned under nos. 2867, 8012. In the printed edition here it read "al-Zubayri"; in the manuscript the letters are undotted and the most likely reading is what is adopted here, which is certainly correct, since Ya'qub ibn Muhammad al-Zuhri is the one who narrates from al-Mughira.
Al-Mughira ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Harith ibn Abd Allah ibn Ayyash ibn Abi Rabi'a al-Makhzumi is disputed. Ibn Hibban mentioned him in al-Thiqat and Ibn Ma'in deemed him trustworthy. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir (4/1/321), and Ibn Abi Hatim (4/1/225), which mention no criticism of him.
His father, Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Harith ibn Ayyash ibn Abi Rabi'a al-Makhzumi, is trustworthy, biographed in al-Tahdhib and Ibn Abi Hatim (2/2/224). Ibn Ishaq related from him in his Sira in several places; see 1:367.
Sulayman ibn Musa al-Umawi, al-Ashdaq, Abu Hisham, is trustworthy, previously mentioned under no. 11382.
Makhul, client of the Hudhayl, is Makhul al-Shami, Abu Abd Allah, the jurist of the Successors (tabi'un). He was among the captives of Kabul, and there was a lisp in his speech; it is related in his report: "What did you do about that *hajja*," meaning *haja* (need), where he changed the *ha'* to a *ha'*-sound. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, Ibn Sa'd (7/2/160), al-Kabir (4/2/21), and Ibn Abi Hatim (4/2/407).
Abu Sallam is al-Aswad al-Habashi al-A'raj, whose name is Mamtur, of the first generation of the Successors of the people of Syria. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir (4/2/57), and Ibn Abi Hatim (4/1/431).
Abu Umama al-Bahili, whose name is Suday ibn Ajlan, was a Companion of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He related from the Messenger of Allah and from a group of the Companions.
This report was transmitted by Makhul once through Abu Sallam from Abu Umama, and in the one following it he transmitted from Abu Umama without an intermediary. Ahmad transmitted it by this first route in his Musnad (5:323, 324), at length, with different wording, through Mu'awiya ibn Amr, from Abu Ishaq, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Ayyash ibn Abi Rabi'a, from Sulayman ibn Musa, from Abu Sallam, from Abu Umama, with no mention of Makhul in it.
Al-Bayhaqi transmitted it in al-Sunan al-Kubra (6:292), through Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Harith, from Sulayman al-Ashdaq, from Makhul, from Abu Sallam, from Abu Umama, at length, like Ahmad's version.
Al-Hakim transmitted it in al-Mustadrak (2:135) in similar form.
As for his words *'an bawa'*: in the printed edition it read *'an bisawa'* here and in the following report, which is a plain error. Its explanation will come in the context of the following report.]]

156655. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, from Muhammad, who said: Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Harith and others of our companions narrated to me, from Sulayman ibn Musa al-Ashdaq, from Makhul, from Abu Umama al-Bahili, who said: I asked Ubada ibn al-Samit about "the spoils" (al-anfal), and he said: "It was revealed concerning us, the company of the people of Badr, when we disputed over the *nafl* (extra portion), and our characters deteriorated over it. So Allah took it from our hands and placed it in the hands of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) divided it among the Muslims *'an bawa'* (equally)" = he means: "equally." "Thus there was in that the fear of Allah, obedience to His Messenger (ﷺ), and the reconciliation of relations among them."

[[The report: 15655. "Sulayman ibn Musa al-Ashdaq" has been mentioned in the preceding note. The printed edition had "al-Asadi," since the editor did not read the undotted manuscript correctly.
This report, transmitted by Muhammad ibn Ishaq, is mentioned in Ibn Hisham's Sira (2:295, 296) with this isnad, and then in (2:322) without an isnad.
Al-Tabari transmitted it with this isnad in his Tarikh (2:285, 286).
Ahmad transmitted it in his Musnad (5:322) by two routes from Muhammad ibn Ishaq.
Al-Hakim transmitted it in al-Mustadrak (2:136), referring to the wording of the report preceding it.
Then al-Hakim transmitted it in al-Mustadrak (2:326) by way of Wahb ibn Jarir ibn Hazim, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, who said: "al-Harith ibn Abd al-Rahman narrated to me, from Makhul, from Abu Umama." He said: "Sound according to the conditions of Muslim, though they did not record it." al-Dhahabi said: "According to the conditions of Muslim." I do not know how this can be, for what is established in Ibn Ishaq's Sira, in the transmission of Ibn Hisham, is that it is from his transmission from "Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Harith," not from "al-Harith ibn Abd al-Rahman," which is an error. Furthermore, it is transmitted with wording other than this in Ibn Hisham's Sira and in all the others who transmitted it from Ibn Ishaq, except Yunus ibn Bukayr.
Al-Bayhaqi transmitted it in al-Sunan al-Kubra (6:292) by way of Yunus ibn Bukayr, from Ibn Ishaq, from "Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Harith," with wording similar to al-Hakim's in al-Mustadrak. Then he said: "Jarir ibn Hazim transmitted it from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, with an abbreviation in its isnad." "Jarir ibn Hazim," through whom al-Hakim transmitted the report, is trustworthy, firm, and a memorizer; the community transmitted from him. But Ibn Hibban and others said: "He used to err, because most of what he narrated was from memory." So this seems to be among the things that caused him to be judged as one who sometimes abbreviates and errs. The pure correctness is what the transmission from Ibn Ishaq unanimously gives: "Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Harith."
Al-Haythami cited it here in Majma' al-Zawa'id (7:26) in its wording, together with the preceding report, from the lengthy route, then said: "The men of both routes are trustworthy." Ibn Kathir took it up in his Tafsir (6:5), and al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur (3:159).]]

* *

Others said: Rather, this verse was revealed [[In the printed edition, the word "rather" (bal) was dropped from the beginning of the statement.]] because some of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) asked him for something from the booty before it was divided, but he did not give it to him, since it was a shared portion among the army. So Allah made all of that belong to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). [[In the printed edition: "to the Messenger of Allah," and I have adopted what is in the manuscript.]]

Mention of those who said this:

156656. Ismail ibn Musa al-Sudi narrated to me, saying: Abu al-Ahwas narrated to us, from Asim, from Mus'ab ibn Sa'd, from Sa'd, who said: "I came to the Prophet (ﷺ) on the day of Badr with a sword, and I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, this sword with which Allah has healed my breast from the polytheists!' So I asked him for it, and he said: 'This is not mine, nor yours!' Then when I turned away, I said: 'I fear he will give it to someone who did not endure what I endured!' Then suddenly the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was behind me. I said: 'I fear something has been revealed concerning it!' He said: 'The sword has come to be mine!' So he gave it to me, and it was revealed: ﴿They ask you about the spoils﴾."

[[The report: 15656. This is the report of "Sa'd ibn Malik," who is Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas. Abu Ja'far transmitted it through seven routes, with different wordings, except no. 15659, whose isnad is broken. These are nos. 15656–15659, then 15662–15664.
He transmitted it through Asim, from Mus'ab ibn Sa'd, under nos. 15656 and 15657.
Through Simak ibn Harb, from Mus'ab ibn Sa'd, under nos. 15658, 15662, 15663.
Through Muhammad ibn Ubayd Allah, Abu Awn al-Thaqafi, from Mus'ab ibn Sa'd, no. 15659, with a broken isnad. Through Mujahid, from Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, no. 15664.
This is the explanation of the isnad of the first report: "Ismail ibn Musa al-Sudi al-Fazari," the teacher of al-Tabari, previously mentioned under nos. 849, 9682.
"Abu al-Ahwas" is Sallam ibn Sulaym al-Hanafi, the trustworthy memorizer, previously mentioned many times.
"Asim" is Asim ibn Abi al-Najud, previously mentioned many times.
"Mus'ab ibn Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas al-Zuhri" is a trustworthy Successor, previously mentioned under nos. 8941, 11450.
This is a sound isnad, and I have not found it in another place through Abu al-Ahwas from Mus'ab.]]

156657. Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Abu Bakr narrated to us, saying: Asim narrated to us, from Mus'ab ibn Sa'd, from Sa'd ibn Malik, who said: "When it was the day of Badr, I came with a sword." He said: "I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, indeed Allah has relieved my breast of the polytheists' = or something like this = 'so give me this sword!' He said to me: 'This is not mine, nor yours!' So I returned and said: 'Perhaps he will give this to someone who did not endure my endurance!' Then the messenger came to me, and I said: 'Something has happened concerning me!' When I arrived, he said: 'O Sa'd, you asked me for the sword, and it is not mine, but it has come to be mine, so it is yours!' And it was revealed: ﴿They ask you about the spoils. Say: The spoils belong to Allah and the Messenger﴾."

[[The report: 15657. Sound isnad. Ahmad transmitted it in his Musnad, no. 1538, similarly, at length. Abu Dawud transmitted it in his Sunan (3:103, no. 2740), similarly, at length. Al-Hakim transmitted it in al-Mustadrak (2:132), similarly, at length, and said: "This is a hadith sound in its isnad, though they did not record it," and al-Dhahabi agreed with him. Al-Bayhaqi transmitted it in al-Sunan (6:291). Ibn Kathir took it up in his Tafsir (4:4), and said: "Abu Dawud transmitted it," and al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i through routes from Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash, and al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan sahih."]]

156658. Ibn Wakih narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Israel, from Simak ibn Harb, from Mus'ab ibn Sa'd, from his father, who said: "I found a sword on the day of Badr and it pleased me, so I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, give it to me!' Then Allah revealed: ﴿They ask you about the spoils. Say: The spoils belong to Allah and the Messenger﴾."

[[The report: 15658. This is an abridgment of the report no. 15662, and its isnad is sound; I will take it up there.]]

156659. Ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Wakih narrated to us. Ibn al-Muthanna said: Abu Mu'awiya narrated to me. Ibn Wakih said: Abu Mu'awiya narrated to us. He said: al-Shaybani narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ubayd Allah, from Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, who said: "When it was the day of Badr, my brother Umayr was killed, and I killed Sa'id ibn al-As and took his sword, and it was called 'Dhu al-Katifa.' [[*Dhu al-Katifa* is on the pattern of *'azima*; *al-katifa* is a broad long piece of iron, and sometimes it is like a page, and sometimes they call the sword a *katif*.]] So I brought it to the Prophet (ﷺ), and he said: 'Go and throw it into the *qabd*!' [[*Al-qabd* (with two fathas): Abu Ubayd al-Qasim ibn Salam said: "*Al-qabd* is that in which the spoils are gathered." Others said: it means *al-maqbud*, which is what is collected from the booty before it is divided.]] So I threw it and returned, and I had within me what none knows but Allah, concerning the killing of my brother and the seizure of my spoils! He said: 'I had not gone beyond a short while when *Surat al-Anfal* was revealed upon him,' and he said: 'Go and take your sword!'" = The wording of the report is that of Ibn al-Muthanna.

[[The report: 15659. "Abu Mu'awiya" is the blind one, Muhammad ibn Khazim al-Tamimi al-Sa'di, trustworthy, one of Ahmad's teachers; the community transmitted from him.
In the printed edition here it read: "Ibn al-Muthanna said: Mu'awiya narrated to me," dropping "Abu," as if the editor thought Ibn al-Muthanna said "Mu'awiya" and Ibn Wakih said "Abu Mu'awiya," and that this was the point of difference! The correct point is that the difference lies in Ibn al-Muthanna's saying "narrated to me" and Ibn Wakih's saying "narrated to us." This is the extent of the mishandling!!
"Al-Shaybani" is Abu Ishaq al-Shaybani, Sulayman ibn Abi Sulayman, the trustworthy authority, previously mentioned many times.
"Muhammad ibn Ubayd Allah ibn Sa'id al-Thaqafi, Abu Awn al-Thaqafi," is a trustworthy Successor, but he did not meet Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, and his transmission from Sa'd is a *mursal* (where a Successor skips the Companion). (See the explanation of the isnad in the Musnad of Ahmad.) Previously mentioned under nos. 7595, 13965.
This report is weak in isnad, because of its break.
Ahmad transmitted it in his Musnad under no. 1556.
Abu Ubayd al-Qasim ibn Salam transmitted it in Kitab al-Amwal (303) in similar form. In the course of the report he said: "...I killed Sa'id ibn al-As." Others said: "al-As ibn Sa'id." Abu Ubayd said: "This, according to us, is the preserved version." Then he remarked, following it: "Abu Ubayd said: The people knowledgeable in the military campaigns said: The killer of al-As was Ali ibn Abi Talib." What Abu Ubayd said is correct.
What came in the report here, "Sa'id ibn al-As," is an error. Sa'id ibn al-As ibn Sa'id ibn al-As ibn Umayya al-Umawi was later; the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) died when he was nine years old, and he never associated others with God. His father, al-As ibn Sa'id, was killed as an unbeliever on the day of Badr. As for his grandfather, Sa'id ibn al-As ibn Umayya, he died an unbeliever before Badr. The correct version, as Ibn Hajar said in al-Isaba in the biography of Umayr ibn Abi Waqqas, is "al-As ibn Sa'id ibn al-As." The disagreement would then be over who killed him: was it Ali ibn Abi Talib or Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas? Though I have not found this disagreement. This point requires further verification. See the note on no. 15664.
Furthermore, I later saw in al-Rawd al-Unuf (2:76) this report from Abu Ubayd, and in it "al-As ibn Sa'id ibn al-As" in the body of the report; and I saw mention of this disagreement in al-Rawd al-Unuf (2:102, 103).]]

156660. Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Yunus ibn Bukayr narrated to us, and Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, all of them, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, who said: "Abd Allah ibn Abi Bakr narrated to me, from Qays ibn Sa'da, who said: I heard Abu Usayd Malik ibn Rabi'a say: 'I found the sword of Ibn A'idh on the day of Badr, and the sword was called "al-Marzuban." When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) commanded them to return what they had of the *nafl* (extra portion), I came with it and threw it into the *nafl*. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would not refuse anything he was asked, and al-Arqam ibn Abi al-Arqam al-Makhzumi saw it, so he asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he gave it to him.'"

[[The report: 15660. "Abd Allah ibn Abi Bakr ibn Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Hazm al-Ansari," trustworthy, transmitted by the community, previously mentioned under no. 4808.
As for his words "a man of the Banu Sa'ida," in the printed edition it was made "Qays ibn Sa'da," for reasons I do not know, altering what is in the manuscript.
As for "Abu Usayd Malik ibn Rabi'a al-Ansari," of the Banu Sa'ida ibn Ka'b ibn al-Khazraj, he is the well-known Companion, but the printed edition made him "Abu Usayd ibn Malik ibn Rabi'a," adding "ibn" without checking.
As for "the sword of Banu A'idh," the printed edition made it "the sword of Ibn A'idh," as in the following report. In the manuscript it is poorly written. The correct version is from Ibn Hisham's Sira, where it says: "the sword of the Banu A'idh al-Makhzumiyyun."
"A'idh" in the manuscript is undotted; in the printed edition it reads "A'id" with a *dal*. The correct version is what is in Ibn Hisham's Sira. Among the Banu Makhzum: "Banu A'idh ibn Imran ibn Makhzum" (with the dotted *dhal*), the kin of the family of al-Musayyab; and among the Banu Makhzum also: "Banu Abid ibn Abd Allah ibn Umar ibn Makhzum" (with *ba'* and undotted *dal*), who are the kin of the family of al-Sa'ib. See al-Rawd al-Unuf (2:76), Nasab Quraysh (333, then 343). I have found nothing to favor one over the other.
This report was transmitted by Ibn Ishaq in his Sira, Ibn Hisham (2:296), in these words. See the note on the following report.]]

156661. Yahya ibn Ja'far narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn Abi Bakr narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Imran, from his grandfather Uthman ibn al-Arqam = and from his uncle, from his grandfather, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said on the day of Badr: "Return what was of the spoils!" So Abu Usayd al-Sa'idi placed the sword of Ibn A'idh, "al-Marzuban," and al-Arqam recognized it, and said: "Give it to me, O Messenger of Allah!" He said: So he gave it to him.

[[The report: 15661. This is an abridgment of the earlier report through another route.
"Yahya ibn Ja'far" is "Yahya ibn Abi Talib," and "Yahya ibn Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr" is the teacher of al-Tabari, a well-known, trustworthy traditionist, previously mentioned under no. 284.
"Ahmad ibn Abi Bakr" is Ahmad ibn al-Qasim ibn al-Harith ibn Zurara ibn Mus'ab ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf al-Zuhri, whose kunya is "Abu Mus'ab al-Zuhri," trustworthy, transmitted by the community. Biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir (1/2/6), and Ibn Abi Hatim (1/1/43).
"Yahya ibn Imran ibn Uthman ibn al-Arqam al-Makhzumi" transmitted from his father and his uncle, "Abd Allah ibn Uthman." Transmitting from him were Attaf ibn Khalid and Abu Mus'ab al-Zuhri, "Ahmad ibn Abi Bakr," and others. Ibn Hibban mentioned him in al-Thiqat. He is biographed in Ta'jil al-Manfa'a (446), al-Kabir (4/2/297), where no criticism of him is mentioned, and Ibn Abi Hatim (4/2/177, 178). Ibn Abi Hatim said: "I asked my father about him, and he said: 'A Medinan teacher, unknown.'"]]

As for his saying, "and from his paternal uncle, from his grandfather" (وعن عمه، عن جده), it appears in the printed edition and in the manuscript as "from his paternal uncle, from his grandfather" without the conjunction waw (واو العطف). That does not stand grammatically and is a plain error. The correct reading is that Yahya ibn Imran (يحيى بن عمران) narrated it directly from his grandfather, and he also narrated it once more from his paternal uncle, Abdullah ibn Uthman (عبد الله بن عثمان), from the same grandfather.

Abdullah ibn Uthman ibn al-Arqam (عبد الله بن عثمان بن الأرقم), in the printed edition "Ibn al-Arqam" is repeated by mistake, is al-Makhzumi (المخزومي). He is biographed in Ta'jil al-Manfa'a (تعجيل المنفعة), p. 228, and in Ibn Abi Hatim (ابن أبي حاتم) 2/2/113. They mention no criticism of him.

This report is an abridged version of the one before it, and I have not found it elsewhere.

15662. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'ba narrated to us, from Simak ibn Harb, from Mus'ab ibn Sa'd, from his father, who said: "I found a sword," — he said — "so I brought it to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, grant it to me as a spoil (nafl)!' He said: 'Put it down!' Then I got up and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, grant it to me as a spoil!' He said: 'Put it down!' He said: Then I got up and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, grant it to me as a spoil! Shall I be like one who has no worth?' The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'Put it back where you took it from!' Then this verse was revealed: ﴿They ask you about the spoils. Say: The spoils belong to Allah and the Messenger.﴾"

[Note on the report: this is another route for the report of Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, as explained in no. 15656. It is a report with a sound chain (sahih al-isnad), through Simak ibn Harb from Mus'ab ibn Sa'd. Ahmad (أحمد) narrated it with this chain in al-Musnad (المسند), no. 1567 and 1614, in a long report part of which passed in the matter of the prohibition of wine, no. 12518 in Tafsir al-Tabari. Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi (أبو داود الطيالسي) narrated it in his Musnad, p. 28, no. 208. Muslim narrated it in his Sahih, 12:53, 54. Al-Bayhaqi narrated it in al-Sunan al-Kubra, 6:291, and Ibn Kathir (ابن كثير) cited it in his Tafsir, 4:5. Abu Ja'far al-Nahhas (أبو جعفر النحاس) narrated it in al-Nasikh wal-Mansukh (الناسخ والمنسوخ), p. 150, through Zuhayr ibn Mu'awiya from Simak ibn Harb, with a different wording.]

15663. Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Isra'il narrated to us, from Simak, from Mus'ab ibn Sa'd, from Sa'd, who said: "I took a sword from the booty, so I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, give this to me!' Then this was revealed: 'They ask you about the spoils.'"

[Note: this is an abridged version of the one before it.]

15664. Al-Harith narrated to me, saying: Abd al-Aziz narrated to us, saying: Isra'il narrated to us, from Ibrahim ibn al-Muhajir, from Mujahid, concerning His saying: ﴿They ask you about the spoils﴾, he said: Sa'd said: "I had taken the sword of Sa'id ibn al-As ibn Umayya, and I came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: 'Give me this sword, O Messenger of Allah!' He remained silent, so this was revealed: ﴿They ask you about the spoils﴾, up to His saying: ﴿if you are believers﴾." He said: "So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gave it to me."

[Note: Isra'il is Isra'il ibn Yunus ibn Abi Ishaq al-Sabi'i (إسرائيل بن يونس بن أبي إسحاق السبيعي), who has passed many times. Ibrahim ibn al-Muhajir ibn Jabir al-Bajali (إبراهيم بن المهاجر بن جابر البجلي) is trustworthy, though some have spoken about him; he passed at no. 1291 with a similar chain. Mujahid is Mujahid ibn Jabr al-Makki al-Makhzumi (مجاهد بن جبر المكي المخزومي), the trustworthy Imam, who narrated from Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas and other Companions. This report therefore has a sound chain from Isra'il up to Mujahid.

As for al-Harith, he is al-Harith ibn Abi Usama (الحارث بن أبي أسامة), who is trustworthy, and passed at no. 10295 and elsewhere.

As for Abd al-Aziz, he is Abd al-Aziz ibn Aban al-Umawi (عبد العزيز بن أبان الأموي), a descendant of Sa'id ibn al-As ibn Umayya. He is a liar and a wicked fabricator of hadith. He passed at no. 10295 and elsewhere; refer to the indexes of narrators. Therefore the chain is weak because of him, until I find a narration from him through someone other than the liar, as the critics of narrators (ahl al-jarh wal-ta'dil) have said.

In this report, the mention of Sa'id ibn al-As ibn Umayya is clear. I had stated in my comment on no. 15659 that Sa'id ibn al-As ibn Umayya died as a polytheist before the day of Badr, which is why his saying in that report, "I killed Sa'id ibn al-As," was not authenticated for us. In this report, however, it is consistent, because he said: "I took the sword of Sa'id ibn al-As." His sword was without doubt well known to Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, and it was with his son who was killed at Badr, al-As ibn Sa'id ibn al-As. It is evident that he was fighting with it on the day of Badr and was killed while carrying it, and Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas took it. Nevertheless, the disagreement over the killing of al-As ibn Sa'id ibn al-As remains as it is: was he killed by Ali ibn Abi Talib, as the authorities on the biographies and campaigns (ashab al-siyar wal-maghazi) said, or was he killed by Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, as the sound report from him indicates? Refer to the comment on no. 15659. See also al-Rawd al-Unf (الروض الأنف) 2:102, 103, which mentions this disagreement.]

* *

Others said: Rather, it was revealed because the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) asked for the distribution of the booty among themselves on the day of Badr, so Allah informed them that it belongs to Allah and to His Messenger, not to them, and they have no share in it. They said: The meaning of "from" (عن) in this place is "from" (من), and the meaning of the statement is: "They ask you from the spoils." They also said: Ibn Mas'ud used to recite it, "yas'aluunaka al-anfal" (يَسْأَلُونَكَ الأنْفَالَ), according to this interpretation.

Those who said this:

15665. Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Mu'ammal narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-A'mash, who said: "The companions of Abdullah (Ibn Mas'ud) used to recite it: 'yas'aluunaka al-anfal'."

15666. Ibn Wakic narrated to us, saying: al-Mahariibi narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, who said: "It is in the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud: 'yas'aluunaka al-anfal'."

* *

Those who said this:

15667. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas concerning His saying: ﴿They ask you about the spoils. Say: The spoils belong to Allah and the Messenger﴾. He said: "The anfal (الأنفال) are the spoils, which were exclusively for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and no one had any share of them. Whatever the Muslim detachments (sara'ya) obtained, they brought to him, and whoever kept a needle or a thread from it, that is ghulul (غلول), embezzlement. [Note: in the manuscript it reads: "in his withholding of it", and the correct reading is what is in the printed edition, which agrees with what is in al-Bayhaqi. Ghulul is the embezzlement of the booty and theft from the spoils.] So they asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to give them some of it, and Allah said: ﴿They ask you about the spoils. Say: The spoils are Mine; I have given them to My Messenger; you have no share in them﴾ — ﴿So fear Allah and set right what is between you, and obey Allah and His Messenger, if you are believers﴾. Then Allah revealed: ﴿And know that whatever you obtain of spoils, a fifth of it belongs to Allah and to the Messenger﴾ [Surah al-Anfal: 41]. Then that fifth was distributed by the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and to those named in the verse."

[Note: this chain has passed at nos. 1833 and 8472, and it is a broken chain (munqati'), because Ali ibn Talha did not hear the Tafsir from Ibn Abbas. This report was narrated by al-Bayhaqi through this same route in al-Sunan al-Kubra, 6:293, in full.]

15668. Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj: "They ask you about the spoils," he said: It was revealed concerning the Muhajirun and the Ansar who witnessed Badr. He said: They disagreed, so they became three groups. He said: Then this was revealed: ﴿They ask you about the spoils. Say: The spoils belong to Allah and the Messenger﴾, and Allah made His Messenger its owner, so he distributed it as Allah showed him. [Note: the printed edition has "so he distributed it" (فقسمه); I have kept what is in the manuscript.]

15669. Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Abbad ibn al-Awwam narrated to us, from al-Hajjaj, from Amr ibn Shu'ayb, from his father, from his grandfather: that the people asked the Prophet (ﷺ) about the booty on the day of Badr, so this was revealed: ﴿They ask you about the spoils﴾.

[Note: Abbad ibn al-Awwam al-Wasiti (عباد بن العوام الواسطي) is trustworthy and one of Ahmad's teachers; he passed at no. 5433. Al-Hajjaj is al-Hajjaj ibn Artat al-Nakha'i (الحجاج بن أرطاة النخعي), who passed at nos. 3299, 3960, 4246, 9631, 10138. He is trustworthy, but he used to conceal his sources (yudallis) in narrating from Amr ibn Shu'ayb. Muhammad ibn Nasr said: "What predominates in his narrations is inqita' (omission of a link), tadlis, and alteration of wordings." The scholars required that his hadith be stated explicitly as heard, and this report is one in which hearing is not stated explicitly. So this report is weak for this reason.

As for Amr ibn Shu'ayb ibn Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As (عمرو بن شعيب بن محمد بن عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص), the critics objected to his frequent narration from his father, from his grandfather Abdullah ibn Amr. Abu Zur'a (أبو زرعة) said: "He only heard a few hadiths, and took a manuscript that was in his possession and narrated from it." He is trustworthy in himself, and his hadiths "from his father, from his grandfather" are acceptable, but they did not include them in the authentic collections (sihah) that they compiled.]

15670. ... He said: Abbad ibn al-Awwam narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak: "They ask you about the spoils," he said: They ask you to grant them spoils.

15671. Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us, saying: Ayyub narrated to us, from Ikrima, concerning His saying: "They ask you about the spoils," he said: They ask you for the spoils.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of the statements on this matter is to say: Allah, exalted is His praise, informed in this verse about a people who asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) for the spoils, that he would give them to them, so Allah informed them that they belong to Allah, and that He had made them for His Messenger.

When that is its meaning, it is permissible that its revelation was because of the disagreement among the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) concerning them. It is also permissible that it was because of the request of the one who asked for the sword which we mentioned from Sa'd, that he asked for it. And it is permissible that it was because of the request of those who asked for its division among the army.

* *

They differed concerning it: is it abrogated (mansukha) or not abrogated?

Some said: It is abrogated. They said: It was abrogated by His saying: ﴿And know that whatever you obtain of spoils, a fifth of it belongs to Allah and to the Messenger﴾, the verse [Surah al-Anfal: 41].

Those who said this:

15672. Ibn Wakic narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Jabir, from Mujahid and Ikrima, who both said: The anfal were for Allah and the Messenger, and it was abrogated by: ﴿And know that whatever you obtain of spoils, a fifth of it belongs to Allah and to the Messenger﴾.

15673. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "They ask you about the spoils," he said: Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas obtained a sword at the day of Badr, and he disputed about it with some men who were with him, so they asked the Prophet (ﷺ), and the Prophet (ﷺ) took it from them. Then Allah said: ﴿They ask you about the spoils. Say: The spoils belong to Allah and the Messenger﴾, the verse. So the booty on that day was exclusively for the Prophet (ﷺ), then Allah abrogated it with the fifth.

15674. Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Salim, the mawla (client) of Umm Muhammad, informed me, from Mujahid, concerning His saying: "They ask you about the spoils," he said: It abrogated it: ﴿And know that whatever you obtain of spoils, a fifth of it belongs to Allah﴾.

[Note: "Salim, mawla of Umm Muhammad" (سليم مولى أم محمد): I have not found him. The one who narrates from Mujahid and whom Ibn Jurayj narrates from is Salim, Abu Ubayd Allah, mawla of Umm Ali (سليم، أبو عبيد الله مولى أم علي), who passed at no. 4305. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 2/2/127, and Ibn Abi Hatim 2/1/213. He is one of the senior students of Mujahid, and Ibn Hibban mentioned him in al-Thiqat.]

15675. Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Shurayk narrated to us, from Jabir, from Mujahid and Ikrima — or: Ikrima and Amir — who both said: The anfal were abrogated by: ﴿And know that whatever you obtain of spoils, a fifth of it belongs to Allah﴾.

* *

Others said: It is muhkama (محكمة), not abrogated. The meaning is only: "Say: the spoils belong to Allah," and they are without doubt for Allah, along with this world and what is in it, and the Hereafter; and for the Messenger, who places them in the places which Allah commanded him to place them.

Those who said this:

15676. Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said concerning His saying: "They ask you about the spoils," and he recited until he reached: "if you are believers." They submitted to Allah and His Messenger, who judge concerning them as they wish, and place them where they wish. So they said: Yes! Then after forty (verses) came: ﴿And know that whatever you obtain of spoils, a fifth of it belongs to Allah and to the Messenger﴾, the verse [Surah al-Anfal: 41], and for you are four-fifths. The Prophet (ﷺ) said on the day of Khaybar: "This fifth is returned to your poor," and Allah and His Messenger do with that fifth what they love, and place it where they love. Then Allah informed us of what is due from it. Then he recited the verse: ﴿And to the near of kin, the orphans, the needy, and the wayfarer, so that it will not be a circulation among the rich among you﴾ [Surah al-Hashr: 7].

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct statement on this matter is to say: Allah, exalted is His praise, informed that He made the anfal for His Prophet (ﷺ), to grant to whom he wills. He granted the slayer the spoils (salab) of the one he killed, and he assigned to the army a quarter in the beginning of the campaign (al-bad'a), and a third on the return (al-raj'a) after the fifth. [Note: al-bad'a is the start of the military journey; al-raj'a is the return from it. When a detachment (sariya) set out from the main army that was advancing against the enemy, and it struck part of the enemy, what they captured belonged to them as a quarter, and the rest of the army shared in the remaining three-quarters of what they captured. When they did this on the army's return, they received a third of everything they captured, because the second attack is harder on them and its danger is greater. That is because their strength is at its height when they go out and weakest when they return; at the beginning they are more energetic and eager for the march and for penetrating deep into enemy land, while on the return they are weaker and more exhausted and eager to return to their homelands, so they were given more for that reason.] He also granted to a group, after their shares, a camel each in some campaigns. So Allah, exalted is His mention, placed the ruling on the anfal in the hands of His Prophet (ﷺ), who grants as he sees fit what contains the welfare of the Muslims, and whoever comes after him among the imams should follow his sunna in that.

There is no proof in the verse that its ruling is abrogated, since it admits the meaning I have described. It is not permissible to rule that a ruling which the Qur'an came with is abrogated, except with a proof to which submission is required. We have shown in more than one place in our books that there is no abrogation except where a ruling is nullified by the emergence of a later ruling contrary to it, negating it in all its meanings, or where a report comes that establishes conclusively that one of them abrogates the other. [Note: see Abu Ja'far's discussion of "al-naskh" (النسخ) in the topical indexes, and the indexes of grammar and Arabic linguistics, and others.]

* *

It has been mentioned from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib that he used to deny that granting spoils (al-tanfil) could be given to anyone after the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), interpreting in this way the saying of Allah, exalted is He: "Say: the anfal belong to Allah and the Messenger."

15677. Ibn Wakic narrated to us, saying: Abdah ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Amr, who said: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib sent his servant to a people who had asked him about something, and he said: "You sent to me asking me about the anfal, but there is no nafl after the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)."

* *

We have shown that the imams may follow the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in their campaigns by his practice, so they may grant spoils in the manner in which he used to grant them, when granting spoils is beneficial for the Muslims.

* *

On the interpretation of His saying: ﴿So fear Allah and set right what is between you, and obey Allah and His Messenger, if you are believers﴾ (1)

Abu Ja'far said: His exalted mention says: So fear Allah, O people, and be mindful of Him by obeying Him and avoiding His disobedience, and set right the state of affairs among you.

* *

The interpreters differed concerning whom He meant by His saying: "and set right what is between you."

Some said: It is a command from Allah to those who took the booty on the day of Badr and witnessed the battle with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), when they disputed over the booty: that some of them return what they obtained of it to others. [Note: in the printed edition it reads "that they return" in the plural, and I have kept what is in the manuscript, which is correct.]

Those who said this:

15678. Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada: "So fear Allah and set right what is between you," he said: The Prophet of Allah used to grant a believing man the salab of a disbelieving man whom he had killed. Then Allah revealed: "So fear Allah and set right what is between you," commanding them that some of them return to others.

15679. Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: It reached me that the Prophet (ﷺ) used to grant a man according to the measure of his effort and his strength, as he saw fit. Then, when it was the day of Badr and the people filled their hands with booty, the weak among the people said: "The people of strength have taken the booty!" They mentioned that to the Prophet (ﷺ), and this was revealed: "Say: the anfal belong to Allah and the Messenger; so fear Allah and set right what is between you," so that the people of strength would return to the people of weakness.

* *

Others said: This is a restriction (tahrij) imposed by Allah on the people, and a prohibition for them against disagreeing over what they disagreed about concerning the matter of the booty and other things.

Those who said this:

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 8, verse 1 (part 4 of 4):

15680 - Muhammad ibn Umarah narrated to me, saying: Khalid ibn Yazid narrated to us. And Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us; both said: Abu Isra'il narrated to us, from Fudayl, from Mujahid, concerning the words of Allah: ﴿So fear Allah and amend the relations among yourselves﴾, he said: He imposed a binding obligation (tahrij) upon them.

15681 - al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Abbad ibn al-Awwam narrated to us, from Sufyan ibn Husayn, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿So fear Allah and amend the relations among yourselves﴾. He said: This is a binding obligation from Allah upon the believers, that they should fear Him and amend the relations among themselves. Abbad said: Sufyan said: This was when they disagreed about the spoils on the day of Badr.

15682 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿So fear Allah and amend the relations among yourselves﴾, meaning: do not revile one another.

* *

The grammarians differed concerning the reason for the feminine form of "al-bayn" (the relations/between).

Some of the grammarians of Basra said: He made "dhat" (possessor of) an adjunct to "al-bayn" and treated it as "dhat," because some things are assigned a feminine noun and some are assigned a masculine, as with "al-dar" (the house), which is feminine, and "al-ha'it" (the wall), which is masculine; he made "al-dar" feminine and "al-ha'it" masculine.

* *

Others said: By His words "dhat baynikum" he meant the state that belongs to the relation, and he said: Likewise "dhat al-'isha" (the evening), meaning the hour in which the evening prayer occurs. He said: They did not assign a masculine form to a feminine thing, nor a feminine form to a masculine thing, except for a meaning.

* *

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: This view is the more correct of the two opinions, for the reason I have mentioned.

* *

As for His words ﴿and obey Allah and His Messenger﴾, their meaning is: Desist, O people who seek the spoils, and submit to the command of Allah and the command of His Messenger concerning what Allah has granted you, for He has made clear to you its aspects and its ways. ﴿If you are believers﴾ means: if you are those who confirm the Messenger of Allah in what he has brought you from your Lord, as follows:

15683 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: ﴿So fear Allah and amend the relations among yourselves and obey Allah and His Messenger, if you are believers﴾, submit to Allah and His Messenger; they judge concerning it as they wish, and place it where they desire.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 8, verse 2:

The exposition of His saying: ﴿The believers are only those who, when Allah is mentioned, their hearts tremble, and when His verses are recited to them, they increase them in faith, and upon their Lord they rely.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, exalted is His mention, says: The believer is not one who opposes Allah and His Messenger, and abandons following what He has sent down to him in His Book of limits and obligations, and submission to His judgment. Rather, the believer is the one who, when Allah is mentioned, his heart trembles, submits to His command, and humbles himself before His remembrance, out of fear of Him and dread of His punishment. And when the verses of His Book are recited to him, he affirms them [see the explanation of "recitation" above, p. 252, footnote 2, and the references there], and is certain that they are from Allah, so his affirmation of that increases him in faith, beyond his affirmation of what had reached him from Him before that, as a confirmation. That is the increase in faith that the verses of Allah recited to them bring them: ﴿and upon their Lord they rely﴾ means: they are certain in Allah that His decree concerning them is binding, so they hope for none other than Him and fear none other than Him. [See the explanation of "al-Wakil" above, vol. 12, p. 563, footnote 1, and the references there.]

* *

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said the same as what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said that:

15684- Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abu Salih told us, he said: Mu'awiyah told me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿The believers are only those who, when Allah is mentioned, their hearts tremble﴾. He said: They are the hypocrites, in whose hearts nothing of the remembrance of Allah enters when fulfilling His obligations, and who do not believe in anything of the verses of Allah, nor rely upon Allah, nor pray when they are absent, nor pay the zakat of their wealth. So Allah, glorified is He, informed that they are not believers. Then He described the believers, saying: ﴿The believers are only those who, when Allah is mentioned, their hearts tremble﴾, so they fulfill His obligations; ﴿and when His verses are recited to them, they increase them in faith﴾, meaning: in affirmation; ﴿and upon their Lord they rely﴾, meaning: they hope for none other than Him.

15685- Ibn Waki' told us, he said: Abdullah told us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Abdullah ibn Kathir, from Mujahid: ﴿those who, when Allah is mentioned, their hearts tremble﴾, he said: they are frightened.

15686- ... he said: My father told us, from Sufyan, from al-Suddi: ﴿those who, when Allah is mentioned, their hearts tremble﴾, he said: when Allah is mentioned at a matter, his heart trembles.

15687- Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told me, he said: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, he said: Asbat told us, from al-Suddi: ﴿The believers are only those who, when Allah is mentioned, their hearts tremble﴾, meaning: when Allah is mentioned, his heart trembles.

15688- Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding the saying of Allah: ﴿their hearts tremble﴾, he said: they are frightened.

15689- Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said: Shibl told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿their hearts tremble﴾, they are frightened.

15690- ... he said: Suwayd told us, he said: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Sufyan, who said: I heard al-Suddi say regarding His saying: ﴿The believers are only those who, when Allah is mentioned, their hearts tremble﴾: he is the man who intends to wrong [someone], or he said: who resolves upon disobedience, I think he said: then he refrains from it.

15691- Al-Harith told me, he said: Abd al-Aziz told us, he said: Sufyan al-Thawri told us, from Abdullah ibn Uthman ibn Khuthaym, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Abu al-Darda regarding His saying: ﴿The believers are only those who, when Allah is mentioned, their hearts tremble﴾, he said: The trembling in the heart is like the burning of the sa'fah [the sa'fah (with two fathahs) is the leaf of the palm frond when it dries]. Do you not find a shiver from it? He said: Yes! He said: When you find that in your heart, then call upon Allah, for supplication removes that.

15692- Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah regarding His saying: ﴿The believers are only those who, when Allah is mentioned, their hearts tremble﴾, he said: fear of Allah, blessed and exalted is He, and trembling before Allah, and dread of Allah, blessed and exalted is He.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿they increase them in faith﴾, I have already mentioned the statement of Ibn Abbas regarding it. [That is, number 15684.]

* *

Others said regarding it:

15693- Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Ishaq told us, he said: Abdullah ibn Abi Ja'far told us, from his father, from al-Rabi': ﴿and when His verses are recited to them, they increase them in faith﴾, he said: fear (khashyah).

15694- Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah: ﴿and when His verses are recited to them, they increase them in faith, and upon their Lord they rely﴾, he said: This is the description of the people of faith; He affirmed their attribute, and described them, so He affirmed their qualities.

The discussion of His saying: ﴿Those who establish prayer and spend of what We have provided for them(3). Those are the true believers﴾

Abu Ja'far said: May His remembrance be exalted, He says: those who perform the obligatory prayer in its prescribed limits, and who spend from what Allah has provided them of wealth in the matters in which Allah has commanded them to spend it, such as zakat, jihad, hajj, umrah, and maintenance of those whose maintenance is obligatory upon them, thus fulfilling their duties to them. "Those," he says: these are the ones who do these deeds [[See the explanations of "establishing prayer," "provision," and "spending" in the linguistic indexes earlier (q-w-m), (r-z-q), (n-f-q).]] "are the true believers," not those who say with their tongues, "We have believed," while their hearts harbor the opposite out of hypocrisy, who neither establish prayer nor pay zakat.

* *

And the people of interpretation have said what is similar to what we have said.

Those who said that:

15695. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah ibn Salih narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas: "Those who establish prayer," he said: the five prayers. "And spend of what We have provided them," he said: the zakat of their wealth [[See the explanation of "haqqan" in the linguistic indexes earlier (h-q-q).]] "Those are the true believers," he said: they are free from disbelief. Then Allah described hypocrisy and its people, saying: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve in Allah and His messengers and wish to make distinction between Allah and His messengers﴾ up to His saying: ﴿Those are the disbelievers in truth﴾ [Surah an-Nisa: 150-151]. So Allah made the believer a believer in truth, and made the disbeliever a disbeliever in truth, and this is His saying: ﴿He is the One who created you, and among you is a disbeliever and among you is a believer﴾ [Surah at-Taghabun: 2].

15696. Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: "Those are the true believers," he said: they deserved faith rightfully, so Allah made it right for them.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 8, verse 4:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿For them are ranks (darajat) with their Lord, and forgiveness and generous provision﴾ (8:4)

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying "For them are ranks" — that is, for these believers whose attributes He has described — "ranks" (darajat), meaning elevated stations. [See the explanation of "ranks" (al-darajah) above, vol. 12, p. 289, footnote 1, and the references there.]

* *

Then the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed concerning these "ranks" which God mentioned as belonging to them with Him: what are they?

Some of them said: They are elevated deeds and virtues they sent forward during their lifetimes.

Those who said this:

15697 - Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to me, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Isra'il narrated to us, from Abu Yahya al-Qattat, from Mujahid: "For them are ranks with their Lord," he said: elevated deeds. [The report 15697: Abu Yahya al-Qattat is weak; it passed as no. 12139.]

* *

Others said: Rather, these are degrees in Paradise.

Those who said this:

15698 - Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Hisham, from Jabalah, from Atiyyah, from Ibn Muhayriz: "For them are ranks with their Lord," he said: The ranks are seventy ranks, each rank the distance a well-trained racing horse runs in seventy years at full gallop. [The report 15698: "Sufyan" is al-Thawri. "Hisham" is Hisham ibn Hassan al-Qardusi, passed as nos. 2827, 7287, 9837, 10258. "Jabalah" is Jabalah ibn Suhaym al-Taymi, passed as nos. 3003, 10258; in the printed and manuscript editions it reads "Hisham ibn Jabalah," which is a clear error. As for "Atiyyah," I do not know who he is, and I am doubtful about him. "Ibn Muhayriz" is Abdullah ibn Muhayriz al-Jumahi, passed as nos. 8720, 10258. A similar report in a different verse was transmitted earlier as no. 10258: "Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Azdi narrated to us, saying: al-Ashja'i narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Hisham ibn Hassan, from Jabalah ibn Suhaym, from Ibn Muhayriz," without the "Ibn Atiyyah" found here. "Al-hudr" (with a vowel on the h and a sukun) is the height of a horse's leap in its running. "Al-mudammar" is the horse prepared for racing and galloping.]

* *

As for His saying "and forgiveness," it means: pardon for their sins and covering over them [see the explanation of "forgiveness" (al-maghfirah) in the lexical indexes above, under the root gh-f-r] — "and generous provision": it has been said this is Paradise. In my view, it is what God has prepared for them in Paradise of abundant foods, drinks and pleasant living. [See the explanation of "generous" (karim) above, vol. 8, p. 259.]

15699 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, from Hisham, from Amr, from Sa'id, from Qatadah: "and forgiveness," he said: for their sins. "and generous provision," he said: Paradise.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 8, verse 5–6:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿As your Lord brought you forth from your house in truth, though a party of the believers were averse﴾ (5) ﴿disputing with you concerning the truth after it had become clear, as if they were being driven to death while they looked on﴾ (6).

Abu Ja'far said: The exegetes differed concerning what the "ka" (the "as") in His saying "as your Lord brought you forth" governs, and what was being compared to God's bringing forth His Prophet ﷺ from his house in truth.

Some of them said: It was compared to what is good for the believers: their being mindful of their Lord, their setting right their mutual relations, and their obedience to God and His Messenger. They said: the meaning is: God says, "Set right your mutual relations, for that is better for you, just as God brought Muhammad ﷺ forth from his house in truth, and it was good for him." [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "kana khayran lahu" without the fa', and the correct reading is what is established here; in the manuscript it is poorly written.]]

Those who said this:

15700- Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us, saying: Dawud narrated to us, from Ikrimah: "So fear God, set right your mutual relations, and obey God and His Messenger, if you are believers. As your Lord brought you forth from your house in truth," the verse; meaning: this is better for you, just as your bringing forth from your house in truth was better for you.

* *

Others said: The meaning is: As your Lord brought you forth, O Muhammad, from your house in truth, despite the aversion of a party of the believers, so too they are averse to fighting, and so they dispute with you concerning it after it has become clear to them.

Those who said this:

15701- Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "As your Lord brought you forth from your house in truth," he said: so they dispute with you concerning the truth.

15702- al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "As your Lord brought you forth from your house in truth," so they dispute with you concerning the truth, the fighting.

15703-. . . . He said: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid concerning His saying: "As your Lord brought you forth from your house in truth," he said: thus your Lord brought you forth. [[So it is in the manuscript and the printed edition; perhaps the correct reading is: "he said: thus they dispute with you," which is what the preceding reports from Mujahid indicate.]]

15704- Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said: God revealed concerning his going forth — meaning the going forth of the Prophet ﷺ — to Badr, and their disputing with him: "As your Lord brought you forth from your house in truth, and indeed a party of the believers were averse," to pursue the polytheists, "disputing with you concerning the truth after it had become clear."

* *

The grammarians differed concerning this.

Some of the Kufan grammarians said: This is a command from God to His Messenger ﷺ to proceed with His command concerning the spoils, despite the aversion of his companions, just as He had proceeded with His command concerning his going forth from his house to pursue the caravan while they were averse. [[See al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1: 403.]]

* *

Others among them said: The meaning is: they ask you about the spoils while disputing, just as they disputed with you on the day of Badr, saying: "You brought us out for the caravan and did not inform us that we would fight, so that we might prepare for it."

Some of the Basran grammarians said: It is permissible that this "ka" in "as You brought you forth" relates to His saying: "Those are the true believers" (8:4), "as your Lord brought you forth from your house in truth." And he said: the "ka" means "upon" ("'ala"). [[In the printed edition: "Qila: al-kaf ..." as if another opinion; the correct reading is what is in the manuscript. The likely speaker of this is al-Akhfash, for he is the one who said: "the kaf means 'upon'," and claimed that among the speech of the Arabs, when one of them is asked "how did you wake?", he says "like good," meaning "upon good."

See the explanation of "kama" earlier, 3: 209, in His saying: "as We sent among you a messenger" [Surah al-Baqarah: 151].]]

* *

Others among them [[In the printed edition: "Wa qala akharun," in the plural; I have kept what is in the manuscript, which is correct, and the one who said this is Abu 'Ubaydah Ma'mar ibn al-Muthanna.]] said: it is in the sense of an oath. He said: the meaning of the statement is: "By Him who brought you forth, your Lord..." [[See Abu 'Ubaydah's Majaz al-Qur'an 1: 240, 241.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most preferable of these sayings to me as correct is the saying of the one who said, following Mujahid, that the meaning is: as your Lord brought you forth in truth despite the aversion of a party of the believers, so they dispute with you concerning the truth after it has become clear. Because both matters occurred: namely, the going forth of some who went out from Madinah in aversion, and their disputing about meeting the enemy when the two groups drew close to one another. So comparing some of this to some of that, given the closeness of the one to the other, is more preferable than comparing it to what is far from it.

* *

Mujahid said that "the truth" concerning which they are said to have disputed with the Prophet ﷺ after it had become clear to them is the fighting.

15705- Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "They dispute with you concerning the truth," he said: the fighting.

15706- al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

15707- Ishaq narrated to us, saying: 'Abd Allah narrated to us, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

* *

As for His saying: "from your house," some of them said: its meaning is: from Madinah.

Those who said this:

15708- al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Bazzah: "As your Lord brought you forth from your house," Madinah, to Badr.

15709- al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj who said: Muhammad ibn 'Abbad ibn Ja'far informed me concerning His saying: "As your Lord brought you forth from your house in truth," he said: from Madinah to Badr.

* *

As for His saying: "and indeed a party of the believers were averse," their aversion was as follows:

15710- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq who said: Muhammad ibn Muslim al-Zuhri, 'Asim ibn 'Umar ibn Qatadah, 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Bakr, and Yazid ibn Ruman narrated to me, from 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr and others of our scholars, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abbas, who said: When the Messenger of God ﷺ heard of Abu Sufyan approaching from al-Sham, he called the Muslims to them, and said: "This is the caravan of Quraysh, in which is their wealth. Go out to it; perhaps God will grant it to you as spoils!" The people responded; some went lightly and some were reluctant, for they did not think that the Messenger of God ﷺ would meet a battle. [[The report: 15710 - Sirah of Ibn Hisham 2: 257, 258.]]

15711- Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "And indeed a party of the believers were averse," to pursue the polytheists.

* *

Then the exegetes differed concerning those meant by His saying: "disputing with you concerning the truth after it had become clear."
