**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 8, verse 7 (part 1 of 2)**

On the interpretation (*ta'wil*, the explanation and meaning) of His saying: ﴿And when Allah promised you one of the two groups, that it would be yours, and you wished that the one without the thorn [of military strength] would be yours﴾.

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: He, may He be exalted, says: Remember, O people, ﴿when Allah promised you one of the two groups﴾, meaning one of the two companies,[[See the explanation of "al-ta'ifa" (the group) above, vol. 12, p. 560, note 3, and the references there.]] the company of Abu Sufyan ibn Harb and the caravan, and the company of the polytheists who set out from Makkah to protect their caravan.

* *

As for His saying ﴿that it would be yours﴾, it means: that what they have with them is booty for you. ﴿And you wished that the one without the thorn would be yours﴾: that is, you loved that the group which had no strength (*shawka*), meaning no force (*hadd*),[["Al-hadd" (with a fatha on the ha') is: sharpness (al-hidda, with a kasra on the ha'), fierce might, and power to inflict harm.]] and in which there was no fighting, would be yours. He means: you wished that the caravan, in which there was no fighting against you, would be yours, rather than the body of the Quraysh who came to protect their caravan, in whose encounter there would be fighting and war.

* *

The root of "al-shawka" is from "al-shawk" (thorns).

* *

Those who engage in interpretation (*ahl al-ta'wil*) have said things like what we have said about this. Those who said so:

15719. Ali ibn Nasr and Abd al-Warith ibn Abd al-Samad narrated to us, both saying: Abd al-Samad ibn Abd al-Warith narrated to us, he said: Aban al-Attar narrated to us, he said: Hisham ibn Urwa narrated to us, from Urwa, that Abu Sufyan came with those of the Quraysh riders who were coming from al-Sham (Syria). [["Al-rukban" and "al-rakb" are the men who ride camels on a journey, and it is a collective noun with no singular.]] They took the coastal road. When the Prophet (ﷺ) heard about them, he summoned his Companions and told them about the wealth they had with them and about their small number. So they set out wanting only Abu Sufyan and the riders with him, seeing them as nothing but booty for themselves, not thinking that there would be great fighting when they saw them. And it is concerning this that Allah revealed ﴿and you wished that the one without the thorn would be yours﴾.[[In the printed edition: "wa-hiya ma anzala Allah", and in the manuscript: "wa-hiya anzala Allah"; I have kept what is in Tarikh al-Tabari.]] [[The narration 15719: "Ali ibn Nasr ibn Ali ibn Nasr ibn Ali al-Jahdami," the trustworthy and retentive transmitter, a teacher of al-Tabari, from whom Muslim, Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i, Abu Zur'a, Abu Hatim and al-Bukhari (in other than the Sahih al-Jami') narrated. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib and in Ibn Abi Hatim 3/1/207.
And "Abd al-Warith ibn Abd al-Samad ibn Abd al-Warith al-Anbari," a teacher of al-Tabari, trustworthy, passed under no. 2340.
And his father: "Abd al-Samad ibn Abd al-Warith ibn Sa'id al-Anbari," trustworthy, passed many times.
And "Aban al-Attar," who is "Aban ibn Yazid al-Attar," trustworthy, passed under nos. 3832 and 9656.
This report Abu Ja'far narrated with this chain in the History 2:267, in full detail. It is a letter from Urwa ibn al-Zubayr to Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan. The letter of Urwa to Abd al-Malik is a long letter, which al-Tabari narrated in scattered form in the History, and I will reproduce it in full in my note on narration 16083.]]

15720. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Salama narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Muhammad ibn Muslim al-Zuhri, and Asim ibn Umar ibn Qatada, and Abd Allah ibn Abi Bakr, and Yazid ibn Ruman, from Urwa ibn al-Zubayr and others of our scholars,[[The speaker of "from our scholars..." to the end of the context is Muhammad ibn Ishaq.]] from Abd Allah ibn Abbas. Each of them narrated to me part of this report, and their accounts converged on what I have related of the Badr account. They said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) heard that Abu Sufyan was coming from al-Sham, he summoned the Muslims against them and said: "This is the caravan of the Quraysh, with their wealth in it. Go out to it, perhaps Allah will grant it to you as spoils!" So the people responded; some went out eagerly and some reluctantly, because they did not think that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would meet a war. Abu Sufyan, as he drew near the Hijaz, was on the alert and was seeking news, and asking the riders he met, out of concern for the people's wealth.[[In the printed edition, in Tarikh al-Tabari, and in Ibn Hisham's Sira: "wa-kana Abu Sufyan hina dana min al-Hijaz yatahassas" — without "yastaqin" and without the conjunction "wa" before "yatahassas." But the manuscript is clear, so I have kept it.
In the printed edition it reads "yatajassas" with a jim, but it is actually with a ha' (unpointed), and "tahassas al-khabar" means to hear it oneself, investigate it, and seek it out.]] [[In the printed edition: "takhawwufan min al-nas," and in Ibn Hisham's Sira: "takhawwufan 'ala amr al-nas"; I have kept what is in Tarikh al-Tabari.]] Until he obtained news from some of the riders: "Muhammad has summoned his Companions against you and your caravan!" [["Istanfara al-nas" means he called them to help and support him, and urged them to go out to fight.]] So he became wary at that point, and he hired Damdam ibn Amr al-Ghifari, and sent him to Makkah, ordering him to go to the Quraysh, calling them to defend their wealth, and informing them that Muhammad had set out for it with his Companions. Damdam ibn Amr set out quickly for Makkah.[[At this point the text of Ibn Hisham's Sira ends (2:257, 258), and it will continue with what follows in the Sira after 2:266. And here the report ends in Tarikh al-Tabari (2:270), and it will continue with what follows in the History also at 2:273.
See the takhrij at the end of this report.]] The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) set out with his Companions until he reached a valley called "Dhafiran," and he crossed it,[[In the Sira alone it reads "fa-jaza fihi," which is more appropriate in this place, but I have kept what is in the printed edition, the manuscript and the History. "Jaza al-wadi" means to cross it transversely.]] until, when he was in part of it, he halted. News came to him of the Quraysh's march to protect their caravan, so the Prophet (ﷺ) consulted the people and informed them about the Quraysh. Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, stood and spoke well. Then Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, stood and spoke well. Then al-Miqdad ibn Amr stood and said: "O Messenger of Allah, proceed to where Allah has commanded you, for we are with you. By Allah, we will not say as the Children of Israel said to Musa: ﴿Go you and your Lord and fight, we are sitting here﴾ [Surah al-Ma'ida: 24], but rather: Go you and your Lord and fight, we are fighting with you both! By Him who sent you with the truth, if you were to set out with us to Barak al-Ghimad (meaning the city of Abyssinia)[["Barak al-Ghimad," "barak" (with fatha or kasra on the ba') and "al-ghimad" (with kasra or damma on the ghayn). Al-Hamdani said: "Barak al-Ghimad" is in the far reaches of Yemen (Mu'jam ma Ista'jam: 244).]] we would fight alongside you against whoever stands in your way until you reach it!" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said good things to him, and then prayed for good for him. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Advise me, O people!" He meant the Ansar, because they were the majority of the people. That was because when they pledged allegiance to him at al-Aqaba, they said: "O Messenger of Allah, we are free of your covenant until you reach our homes. When you reach us, you are in our protection, and we will protect you from what we protect our sons and wives from." So it seemed that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) feared that the Ansar would not consider it incumbent upon them to support him except against whoever attacked him in Madina from his enemies, and that it was not incumbent on them to take him to an enemy from among their own lands.[["Al-dhimam" and "al-dhimma" mean covenant, guarantee and sanctity.]] [[In the printed edition: "khaffa an la takuna al-Ansar," and I have kept what Ibn Hisham's Sira and Tarikh al-Tabari have. "Yatakhawwaf" is missing from the manuscript.
"Dahamahu" (with fatha or kasra on the ha'): if it surprised him unprepared.]] He said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said that, Sa'd ibn Mu'adh said to him: "It is as if you mean us, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Yes!" He said: "We have believed in you and affirmed you, and we testified that what you have brought is the truth, and we have given you our covenants and pledges to hear and obey upon that. So proceed, O Messenger of Allah, to what you wish. By Him who sent you with the truth, if you were to lead us into this sea and plunge into it, we would plunge in with you. Not one man of us would stay behind, and we do not dislike that you meet our enemy with us tomorrow.[["Istaradha al-bahr aw al-khatar": he approached it heedlessly, not caring about its danger. This is an explanation of the word that I extracted; you will not find it in the dictionaries.]] [[In the printed edition: "an yalqana 'aduwwuna ghadan," which did not read the manuscript well; this is what agrees with Ibn Hisham's Sira and Tarikh al-Tabari.]] Indeed we are steadfast in war, truthful at the encounter.[["Sudug" (with two dammas) is the plural of "sadduq," its meaning being: that he is sincere in his fighting or his work, that is, he exerts himself in it, like sincerity in speech that is not mixed with falsehood, i.e., weakness.]] Perhaps Allah will show you from us what will delight your eye. So march with us in the blessing of Allah!" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was delighted by Sa'd's words, and it energized him. Then he said: "Proceed in the blessing of Allah and rejoice, for Allah has promised me one of the two groups.[[His saying at the end of the next clause, "ghadan" (tomorrow), is not in Ibn Hisham's Sira or the History, but it is established in the manuscript.]] By Allah, it is as if I am looking now at the places where the people will fall tomorrow."" [[Narration 15720: part of this report was previously narrated: 15710. It is in Ibn Hisham's Sira scattered at 2:257, 258, then 2:266, 267.
And in Tarikh al-Tabari at 2:270, then 2:273, and then its completion also at 2:273.]]

15721. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, he said: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, he said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: that Abu Sufyan came with a caravan from al-Sham in which was the trade of the Quraysh, and it was the "lutayma," [["Al-lutayma" is perfume, and "lutaymat al-misk" is its container. Then they called the caravan that carries perfume and gold, and the precious goods of merchants, "al-lutayma."]] and the news reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that it had approached, so he summoned the people, and they went out with him, three hundred and some ten men. He sent a spy of his from Juhayna, an ally of the Ansar, called "Ibn Uraygit,"[[In the printed edition: "Ibn al-Uraygit," and I have kept what is in the manuscript.]] and he brought him news of the people. News of the Prophet's (ﷺ) departure reached Abu Sufyan, so he sent to the people of Makkah asking for their help, and sent a man from the Banu Ghifar called Damdam ibn Amr. The Prophet (ﷺ) set out without knowing that the Quraysh had gone out, and Allah informed him of their departure. He feared that the Ansar would abandon him and say: "We pledged that we would protect you if anyone wanted you in our land!" So he turned to his Companions and consulted them about pursuing the caravan. Abu Bakr, may Allah have mercy on him, said to him: "I have traveled this route, and I know it well, and the man left them at such-and-such a place." The Prophet (ﷺ) was silent, then returned and consulted them again, and they began to advise him to pursue the caravan. When the consultation grew long, Sa'd ibn Mu'adh spoke and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I see you consulting your Companions, and they advise you, and you return and consult them again, as if you are not satisfied with what they advise you, and as if you fear that the Ansar will hold back from you! You are the Messenger of Allah, and the Book was sent down to you, and Allah has commanded you to fight and promised you victory, and Allah does not break His promise. Proceed with what you were commanded! By Him who sent you with the truth, not one man of the Ansar will stay behind you!" Then al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad al-Kindi stood and said: "O Messenger of Allah, we will not say to you as the Children of Israel said to Musa: (Go you and your Lord and fight, we are sitting here) [Surah al-Ma'ida: 24], but rather we say: Advance and fight, we are fighting with you!" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) rejoiced at that and said: "My Lord has promised me the people, and they have come out, so march toward them!" So they marched.

15722. Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His saying: ﴿And when Allah promised you one of the two groups, that it would be yours, and you wished that the one without the thorn would be yours﴾: He said: The two groups: one of them was Abu Sufyan ibn Harb, when he came with the caravan from al-Sham, and the other group was Abu Jahl with a band of the Quraysh. The Muslims disliked the strength (*shawka*) and the fighting, and they loved to meet the caravan. But Allah willed what He willed.

15723. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, he said: Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, he said: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talha, from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿And when Allah promised you one of the two groups﴾: He said: The caravan of the people of Makkah came [meaning from al-Sham][[In the manuscript: "yurid al-Sham," and what is in the printed edition is correct.]] and news of it reached the people of Madina, so they set out with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), intending the caravan. News of this reached the people of Makkah, so they hastened their march toward it, so that the Prophet (ﷺ) and his Companions would not prevail over it. The caravan outpaced the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and Allah had promised them one of the two groups. They preferred to meet the caravan, as it was more beloved to them, less strength, and more booty. When the caravan had gone ahead and escaped the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) marched with the Muslims intending the people, and the people disliked their march because of the strength that was among the people.

15724. Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, he said: My father narrated to me, he said: My paternal uncle narrated to me, he said: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿And when Allah promised you one of the two groups, that it would be yours, and you wished that the one without the thorn would be yours﴾: He said: They wanted the caravan. He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) entered Madina in the month of Rabi' al-Awwal, and Kurz ibn Jabir al-Fihri raided, intending the livestock of Madina, until he reached al-Safra.[["Al-sarh" is property that is pastured, of cattle and livestock that graze. "Al-Safra'" is a village above Yanbu', abounding in farms and palm trees, six stages from Madina, and the Juhayna, the Ansar, and Nahd used to live there.]] News of this reached the Prophet (ﷺ), and he mounted in pursuit, but Kurz ibn Jabir outpaced him. The Prophet (ﷺ) returned and remained there for a year. Then Abu Sufyan came from al-Sham with a caravan of the Quraysh, and when he was near Badr, Jibril descended to the Prophet (ﷺ) and revealed to him: ﴿And when Allah promised you one of the two groups, that it would be yours, and you wished that the one without the thorn would be yours﴾. So the Prophet (ﷺ) mobilized all the Muslims, and they were then three hundred and thirteen men, of whom two hundred and seventy were from the Ansar, and the rest were from the Muhajirun. News reached Abu Sufyan while he was at al-Batm,[[So it appears in the printed edition and the manuscript, and I have found no place or thing called "al-Batm." I almost swear that it is a pure distortion, and that the correct reading is (Bi-Idam). "Idam" is a valley in the mountains of Tihama, the valley in which Madina lies. It is called "Qanat" near Madina, and from above it at the dam it is called "al-Shazat," and from al-Shazat down it is called "Idam." Ibn al-Sikkit said: "Idam" is a valley that cuts through the Hijaz until it empties into the sea, and the upper part of Idam is the "Qanat" which passes before Madina. "Idam" is in the lands of Juhayna.
It is well known in the biographies that Abu Sufyan, in those days, stopped at a water source which was owned by Majdi ibn Amr al-Juhani. When he sensed the news of the Muslims, he turned the face of his caravan and went along the coast, leaving Badr on his left. So he had then indeed stopped in the land of Juhayna, and Idam is from their land, and it flows into the sea, so this seems to be the route he took. I have not found the report in any place that would allow me to verify this completely.]] So he sent to all the Quraysh while they were in Makkah, and the Quraysh were roused and angered.

15725. Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: Al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj: ﴿And when Allah promised you one of the two groups, that it would be yours, and you wished that the one without the thorn would be yours﴾: He said: Jibril, peace be upon him, had descended and informed him of the Quraysh's march, and they wanted their caravan, and He promised him either the caravan or the Quraysh, and that was at Badr. They took the water-carriers and questioned them, and they informed them. That is His saying: ﴿and you wished that the one without the thorn would be yours﴾. They were the people of Makkah.

15726. Yunus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying: ﴿and you wished that the one without the thorn would be yours﴾, to the end of the verse: The Prophet (ﷺ) went out to Badr, and they intended to intercept a caravan of the Quraysh. He said: The Satan went out in the form of Suraqa ibn Ju'shum, until he came to the people of Makkah and misled them, and said: "Muhammad and his Companions have intercepted your caravan!" And he said: "There is no one who can overcome you today among the people, like you. I am a protector for you, that you should be upon what Allah dislikes!" So they went out and proclaimed that no one among us would stay behind, or we would demolish his house and seize his property! The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his Companions captured a spy of the people at al-Rawha, and he informed them about them. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah has promised you the caravan or the people!" So the caravan was more beloved to the people than the people; the fighting was in the strength, and the caravan had no fighting in it. This is the saying of Allah, mighty and majestic: ﴿and you wished that the one without the thorn would be yours﴾. He said: "The strength" is the fighting, and "the one without the strength" is the caravan.

15727 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Ya'qub ibn Muhammad al-Zuhri narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Wahb narrated to us, from Ibn Lahi'ah, from Ibn Abi Habib, from Abu Imran, from Abu Ayyub, who said: Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed: ﴿And [recall] when Allah promised you one of the two groups, that it would be yours﴾. So when He promised us that one of the two groups would be ours, our souls were content. The "two groups" were the caravan of Abu Sufyan or the Quraysh.

[[The report 15727: Ya'qub ibn Muhammad al-Zuhri, mentioned shortly before, no. 15715.
And Abdullah ibn Wahb al-Misri, the trustworthy (al-thiqah), passed with nos. 6613 and 10330.
And Ibn Lahi'ah: the discussion of his reliability has passed many times.
And Ibn Abi Habib: he is Yazid ibn Abi Habib al-Misri, trustworthy, passed many times.
And Abu Imran: he is Aslam Abu Imran, Aslam ibn Yazid al-Tujibi, who narrated from Abu Ayyub. He was a trustworthy Successor (tabi'i) and was a notable figure in Egypt. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 1/2/25, and Ibn Abi Hatim 1/1/307. He will appear in this report with another chain, in the one that follows.
Al-Haythami mentioned it in Majma' al-Zawa'id 6: 73, 74, in full, and said: "Al-Tabarani narrated it, and its chain is good."]]

15728 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Suwayd ibn Nasr narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Ibn Lahi'ah, from Yazid ibn Abi Habib, from Aslam Abu Imran al-Ansari, I think he said: Abu Ayyub said: ﴿And [recall] when Allah promised you one of the two groups, that it would be yours, and you wished that the unarmed one would be yours﴾. They said: "The armed one (al-shawkah)" is the people (the enemy army), and "the unarmed one" is the caravan. So when Allah promised us one of the two groups, either the caravan or the people, our souls were content.

[[The report 15728: "Aslam Abu Imran al-Ansari" is the one who appeared in the previous chain, and its takhrij has already been given.]]

15729 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Ya'qub ibn Muhammad narrated to me, saying: Someone other than one [narrator] narrated to me concerning His words: ﴿and you wished that the unarmed one would be yours﴾, that "the armed one" is the Quraysh.

15730 - I was told, from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say concerning His words: ﴿and you wished that the unarmed one would be yours﴾: it is the caravan of Abu Sufyan. The companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) wished that the caravan were theirs, and that the fighting would be turned away from them.

15731 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: ﴿and you wished that the unarmed one would be yours﴾, that is, the booty rather than the war.

[[The report 15731: Sirat Ibn Hisham 2: 322. It follows the two preceding reports, nos. 15713 and 15718.]]

* *

As for His words: ﴿that it would be yours﴾, it is in the accusative (fatahat) by the repetition of "promised" (ya'idu), because His words ﴿Allah promised you﴾ have governed ﴿one of the two groups﴾.

So the meaning of the speech is: ﴿And [recall] when Allah promised you one of the two groups﴾, promising you that one of the two groups would be yours, as He said: ﴿Do they await anything but the Hour, that it come upon them suddenly?﴾ [Surah Muhammad: 18]. [[See the Ma'ani al-Qur'an of al-Farra' 1: 404, where he adds: "Then 'an' is in the position of the accusative, just as 'the Hour' is in the accusative."]]

* *

He said: ﴿and you wished that the unarmed one would be yours﴾. He made "dhat" feminine because the group is what is intended. [[See what he said earlier concerning "dhat baynikum", p. 384.]] The meaning of the speech is: and you wished that the group which is unarmed would be yours, rather than the armed group.

The interpretation of His words: ﴿And Allah wills to establish the truth by His words and to cut off the remnant of the disbelievers﴾ (8:7)

* *

Abu Ja'far says: Exalted is He, He says: And Allah wills to establish Islam and make it supreme [[See the explanation of "haqq" in the earlier language indexes (haqqaqa).]], ﴿by His words﴾, meaning: by His command to you, O believers, to fight the disbelievers, while you desire the booty and the wealth [[See the explanation of "the words of Allah" in the earlier passages, 11: 335, and the language indexes (kalama).]]. As for His words: ﴿and to cut off the remnant of the disbelievers﴾, He means: He wills to uproot the root of those who deny the Oneness of Allah.

* *

We have already explained the meaning of "dabir", that it is the last remaining part, and that the meaning of "cutting it off" is reaching all of them. [[See the explanation of "cutting off the remnant" at 11: 363, 364 and 12: 523, 524.]]

* *

The interpretation given by the scholars of tafsir (ahl al-ta'wil) is in accord with what we have said on this.

Those who said that:

15731 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning Allah's words: ﴿And Allah wills to establish the truth by His words﴾: that He kill those whose remnant He wills to cut off; this is better for you than the caravan.

15732 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: ﴿And Allah wills to establish the truth by His words and to cut off the remnant of the disbelievers﴾, that is: the battle which He inflicted upon the chiefs and leaders of Quraysh on the day of Badr. [[The report 15731: Sirat Ibn Hisham 2: 322. It follows the preceding report no. 15730.]]

The discussion of His saying: ﴿That He may establish the truth and nullify falsehood, even though the criminals dislike it﴾ (8)

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is He, means: "And Allah intends to cut off the last remnant of the disbelievers, so that the truth may be established" — so that Allah may be worshipped alone, without the gods and idols, and so that Islam may be honoured. This is "the establishment of the truth." ﴿And nullify falsehood﴾ means: He nullifies the worship of gods, idols, and disbelief. "Even though the criminals dislike it" means: even though those who committed crime, who acquired sins and burdens from among the disbelievers, dislike that. [See the explanation of "al-mujrimun" (the criminals) above, p. 70, note 2, and the references there.]

15733- Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿that He may establish the truth and nullify falsehood, even though the criminals dislike it﴾: they are the polytheists.

* *

It has also been said: the "truth" in this place refers to Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

The Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 8, Verse 9 (Part 1 of 2):

On the interpretation of His words: ﴿When you sought help from your Lord, and He answered you: "I will reinforce you with a thousand of the angels, following one another."﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is He, He says: "and He will establish the truth and nullify falsehood" when you sought help from your Lord. So "idh" (when) is connected to "yubtil" (He nullifies).

* *

The meaning of His words ﴿when you sought help from your Lord﴾ is: you sought refuge with Him from your enemy and called upon Him for victory over them. "Then He answered you" means He responded to your supplication [[See the explanation of "istajaba" (answered) in what preceded, p. 321, note 2, and the references there.]] "that I will reinforce you with a thousand of the angels, following one another and succeeding one another." [[See the explanation of "al-imdad" (reinforcement) in what preceded, 1: 307–308, and 7: 181.]]

* *

The People of Interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) said in agreement with what we have said on this, and reports have come down from the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Mention of the reports on this:

15734: Muhammad ibn Ubayd al-Muharibi narrated to me, saying: Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, from Ikrimah ibn Ammar, who said: Simak al-Hanafi narrated to me, who said: I heard Ibn Abbas say: Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to me, saying: When the Day of Badr came, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ looked at the polytheists and their number, and he looked at his Companions, who were slightly more than three hundred. So he turned toward the qiblah and began to supplicate, saying: "O Allah, fulfill for me what You have promised me! O Allah, if this small group of the people of Islam is destroyed, You will not be worshipped on the earth!" He continued in this state until his cloak (rida') fell from his shoulders. Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him) took it and placed his cloak upon him, then embraced him (iltazamahu) from behind, [["iltazamahu": he embraced him or clasped him.]] and said: "It is enough for you, O Prophet of Allah, with my father and mother, to implore your Lord, for He will surely fulfill for you what He has promised you!" So Allah revealed: ﴿When you sought help from your Lord, and He answered you: "I will reinforce you with a thousand of the angels, following one another."﴾ [[The report 15734: Ikrimah ibn Ammar al-Yamami al-Ajli is reliable (thiqa); he has passed under nos. 849, 2185, 8224, 13832.
And "Simak al-Hanafi" is Simak ibn al-Walid al-Hanafi, Abu Zumayl, reliable; he has passed under no. 13832.
This report was narrated by Muslim in his Sahih (12: 84–87) in a lengthy form, through Hannad ibn al-Sarri, from Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak, from Ikrimah.
It was narrated by Ahmad in his Musnad, nos. 208 and 221, through Abu Nuh Qarad, from Ikrimah ibn Ammar, in a lengthy form.
Part of it was narrated by Abu Dawud in his Sunan (3: 82).
It was narrated by al-Tirmidhi in the Book of Tafsir, in an abridged form, through Muhammad ibn Bashshar, from Umar ibn Yunus al-Yamami, from Ikrimah, and he said: "This is a hasan sahih gharib hadith; we do not know it from the hadith of Umar except through the hadith of Ikrimah ibn Ammar, from Abu Zumayl."
Abu Ja'far al-Tabari also narrated it in his History, through the same chain, 2: 280.]]

15735: Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, who said: When the two sides lined up, Abu Jahl said: "O Allah, grant victory to the one of us who is more in the right, and support him!" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ raised his hand and said: "O Lord, if this small group is destroyed, You will never be worshipped on the earth again!"

15736: Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Prophet ﷺ stood up and said: "O Allah, our Lord, You have sent down the Book to me, You have commanded me to fight, and You have promised me victory, and You do not break the promise!" Then Gabriel (peace be upon him) came to him, and Allah revealed: ﴿Is it not enough for you that your Lord reinforce you with three thousand angels sent down? Yes indeed! If you are patient and God-fearing, and they come upon you suddenly in this very moment, your Lord will reinforce you with five thousand angels, marked (musawwimin).﴾ [[The report 15736: Abu Ja'far did not mention this report in his interpretation of the verse of Surah Al Imran, 7: 173–190.]]
[Surah Al Imran: 124–125].

15737: Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to me, saying: Abu Mu'awiya narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Ishaq, from Zayd ibn Yuthay', who said: Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him) was with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the arish (a shelter of branches). The Prophet ﷺ began to supplicate, saying: "O Allah, grant victory to this small group, for if You do not, You will not be worshipped on the earth!" He said: Abu Bakr said: "Some of your supplication is sufficient, for He will fulfill what He has promised you!" [[The report 15737: "Abu Ishaq" is al-Hamdani al-Subay'i. In the printed edition it read "Ibn Ishaq," which differs from the manuscript, and this was an error.
And "Zayd ibn Yuthay' al-Hamdani," it is also said: "... Uthay'" and "Uthayl," ending with a lam. He narrated from Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, Ali, Hudhayfa and Abu Dhar, and from him only Abu Ishaq al-Subay'i narrated. Ibn Hibban mentioned him in al-Thiqat; he is biographed in al-Tahdhib, and by Ibn Sa'd (155), al-Kabir (2/1/373), and Ibn Abi Hatim (1/2/573), under the name "Zayd ibn Nafi' al-Hamdani," which is an error; the correct form is what we have recorded. But it is strange that "Zayd ibn Nafi'" also appeared in both the printed and manuscript editions.
And "Yuthay'," with the ya and tha, diminutive, is thus vocalized. Ibn Durayd said in Kitab al-Ishtiqaq (249): "Yuthay'" is "yuf'il" from "tha'a, yathi'u," meaning it expanded and spread out.]]

15738: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said: The Prophet ﷺ began to call upon Allah, to implore Him and to seek His help, so Allah sent down the angels to him.

15739: Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding His words: ﴿When you sought help from your Lord﴾, he said: It was the supplication of the Prophet ﷺ.

15740: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: ﴿When you sought help from your Lord﴾, that is: by your supplication, when they saw the multitude of their enemy and the fewness of their number. ﴿Then He answered you﴾, by the supplication of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and your supplication along with him. [[The report 15740: Sirat Ibn Hisham 2: 322–323. It is a continuation of the earlier report no. 15731. In Sirat Ibn Hisham, the word "ma'ahu" ("with him") does not appear at the end of the report.]]

15741: Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash narrated to us, from Abu Husayn, from Abu Salih, who said: When the Day of Badr came, the Prophet ﷺ began to implore his Lord with the most intense entreaty, supplicating. [["Al-nishda" (with a kasra and sukun) is a verbal noun from "nashadtuka Allah," meaning I asked you by Him and made you swear by Him.]] So Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) came to him and said: "O Messenger of Allah, some of your entreaty is enough; by Allah, He will surely fulfill for you what He has promised you!"

* *

As for His words ﴿that I will reinforce you with a thousand of the angels, following one another﴾, we have already explained their meaning. [[See what preceded, p. 409.]]

* *

The People of Interpretation said in agreement with what we have said on this.
Mention of those who said this:

15742: Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿that I will reinforce you with a thousand of the angels, following one another﴾, he said: "al-mizid" (the additional ones), as you say: "Go to the man and add to him such and such."

15743: Ibn WakI' narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Bashir narrated to us, from Harun ibn Antara [from his father], from his father, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿mardifin﴾, he said: following one another. [[The report 15743: Ahmad ibn Bashir al-Kufi, passed under nos. 7819, 11084.
And "Harun ibn Antara ibn Abd al-Rahman," passed many times, the last under no. 11084.
And his father "Antara ibn Abd al-Rahman," also passed, see no. 11084.]]

15744: ... He said: My father narrated to me, from Sufyan, from Harun ibn Antara, [from his father], from Ibn Abbas, the same. [[The report 15744: The addition "from his father" between brackets is, I believe, the correct reading, and its omission was by the copyist. See the chain above.]]

15745: Sulayman ibn Abd al-Jabbar narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Salt narrated to us, saying: Abu Kudayna narrated to us, from Qabus, from his father, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿reinforce you with a thousand of the angels, following one another﴾, he said: behind every angel is an angel. [[The report 15745: Sulayman ibn Abd al-Jabbar ibn Zurayq al-Khayyat, the teacher of al-Tabari, passed under nos. 5994, 9745.
And Muhammad ibn al-Salt ibn al-Hajjaj al-Asadi, passed under nos. 3002, 5994, 9745.
And Abu Kudayna, Yahya ibn al-Muhallab al-Bajali, passed under nos. 4193, 5994, 9745.
And Qabus ibn Abi Zabyan al-Janbi, passed under nos. 9745, 10683.
And his father Abu Zabyan, he is Husayn ibn Jundab al-Janbi, passed under nos. 9745, 10683.]]

15746: Ibn WakI' narrated to me, saying: Abu Usama narrated to us, from Abu Kudayna Yahya ibn al-Muhallab, from Qabus, from his father, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿mardifin﴾, he said: following one another. [[The report 15746: See the men of the earlier chain.]]

15747: ... He said: Hani ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from Hajjaj ibn Artat, from Qabus, who said: I heard Abu Zabyan say: ﴿mardifin﴾, he said: the angels, one following upon another. [[The report 15747: "Hani ibn Sa'id al-Nakha'i," the teacher of Ibn WakI', was mentioned earlier under nos. 13159, 13965, 14836.]]

15748: ... He said: al-Muharibi narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak: ﴿mardifin﴾, he said: one following upon another.

15749: Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abdullah narrated to us, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

15750: Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿mardifin﴾, he said: "reinforcing" (mumiddin). Ibn Jurayj said, from Abdullah ibn Kathir, who said: ﴿mardifin﴾: "al-irdaf" is reinforcing with them.

15751: Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to me, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada: ﴿with a thousand of the angels, following one another﴾, that is, successive.

15752: [Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr] narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿with a thousand of the angels, following one another﴾, one following another. [[The report 15752: The beginning of this chain is an undoubted error. It is, as I have placed it between the brackets, as it appears in the printed edition. As for the manuscript, it reads there: "Muhammad ibn Abd Allah narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us..." which is a clear confusion, as these are two chains.
The first chain is: "Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar..." and it is a chain that recurs in the tafsir.
The second chain, and it is this as it must be: "Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us..." and it is a chain that recurs in the tafsir, the nearest of which is no. 15738.
It is evident that the end of the chain of "Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la" has fallen out.]]

15753: Yunus narrated to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words: ﴿mardifin﴾, he said: "the mardifin" are one following upon another, one succeeding another.

15754: It was related from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words: ﴿with a thousand of the angels, following one another﴾, he says: successive, on the Day of Badr.

* *

The readers (qurra') differed in their recitation of this.
The general body of the readers of Medina recited it as "mURDaFIN," with a fatha on the dal.

* *

Some of the Meccan readers, and the majority of the readers of Kufa and Basra, recited: ﴿mUrdiFIN﴾, with a kasra on the dal.

* *

Abu Amr also recited it in this way, and he said, as is reported from him: it is from "ardafaba'duhum ba'dan" (some of them reinforced others).

* *

Some scholars of the Arabic language rejected this statement of Abu Amr and said: "al-irdaf" is only that a man carries his companion behind him. He said: This was not heard in the description of the angels on the Day of Badr.

* *

The scholars of the Arabic language differed on the meaning of this when it is read with a fatha or a kasra on the dal.
Some of the Basran and Kufan scholars said: The meaning of this when it is read with a kasra is that the angels came one following another, according to the dialect of one who says "ardaftuhu." They said: The Arabs say "ardaftuhu" and "radiftuhu," meaning "I followed him" and "I caused him to follow." To support their claim, they cited what the poet said: [[He is Huzayma ibn Nahd ibn Zayd ibn Layth ibn Sawd ibn Aslam ibn al-Hāf ibn Quda'a, among the early poets of the Jahiliyya. "Huzayma," with an unpointed ha (ḥ) that is fatḥa and a zay with a kasra, is so vocalized in Taj al-'Arus, which says "Huzayma ibn Nahd" in Quda'a. In many books it is "Khuzayma ibn Nahd" or "Khuzayma ibn Malik ibn Nahd" (al-Lisan: r-d-f). I have read in Jamharat al-Ansab of Ibn Hazm (418) that "Nahd ibn Zayd" was the father of "Khuzayma" and "Huzayma," which requires caution and examination as to its vocalization, and which of them was the subject of the story and the poem, though the first is more probable.]]

"When al-Jawza' (Orion) reinforced al-Thurayya (the Pleiades),
I suspected the family of Fatima of suspicions."

They said: The poet said "ardafat," but he meant "radifat," "came after," because Orion comes after the Pleiades.

They said: Its meaning when it is read as "mardafin" is that it is in the passive, as if its meaning is: with a thousand of the angels whom Allah causes to follow one another.

* *

Others said: The meaning of this, when the dal is read with a kasra, is: the angels reinforced one another; and when it is read with a fatha: Allah reinforced the Muslims with them.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct reading in this matter, in my opinion, is the reading of the one who recited: ﴿with a thousand of the angels, mURDiFIN﴾, with a kasra on the dal, because of the consensus of the People of Interpretation on what I have mentioned of their interpretation, that its meaning is: they follow one another, and succeed one another. In their consensus on this interpretation is the clear evidence that the sound reading is what we have chosen in this matter, with a kasra on the dal, meaning: some of the angels reinforced others; and it is heard from the Arabs: "I came mURDiFan (reinforcing) to so-and-so," meaning: I came after him.

As for the view of those who said that the meaning of this, when "mardafin" is read with a fatha on the dal, is that Allah reinforced the Muslims with them: this is a statement without meaning, since the pronoun in "mardafin" refers to the angels, not to the believers. The meaning of the speech is: that He reinforces you with a thousand of the angels, some of whom are reinforced by others. Then the mention of the agent was omitted, and the predicate was expressed with its subject unnamed, so it is said: ﴿mardafin﴾, meaning: some of the angels are reinforced by others.

Now if the matter were as the one whose statement we have mentioned said, it would be necessary that the mention in "al-murdifin" be of the Muslims, not of the angels. And that contradicts what the apparent meaning of the Qur'an indicates.

It has also been reported in this regard another reading, namely:

15755 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Yazid said: "murdifin" and "murdifin" and "murdufin" are read with a doubled letter (mu thaqqal) [[Al-Qurtubi recorded its vocalization in his tafsir, 7:371.]] in the sense of "murtadifin" (those who follow one another in succession).

15756 - Al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Yaqub ibn Muhammad al-Zuhri narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Aziz ibn Imran narrated to me, from al-Zum'i, from Abu al-Huwayrith, from Muhammad ibn Jubayr, from Ali (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: Jibril descended with a thousand angels on the right flank of the Prophet (ﷺ), and Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) was there; and Mika'il (peace be upon him) descended with a thousand angels on the left flank of the Prophet (ﷺ), and I was among them. [[Al-Tabari: 15756 – "Abd al-Aziz ibn Imran ibn Abd al-Aziz ibn Umar ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf al-Zuhri," al-A'raj, known as "Ibn Abi Thabit," was a man of genealogy and poetry, but not a man of hadith, and he used to revile people and attack their lineages. Al-Bukhari said: "munkar al-hadith (weak narrator whose reports are rejected), his hadith is not to be written down," and Ibn Abi Hatim said: "very munkar al-hadith." It passed as no. 8012.
And "al-Zum'i" is "Musa ibn Yaqub al-Zum'i al-Qurashi," trustworthy, though spoken of (mutakallam fihi), passed as no. 9923; in the printed edition there it was "al-Rab'i," but in the manuscript it is undotted, and this is its correct form, and he is the one who narrates from Abu al-Huwayrith.
And "Abu al-Huwayrith" is "Abd al-Rahman ibn Mu'awiya ibn al-Huwayrith al-Ansari al-Zuraqi," trustworthy, though spoken of to the point that they said: "his hadith is not used as evidence"; he is biographed in al-Tahdhib, and Ibn Abi Hatim 2/2/284. And "Muhammad ibn Jubayr ibn Mut'im," trustworthy, a Tabi'i, passed as no. 9269. This is a very weak chain of narration.]]

Commentary on the words of God Almighty: ﴿And God made it not but as good news, and that your hearts might be assured thereby. And victory is not but from God. Indeed, God is Almighty, Wise.﴾ (8:10)

Abu Ja'far said: God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: God did not make the sending of the angels one after another, following one another in coming to you, O believers, as a reinforcement for you, except as "good news" for you, meaning a glad tiding to you, giving you good news of God's victory over your enemies. [[See the explanation of "al-bushra" (good news) above, p. 303, note 2, and the references there.]] "And that your hearts might be assured thereby": that is, that your hearts might be at rest through their coming to you, and be certain of God's support for you. [[See the explanation of "al-iṭmi'nan" (assurance/tranquility) above, 5:492; 9:165; 11:224.]] "And victory is not but from God": that is, you will not be made victorious over your enemy, O believers, except that God gives you victory over them, not by the strength of your might and your power, but by God's victory for you, because that is in His hand and belongs to Him; He gives victory to whomever He wills of His creation. "Indeed, God is Almighty, Wise": that is, indeed God, who gives you victory, and in whose hand is the victory of whomever He wills of His creation, is "Almighty," nothing overpowers Him and no conqueror defeats Him, rather He subdues everything and overcomes it, for He created it. "Wise": that is, wise in His management, in granting victory to whom He grants it, and in forsaking whom He forsakes of His creation; no weakness or flaw enters His management. [[See the explanation of "ʿazīz" (almighty) and "ḥakīm" (wise) in the lexical indexes above under (ʿ-z-z) and (ḥ-k-m).]]

* *

It has been related from ʿAbd Allah ibn Kathir, from Mujahid, regarding this, that:

15757 – al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn Kathir informed me that he heard Mujahid say: The Prophet (ﷺ) was not reinforced with anything that God mentioned except a thousand angels following one another. He mentioned that the "three" and the "five" were good news; they did not reinforce with more than this thousand which God, Mighty and Majestic, mentioned in "al-Anfal." As for the "three" and the "five," they were good news.

* *

We have already dealt with this in "Surat Al ʿImran," sufficiently. [[See above, 7:173–192.]]

القول في تأويل قوله: ﴿إِذْ يُغَشِّيكُمُ النُّعَاسَ أَمَنَةً مِنْهُ وَيُنَزِّلُ عَلَيْكُمْ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ مَاءً لِيُطَهِّرَكُمْ بِهِ وَيُذْهِبَ عَنْكُمْ رِجْزَ الشَّيْطَانِ وَلِيَرْبِطَ عَلَى قُلُوبِكُمْ وَيُثَبِّتَ بِهِ الأقْدَامَ (١١) إِذْ يُوحِي رَبُّكَ إِلَى الْمَلائِكَةِ أَنِّي مَعَكُمْ فَثَبِّتُوا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾

(The explanation of His words: ﴿When He covered you with drowsiness as security from Him, and sent down upon you water from the sky to purify you by it, to remove from you the defilement of Satan, to strengthen your hearts and make your feet firm thereby (11). When your Lord inspired the angels: "I am with you, so strengthen those who believe."﴾)

قال أبو جعفر (Abu Ja'far, i.e., al-Tabari): يقول تعالى ذكره: "ولتطمئن به قلوبكم"، "إذ يغشيكم النعاس"، ويعني بقوله: ﴿يغشيكم النعاس﴾، يلقي عليكم النعاس [[انظر تفسير "يغشى" فيما سلف ١: ٢٦٥، ٢٦٦ \ ١٢: ٤٣٦: ٤٨٣. وتفسير "النعاس" فيما سلف ٧: ٣١٦.]] ﴿أمنة﴾ يقول: أمانًا من الله لكم من عدوكم أن يغلبكم، وكذلك النعاس في الحرب أمنة من الله عز وجل.

* *

١٥٧٥٨- حدثني المثنى قال، حدثنا أبو نعيم قال، حدثنا سفيان، عن عاصم، عن أبي رزين، عن عبد الله قال: النعاس في القتال أمنةٌ من الله عز وجل، وفي الصلاة من الشيطان. [[الأثر: ١٥٧٥٨ - انظر هذا الخبر بإسناد آخر فيما سلف رقم: ٨٠٨٣.]]

١٥٧٥٩- حدثني الحسن بن يحيى قال، أخبرنا عبد الرزاق قال، أخبرنا الثوري في قوله: "يغشاكم النعاس أمنة منه"، [[قوله: "يغشاكم النعاس" قراءة أخرى في الآية، وسأثبتها كما جاءت في المخطوطة بعد.]] عن عاصم، عن أبي رزين، عن عبد الله، بنحوه، قال: قال عبد الله، فذكر مثله.

١٥٧٦٠- حدثنا ابن وكيع قال، حدثنا أبي، عن سفيان، عن عاصم، عن أبي رزين، عن عبد الله بنحوه.

* *

و"الأمنة" مصدر من قول القائل: "أمنت من كذا أمَنَة، وأمانًا، وأمْنًا"، وكل ذلك بمعنى واحد. [[انظر تفسير "أمنة" فيما سلف ٧: ٣١٥، تعليق: ١، والمراجع هناك.]]

* *

وبنحو الذي قلنا في ذلك قال أهل التأويل (ta'wil, i.e., the early exegetes).

ذكر من قال ذلك:

١٥٧٦١- حدثني محمد بن عمرو قال، حدثنا أبو عاصم قال، حدثنا عيسى، عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد: ﴿أمنة منه﴾، أمانًا من الله عز وجل.

١٥٧٦٢- ... قال، حدثنا إسحاق قال، حدثنا عبد الله، عن ورقاء، عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد: ﴿أمنة﴾، قال: أمنًا من الله.

١٥٧٦٣- حدثني يونس قال، حدثنا ابن وهب قال، قال ابن زيد قوله: ﴿إذ يغشيكم النعاس أمنة منه﴾، قال: أنزل الله عز وجل النعاس أمنة من الخوف الذي أصابهم يوم أحد. فقرأ: ﴿ثُمَّ أَنزلَ عَلَيْكُمْ مِنْ بَعْدِ الْغَمِّ أَمَنَةً نُعَاسًا﴾ [سورة آل عمران: ١٥٤].

* *

واختلفت القرأة (the reciters of the Qur'an) في قراءة قوله: "إذ يغشيكم النعاس أمنة منه"،

فقرأ ذلك عامة قرأة أهل المدينة: "يُغْشِيكُمُ النُّعَاسَ" بضم الياء وتخفيف الشين، ونصب "النعاس"، من: "أغشاهم الله النعاس فهو يغشيهم".

* *

وقرأته عامة قرأة الكوفيين: ﴿يُغَشِّيكُمُ﴾، بضم الياء وتشديد الشين، من: "غشّاهم الله النعاس فهو يغشِّيهم".

* *

وقرأ ذلك بعض المكيين والبصريين: "يَغْشَاكُمُ النُّعَاسُ"، بفتح الياء ورفع "النعاس"، بمعنى: "غشيهم النعاس فهو يغشاهم".

واستشهد هؤلاء لصحة قراءتهم كذلك بقوله في "آل عمران": ﴿يَغْشَى طَائِفَةً﴾ [سورة آل عمران: ١٥٤].

* *

قال أبو جعفر: وأولى ذلك بالصواب: ﴿إِذْ يُغَشِّيكُمْ﴾، على ما ذكرت من قراءة الكوفيين، لإجماع جميع القراء على قراءة قوله: ﴿وينزل عليكم من السماء ماء﴾، بتوجيه ذلك إلى أنه من فعل الله عز وجل، فكذلك الواجب أن يكون ﴿يغشيكم﴾، إذ كان قوله: ﴿وينزل﴾ عطفًا على "يغشي"، ليكون الكلام متسقًا على نحو واحد.

* *

وأما قوله عز وجل: ﴿وينزل عليكم من السماء ماء ليطهركم به﴾، فإن ذلك مطرٌ أنزله الله من السماء يوم بدر ليطهر به المؤمنين لصلاتهم، لأنهم كانوا أصبحوا يومئذ مُجْنبِين على غير ماء. فلما أنزل الله عليهم الماء اغتسلوا وتطهروا، وكان الشيطان قد وسوس إليهم بما حزنهم به من إصباحهم مجنبين على غير ماء، فأذهب الله ذلك من قلوبهم بالمطر. فذلك ربطه على قلوبهم، وتقويته أسبابهم، وتثبيته بذلك المطر أقدامهم، لأنهم كانوا التقوا مع عدوهم على رملة ميثاء، [[في المطبوعة: "على رملة هشاء"، ولا أصل لذلك في اللغة، فهو كلام لا يقال. وهو في المخطوطة سيء الكتابة قليلًا، وصواب قراءته ما أثبت. و"الرملة الميثاء": اللينة السهلة، قد تسوخ فيها الرجل قليلًا.]] فلبَّدها المطر، حتى صارت الأقدام عليها ثابتة لا تسوخ فيها، توطئةً من الله عز وجل لنبيه عليه السلام وأوليائه أسبابَ التمكن من عدوهم والظفر بهم.

* *

وبمثل الذي قلنا تتابعت الأخبار عن [أصحاب] رسول الله ﷺ وغيره من أهل العلم. [[هذه الزيادة بين القوسين لا بد منها، والأخبار الآتية تدل على صحة ذلك. وكان في المخطوطة أمام هذا السطر حرف (ط) دلالة على الخطأ والشك.]]

ذكر الأخبار الواردة بذلك:

١٥٧٦٤- حدثنا هارون بن إسحاق قال، حدثنا مصعب بن المقدام قال، حدثنا إسرائيل قال، حدثنا أبو إسحاق، عن حارثة، عن علي رضي الله عنه قال: أصابنا من الليل طَشّ من المطر [["الطش": المطر القليل، وهو فوق "الرذاذ".]] = يعني الليلة التي كانت في صبيحتها وقعة بدر = فانطلقنا تحت الشجر والحَجَف نستظل تحتها من المطر، [[في المطبوعة: "تحت الشجر"، وأثبت ما في المخطوطة، وهو صواب جيد. و"الحجف" (بفتحتين) جمع "جحفة"، وهي الترس يكون من الجلود ليس فيه خشب ولا عقب، وهو مثل "الدرقة".]] وبات رسول الله ﷺ يدعو ربه: "اللهم إن تهلك هذه العصابة لا تعبد في الأرض!" فلما أن طلع الفجر، نادى: "الصلاة عبادَ الله!"، فجاء الناس من تحت الشجر والحجف، فصلى بنا رسول الله ﷺ، وحرّض على القتال. [[الأثر: ١٥٧٦٤ - "هارون بن إسحاق الهمداني"، شيخ الطبري، مضى برقم: ٣٠٠١، ١٠٨٧٣. و"مصعب بن المقدام الخثعمي"، ثقة، مضى برقم: ١٢٩١، ٣٠٠١، ١٠٨٧٣ وغيرها. و"إسرائيل" هو "إسرائيل بن يونس بن إسحاق السبيعي"، ثقة حافظ، مضى مرارًا كثيرة. و"حارثة" هو "حارثة بن مضرب العبدي"، من ثقات التابعين، مضى برقم: ٢٠٥٧، ٨٥٩٧. وهو خبر صحيح الإسناد، خرّجه السيوطي مختصرًا بغير هذا اللفظ، ونسبه إلى ابن جرير، وأبي الشيخ، وابن مردويه. الدر المنثور ٣: ١٧١.]]

١٥٧٦٥- حدثنا ابن وكيع قال، حدثنا حفص بن غياث وأبو خالد، عن داود، عن سعيد بن المسيب: ﴿ماء ليطهركم به﴾، قال: طشٌّ يوم بدر.

١٥٧٦٦- حدثني الحسن بن يزيد قال، حدثنا حفص، عن داود، عن سعيد، بنحوه. [[الأثر: ١٥٧٦٦ - "الحسن بن يزيد"، لم أجد في شيوخ أبي جعفر، ولا فيمن روى عن حفص بن غياث، من يقال له "الحسن بن يزيد"، وأرجح أنه "الحسن بن عرفة بن يزيد العبدي"، شيخ أبي جعفر، نسبه إلى جده، وقد مضى برقم: ٩٣٧٣، ١٢٥٨١.]]

١٥٧٦٧- حدثنا ابن وكيع قال، حدثنا محمد بن أبي عدي وعبد الأعلى، عن داود، عن الشعبي وسعيد بن المسيب، قالا: طشٌّ يوم بدر.

١٥٧٦٨- حدثنا ابن المثنى قال، حدثنا ابن أبي عدي، عن داود، عن الشعبي وسعيد بن المسيب في هذه الآية: ﴿ينزل عليكم من السماء ماء ليطهركم به، ويذهب عنكم رجز الشيطان﴾، قالا: طشٌّ كان يوم بدر، فثبَّت الله به الأقدام.

١٥٧٦٩- حدثنا بشر بن معاذ قال، حدثنا يزيد قال، حدثنا سعيد، عن قتادة قوله: "إذ يغشاكم النعاس أمنة منه" الآية، قال: ذُكر لنا أنهم مُطِروا يومئذ حتى سال الوادي ماءً، واقتتلوا على كثيب أعفر، [["الأعفر": الرمل الأحمر.]] فلبَّده الله بالماء، وشرب المسلمون وتوضأوا وسقوا، وأذهب الله عنهم وسواس الشيطان.

١٥٧٧٠- حدثني المثنى قال، حدثنا عبد الله قال، حدثني معاوية، عن علي، عن ابن عباس قال: نزل النبي ﷺ = يعني: حين سار إلى بدر = والمسلمون بينهم وبين الماء رملة دَعْصَة، [["رملة دعصة": هكذا جاء في التفسير، في المخطوطة والمطبوعة، وفي ابن كثير، وضبطته بفتح الدال، لأني رجوت أن يكون صفة، كقولهم: "الدعصاء"، وهي أرض سهلة فيها رملة تحمي عليها الشمس، فتكون رمضاؤها أشد من غيرها، قال: وَالمُسْتَجِيرُ بِعَمْرٍو عِنْدَ كُرْبَتِهِ ... كَالمُسْتَجِيرِ مِنَ الدَّعْصَاءِ بِالنَّارِ. ولكن كتب اللغة لم تذكر "دعصة" هذه. وفي بعض الأخبار الأخرى "رملة دهسة"، و"الدهس" و"الدهاس" أرض سهلة لينة يثقل فيها المشي.]] فأصاب المسلمين ضعفٌ شديد، وألقى الشيطان في قلوبهم الغيظ، فوسوس بينهم: تزعمون أنكم أولياء الله وفيكم رسوله، وقد غلبكم المشركون على الماء، وأنتم تصلّون مُجْنِبين! فأمطر الله عليهم مطرًا شديدًا، فشرب المسلمون وتطهروا، وأذهب الله عنهم رجز الشيطان، وثبت الرمل حين أصابه المطر، ومشى الناس عليه والدوابّ، فساروا إلى القوم، وأمدّ الله نبيه بألف من الملائكة، فكان جبريل عليه السلام في خمسمائة من الملائكة مُجَنِّبةً، وميكائيل في خمسمائة مجنّبةً. [["المجنبة" (بتشديد النون مكسورة): هي الكتيبة التي تأخذ إحدى ناحيتي الجيش: "المجنبة اليمنى" و"المجنبة اليسرى"، وهي "الميمنة" و"الميسرة".]]

١٥٧٧١- حدثني محمد بن سعد قال، حدثني أبي قال، حدثني عمي قال، حدثني أبي، عن أبيه، عن ابن عباس قوله: "إذ يغشاكم النعاس أمنة منه" إلى قوله: ﴿ويثبت به الأقدام﴾، وذلك أن المشركين من قريش لما خرجوا لينصروا العير ويقاتلوا عنها، نزلوا على الماء يوم بدر، فغلبوا المؤمنين عليه، فأصاب المؤمنين الظمأ، فجعلوا يصلّون مجنبين مُحْدِثين، حتى تعاظم ذلك في صدور أصحاب رسول الله ﷺ، فأنزل الله من السماء ماء حتى سال الوادي، فشرب المسلمون، وملأوا الأسقية، وسقوا الرِّكاب، واغتسلوا من الجنابة، فجعل الله في ذلك طهورًا، وثبّت الأقدام. وذلك أنه كانت بينهم وبين القوم رملة، فبعث الله عليها المطر، فضربها حتى اشتدّت، وثبتت عليها الأقدام.

١٥٧٧٢- حدثني محمد بن الحسين قال، حدثنا أحمد بن المفضل قال، حدثنا أسباط، عن السدي قال: بينا رسول الله ﷺ والمسلمون، فسبقهم المشركون إلى ماء بدر فنزلوا عليه، وانصرف أبو سفيان وأصحابه تِلقاء البحر، فانطلقوا. قال: فنزلوا على أعلى الوادي، ونزل محمد ﷺ في أسفله. فكان الرجل من أصحاب محمد عليه السلام يُجْنِب فلا يقدر على الماء، فيصلي جُنُبًا، فألقى الشيطان في قلوبهم فقال: كيف ترجون أن تظهروا عليهم، وأحدكم يقوم إلى الصلاة جنبًا على غير وضوء!، قال: فأرسل الله عليهم المطر، فاغتسلوا وتوضأوا وشربوا، واشتدّت لهم الأرض، وكانت بطحاء تدخل فيها أرجلهم، [["البطحاء": تراب لين جرته السيول، وهو "الأبطح"، يكون في مسيل الوادي.]] فاشتدت لهم من المطر، واشتدّوا عليها.

١٥٧٧٣- حدثنا القاسم قال، حدثنا الحسين قال، حدثني حجاج، عن ابن جريج قال: قال ابن عباس: غلب المشركون المسلمين في أول أمرهم على الماء، فظمئ المسلمون وصلّوا مجنبين محدثين، وكانت بينهم رمال، فألقى الشيطان في قلوب المؤمنين الحَزَن، فقال: تزعمون أن فيكم نبيًّا، وأنكم أولياء الله، وقد غُلبتم على الماء، وتصلّون مُجْنبين محدثين! قال: فأنزل الله عز وجل ماءً من السماء، فسال كل وادٍ، فشرب المسلمون وتطهروا، وثبتت أقدامهم، وذهبت وسوسة الشيطان.

١٥٧٧٤- حدثني محمد بن عمرو قال، حدثنا أبو عاصم قال، حدثنا عيسى، عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد في قوله: ﴿ماء ليطهركم به﴾، قال: المطر، أنزله عليهم قبل النعاس. ﴿رجز الشيطان﴾، قال: وسوسته. قال: فأطفأ بالمطر الغبار، واشتدت به الأرض، [[في المخطوطة: "واصـ به" غير منقوطة، كأنها "وأثبتت به"، بالبناء للمجهول، والذي في المطبوعة جيد، وقريب أن يكون الناسخ قد حرّفه.]] وطابت به أنفسهم، وثبتت به أقدامهم.

١٥٧٧٥- حدثنا المثنى قال، حدثنا أبو حذيفة قال، حدثنا شبل، عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد: ﴿ماء ليطهركم به﴾، أنزله عليهم قبل النعاس، طبَّق بالمطر الغبار، ولبّد به الأرض، وطابت به أنفسهم، وثبتت به الأقدام.

١٥٧٧٦- حدثني المثنى قال، حدثنا أبو حذيفة قال، حدثنا شبل، عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد: ﴿ماء ليطهركم به﴾، قال: القطر. ﴿ويذهب عنكم رجز الشيطان﴾، وساوسه. أطفأ بالمطر الغبار، ولبّد به الأرض، [[في المخطوطة: "تطفي بالمطر الغبار، وبدت به الأرض"، وهو محرّف، والذي في المطبوعة أشبه بالصواب.]] وطابت به أنفسهم، وثبتت به أقدامهم.

١٥٧٧٧- حدثني المثنى قال، حدثنا أبو حذيفة قال، حدثنا شبل، عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد: "رجز الشيطان"، وسوسته.

١٥٧٧٨- حدثني يونس قال، أخبرنا ابن وهب قال، قال ابن زيد في قوله: ﴿وينزل عليكم من السماء ماء ليطهركم به﴾، قال: هذا يوم بدر، أنزل عليهم القطر. ﴿وليذهب عنكم رجز الشيطان﴾، الذي ألقى في قلوبكم: ليس لكم بهؤلاء طاقة! ﴿وليربط على قلوبكم ويثبت به الأقدام﴾.

١٥٧٧٩- حُدِّثت عن الحسين بن الفرج قال، سمعت أبا معاذ يقول: حدثنا عبيد بن سليمان قال، سمعت الضحاك يقول في قوله: ﴿إذ يغشاكم النعاس أمنة منه﴾ إلى قوله: ﴿ويثبت به الأقدام﴾: إن المشركين نزلوا بالماء يوم بدر، وغلبوا المسلمين عليه، فأصاب المسلمين الظمأ، وصلّوا محدثين مجنبين، فألقى الشيطان في قلوب المؤمنين الحزَن، ووسوس فيها: إنكم تزعمون أنكم أولياء الله، وأن محمدًا نبي الله، وقد غلبتم على الماء، وأنتم تصلّون محدثين مجنبين! فأمطر الله السماء حتى سال كل واد، فشرب المسلمون وملأوا أسقيتهم، [[في المخطوطة: "وبلوا أسقيتهم"، كأنها تُقرأ "وبلّوا"، والذي في المطبوعة جيد، وقد مضى مثله في الأخبار.]] وسقوا دوابهم، واغتسلوا من الجنابة، وثبّت الله به الأقدام. وذلك أنه كان بينهم وبين عدوهم رملة لا تجوزها الدواب، ولا يمشي فيها الماشي إلا بجَهد، فضربها الله بالمطر حتى اشتدت، وثبتت فيها الأقدام.

١٥٧٨٠- حدثنا ابن حميد قال، حدثنا سلمة، عن ابن إسحاق: "إذ يغشاكم النعاس أمنة منه"، أي: أنزلت عليكم الأمنة حتى نمتم لا تخافون، = "وينزل عليكم من السماء ماء"، للمطر الذي أصابهم تلك الليلة، [[في المطبوعة: "ونزل عليكم من السماء المطر الذي أصابهم..."، وفي المخطوطة: "ونزلت عليكم من السماء المطر الذي أصابهم..."، وأثبت ما في سيرة ابن هشام وهو الجيد.]] فحبس المشركون أن يسبقوا إلى الماء، وخُلِّي سبيل المؤمنين إليه = ﴿ليطهركم به ويذهب عنكم رجز الشيطان وليربط على قلوبكم ويثبت به الأقدام﴾، ليذهب عنهم شك الشيطان، بتخويفه إياهم عدوهم، واستجلاد الأرض لهم، [["استجلاد الأرض": من "الجلد" (بفتحتين)، وهي الأرض الصلبة، يعني أنها صارت أرضًا صلبة غليظة بعد أن كانت رملة ميثاء لينة. و"استجلدت الأرض" مما لم تذكره معاجم اللغة، وهو عريق فصيح.]] حتى انتهوا إلى منزلهم الذي سبق إليه عدوهم. [[الأثر: ١٥٧٨٠ - سيرة ابن هشام ٢: ٣٢٣، وهو تابع الأثر السالف رقم: ١٥٧٤٠. وكان في المطبوعة: "الذي سبق"، غير ما كان في المخطوطة، وهو المطابق لما في سيرة ابن هشام، وهو الصواب.]]

١٥٧٨١- Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said: Then He mentioned what Satan cast into their hearts regarding the matter of major impurity (janabah) and their standing to pray without ablution. So He said: ﴿When He covers you with drowsiness as a security from Him, and sends down upon you water from the sky to purify you by it, and to remove from you the defilement of Satan, and to strengthen your hearts, and to make your feet firm thereby﴾, until you walk firmly upon the sand, which was like the (firm) ground.

١٥٧٨٢- Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, saying: Dawud ibn Abi Hind narrated to us, saying: A man said in the presence of Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib (and at one point he said: "recited") ﴿and sends down upon you water from the sky to purify you by it﴾, [[In the printed edition it is written "ليطهركم بها" (to purify you by them), which differs from the manuscript, and I do not know where it came from; I have not found a reading like this one. Rather, the known reading of the majority of reciters is "ليطهركم به" with the ha' doubled and kasrah, from "طهر" in the intensive form, while Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib alone read "ليطهركم", as I have vocalized it, with a dammah on the ya', a sukun on the ta' and a kasrah on the ha', from "أطهر", and this is an anomalous reading. See Shawadh al-Qira'at by Ibn Khalawayh: 49, and Tafsir Abi Hayyan 4: 468.]] Sa'id said: "It is only: ﴿وَيُنَزِّلُ عَلَيْكُمْ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ مَاءً لِيُطَهِّرَكُمْ بِهِ﴾." He said: And al-Sha'bi said: That was a light rain on the day of Badr.
* *
Some scholars of the strange (gharib) vocabulary from the people of Basra claimed that the figurative sense (majaz) of His words ﴿and to make your feet firm thereby﴾ is: "and He pours patience upon them and sends it down to them, so that they stand firm against their enemy." [[This is Abu 'Ubaydah in Majaz al-Qur'an 1: 242.]]
This is a statement contrary to the view of all the interpreters among the Companions and the Followers, and it suffices as an error that it opposes the view of those we have mentioned. We have already explained their views on it, and that its meaning is: and to make the feet of the believers firm by the rain packing down the sand, so that their feet and their animals' hooves do not sink into it. [[See the explanation of "tathbit al-aqdam" (making the feet firm) above, 5: 354 and 7: 272, 273.]]
* *
Moreover, Abu Ja'far has here omitted separately explaining "﴿and to remove from you the defilement of Satan﴾" and "﴿and to strengthen your hearts﴾". See the explanation of "rijz" (defilement) above, p. 179, note 3, and the references there.
* *
As for His words: ﴿When your Lord revealed to the angels: "I am with you; so strengthen those who believe"﴾, [[See the explanation of "ma'" (with) above, 3: 214 and 5: 353.]] meaning: I will help you, ﴿so strengthen those who believe﴾, He says: strengthen their resolve and make their intentions sound in fighting their enemy among the polytheists. [[See the explanation of "tathbit" (strengthening) above, 5: 354 and 7: 272, 273, and the root (th-b-t) in the linguistic indexes.]]
* *
It has been said: The angels' strengthening of the believers was their presence in the battle alongside them.
* *
It has also been said: That was their aid to them in fighting their enemies.
* *
It has also been said: That was that an angel would come to a man among the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ and say: "I heard these people, meaning the polytheists, saying: By God, if they charge at us, we will surely be routed!" [[" al-Inkishaf" means defeat.]] Then the Muslims would relate that to one another, and their souls would be strengthened. They said: That was God's revelation to His angels.
* *
As for Ibn Ishaq, he said:
١٥٧٨٣- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: ﴿so strengthen those who believe﴾, i.e., support those who believe. [[The report 15783 is the continuation of the earlier report no. 15780; see Sirat Ibn Hisham 2: 323.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 8, verse 12:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿I will cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieve, so strike above the necks and strike every fingertip of them﴾ (12).

Abu Ja'far said: He, may He be exalted, says: I will terrify the hearts of those who disbelieve in Me, O believers, among you, and fill them with fear until they flee from you [[See the explanation of "casting terror" above, 7:279.]] = "So strike above the necks."

* *

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed regarding the interpretation of His saying: ﴿above the necks﴾.

Some of them said: its meaning is: strike the necks.

Those who said this:

15784. Ibn Wakī' related to us, saying: Ibn Idris related to us, from his father, from ʿAṭiyya: ﴿So strike above the necks﴾, he said: Strike the necks.

15785. ... He said: My father related to us, from al-Mas'udi, from al-Qasim, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I was not sent to punish with the punishment of Allah; I was only sent to strike necks and bind captives."

15786. It was related to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: ʿUbayd ibn Sulayman related to us, who said: I heard al-Dahhak say concerning His saying: ﴿So strike above the necks﴾: he says, strike the necks.

* *

Those who held this view argued that the Arabs say, "I saw the self (nafs) of so-and-so," meaning: I saw him. They said: likewise His saying: ﴿So strike above the necks﴾ means only: strike the necks.

* *

Others said: rather, the meaning is: strike the heads.

Those who said this:

15787. Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, from Yazid, from ʿIkrima: ﴿So strike above the necks﴾, he said: The heads.

* *

Those who held this view argued that what is "above the necks" is the heads. They said: it is not permissible to say "above the necks" and mean "the necks." They said: if that were permissible, it would be permissible to say "below the necks" and mean "the necks." They said: that is contrary to the understood sense of the address and a reversal of the meanings of speech.

* *

Others said: the meaning is: strike upon the necks, and they said: "upon" (ʿalā) and "above" (fawq) have close meanings, so one may be placed in the position of the other. [[See Majaz al-Qur'an of Abu ʿUbayda, 1:242.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct view on this is to say that God commanded the believers, teaching them how to kill the polytheists and strike them with the sword: that they strike above the necks of them, and the hands and feet. His saying ﴿above the necks﴾ may be intended to mean the heads, and it may be intended to mean: from above the skin of the necks, [[In the printed edition the word "min" is omitted; in the manuscript it is poorly written.]] so its meaning would be: upon the necks. Since this is possible, the saying of the one who said its meaning is "the necks" is valid. And since the matter admits of the interpretations we have mentioned, it is not for us to direct it to some of its meanings to the exclusion of others, except by a proof that must be accepted, and there is no proof indicating its specificity. So it is necessary to say: God commanded the striking of the heads of the polytheists and their necks and their hands and their feet, addressing the companions of His Prophet ﷺ who witnessed Badr with him.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and strike every fingertip of them﴾, its meaning is: and strike, O believers, from your enemy, every joint and articulation of their hands and feet.

* *

And "al-banan" is the plural of "bananah," which are the tips of the fingers of the hands and feet, and from this is the saying of the poet: [[He is al-ʿAbbas ibn Mirdas al-Sulami.]]

Ala laytani qatta'tu minni bananatan wa-laqaytuhu fi al-bayti yaqzana hadhara

"Would that I had cut off from myself a fingertip, and that I had met him in the house, alert and wary."

By "bananah" he means one of "al-banan."

* *

And the people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said.

Those who said this:

15788. Abu al-Sa'ib related to us, saying: Ibn Idris related to us, from his father, from ʿAṭiyya: ﴿and strike every fingertip of them﴾, he said: every joint.

15789. Ibn Wakī' related to us, saying: Ibn Idris related to us, from his father, from ʿAṭiyya: ﴿and strike every fingertip of them﴾, he said: the joints.

15790. ... He said: al-Muharibi related to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak: ﴿and strike every fingertip of them﴾, he said: every joint.

15791. Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, from Yazid, from ʿIkrima: ﴿and strike every fingertip of them﴾, he said: the extremities. It is also said: every joint.

15792. Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiya related to me, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas: ﴿and strike every fingertip of them﴾, meaning: by the fingertips, the extremities.

15793. al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Juraydj concerning His saying: ﴿and strike every fingertip of them﴾, he said: the extremities.

15794. It was related to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: ʿUbayd ibn Sulayman related to us, who said: I heard al-Dahhak say concerning His saying: ﴿and strike every fingertip of them﴾, meaning: the extremities.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 8, verse 13–14:

The interpretation of His words: ﴿That is because they opposed God and His Messenger. And whoever opposes God and His Messenger, indeed God is severe in punishment﴾ (13).

Abu Ja'far said: By His words, may His remembrance be exalted, ﴿That is because they﴾, He means: this act of striking these disbelievers above the necks and striking every fingertip of them is a recompense for them for their opposition (shiqaq) to God and His Messenger, and a punishment for them for it.

* *

The meaning of His words ﴿opposed God and His Messenger﴾ is: they separated from the command of God and His Messenger, disobeyed both of them, and obeyed the command of Satan. [See the explanation of "shiqaq" (opposition) above: 3:115, 116, 336; 8:319; 9:204.]

* *

The meaning of His words ﴿And whoever opposes God and His Messenger﴾ is: whoever contradicts the command of God and the command of His Messenger and departs from obeying them = ﴿indeed God is severe in punishment﴾ upon him. And the severity of His punishment for him: in this world, His bringing down upon him the same vengeance that came upon His enemies, and in the Hereafter, abiding eternally in the fire of Hell. The word "upon him" (lahu) has been omitted from the speech, as the context indicates it.

* *

The interpretation of His words: ﴿That, so taste it, and that for the disbelievers is the punishment of the Fire﴾ (14).

Abu Ja'far said: May His remembrance be exalted, He says: this is the punishment which I have hastened for you, O disbelievers who oppose God and His Messenger, in this world: the striking of you above the necks and the striking of every fingertip, at the hands of My believing allies. So taste it now, and know that for you in the next life and the return is the punishment of the Fire. [See the explanation of "dhawq" (tasting) above: 12:420, footnote 1, and the references there.]

* *

Regarding the vowelling of "anna" (that) in His words ﴿and that for the disbelievers﴾, there are two grammatical possibilities:

One is the nominative (raf'), and the other is the accusative (nasb).

As for the nominative, the meaning is: "That, so taste it; that, and that for the disbelievers is the punishment of the Fire," with the intention of repeating "that" (dhalikum), as if it were said: "That matter, and this."

As for the accusative, there are two ways: One is: "That, so taste it, and know," or "and be certain that for the disbelievers" — so its accusative is by the implied presence of a hidden verb. The poet said:

"And you saw your husband in battle, girding a sword and a spear"

meaning: "and carrying a spear."

The other: meaning "That, so taste it, and [know] that for the disbelievers is the punishment of the Fire," then the preposition "bi" (with) was deleted, and so it became accusative. [See al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1:405, 406.]

Mention of those who said that:

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The more correct of the two interpretations of this verse, in my view, is the saying of the one who said: its ruling is muhkam (firm, not abrogated), and it was revealed concerning the people of Badr, but its ruling applies to all the believers; and that Allah forbade the believers, when they meet the enemy, to turn their backs to them in flight, except for swerving for the purpose of battle or joining a company of the believers wherever it may be in the land of Islam; and that whoever turns his back to them after the advance, fleeing without intending one of the two circumstances in which Allah permitted turning away, has deserved His threat, unless He graciously pardons him.

We have said it is muhkam and not abrogated, because of what we have shown in more than one place in this book and others: [[See what he said about "naskh" (abrogation) in the subject indexes, and in the indexes of language, grammar and others.]] that it is not permissible to rule that a verse's ruling has been abrogated, when it has another meaning apart from abrogation, except by a proof that must be accepted, either a report that removes all excuse, or a proof of reason. And neither of these two kinds of proof indicates the abrogation of the ruling of the words of Allah, mighty and majestic: ﴿And whoever turns to them on that day his back, unless swerving for battle or joining a company﴾.

[[For the explanation of "ma'wa" (refuge) see what has preceded at 10:481, note 3, and the references there.]] "And wretched is the destination", meaning: wretched is the place to which that destination leads. [[For the explanation of "al-masir" (destination) see what has preceded at 9:205, note 5, and the references there.]]

Al-Dhahabi agreed with him.]]

15802 – Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Dawud narrated to us, from Abu Nadra: ﴿And whoever turns to them on that day his back﴾, he said: This was revealed concerning the people of Badr.

15803 – Ya'qub narrated to us, saying: Ibn Ulayya narrated to us, from Ibn Awn, who said: I wrote to Nafi' asking him about the words ﴿And whoever turns to them on that day his back﴾: Was that on that day, or is it after it? He said: He wrote back to me: "That was only on the day of Badr."

15804 – Ali ibn Sahl narrated to us, saying: Zayd narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, who said: Fleeing was only on the day of Badr, when they had no refuge to which they could take shelter. As for today, there is no fleeing.

15805 – Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from al-Rabi', from al-Hasan regarding ﴿And whoever turns to them on that day his back﴾, he said: This was specific to the day of Badr; fleeing from the battle is not among the major sins.

15806 – ... He said: My father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from a man, from al-Dahhak regarding ﴿And whoever turns to them on that day his back﴾, he said: This was specific to the day of Badr.

15807 – ... He said: Rawh ibn Ubada narrated to us, from Habib ibn al-Shahid, from al-Hasan regarding ﴿And whoever turns to them on that day his back﴾, he said: It was revealed concerning the people of Badr.

15808 – Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada regarding ﴿And whoever turns to them on that day his back﴾, he said: That is the day of Badr.

15809 – al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Suwayd narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from al-Mubarak ibn Fudala, from al-Hasan regarding ﴿And whoever turns to them on that day his back﴾, he said: That was the day of Badr. As for today, if one withdraws to a company or to a city — I think he said — then there is no harm in it.

15810 – al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Qabisa ibn Uqba narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ibn Awn who said: I wrote to Nafi' about ﴿And whoever turns to them on that day his back﴾, and he said: This is only the day of Badr.

15811 – al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Suwayd ibn Nasr narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, from Ibn Lahi'a, who said: Yazid ibn Abi Habib narrated to me: Allah made the Fire obligatory for whoever fled on the day of Badr. He said: "And whoever turns to them on that day his back, unless swerving for battle or joining a company, he has certainly returned with anger from Allah" — then, when the day of Uhud came after that, He said: ﴿It was only Satan who caused them to slip because of some of what they had earned. And Allah has already pardoned them﴾ [Surah Al ʿImran: 155]. Then Hunayn came seven years later, and He said: ﴿Then you turned back in retreat﴾ [Surah al-Tawba: 25], and: ﴿Then Allah accepts repentance after that from whom He wills﴾ [Surah al-Tawba: 27].

15812 – Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn Ulayya narrated to us, saying: Ibn Awn narrated to us, from Muhammad, that Umar, may Allah have mercy on him, was informed of the killing of Abu Ubayd, and he said: If only he had withdrawn to me! Indeed, I would have been a company for him! [[The report 15812: "Abu Ubayd ibn Mas'ud al-Thaqafi" was a Companion, and he was the one of the Battle of the Bridge, known as the Bridge of Abu Ubayd. When Umar assumed the caliphate, he removed Khalid ibn al-Walid from Iraq and its frontiers, and appointed Abu Ubayd ibn Mas'ud al-Thaqafi in the year 13. When Yazdajird directed his armies against the army of Abu Ubayd, Abu Ubayd crossed the bridge into the narrow passage, and they fought a fierce battle; Abu Ubayd dealt heavy blows to the Persians, and he struck the trunk of the elephant, so the elephant knelt upon him and killed him. There were martyred from the Muslims that day one thousand eight hundred, and it is said four thousand, between the slain and the drowned. See al-Istiʿab: 671, and Tarikh al-Tabari 4:67–70. See also the reports nos. 15814, 15815. In many books "Abu Ubayda" appears in this report, and that is an error. In the printed edition here was: "If he had withdrawn to me, I would have been a company for him," which differs from the manuscript, without fidelity or knowledge.]]

15813 – al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Suwayd narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, from Jarir ibn Hazim, who said: Qays ibn Sa'd narrated to me, who said: I asked Ata' ibn Abi Rabah about the words ﴿And whoever turns to them on that day his back﴾, and he said: This is abrogated (mansukha) by the verse in al-Anfal: ﴿Now Allah has lightened [the burden] for you, and He knows that among you is weakness. So if there are among you one hundred patient, they will overcome two hundred﴾ [Surah al-Anfal: 66]. He said: It is not permissible for a people to flee from twice their number. He said: That verse was abrogated except for this number. [[The report 15813: "Qays ibn Sa'd al-Makki" is trustworthy, passed at no. 2943 and 9413. In the manuscript and the printed edition it was "Qays ibn Sa'id", which is an error.]]

15814 – al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Suwayd narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Sulayman al-Taymi, from Abu Uthman who said: When Abu Ubayd was killed, the news reached Umar, and he said: O people, I am your company!  [[The report 15814: "Abu Uthman" is unknown (majhul); he related from Anas ibn Malik and Ma'qil ibn Yasar. Al-Taymi related from him. Ibn al-Madini said: "No one related from him except him, and he is unknown." He is mentioned in al-Tahdhib and in Ibn Abi Hatim 4/2/408.]]

15815 – ... He said: Ibn al-Mubarak narrated, from Ma'mar, Sufyan al-Thawri and Ibn Uyayna, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, said: I am the company of every Muslim.

* *
