Others said: Rather, the ruling of this verse is general, applying to everyone who turns his back to the enemy in flight.

Mention of those who said that:

15816 – al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talha, from Ibn Abbas who said: The greatest of the major sins are associating partners with Allah and fleeing from the battle, because Allah, mighty and majestic, says: ﴿And whoever turns to them on that day his back … he has certainly returned with anger from Allah, and his refuge is Hell, and wretched is the destination﴾.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The more correct of the two interpretations of this verse, in my view, is the saying of the one who said: its ruling is muhkam (firm, not abrogated), and it was revealed concerning the people of Badr, but its ruling applies to all the believers; and that Allah forbade the believers, when they meet the enemy, to turn their backs to them in flight, except for swerving for the purpose of battle or joining a company of the believers wherever it may be in the land of Islam; and that whoever turns his back to them after the advance, fleeing without intending one of the two circumstances in which Allah permitted turning away, has deserved His threat, unless He graciously pardons him.

We have said it is muhkam and not abrogated, because of what we have shown in more than one place in this book and others: [[See what he said about "naskh" (abrogation) in the subject indexes, and in the indexes of language, grammar and others.]] that it is not permissible to rule that a verse's ruling has been abrogated, when it has another meaning apart from abrogation, except by a proof that must be accepted, either a report that removes all excuse, or a proof of reason. And neither of these two kinds of proof indicates the abrogation of the ruling of the words of Allah, mighty and majestic: ﴿And whoever turns to them on that day his back, unless swerving for battle or joining a company﴾.

* *

As for His words: ﴿he has certainly returned with anger from Allah﴾, meaning: he has returned with anger from Allah. [[For the explanation of "ba'a" (returned) see what has preceded at 10:216, note 2, and the references there.]] ﴿And his refuge is Hell﴾, meaning: his destination to which he goes in his return on the Day of Resurrection is Hell. [[For the explanation of "ma'wa" (refuge) see what has preceded at 10:481, note 3, and the references there.]] "And wretched is the destination", meaning: wretched is the place to which that destination leads. [[For the explanation of "al-masir" (destination) see what has preceded at 9:205, note 5, and the references there.]]

The discussion concerning His saying: ﴿So you did not kill them, but God killed them, and you did not throw when you threw, but God threw, that He might bestow upon the believers a fine favour from Him. Indeed God is All-Hearing, All-Knowing﴾ (8:17).

Abu Ja'far said: God, may His remembrance be exalted, says to the believers in Him and His Messenger, among those who witnessed Badr with the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and fought alongside him against the unbelievers of Quraysh, the enemies of His religion: ﴿So you did not kill them﴾, O believers, you yourselves, ﴿but God killed them﴾.

* *

He, may His praise be exalted, attributed their killing to Himself and negated it from the believers in Him who fought the polytheists, since He, may His praise be exalted, was the one who caused their killing, and the fighting of the believers against them was by His command. In this is the clearest proof of the falsehood of the view of those who deny that God has any action in the deeds of His creatures, which they reach.

Likewise is His saying to His Prophet, peace be upon him: ﴿And you did not throw when you threw, but God threw﴾. He attributed the throwing to the Prophet of God, then negated it from him, and informed about Himself that He is the thrower, since He, may His praise be exalted, is the one who delivered what was thrown to those of the polytheists against whom it was thrown, and the one who caused the throw for His Messenger.

It is said to those who deny what we have mentioned [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "to the Muslims what we have mentioned", which is a clear error. It is evident that the copyist of the manuscript from which the scribe copied wrote the "rā'" of "al-munkirīn" joined with the yā' and nūn, and did not place the dot of the kāf as was their custom, so he read it wrongly and transcribed it wrongly.]]: You know that God attributed to Himself the throwing of His Prophet (ﷺ) at the polytheists, after describing His Prophet with it and attributing it to him. That is a single act, [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "that" without a wāw, and the sentence does not stand without it.]] which was from God by causing and confirming it, and from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) by the casting and sending. So why do you deny that all the acquired actions of creatures are likewise: from God is the origination and accomplishment through causation, and from the creatures is the acquisition through their powers? They will not say anything about one of the two but that they are bound to say the same about the other.

* *

The people of interpretation (ta'wil, i.e. tafsir) said the same as what we have said about this.

Those who said so:

15817. Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding God's saying: ﴿So you did not kill them﴾, to the Companions of Muhammad (ﷺ) when he said this: "I killed", and this: "I killed". ﴿And you did not throw when you threw﴾, he said: to Muhammad when he threw pebbles at the unbelievers.

15818. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, in similar terms.

15819. Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada: ﴿And you did not throw when you threw, but God threw﴾. He said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) threw pebbles at them on the day of Badr.

15820. Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Ayyub, from Ikrima, who said: Not a single one of them fell except into the eye of a man.

15821. 'Abd al-Warith ibn 'Abd al-Samad ibn 'Abd al-Warith narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, saying: Aban al-'Attar narrated to us, saying: Hisham ibn 'Urwa narrated to us, saying: When the Messenger of God (ﷺ) arrived at Badr, he said: "This is where they will fall!" The polytheists found that the Prophet (ﷺ) had preceded them to it and had alighted there. When they came in sight of him, they claimed that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "These are Quraysh, who have come with their clamour and pride, opposing you and calling your Messenger a liar. O God, I ask You for what You promised me!" When they approached, he confronted them, threw dust into their faces, and God, mighty and majestic, routed them. [[The report 15821: "Aban al-'Attar" is "Aban ibn Yazid al-'Attar", trustworthy. Mentioned previously: 3832, 9656, 13518, 15719.

This report Abu Ja'far also related in his History 2:268, within a long report, part of which has passed under number 15719. It is from the letter of 'Urwa to 'Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan, which Abu Ja'far related in scattered form in the History. I will cite it in full in the takhrij of report number 16083.

In the printed edition here was: "they came with their pride and their boasting", which is an ugly alteration. I have retained what is in the manuscript, which agrees with the History.

And "al-jalaba" is the mingling of people when they gather, and some of them shout at others urging and spurring them on, as happens in the gathering of armies.]]

15822. Ahmad ibn Mansur narrated to us, saying: Ya'qub ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn 'Imran narrated to us, saying: Musa ibn Ya'qub ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Zam'a narrated to us, from Yazid ibn 'Abd Allah, from Abu Bakr ibn Sulayman ibn Abi Hathma, from Hakim ibn Hizam, who said: When it was the day of Badr, we heard a sound fall from the sky as if it were the sound of a pebble falling into a basin, and the Messenger of God (ﷺ) threw that throw, and we were routed. [[Report 15822: "Ahmad ibn Mansur ibn Sayyar ibn al-Ma'arik al-Ramadi", the teacher of al-Tabari, trustworthy. Passed under numbers 10260, 10521.

And "Ya'qub ibn Muhammad al-Zuhri", disputed concerning him; he is truthful, but he does not care from whom he narrates. Passed under numbers 2867, 8012, 15654, 15714.

And "'Abd al-'Aziz ibn 'Imran ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz al-Zuhri", al-A'raj, known as Ibn Abi Thabit. Weak; he was a man of genealogy, not one of the people of hadith. Passed under numbers 8012, 15756.

And "Musa ibn Ya'qub ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Wahb ibn Zam'a al-Asadi al-Qurashi", trustworthy, but spoken of; Ahmad said: "His hadith does not please me", and Abu Dawud said: "He has unknown teachers". Passed under numbers 9923, 15756.

And "Yazid ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Wahb ibn Zam'a al-Asadi al-Qurashi", whose nephew Musa ibn Ya'qub narrated from him. Mentioned in al-Kabir 4/2/346, and Ibn Abi Hatim 4/2/276, and neither of them mentioned any criticism of him.

And "Abu Bakr ibn Sulayman ibn Abi Hathma al-'Adawi", he was one of the scholars of Quraysh. Trustworthy. Mentioned in al-Tahdhib, and al-Kuna of al-Bukhari: 13, and Ibn Abi Hatim 4/2/341.

This report is weak in its chain, because of the weakness of "'Abd al-'Aziz ibn 'Imran al-Zuhri". Ibn Kathir mentioned it in his tafsir 4:32 and said: "Strange from this route", but he was lax in explaining its chain.

However, al-Haythami mentioned it in Majma' al-Zawa'id 6:84 and said: "al-Tabarani related it in al-Kabir and al-Awsat, and its chain is good", so perhaps it is a chain other than this one, for he has weakened 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn 'Imran on this subject many times.

al-Suyuti cited it in al-Durr al-Manthur 3:174, and added its attribution to Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, and Ibn Mardawayh.]]

15823. al-Harith narrated to me, saying: 'Abd al-'Aziz narrated to us, saying: Abu Ma'shar narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Qays and Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, who both said: When the two groups drew near to each other, the Messenger of God (ﷺ) took a handful of dust and threw it into the faces of the people, and said: "May the faces be disfigured!" It entered all their eyes, and the Companions of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) advanced, killing them and taking them captive. Their rout was at the throw of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and God revealed: ﴿And you did not throw when you threw, but God threw﴾, the verse, up to: ﴿Indeed God is All-Hearing, All-Knowing﴾.

15824. Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada regarding His saying: ﴿And you did not throw when you threw﴾, the verse. It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God (ﷺ) took three stones on the day of Badr and threw them at the faces of the unbelievers, and they were routed at the third stone.

15825. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said to 'Ali when the two hosts met on the day of Badr: "Give me pebbles from the earth." He handed him pebbles with dust on them, and he threw them at the faces of the people, and there was not a polytheist but some of that dust entered his eyes. Then the believers pursued them, killing them and taking them captive. [["Radafa" (with fatha then kasra): he followed him and overtook him.]] He mentioned the throw of the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: ﴿So you did not kill them, but God killed them. And you did not throw when you threw, but God threw﴾.

15826. Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying: ﴿And you did not throw when you threw, but God threw﴾: This is the day of Badr. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) took three pebbles, threw one pebble at the right wing of the people, one pebble at the left wing of the people, and one pebble in their midst, and said: "May the faces be disfigured!" And they were routed. That is the saying of God, mighty and majestic: ﴿And you did not throw when you threw, but God threw﴾.

15827. al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) raised his hand on the day of Badr and said: "O Lord, if this band perishes, You will never be worshipped on earth again!" Gabriel said to him: "Take a handful of dust!" He took a handful of dust and threw it into their faces, and there was not one of the polytheists whose eyes, nostrils and mouth were not struck by dust from that handful, and they turned their backs in flight.

15728. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: God, mighty and majestic, said regarding the throw of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) at the polytheists with pebbles from his hand when he threw at them: ﴿And you did not throw when you threw, but God threw﴾, meaning: that throw was not by your throwing, were it not for what God placed in it of your victory, and what He cast into the hearts of your enemy from it when God routed them. [[Report 15828: Ibn Hisham's Sira 2:323, and it follows the report passed under number 15783. In the printed edition and the manuscript, the words "And you did not throw when you threw" were omitted, and the rest of the verse was given. In the manuscript was "when He routed them", without mention of the divine name, and in the printed edition it was altered to "so they were routed". I have retained what is in Ibn Hisham's Sira.]]

* *

It was related from al-Zuhri regarding this a saying contrary to these sayings, which is:

15829. al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri: ﴿And you did not throw when you threw﴾. He said: Ubayy ibn Khalaf al-Jumahi came to the Prophet (ﷺ) with a decayed bone, and said: "O Muhammad, does God give life to this while it is crumbled?" He was crumbling the bone, and the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "God will give it life, then He will cause you to die, then He will enter you into the Fire!" He said: When it was the day of Uhud, he said: "By God, I will surely kill Muhammad when I see him!" This reached the Prophet (ﷺ), and he said: "Rather, I will kill him, God willing."

[[I fear that there is a deficiency in this place of the tafsir, for I found that Ibn Kathir (4:32) mentioned in the tafsir of this verse what he attributed to Ibn Jarir, and this is its text in its order and commentary:

Here are two other sayings, very strange indeed:

The first: Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn 'Awf al-Ta'i narrated to me, saying: Abu al-Mughira narrated to us, saying: Safwan ibn 'Amr narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr narrated to us, that the Messenger of God (ﷺ), on the day of Ibn Abi al-Huqayq at Khaybar, called for a bow. A long bow was brought to him, and he said: "Bring me a bow other than it." They brought him a bow of the kabda type, and the Prophet (ﷺ) shot at the fortress, and the arrow came down until it killed Ibn Abi al-Huqayq while he was in his bed. So God revealed: "And you did not throw when you threw, but God threw."

This is strange, and its chain is good up to 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr ibn Nufayr, but perhaps he was confused, or he meant that the verse encompasses all of this. Otherwise, the context of the verse in Surah al-Anfal concerns the story of Badr beyond doubt, and this is not hidden from the imams of knowledge, and God knows best.

The second: Ibn Jarir also related, and al-Hakim in his Mustadrak, with a sound chain, to Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab and al-Zuhri, that they both said: It was revealed concerning the throw of the Prophet (ﷺ) on the day of Uhud, when he struck Ubayy ibn Khalaf with a spear through his coat of mail, grazing his collarbone, so that he began to slip from his horse repeatedly, until his death came some days later, after he had suffered the painful torment, joined to the torment of the barzakh, which is linked to the torment of the Hereafter.

This saying from these two imams is also very strange indeed, and perhaps they meant that the verse encompasses him in its generality, not that it was revealed specifically about him, as has passed, and God knows best.

I say: The first of these two reports was related by al-Wahidi in Asbab al-Nuzul: 174, through "Safwan ibn 'Amr, from 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Jubayr". His saying "'Abd al-'Aziz" is an error; the correct version is what is in Ibn Kathir's tafsir.

Then al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur 3:175 cited these two reports as also attributed to Ibn Jarir, and added the attribution of the first to Ibn Abi Hatim. He mentioned the second and added its attribution to Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim.

Then al-Suyuti added in al-Durr al-Manthur, and I quote these two reports from it with their text:

The first: "'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim related, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, who said: When it was the day of Uhud, Ubayy ibn Khalaf began to spur his horse until he came near the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and some men from the Muslims stood in the way of Ubayy ibn Khalaf to kill him. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said to them: "Withdraw! Withdraw!" Then the Messenger of God (ﷺ) took his spear in his hand and threw it at Ubayy ibn Khalaf, and broke one of his ribs. Ubayy ibn Khalaf returned to his companions heavily wounded, and they carried him when they turned back, retreating. They began to say: "There is no harm!" Ubayy said when they said that: "By God, if it had been with the people, it would have killed them all! Did he not say: 'I will kill you, God willing'?" His companions took him away, supporting him, until he died at some point along the way, and they buried him.

Ibn al-Musayyab said: In that, God, may He be exalted, revealed: "And you did not throw when you threw, but God threw", the verse.

The second: "Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir related, from al-Zuhri regarding His saying: 'And you did not throw when you threw, but God threw.' He said: When he threw at Ubayy ibn Khalaf on the day of Uhud with his spear."

This is all, and it is likely that some reports of Abu Ja'far have fallen out at this place, unless these reports come later in another place. As for what has preceded, the report of "Ubayy ibn Khalaf" has passed in the hadith of al-Suddi under number 7943 (vol. 7: 255).

The first report was related by al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak 2:327, through Muhammad ibn Falih, from Musa ibn 'Uqba, from Ibn Shihab, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, and he said: This is a sound hadith according to the criteria of the two Shaykhs, though they did not record it, and al-Dhahabi agreed with him.]]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And that He might bestow upon the believers a fine favour from Him﴾, its meaning is: so that He might bless the believers in God and His Messenger with victory over their enemies, [[In the printed edition: "and that He might bless", and I have retained what is in the manuscript.]] and grant them the spoils of what they had, and record for them the rewards of their deeds and their struggle with the Messenger of God (ﷺ). [[In the printed edition: "and establish for them the rewards of their deeds", which has no meaning, and it did not read the manuscript well, due to an error in its pointing.]]

* *

And that "fine favour" is the throw of God at these polytheists. By "fine favour" is meant a good, beautiful blessing, and it is what has been described and what is in its meaning. [[See the explanation of "bala'" (trial, favour) above, p. 85, note 5, and the references there.]]

15830. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said regarding His saying: ﴿And that He might bestow upon the believers a fine favour from Him﴾, meaning: that He might make the believers recognise His blessings upon them, in granting them victory over their enemy despite the abundance and the scarcity of their numbers, so that by that they might recognise His right and by that give thanks for His blessing. [[Report 15830: Ibn Hisham's Sira 2:323-324, and it follows the report passed under number 15828. In the Sira, the words "despite the abundance of their numbers" fell out of the wording; this should be corrected there.]]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Indeed God is All-Hearing, All-Knowing﴾, it means: indeed God is All-Hearing, O believers, of the supplication of the Prophet (ﷺ), and his entreaty to his Lord, and his request to Him for the destruction of His enemy and your enemy. It was said to him: "It is only a young camel!" He said: "Did He not say: 'I will kill you'? By God, if He had said it to all of creation, they would have died!" And He is All-Knowing of your speech and the speech of all His creation, of all that, and of what is in it of your welfare and the welfare of His servants, and of other things; He encompasses it all. So fear Him, and obey His command and the command of His Messenger. [[See the explanation of "Hearing" and "Knowing" above, in the indices of language (s-m-') and ('-l-m).]]

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿That is so, and that Allah weakens the plot of the disbelievers﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying, may His praise be exalted, ﴿That﴾ He means this act: the killing of the polytheists, and the shooting at them until they were routed, and the testing of the believers with a good trial through victory over them and His enabling them to kill and capture them. ﴿We did what We did.﴾ ﴿And that Allah weakens the plot of the disbelievers﴾ means: Know that, along with that, Allah weakens and diminishes [[See the explanation of "al-wahn" (weakening) earlier: 7:234, 269; 9:170.]] ﴿the plot of the disbelievers﴾, meaning their scheming, [[See the explanation of "al-kayd" (plotting) earlier, p. 322, note 2, and the references there.]] until they are humbled and submit to the truth, or are destroyed. [[In the manuscript: "wa-yuhlakū" (and they are destroyed); the correct reading in context is what has been adopted here.]]

* *

As for the reading of "anna" (that), the possibilities are the same as in His saying: ﴿That, so taste it, and that for the disbelievers﴾ [Surat al-Anfal: 14]. I have explained this there. [[See what preceded, p. 434.]]

* *

The reciters have differed concerning the reading of His saying: ﴿mūhinu﴾ (weakening).

The majority of the reciters of Madina, some of the Makkans, and the Basrans read it as "muwahhinu" with a shadda (doubled letter), from "wahhantu al-shay'" (I weakened the thing), meaning I made it weak.

* *

The majority of the reciters of Kufa read it as ﴿mūhinu﴾, from "awhantuhu, fa-ana mūhinuhu" (I weakened him, so I am one who weakens him), meaning I made him weak.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The doubled form is more pleasing to me in this, because Allah, exalted is He, used to undo what the polytheists fastened against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his Companions, knot after knot and thing after thing. Yet the other reading is also a sound way of reading it.

**The Interpretation of His Words:** ﴿If you seek a decision, then the decision has indeed come to you; and if you desist, it is better for you; and if you return, We will return; and your company will avail you nothing, however numerous it is; and indeed Allah is with the believers﴾ (8:19)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: May He be exalted and remembered, says to the polytheists who fought the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at Badr: ﴿If you seek a decision, then the decision has indeed come to you﴾, meaning: If you ask Allah to judge between the two parties, the one that is more severed from kinship and the one that is more unjust, and you ask Him to give you victory over it, then the judgment of Allah has come to you, and His victory for the wronged over the wrongdoer, and for the one in the right over the one in falsehood. [[See the explanation of "al-istiftah" (seeking a decision/opening) and "al-fath" (the decision/victory) earlier: 2:254; 10:405, 406; 12:563.]]

* *

The people of ta'wil (interpretation, the tafsir scholars) said the same as what we have said about this.

Those who said so:

15831. Ibn Wakic narrated to us, saying: al-Muharibi narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, regarding ﴿If you seek a decision, then the decision has indeed come to you﴾: He said: "If you seek a judgment, then the judgment has indeed come to you."

15832. ... He said: Suwayd ibn Amr al-Kalbi narrated to us, from Hammad ibn Zayd, from Ayyub, from Ikrimah, regarding ﴿If you seek a decision, then the decision has indeed come to you﴾: He said: "If you seek a judgment, then the judgment has indeed come to you."

15833. Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas regarding His words: ﴿If you seek a decision, then the decision has indeed come to you﴾, meaning by that the polytheists: "If you seek help, then reinforcements have indeed come to you."

15834. al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Abd Allah ibn Kathir informed me, from Ibn Abbas regarding His words: ﴿If you seek a decision﴾, he said: "If you seek a judgment, the judgment..." And he used to say: ﴿And if you desist, it is better for you; and if you return, We will return; and your company will avail you nothing, however numerous it is﴾. I said: "For the polytheists?" He said: "We do not know it except that." [[In the printed edition and the manuscript it reads "we do not know," and the correct reading is what has been established.]]

15835. Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding His words: ﴿If you seek a decision, then the decision has indeed come to you﴾, he said: The unbelievers of Quraysh, in their saying: "Our Lord, decide between us and Muhammad and his companions!" So the decision was made between them on the day of Badr.

15836. al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similarly.

15837. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri regarding ﴿If you seek a decision, then the decision has indeed come to you﴾, he said: Abu Jahl sought a decision, saying: "O Allah, = meaning Muhammad and himself = whichever of us was more wicked toward You, and more severed in kinship, then destroy him today!" [[It is said "ahanahu Allah," meaning Allah destroyed him. And "al-hayn" (with a fatha and then a sukun): destruction, or the appointed time of destruction, in precise terms.]] Allah said: ﴿If you seek a decision, then the decision has indeed come to you﴾.

15838. al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri regarding His words: ﴿If you seek a decision, then the decision has indeed come to you﴾, he said: Abu Jahl ibn Hisham sought a decision, saying: "O Allah, whichever of us was more wicked toward You and more severed in kinship, then destroy him today!" Meaning Muhammad, peace be upon him, and himself. Allah, mighty and majestic, said: ﴿If you seek a decision, then the decision has indeed come to you﴾. So the two sons of Afra', Awf and Mu'awwidh, struck him, and Ibn Mas'ud finished him off.

15839. al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: al-Layth narrated to me, saying: Uqayl narrated to me, from Ibn Shihab, who said: Abd Allah ibn Tha'laba ibn Su'ayr al-Adawi, an ally of Banu Zuhra, informed me that the one who sought the decision that day was Abu Jahl, and that when the two sides met he said: "Whichever of us is more severed in kinship and has brought what is not known, then destroy him this morning!" That was his seeking, so Allah revealed concerning it: ﴿If you seek a decision, then the decision has indeed come to you﴾, the verse. [[The report 15839: Abd Allah ibn Tha'laba ibn Su'ayr al-Adawi, whom the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wiped over his face and head at the time of the Conquest, and supplicated for him. Abu Hatim said: "He saw the Prophet ﷺ while he was young." al-Bukhari said in al-Tarikh: "Abd Allah ibn Tha'laba, from the Prophet ﷺ, is mursal (a narration whose chain skips a companion), unless it is from his father, and this is more likely." He is listed in al-Isaba, al-Tahdhib, Usd al-Ghaba, al-Istee'ab: 341, and Ibn Abi Hatim 2/2/19.

This report will come through the chain of Ibn Ishaq, from al-Zuhri, under numbers 15846 and 15848, and through the chain of Salih ibn Kaysan, from al-Zuhri, number 15847.

Ahmad narrated it in his Musnad 5: 431, 4, through Yazid ibn Harun, from Ibn Ishaq, from al-Zuhri; and p. 431, 432, through Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim ibn Sa'd, from his father, from Ibn Ishaq, from al-Zuhri.

al-Hakim narrated it in al-Mustadrak 2: 328, through Yazid ibn Harun, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from al-Zuhri; then through Abd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Hanbal, from his father, from Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim ibn Sa'd, from his father, from Salih ibn Kaysan, from al-Zuhri. He said: "This is a sound hadith according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim), though they did not record it," and al-Dhahabi agreed with him.

I did not find this second chain which al-Hakim mentioned in the Musnad, and Ibrahim ibn Sa'd narrates from Salih ibn Kaysan, and from al-Zuhri, from Ibn Ishaq.]]

15840. Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada regarding His words: ﴿If you seek a decision, then the decision has indeed come to you﴾, the verse, he says: Badr was indeed a judgment and a lesson for whoever takes heed.

15841. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said: When the polytheists went out from Mecca toward the Prophet ﷺ, they clung to the curtains of the Ka'ba and sought help from Allah, saying: "O Allah, give victory to the mightier of the two armies, the more honourable of the two parties, and the better of the two tribes!" So Allah said: ﴿If you seek a decision, then the decision has indeed come to you﴾, meaning: He granted what you said, and that is Muhammad ﷺ.

15842. al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj narrated to us, saying: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words: ﴿If you seek a decision, then the decision has indeed come to you﴾, to His words: ﴿and indeed Allah is with the believers﴾, and that was when the polytheists went out to watch their caravan. The people of the caravan, Abu Sufyan and his companions, sent to the polytheists in Mecca asking them for help. Abu Jahl said: "Whichever of us is better in your sight, support him!" That is His words: ﴿If you seek a decision﴾, meaning: if you seek help.

15843. Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words: ﴿If you seek a decision, then the decision has indeed come to you﴾: He said: "If you seek the punishment, then they were punished on the day of Badr." He said: Their seeking was in Mecca, when they said: ﴿O Allah, if this is indeed the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky, or bring us a painful punishment﴾ [Surah al-Anfal: 32]. He said: So the punishment came to them on the day of Badr. And He informed about the day of Uhud: ﴿And if you return, We will return; and your company will avail you nothing, however numerous it is; and indeed Allah is with the believers﴾.

15844. Ibn Wakic narrated to us, saying: Ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from Mutarrif, from Atiyya, who said: Abu Jahl said on the day of Badr: "O Allah, give victory to the most rightly guided of the two parties, the better of the two parties, and the most excellent!" So the verse was revealed: ﴿If you seek a decision, then the decision has indeed come to you﴾.

15845. ... He said: Abd al-A'la narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri: that Abu Jahl was the one who sought a decision on the day of Badr, and said: "O Allah, whichever of us is more wicked and more severed in kinship to his relative, then destroy him today!" So Allah revealed: ﴿If you seek a decision, then the decision has indeed come to you﴾.

15846. ... He said: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from al-Zuhri, from Abd Allah ibn Tha'laba ibn Su'ayr: that Abu Jahl said on the day of Badr: "O Allah, sever us from the one who is more severed in kinship to him, and bring what we do not know, then destroy him this morning!" And that was his seeking, so it was revealed: ﴿If you seek a decision, then the decision has indeed come to you﴾, the verse. [[The report 15846: see the takhrij of report number 15839 and the two following reports.]]

15847. ... He said: Yahya ibn Adam narrated to us, from Ibrahim ibn Sa'd, from Salih ibn Kaysan, from al-Zuhri, from Abd Allah ibn Tha'laba ibn Su'ayr, who said: The one who sought a decision on the day of Badr was Abu Jahl, who said: "O Allah, sever us for the one who is more severed in kinship, and bring what we do not know, then destroy him this morning!" So Allah revealed: ﴿If you seek a decision, then the decision has indeed come to you﴾. [[The report 15847: see the takhrij of the preceding reports and the one that follows it.]]

15848. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: Muhammad ibn Muslim al-Zuhri narrated to me, from Abd Allah ibn Tha'laba ibn Su'ayr, an ally of Banu Zuhra, who said: When the people met and drew near to one another, Abu Jahl said: "O Allah, sever us for the one who is more severed in kinship, and bring what we do not know, then destroy him this morning!" He was the one who sought a decision against himself. [[The words "against himself" are not in Ibn Hisham's Sira 2: 280. See the takhrij of the report below.]] Ibn Ishaq said: Allah said: ﴿If you seek a decision, then the decision has indeed come to you﴾, in response to the saying of Abu Jahl: "O Allah, sever us for the one who is more severed in kinship, and bring what we do not know, then destroy him this morning!" He said: "The seeking": the fairness in supplication. [[The report 15848: it consists of two reports. The first, up to the words "the one who sought a decision against himself," was narrated by Ibn Hisham in his Sira 2: 280, and the rest of the report was narrated in his Sira 2: 324, and it is a follower of report 15830.

See the takhrij of report number 15839.]]

15849. al-Harith narrated to me, saying: Abd al-Aziz narrated to us, saying: Abu Ma'shar narrated to us, from Yazid ibn Ruman and others: Abu Jahl said on the day of Badr: "O Allah, give victory to the more beloved of the two religions to You: our ancient religion, or their new religion!" So Allah revealed: ﴿If you seek a decision, then the decision has indeed come to you﴾, to His words: ﴿and indeed Allah is with the believers﴾.

* *

As for His words: ﴿And if you desist, it is better for you﴾, He says: "And if you desist," O assembly of Quraysh, and the company of unbelievers, from disbelief in Allah and His Messenger, and from fighting His Prophet ﷺ and the believers in him, "it is better for you," in your worldly life and your Hereafter. [[See the explanation of "al-intihaa" (desisting) earlier: 20: 566, note 1, and the references there.]] ﴿And if you return, We will return﴾, He says: And if you return to waging war against him and fighting him and fighting his followers the believers, "We will return," meaning: with the like of the encounter which befell you on the day of Badr.

* *

As for His words: ﴿Your company will avail you nothing, however numerous it is﴾, He says: And if you return, We will return to your destruction at the hands of My friends and your defeat, and your company will avail you nothing when I return to kill you at their hands, take you captive, and defeat you [[See the explanation of "aghna" (to avail) earlier: 7: 133.]] "however numerous it is," meaning: their host and their group of polytheists, [[See the explanation of "fi'a" (company) earlier: p. 435, note 3, and the references there.]] just as they did not avail them on the day of Badr despite their great number and the small number of the believers = ﴿and indeed Allah is with the believers﴾, He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Indeed Allah is with those of His servants who believe in Him against those among them who disbelieve in Him, to give them victory over them, or to make them prevail, as He made them prevail over the polytheists on the day of Badr. [[See the explanation of "ma'a" (with) earlier: p. 428, note 2, and the references there.]]

* *

The people of ta'wil said the same as what we have said about this.

Those who said so:

15850. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq regarding His words: ﴿And if you desist, it is better for you﴾, he said: He says to Quraysh: "And if you return, We will return," to the like of the encounter which struck you on the day of Badr. ﴿And your company will avail you nothing, however numerous it is; and indeed Allah is with the believers﴾, meaning: even if your number increases among yourselves, it will avail you nothing. And I am with the believers, giving them victory over those who oppose them. [[The report 15850: Ibn Hisham's Sira 2: 324, a follower of the preceding report 15848, in its second part.

In the printed edition it read "indeed Allah is with the believers, He gives them victory," and in the manuscript likewise except that it has "I give them victory." I have established the text of Ibn Hisham's Sira, and what is in the manuscript is partly a scribal error and haste.]]

* *

It has been said that the meaning of His words: ﴿And if you return, We will return﴾ is: "And if you return to seeking a decision, We will return with the victory of Muhammad ﷺ."

But this view has no meaning, because Allah had already guaranteed to His Prophet, peace be upon him, when He permitted him to fight his enemies, the manifestation of his religion and the elevation of his word, before Abu Jahl and his party sought a decision. So there is no basis for saying, when the matter is as it is: "If you desist from seeking a decision, it is better for you, and if you return, We will return," because Allah had already promised His Prophet ﷺ victory by His words: ﴿Permission is given to those who are fought against, because they have been wronged; and indeed Allah is able to give them victory﴾ [Surah al-Hajj: 39], whether the polytheists sought a decision or did not seek it.

The people who said so:

15851. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿And if you return, We will return﴾, if you seek a decision a second time, We will give victory to Muhammad ﷺ = ﴿and your company will avail you nothing, however numerous it is; and indeed Allah is with the believers﴾, Muhammad and his companions.

* *

The readers differed regarding the reading of His words: ﴿and indeed Allah is with the believers﴾.

The majority of the readers of Medina read it with a fatha (inna, "indeed," with an opened alif), meaning: "And your company will avail you nothing, however numerous it is, and indeed Allah is surely with the believers" [[In the printed edition: "with the believers" without the lam, and I have established what is in the manuscript, though I have doubts about it.]]. They conjoined with "anna" (that) to the position of "wa law kathurat" (even if they were numerous), as if he said: "Because of its numerousness, and because Allah is with the believers." The position of "anna" in this case would then be in the accusative according to this view. [[See the Ma'ani al-Qur'an of al-Farra' 1: 407.]]

* *

Some of the grammarians claimed that its fatha, when it is opened, is based on: ﴿And that Allah is weakening the scheme of the unbelievers﴾ and ﴿and that Allah is with the believers﴾, conjoining the latter to the former.

* *

The majority of the readers of Kufa and Basra read it: "wa inna Allah" with a kasra on the alif, as a beginning (a new sentence), and they reasoned that it is in the reading of Abd Allah (ibn Mas'ud): "wa inna Allaha la-ma'a al-mu'minin."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The more correct of the two readings is the reading of the one who read "inna" with a kasra as a beginning, because the preceding report had concluded in a way that makes the statement "and indeed Allah is with the believers" fitting. [[In the printed edition: "what his words suggest" ("ma yaqdi qawluhu"), and the correct reading is what is in the manuscript.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 8, verse 20:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿O you who believe, obey Allah and His Messenger, and do not turn away from him while you hear﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, exalted is His remembrance, says: O you who have affirmed Allah and His Messenger, ﴿obey Allah and His Messenger﴾ in what He commands you and what He forbids you; ﴿and do not turn away from him﴾, meaning: do not turn your backs on the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), opposing his command and his prohibition [[See the explanation of "al-tawalli" (turning away) in what has passed from the lexicon of Faris, under (wly).]]. ﴿While you hear﴾ his command to you and his prohibition, and you are believers in it, as follows:

15852. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, who said: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, regarding ﴿O you who believe, obey Allah and His Messenger, and do not turn away while you hear﴾: that is, do not oppose his command, while you hear his words and claim that you are from him. [[The report: 15852 - Sirat Ibn Hisham 2: 324, and it follows the previous report no. 15850.

In the printed edition here it read "and you claim that you are believers," and I have adopted what is in the manuscript, which agrees with what is in Sirat Ibn Hisham.]]

**The explanation of His words: ﴿And do not be like those who said, "We hear," while they do not hear﴾ (8:21)**

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says to the believers in God and His Messenger among the companions of the Prophet (ﷺ): Do not be, O believers, in opposing the Messenger of God (ﷺ), like the polytheists who, when the Book of God was recited to them, said, "We have heard," with our ears, ﴿while they do not hear﴾, meaning: they do not take heed of what they hear with their ears, nor do they benefit from it, because of their turning away from it and their failure to let it settle in their hearts and to contemplate it. God made them, since they did not benefit from the admonitions of the Qur'an even though they had heard them with their ears, [[In the printed edition: "So God made them, since they did not benefit," and I have kept what is in the manuscript.]] equal to one who had not heard them. He, may His praise be exalted, says to the companions of the Messenger of God (ﷺ): Do not be, you, in turning away from the command of the Messenger and in failing to submit to it, while you hear it with your ears, like these polytheists who hear the admonitions of the Book of God with their ears and say, "We have heard," while they are turned away from listening to them and from being admonished by them, like one who does not hear them. [[In the manuscript: "and they [turn away] from its use and being admonished by it," and the correct reading is what is in the printed edition; it is an omission by the copyist. The printed edition had: "like one who did not hear them," and I have kept what is in the manuscript.]]

* *

Ibn Ishaq used to say about this:

1585З- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Ishaq, regarding ﴿And do not be like those who said, "We hear," while they do not hear﴾, that is: like the hypocrites who show obedience to Him and conceal disobedience. [[The report 15853 is in Sirat Ibn Hisham 2:324, and it follows the earlier report No. 15852.]]

1585four- Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the words of God ﴿and they do not hear﴾, he said: "Disobedient."

1585five- Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: 'Abd Allah related to us, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: What Ibn Ishaq said has a basis, but His words ﴿And do not be like those who said, "We hear," while they do not hear﴾ come within the narrative about the polytheists, and it is followed by the report about them in condemnation, which is His words: ﴿Indeed, the worst of living beings in God's sight are the deaf and the dumb who do not reason﴾ (8:22). So it is more fitting that what lies between them be a report about them than a report about others.

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Indeed, the worst of living creatures in the sight of Allah are the deaf and the dumb who do not reason﴾ (22).

Abu Ja'far said: He, exalted is His mention, says: Indeed, the worst of what crawls upon the earth of Allah's creation in the sight of Allah [[See the explanation of "dabbah" (living creature/beast) above: 3:275 \ 11:344.]] are those who are deaf to the truth so that they do not hear it, [[See the explanation of "ṣamm" (deafness): 1:328-331 \ 3:315 \ 10:478 \ 11:350.]] so that they would not take heed from it and be admonished by it, and who recoil from it if they speak of it. [[See the explanation of "bukm" (dumbness) above: 1:328-331 \ 3:315 \ 11:350.]] They are those who do not understand from Allah His command and His prohibition, so that they would employ these with their bodies.

* *

In accordance with what we have said regarding this, the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have spoken.

Mention of those who said that:

15856. Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, the worst of living creatures in the sight of Allah﴾, he said: "The living creatures" are the creation.

15857. al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, saying: Ibn Jurayj said, on the authority of Ikrimah, who said: "They used to say: 'We are deaf and dumb to what Muhammad calls to; we do not hear it from him, and we do not respond to it with affirmation!'" So they were all killed at Uhud, and they were the standard-bearers.

15858. Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Najih, on the authority of Mujahid: "The deaf, the dumb, who do not reason," he said: Those who do not follow the truth.

15859. Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, the worst of living creatures in the sight of Allah are the deaf and the dumb who do not reason﴾, "and they are not deaf or dumb in the world, but rather the hearts are deaf, dumb and blind!" And he recited: ﴿For indeed, it is not the eyes that are blinded, but it is the hearts within the breasts that are blinded﴾ [Surah al-Hajj: 46].

* *

And there was disagreement regarding who is meant by this verse.

Some of them said: It refers to a group of the polytheists.

Mention of those who said that:

15860. al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Najih, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: Ibn Abbas said: "The deaf, the dumb who do not reason" are a group from Banu Abd al-Dar, who do not follow the truth.

15861. ... [narrated] to us, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abd Allah narrated to us, on the authority of Warqa', on the authority of Ibn Abi Najih, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿The deaf, the dumb who do not reason﴾, he said: They do not follow the truth. He said: Ibn Abbas said: They are a group from Banu Abd al-Dar.

15861. al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, similarly.

* *

Others said: It refers to the hypocrites.

Mention of those who said that:

15862. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq: ﴿Indeed, the worst of living creatures in the sight of Allah are the deaf and the dumb who do not reason﴾ [i.e., the hypocrites whom I forbade you to be like, dumb regarding good, deaf regarding truth, who do not reason], who do not know what retribution and consequence they will face for that. [[The report: 15862 - Sirat Ibn Hisham 2:324, and it follows the previous report No. 15853. What is between the parentheses has undoubtedly been dropped by the copyist of the manuscript, because its omission makes the report not match the heading, since there is then no mention of the hypocrites in it. Moreover, Abu Ja'far transmits Ibn Ishaq's exegesis from his Sirah verbatim in all that has passed, so there is no sense in abridging it here in a way that is damaging. Thus it is established that this is from the copyist, so I added it from the Sirah.

As for the sentence the copyist recorded outside the parentheses, it was in the manuscript: "... min al-ni'mah wa al-sa'ah" — the first is an error, and its correct form is what has been established.

The editor came and did not understand the meaning of the speech, so he made it thus: "... min al-ni'mah wa al-si'ah," which became a confusion with no good in it and no meaning. I returned it to correctness, praise be to Allah.

And "al-tibā'ah" (with a kasrah on the ta'), like "al-tabi'ah" (with a fatha on the ta' and kasrah on the ba'): that which contains sin which its possessor is followed for. It is said: "He has no tabi'ah or tibā'ah from Allah in this," meaning: a demand for which its sin is sought.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of the two opinions regarding this, is the opinion of the one who holds the view of Ibn Abbas: that this verse refers to the polytheists of Quraysh, because it is within the context of the report about them.

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 8, verse 23:**

The discussion of the interpretation (*ta'wil*, the explanation of the meaning) of His saying: ﴿And if Allah had known any good in them, He would have made them hear. And if He had made them hear, they would have turned away while they were refusing﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The people of *ta'wil* (exegesis, the explanation of the Qur'an's meaning) differed concerning who is meant by this verse, and concerning its meaning.

Some of them said: It refers to the polytheists. And they said: Its meaning is that if Allah had granted them understanding of what He sent down to His Prophet (ﷺ), they still would not have believed in it, because Allah had decreed against them that they would not believe.

Mention of those who said that:

15863. Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, saying: Ibn Jurayj said, concerning His saying: ﴿And if Allah had known any good in them, He would have made them hear. And if He had made them hear﴾: They would have said: ﴿Bring a Qur'an other than this﴾ [Surah Yunus: 15], and they would have said: ﴿Why did you not choose it?﴾ [Surah al-A'raf: 203]. And if he had brought them a Qur'an other than it, ﴿they would have turned away while they were refusing﴾.

15864. Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying: ﴿And if He had made them hear, they would have turned away while they were refusing﴾: He said: If He had made them hear after He knew that there was no good in them, they would not have benefited from it, and they would have turned away while they were refusing.

15865. And he narrated it to me another time, saying: "If Allah had known any good in them, He would have made them hear. And if He had made them hear," after He knew that there was no good in them, it would not have benefited them, since His knowledge had already passed that they would not benefit from it.

* *

Others said: Rather, it refers to the hypocrites. They said: Its meaning is as follows:

15866. Ibn Humayd narrated it to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: ﴿And if Allah had known any good in them, He would have made them hear﴾, meaning: He would have carried out for them the words they uttered with their tongues. [[In the printed edition: "the words they uttered" (alladhi qalahu); I have adopted what is in the manuscript, matching what is in the Sirah.]] But their hearts opposed that from them. And if they had gone out with you, ﴿they would have turned away while they were refusing﴾; they would not have fulfilled anything of what they had set out for. [[The following sentence appeared in the manuscript and the printed edition as: "fa-awfu lakum bi-sharr mimma kharaju 'alayhi" [“they fulfilled for you with evil of what they had gone out upon”], which has no meaning. Its correct form is what I have adopted from the Sirah of Ibn Hisham.]] [[The report 15866: Sirah of Ibn Hisham 2:324, and it follows the earlier report no. 15862.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct interpretation of this in my view is what Ibn Jurayj and Ibn Zayd said, for the reason we mentioned earlier, and because that is not a characteristic of the hypocrites. [[See p. 461.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The interpretation of the verse, then, is: If Allah had known any good in these speakers, He would have made them hear the admonitions and lessons of the Qur'an, until they understood from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, His proofs from Him. But He knew that there was no good in them, and that they are among those for whom wretchedness has been decreed, so they do not believe. And if He had caused them to understand that so that they would know and comprehend, they would have turned away from Allah and His Messenger, [[See the explanation of "tawalli" (turning away) earlier, vol. 12, p. 571, note 1, and the references there.]] while they were refusing to believe in what the admonitions, lessons, and proofs of Allah had shown them to be sound, [[In the printed edition: "...showed them the truth (haqiqah)"; in the manuscript: "...showed them His proof (hujjatihi)," and this is the correct reading.]] opposing the truth after knowing it. [[See the explanation of "i'rad" (refusal) earlier, p. 332, note 1, and the references there.]]

**The interpretation of His saying: ﴿O you who believe, respond to Allah and to the Messenger when he calls you to that which gives you life﴾**

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The people of ta'wil (interpretation; the scholars of tafsir) differed over the meaning of His saying: ﴿when he calls you to that which gives you life﴾.

Some of them said: its meaning is: respond to Allah and to the Messenger when he calls you to faith (iman).

Those who said this:

15867. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿O you who believe, respond to Allah and to the Messenger when he calls you to that which gives you life﴾, he said: As for "that which gives you life," [In the printed edition and the manuscript: "amma yuhyikum," with "ma" omitted; the correct reading is to keep it.] it is Islam; He gave them life after their death, after their disbelief.

* *

Others said: it means the truth (al-haqq).

Those who said this:

15868. Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the saying of Allah: ﴿li-ma yuhyikum﴾, he said: the truth.

15869. al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

15870. al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: 'Abd Allah narrated to us, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿when he calls you to that which gives you life﴾, he said: the truth.

15871. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, saying: 'Anbasa narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿respond to Allah and to the Messenger when he calls you to that which gives you life﴾, he said: to the truth.

* *

Others said: its meaning is: when he calls you to what is in the Qur'an.

Those who said this:

15872. Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada regarding His saying: ﴿O you who believe, respond to Allah and to the Messenger when he calls you to that which gives you life﴾, he said: it is this Qur'an, in which is life, trust, deliverance, and protection in this world and the Hereafter. [In the printed edition: "al-hayat wal-iffa" (life and chastity); in the manuscript, as I have restored it, the letter "tha" is undotted, and then its editor also dropped "wal-najat" (and deliverance) from the text, which is among the worst and most ugly of distortions.]

* *

Others said: its meaning is: when he calls you to war and to jihad against the enemy.

Those who said this:

15873. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: ﴿O you who believe, respond to Allah and to the Messenger when he calls you to that which gives you life﴾, i.e., to the war by which Allah has honored you after humiliation, strengthened you after weakness, and protected you by it from your enemy after they had subdued you. [The report 15873 is in Ibn Hisham's Sirah 2:324, and it follows the earlier report numbered 15866.]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of these opinions, in my view, is the saying of the one who said: its meaning is: respond to Allah and to the Messenger with obedience, when the Messenger calls you to that which gives you life of truth. For if this is its meaning, it includes the command to respond to them for fighting the enemy and jihad, and responding when he calls you to the judgment of the Qur'an; and in responding to all of that is the life of the one who responds. As for in this world, it is the enduring of a good remembrance, [In the printed edition and manuscript: "fayuqal al-dhikr al-jamil" (so it is said of the good remembrance), which has no sense; the correct reading is what I have written.] and this is a life for him in it. And as for the Hereafter, it is the eternal life in the Gardens and abiding therein. [See the explanation of "al-istijaba" (responding) earlier, p. 409, note 1, and the references there.]

* *

As for the saying of those who said its meaning is Islam, it is a saying with no sense, because Allah has described them as believers by His saying: ﴿O you who believe, respond to Allah and to the Messenger when he calls you to that which gives you life﴾. So there is no basis for saying to a believer: respond to Allah and to the Messenger when he calls to Islam and faith. [In the printed edition: "idha da'aka" (when he calls you, singular); I have kept what is in the manuscript.]

* *

Furthermore, among what supports this:

15874. Ahmad ibn al-Miqdam al-'Ijli narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Zuray' narrated to us, saying: Rawh ibn al-Qasim narrated to us, from al-'Ala' ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from his father, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) passed by Ubayy while he was praying, and called him: "O Ubayy!" Ubayy turned to him but did not answer. Then Ubayy shortened the prayer, then turned to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "Peace be upon you, O Messenger of Allah!" He said: "And upon you. What prevented you, when I called you, from answering me?" He said: "O Messenger of Allah, I was praying!" He said: "Did you not find in what was revealed to me: ﴿respond to Allah and to the Messenger when he calls you to that which gives you life﴾?" He said: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah! I will not do it again." [Report 15874: it will come by another route in the following report. Ahmad ibn al-Miqdam ibn Sulayman al-'Ijli, a shaykh of al-Tabari, trustworthy, passed at 12861. Yazid ibn Zuray' al-'Aysh, trustworthy and a memorizer, has passed many times, at 1769, 2533, 5429, 5438, and elsewhere. Rawh ibn al-Qasim al-Tamimi al-Tabari, trustworthy, passed at 6613. Al-'Ala' ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ya'qub, mawla al-Hurqa, a trustworthy Successor, passed at 221 and 14210. His father, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ya'qub, mawla al-Hurqa, a trustworthy Successor, passed at 14210. This report was narrated by Ahmad in his Musnad 2:412–413, through 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ibrahim, from al-'Ala' ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from his father, in similar form but longer. It was also narrated by al-Tirmidhi in "Fada'il al-Qur'an, chapter on what has come concerning the virtue of al-Fatiha," through 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Muhammad al-Darawardi, from al-'Ala', in similar form, longer, and he said: "This is a hasan sahih hadith." And on this there is a report from Anas ibn Malik. Ibn Kathir took it up in his tafsir 1:22–23. See also al-Bukhari's hadith (al-Fath 8:119, 231), which is the hadith of Abu Sa'id ibn al-Mu'alla, with a similar account from Ubayy ibn Ka'b; the Hafiz Ibn Hajar discussed it there at length and took up the hadith of Ubayy ibn Ka'b. See also the Muwatta', p. 83, the report of Malik from al-'Ala' ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ya'qub, that Abu Sa'id, mawla 'Amir ibn Kurayz, informed him that "the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called Ubayy ibn Ka'b while he was praying..." in a different wording, and what Hafiz Ibn Hajar and Ibn Kathir said about it in their tafsir, where we have indicated its place.]

15875. Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Khalid ibn Makhlad narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ja'far, from al-'Ala', from his father, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) passed by Ubayy while he was standing and praying, and he called out to him [but he did not answer him, then he came], [What is between the brackets is not in the manuscript; the editor of the printed edition added it, and I do not know from where. There is undoubtedly a gap in the report, but I have not found the report in this exact wording.] and said: "O Ubayy, what prevented you from answering me when I called you? Does Allah not say: ﴿O you who believe, respond to Allah and to the Messenger when he calls you to that which gives you life﴾?" Ubayy said: "Certainly, O Messenger of Allah, you will never call me but I will answer, even if I am praying!" [Report 15875 is another chain for the previous report, which I have already traced there. Khalid ibn Makhlad al-Qatwani, trustworthy, one of al-Bukhari's shaykhs, from whom Muslim also narrated, has passed many times, at 2206, 4577, 8166, 8397, and elsewhere. Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn Abi Kathir al-Zuraqi, a known trustworthy narrator, passed at 2206 and 8397.]

* *

This clarifies that those intended by the verse are those whom the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) calls to that in which their life lies, by their responding to him with the truth after their Islam, because Ubayy, without doubt, was a Muslim at the time the Prophet (ﷺ) said to him what we mentioned in these two reports.

* *

**The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And know that Allah intervenes between a man and his heart, and that to Him you will be gathered﴾ (24)**

Abu Ja'far said: The people of ta'wil differed over the interpretation of this.

Some of them said: its meaning is: He intervenes between the disbeliever and faith, and between the believer and disbelief.

Those who said this:

15876. Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd Allah al-Razi, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr regarding ﴿He intervenes between a man and his heart﴾, he said: He intervenes between the disbeliever and believing, and between the believer and disbelieving. [Report 15876: "'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd Allah al-Razi," Abu Ja'far al-Razi, judge of al-Rayy, trustworthy, with no fault. He is listed in al-Tahdhib and in Ibn Abi Hatim 2/2/92. He is not to be confused with "Abu Ja'far al-Razi al-Tamimi," who is 'Isa ibn Mahan.]

15877. Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, and Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, both saying: Sufyan narrated to us, and al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: al-Thawri narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd Allah al-Razi, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, in similar wording.

15878. Abu Za'ida Zakariyya ibn Abi Za'ida narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-A'mash, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd Allah, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, the same.

15879. Abu al-Sa'ib and Ibn Waki' narrated to me, both saying: Abu Mu'awiya narrated to us, from al-Minhal, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr regarding ﴿He intervenes between a man and his heart﴾, he said: He intervenes between the believer and disbelief, and between the disbeliever and faith.

15880. Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd Allah al-Razi, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿He intervenes between a man and his heart﴾, He intervenes between the disbeliever and faith and the obedience of Allah.

15881. ... narrated to us, saying: Hafs narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿He intervenes between a man and his heart﴾, he said: He intervenes between the believer and disbelief, and between the disbeliever and faith.

15882. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, saying: 'Ubayd ibn Sulayman, and 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Abi Rawwad, narrated to us, from al-Dahhak regarding His saying: (He intervenes between a man and his heart), he said: He intervenes between the disbeliever and his obedience, and between the believer and his disobedience.

15883. Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Abu Usama narrated to us, from Abu Rawq, from al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim, similarly.

15884. ... narrated to us, saying: al-Muharibi narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, who said: He intervenes between a man and that he should disbelieve, [So it is in the manuscript and the printed edition: "between a man"; had I supposed it to be "between the believer," what preceded would support it.] and between the disbeliever and that he should believe.

15885. al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Abi Rawwad narrated to us, from al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim regarding ﴿He intervenes between a man and his heart﴾, he said: He intervenes between the disbeliever and the obedience of Allah, and between the believer and the disobedience of Allah.

15886. Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Rawwad narrated to us, from al-Dahhak, similarly.

15887. And it was narrated to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, who said: I heard al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim say, and he mentioned something similar.

15888. al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: al-Hajjaj ibn Minhal narrated to us, saying: al-Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, saying: I heard 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Abi Rawwad relate, from al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim, regarding His saying: ﴿He intervenes between a man and his heart﴾, he said: He intervenes between the believer and his disobedience.

15889. al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿And know that Allah intervenes between a man and his heart﴾, meaning: He intervenes between the believer and disbelief, and intervenes between the disbeliever and faith.

15890. Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿And know that Allah intervenes between a man and his heart﴾, meaning: He intervenes between the disbeliever and his obedience, and intervenes between the believer and his disobedience.

15891. Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: al-Muharibi narrated to us, from Layth, from Mujahid: ﴿He intervenes between a man and his heart﴾, he said: He intervenes between the believer and disbelief, and between the disbeliever and faith.

15892. ... said: My father narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Rawwad, from al-Dahhak: ﴿He intervenes between a man and his heart﴾, meaning: He intervenes between the disbeliever and his obedience, and between the believer and his disobedience.

15893. ... said: Ishaq ibn Isma'il narrated to us, from Ya'qub al-Qummi, from Ja'far, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: ﴿He intervenes between a man and his heart﴾, he intervenes between the believer and sins, and between the disbeliever and faith.

15894. ... said: 'Ubayda narrated to us, from Isma'il, from Abu Salih: ﴿He intervenes between a man and his heart﴾, he said: He intervenes between him and sins.

* *

Others said: rather, the meaning of that is: He intervenes between a man and his intellect, so he does not know what he does.

Those who said this:

15895. 'Ubayd Allah ibn Muhammad al-Firyabi narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Majid narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid regarding His saying: ﴿He intervenes between a man and his heart﴾, he said: He intervenes between a man and his intellect.

15896. Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿He intervenes between a man and his heart﴾, until He leaves him not understanding.

15897. al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

15898. al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: 'Abd Allah narrated to us, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding His saying: ﴿He intervenes between a man and his heart﴾, he said: It is like His saying "hala" (he intervened), until He leaves him not understanding. [In the printed edition: "he said: it is 'yahulu bayna al-mar' wa-qalbihi hatta yatrukahu la ya'qilu'" (he intervenes between a man and his heart until He leaves him not understanding), which differs entirely from the manuscript, because the editor did not understand it. This is among the worst and most ugly of alterations and farthest from trustworthiness. He meant that "yahulu" is the present tense of the past "hala," and that is why he said "until He leaves him not understanding." See how much corruption the editor introduced without scruple!]

15899. Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Ma'qil ibn 'Ubayd Allah narrated to us, from Humayd, from Mujahid: ﴿He intervenes between a man and his heart﴾, he said: If He intervenes between you and your heart, how will you act?

15900. He said: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Sharik narrated to us, from Khasif, from Mujahid: ﴿He intervenes between a man and his heart﴾, he said: He intervenes between the heart of the disbeliever and doing any good.

* *

Others said: its meaning is: He intervenes between a man and his heart, so that he cannot be able to have faith or disbelief except by His permission.

Those who said this:

15901. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿And know that Allah intervenes between a man and his heart﴾, he said: He intervenes between a person and his heart, so he is not able to believe or disbelieve except by His permission.

* *

Others said: the meaning of that is that He is near to his heart, and nothing is hidden from Him of what he reveals or conceals.

Those who said this:

15902. Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, saying: Ma'mar narrated to us, from Qatada regarding His saying: ﴿He intervenes between a man and his heart﴾, he said: It is like His saying: ﴿We are nearer to him than his jugular vein﴾ [Surah Qaf 50:16].

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of these sayings, in my view, is that it should be said: this is a report from Allah, mighty and majestic is He, that He is more in control of the hearts of His servants than they are themselves, and that He intervenes between them and their hearts whenever He wills, so that no possessor of a heart can perceive by it anything of faith or disbelief, nor retain anything, nor understand, except by His permission and will. For "intervention between one thing and another" is nothing but a barrier between them; and when He, great is His praise, places a barrier between a servant and his heart concerning something that he might perceive or understand, the servant has no way to perceive what Allah has prevented his heart from perceiving. [See the explanation of "al-mar'" (the man) above, 2:446 / 9:430.]

And if this is its meaning, it includes the saying of the one who said: "He intervenes between the believer and disbelief, and between the disbeliever and faith," and the saying of the one who said: "He intervenes between him and his intellect," and the saying of the one who said: "He intervenes between him and his heart, so that he cannot believe or disbelieve except by His permission." For when Allah, mighty and majestic is He, intervenes between a servant and his heart, the servant does not understand with the heart from which he has been barred what has been prevented from being perceived by it, as I have explained.

However, it should be said that by His saying: ﴿And know that Allah intervenes between a man and his heart﴾, Allah has given a general report that He intervenes between the servant and his heart, and He did not specify any of the meanings we have mentioned over others. The utterance admits all of these meanings, so the report is general until something specifies it that must be accepted.

* *

And as for His saying ﴿And that to Him you will be gathered﴾, its meaning is: Know also, O believers, along with knowing that Allah comes between a person and his heart, that Allah, who has power over your hearts and is more in control of them than you are, is the One to whom your return and resting-place are on the Day of Resurrection. [See the explanation of "al-hashr" (gathering) above, p. 23, note 1, and the references there.] So He will fully repay you for your deeds: the one of you who does good will be repaid with His goodness, and the one who does evil with his evil. So fear Him and be watchful of Him in what He and His Messenger have commanded you and forbidden you, lest you neglect it, and lest you fail to respond to His Messenger when he calls you to that which gives you life, thereby incurring His wrath and deserving His painful punishment when you are gathered to Him.

The interpretation (ta'wil) of His words: ﴿And beware of a trial which will not afflict only those among you who have done wrong; and know that Allah is severe in punishment.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says to the believers in Him and His Messenger: "Beware" (ittaqu), O believers, "of a trial" (fitnah), meaning a test from Allah by which He tests you and an affliction by which He afflicts you [[See the explanation of "fitnah" above, p. 151, note 1, and the references there.]], "which will not afflict" (la tusibanna), this trial which He has warned you of, "those who have done wrong" (alladhina zalamu), meaning those who did what was not theirs to do, whether by committing a crime they incurred or by committing sins between themselves and Allah which they undertook. He, may His praise be exalted, warns them that they should not commit disobedience against Him or commit a sin for which they would deserve punishment from Him. [[See the explanation of "khusus" (specific) above, 2:471 and 6:517.]]

* *

It has been said: This verse was revealed concerning a group of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and they are the ones meant by it.

Those who said this:

15903. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, who said: Muhammad ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, who said: al-Hasan ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, who said: Dawud ibn Abi Hind narrated to us, from al-Hasan, regarding His words: ﴿And beware of a trial which will not afflict only those among you who have done wrong﴾, he said: It was revealed concerning Ali, Uthman, Talhah and al-Zubayr, may Allah have mercy on them.

15904. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, who said: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, regarding ﴿And beware of a trial which will not afflict only those among you who have done wrong﴾. Qatadah said: al-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam said: It was revealed, and we did not think any of us would be struck by it. Then we were singled out in being struck by it specifically. [[In the printed edition: "thumma khassatna fi isabatina khassah" (then it singled us out in our being afflicted specifically). I have adopted what is in the manuscript, where it is unpointed, and I thought the correct pointing is what I have adopted. The meaning is: they remained after those who had passed away, so it was specifically concerning their affliction.]]

15905. al-Muthanna narrated to me, who said: Zayd ibn Awf Abu Rabi'ah narrated to us, who said: Hammad narrated to us, from Humayd, from al-Hasan, that al-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam said: This verse was revealed: ﴿And beware of a trial which will not afflict only those among you who have done wrong﴾, and we did not think we were its people, yet we were the ones meant by it. [[Narration 15905: Zayd ibn Awf al-Qat'i, Abu Rabi'ah, whose epithet is "Fahd," is spoken of (criticized), weak. Previously mentioned under nos. 5623, 14215, 14218.]]

15906. ... who said: Qabisah narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-Salt ibn Dinar, from Ibn Sahban, who said: I heard al-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam say: I recited this verse for a time, and I did not think we were its people, then we turned out to be the ones meant by it: ﴿And beware of a trial which will not afflict only those among you who have done wrong; and know that Allah is severe in punishment.﴾ [[Narration 15906: al-Salt ibn Dinar al-Azdi, Abu Shu'ayb, "al-Majnun" (the insane). Abandoned; his narrations are not to be relied upon. He is mentioned in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 2/2/305, Ibn Abi Hatim 2/1/437, and Mizan al-I'tidal 1:468. "Ibn Sahban" is 'Uqbah ibn Sahban al-Huddani al-Azdi, a trustworthy Successor (tabi'i), mentioned in al-Tahdhib and Ibn Abi Hatim 1/13/312. I did not find that they mentioned that he narrated from al-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam, but he narrated from Uthman, 'Iyad ibn Himar, Abdullah ibn Mughaffal, Abu Bakrah al-Thaqafi and A'ishah.]]

15907. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, who said: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, who said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿And beware of a trial which will not afflict only those among you who have done wrong﴾, he said: This was revealed concerning the people of Badr specifically, and it afflicted them on the Day of the Camel, so they fought one another.

15908. Ibn Wakic narrated to us, who said: My father narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Khalid, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿And beware of a trial which will not afflict only those among you who have done wrong; and know that Allah is severe in punishment.﴾ He said: The companions of the Camel.
