15909. al-Muthanna narrated to me, who said: Abu Salih narrated to us, who said: Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿And beware of a trial which will not afflict only those among you who have done wrong﴾, he said: Allah commanded the believers not to tolerate evil among them, lest Allah encompass them all with punishment.

15910. ... who said: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, who said: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿And beware of a trial which will not afflict only those among you who have done wrong﴾, he said: It is also for you.

15911. Yunus narrated to me, who said: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿And beware of a trial which will not afflict only those among you who have done wrong﴾: "The trial" (al-fitnah) is misguidance.

15912. Ibn Wakic narrated to us, who said: My father narrated to us, from al-Mas'udi, from al-Qasim, who said: Abdullah said: There is none among you but he is enveloped in a trial. Allah says: ﴿Your wealth and your children are only a trial﴾ [Surah al-Anfal: 28]. So let him seek refuge in Allah from misleading trials. [[Narration 15912: See the following narration no. 15934, whose text is: "So whoever among you seeks refuge, let him seek refuge..." and this seems to be the correct version.]]

15913. al-Harith narrated to me, who said: Abd al-Aziz narrated to us, who said: Mubarak ibn Fudalah narrated to us, from al-Hasan, who said: al-Zubayr said: We were warned by it, meaning His words: ﴿And beware of a trial which will not afflict only those among you who have done wrong﴾.

* *

The grammarians differed regarding its interpretation.

One of the grammarians of Basra said: In ﴿Beware of a trial which will not afflict those who have done wrong﴾, His words "la tusibanna" (will not afflict) are not an answer (jawab), but a prohibition following a command. Had it been an answer, the "nun" (of emphasis) would not have been added.

* *

One of the grammarians of Kufa said regarding ﴿And beware of a trial which will not afflict those who have done wrong﴾: He commanded them, then forbade them. There is in it an element of the conditional (jaza'), even though it is a prohibition. He said: Similar to it is His words: ﴿O ants, enter your dwellings, lest Suleiman and his soldiers crush you﴾ [Surah al-Naml: 18], He commanded them, then forbade them, and in it is the sense of the conditional. [[This is the view of al-Farra' in Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1:407.]]

It seems that the meaning of the statement according to him is: Beware of a trial; if you do not guard against it, it will afflict you.

* *

As for His words ﴿And know that Allah is severe in punishment﴾, it is a warning from Allah and a threat to whoever falls into the trial He warned them of by His words ﴿And beware of a trial﴾. He says: Know, O believers, that your Lord is severe in His punishment for whoever is tried through wronging himself, opposes His command, and thereby sins. [[See the explanation of "severe in punishment" in the earlier linguistic indices under (sh-d-d) and ('-q-b).]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 8, verse 26:

The explanation of His saying: ﴿And remember when you were few and oppressed in the land, fearing that the people would snatch you away, but He sheltered you and strengthened you with His help and provided for you of the good things, that you may be grateful﴾.

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: This is a reminder from Allah, mighty and majestic, to the companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and sincere counsel. He means: Obey Allah and His Messenger, O believers, and respond to him when he calls you to that which gives you life, and do not oppose his command even if he commands you with that which involves hardship and difficulty, for Allah will make it easy for you through your obedience to Him, and will hasten for you from Him what you love, just as He did with you when you believed in Him and followed him while you were few, and the disbelievers oppressed you and tried to turn you away from your religion, [See the explanation of "few" (al-qalil) above: 1:329; 8:439, 577; 9:331.] and would harm you in your persons and honour, [See the explanation of "oppressed" (al-mustad'af) above: 12:542; 13:76, 131.] fearing from them that they would snatch you away, kill you and wipe out all of you [See the explanation of "snatch" (al-khatf) above: 1:357.] = ﴿and sheltered you﴾, he says: so He made for you a refuge to which you could retreat from them [See also the explanation of "refuge" (al-ma'wa) above: p. 441, note 3, and the references there.] = ﴿and strengthened you with His help﴾, he says: and He fortified you with His help against them until you killed those of them whom you killed at Badr [See the explanation of "strengthened" (ayyada) above: 2:319, 320; 5:379; 6:242; 11:213, 214.] = ﴿and provided for you of the good things﴾, he says: and He fed you with their spoils, lawful and good [See the explanation of "provision" (al-rizq) above in the lexical indices (r-z-q), and "the good things" (al-tayyibat) above under (t-y-b).] = ﴿that you may be grateful﴾, he says: that you may thank Him for what He has provided you and bestowed upon you of that and of His other blessings upon you. [In the printed edition: "that you (pl.) may be grateful", and in the manuscript: "that you (pl.) may be grateful" [sic]; I preferred what is recorded.]

* *

The commentators differed concerning "the people" whom He meant by His saying: ﴿that the people would snatch you away﴾.

Some of them said: They are the disbelievers of Quraysh.

Those who said this:

15914 – Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ikrimah regarding His saying: ﴿And remember when you were few and oppressed in the land, fearing that the people would snatch you away﴾, he said: He means in Makkah, with the Prophet (ﷺ) and those who followed him from Quraysh, its allies and its clients, before the Hijrah.

15915 – Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Kalbi – or Qatadah, or both [thus in the manuscript and the printed edition: "or both", which is permissible] – regarding ﴿And remember when you were few and oppressed﴾, that it was revealed concerning the day of Badr; they were then fearing that the people would snatch them away, so Allah sheltered them and strengthened them with His help.

15916 – Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, similarly.

* *

Others said: Rather, it refers to others than Quraysh.

Those who said this:

15917 – Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, saying: My father informed me, saying: I heard Wahb ibn Munabbih say concerning His mighty and majestic saying: ﴿fearing that the people would snatch you away﴾, he said: Persia.

15918 – ... He said: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Isma'il ibn Abd al-Karim narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Samad told me that he heard Wahb ibn Munabbih say, and he recited: ﴿And remember when you were few and oppressed in the land, fearing that the people would snatch you away﴾, and "the people" at that time were Persia and Byzantium.

15919 – ... He said: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah regarding His saying: ﴿And remember when you were few and oppressed in the land﴾, he said: This tribe of the Arabs was the most humiliated of people in abasement, the most wretched in life, the hungriest in belly, the most naked in skin, and the most misguided in error [clenched, on the edge of a stone, between the two lions, Persia and Byzantium, and by Allah, in their lands at that time there was nothing that anyone would envy them for]. [This sentence between brackets is necessary, for the sense is that Persia and Byzantium are the two meant by this. I have included it from the earlier narration of al-Tabari, as will come in the takhrij. Omitting it from the report causes confusion and obscurity.] Whoever of them lived, lived wretchedly, and whoever of them died was cast into the Fire; they were eaten but did not eat; and by Allah, we know of no tribe of the inhabitants of the earth at that time who were of lower station than them [the phrase "lower station than them" does not appear in the preceding report, where in its place was: "by Allah, we know of no tribe at that time among the inhabitants of the earth who had less share and were of smaller account than them"], until Allah brought Islam, and He established them in the lands through it, widened their provision through it, and made you kings over the necks of the people because of it. So through Islam Allah gave what you have seen, so thank Allah for His blessings, for your Lord is the Bestower of blessings who loves gratitude, and the people of gratitude are in increase from Allah, blessed and exalted. [The report: 15919 – this report has passed in full with its chain earlier as no. 7591, and the addition and correction are drawn from it.]

* *

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The more correct of the two opinions in my view is the saying of the one who said: "It refers to the polytheists of Quraysh," because the Muslims were not fearing for themselves from others before the Hijrah, since they were the nearest of the disbelievers to them and the most hostile to them at that time, along with their great number and the small number of the Muslims.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and sheltered you﴾, it means: He sheltered you in Madinah.

Likewise His saying: ﴿and strengthened you with His help﴾, with the Ansar.

* *

The commentators of interpretation said things similar to what we have said on this.

Those who said this:

15920 – Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn Mufadhdhal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿and sheltered you﴾, he said: to the Ansar in Madinah = ﴿and strengthened you with His help﴾, and these were the companions of Muhammad (ﷺ), whom He strengthened with His help on the day of Badr.

15921 – Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ikrimah: ﴿and sheltered you and strengthened you with His help and provided for you of the good things﴾, he means in Madinah.

The commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 8, verse 27:

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿O you who believe, do not betray Allah and the Messenger, nor betray your trusts while you know﴾ (8:27).

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says to the believers in Allah and His Messenger among the companions of His Prophet (ﷺ): O you who have affirmed Allah and His Messenger, ﴿do not betray Allah﴾. Their betrayal of Allah and His Messenger was by the display, by those among them who showed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the believers faith and sincere counsel outwardly, while they concealed disbelief and deceit toward them inwardly. They would point the polytheists to the weak points of the Muslims and inform them of what was hidden from them of their affairs. [[See the explanation of "betrayal" (al-khiyana) above, 9:190.]]

* *

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed about who this verse was revealed concerning, and about the occasion of its revelation.

Some said: It was revealed concerning a hypocrite who wrote to Abu Sufyan informing him of the secret of the Muslims.

Those who said this:

15922. Al-Qasim ibn Bishr ibn Ma'ruf narrated to us, saying: Shababa ibn Sawwar narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Muharram narrated to us, saying: I met Ata' ibn Abi Rabah and he related to me, saying: Jabir ibn Abdullah related to me: that Abu Sufyan left Mecca, and Jibril (Gabriel) came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "Abu Sufyan is in such-and-such a place!" The Prophet (ﷺ) said to his companions: "Abu Sufyan is in such-and-such a place, so go out to him and keep it secret!" He said: A man among the hypocrites wrote to Abu Sufyan: "Muhammad is coming to you, so take your precautions!" Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿Do not betray Allah and the Messenger, nor betray your trusts﴾. [[The report 15922: Al-Qasim ibn Bishr ibn Ma'ruf, the teacher of al-Tabari, passed earlier under numbers 10509 and 10531.

And Shababa ibn Sawwar al-Fazari is trustworthy (thiqa); he has passed several times: 37, 6701, 10051, and elsewhere.

And "Muhammad al-Muharram" is Muhammad ibn Umar al-Muharram. The author of Lisan al-Mizan has treated three persons: "Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Ubayd ibn Umayr al-Makki" (vol. 5, p. 216), "Muhammad ibn Umar al-Muharram" (vol. 5, p. 320), and "Muhammad al-Muharram" (vol. 5, p. 439). He said they are one person, and that "Muhammad ibn Umar" is correctly "Muhammad ibn Umayr," attributed to his grandfather. "Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Ubayd ibn Umayr al-Laythi" passed under number 7484.

Al-Bukhari, in al-Kabir (1/1/142), treated "Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Ubayd ibn Umayr al-Laythi al-Makki," from Ata', and said he is not that trustworthy. He did not mention that he is "Muhammad al-Muharram."

Then he also treated in al-Kabir (1/1/248) "Muhammad al-Muharram," from Ata' and al-Hasan, and said: "munkar al-hadith" (of rejected narrations). So they are two men in his view.

Ibn Abi Hatim (3/2/300) treated "Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Ubayd ibn Umayr al-Laythi" and declared him weak, without mentioning that he is "Muhammad al-Muharram."

Then he treated "Muhammad ibn Umar al-Muharram," who narrated from Ata', and from whom Shababa narrated, and said: "weak in hadith, and unsound in hadith," without mentioning that he is the one before him.

Al-Dhahabi in Mizan al-I'tidal (3/77) treated "Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Ubayd ibn Umayr al-Laythi," who is also called "Muhammad al-Muharram."

Then in the Mizan (3/113) he treated "Muhammad ibn Umar al-Muharram," from Ata', and from him Shababa, and declared him weak, without mentioning that he is the one before him.

Abd al-Ghani ibn Sa'id, in al-Mu'talif wa al-Mukhtalif (p. 117), treated "Muhammad ibn Ubayd ibn Umayr al-Muharram," from "Ata' ibn Abi Rabah."

The apparent view, that what the hafiz (Ibn Hajar) said in Lisan al-Mizan, that these are all one person, is correct, God willing.

In the printed edition it reads "Muhammad ibn al-Muharram," differing from the manuscript by the addition of "ibn" between them.

This report is extremely weak, because of the weakness of "Muhammad al-Muharram," who is abandoned in hadith (matruk al-hadith). Ibn Kathir mentioned the report in his tafsir (4/43-44), then said: "This hadith is extremely strange, and there is scrutiny in its chain and its context."]] Others said: Rather, it was revealed concerning Abu Lubaba, regarding what happened from him and the affair of the Banu Qurayza. [[In the printed and manuscript editions: "concerning Abu Lubaba, the one of whose affair..." The context requires the addition of "fi" (concerning), as I have set it.]]

Those who said this:

15923. Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Abu Sufyan related to me, from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, regarding His saying: "Do not betray Allah and the Messenger, nor betray your trusts," he said: It was revealed concerning Abu Lubaba, whom the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent, and he gestured with his hand to his throat, meaning slaughter. Al-Zuhri said: Abu Lubaba said: "No, by Allah, I will not taste food or drink until I die or Allah accepts my repentance!" He remained seven days without tasting food or drink until he fell unconscious. Then Allah accepted his repentance. It was said to him: "O Abu Lubaba, you have been forgiven!" He said: "By Allah, I will not release myself until the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is the one who releases me." So he came to him and untied him with his own hand. Then Abu Lubaba said: "Indeed, among my repentance is that I abandon the house of my people in which I committed the sin, and that I strip myself of my wealth!" He said: "A third will suffice you, to give in charity." [[The report 15923: the account of Abu Lubaba ibn Abd al-Mundhir al-Ansari, when he did that on the day of the Banu Qurayza, and realised that he had betrayed Allah and His Messenger, is in the Sira of Ibn Hisham (3/247-248) and in other works. Then, when he realised this, he tied himself to a pillar of the mosque and said: "I will not move from this place until Allah accepts my repentance for what I did."

Al-Wahidi narrated it in Asbab al-Nuzul (p. 175), and Malik narrated part of it in al-Muwatta' (p. 481).]]

15924. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr narrated to us, from Ibn Uyayna, who said: Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid narrated to us, saying: I heard Abdullah ibn Abi Qatada say: "O you who believe, do not betray Allah and the Messenger, nor betray your trusts while you know" was revealed concerning Abu Lubaba. [[The report 15924: Abdullah ibn Abi Qatada al-Ansari, a trustworthy Successor (tabi'i), whom the group of compilers narrated from, and who is treated in al-Tahdhib.]]

* *

Others said: Rather, it was revealed concerning the matter of Uthman, may Allah have mercy on him.

Those who said this:

15925. Al-Harith narrated to me, saying: Abd al-Aziz narrated to us, saying: Yunus ibn al-Harith al-Ta'ifi narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ubayd Allah ibn Sa'id, Abu Awn al-Thaqafi, narrated to us, from al-Mughira ibn Shu'ba, who said: This verse was revealed concerning the killing of Uthman, may Allah have mercy on him: "O you who believe, do not betray Allah and the Messenger," the verse. [[The report 15925: Yunus ibn al-Harith al-Ta'ifi al-Thaqafi is weak, though he is not accused of lying. Ibn Mu'in said: "We used to weaken him severely." Ahmad said: "His hadiths are confused."

He is treated in al-Tahdhib, in al-Kabir (4/2/409), where no criticism is mentioned, and in Ibn Abi Hatim (4/2/237), where he is declared weak.

"Muhammad ibn Ubayd Allah ibn Sa'id," Abu Awn al-Thaqafi, is trustworthy, and passed under numbers 7595, 13965, and 15659.

In the printed edition it reads "Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Awn al-Thaqafi," and the manuscript is similar. It may be read "Muhammad ibn Ubayd Allah," and the correct form is what I have set, because Yunus ibn al-Harith al-Ta'ifi narrates from Abu Awn al-Thaqafi, and "Abu Awn" has as the name of his grandfather "Sa'id," not "Awn."

As for Abu Awn al-Thaqafi, I do not think he narrated from al-Mughira ibn Shu'ba, for al-Mughira died in the year fifty (AH), or it is said before that. What is mentioned in his biography is that he narrates from "Affan ibn al-Mughira ibn Shu'ba," so this, in my judgement, is a disconnected chain (munqati') in all likelihood.

As for his saying "it was revealed concerning the killing of Uthman," he means that its ruling includes the act of Uthman, may Allah be pleased with him, for he was killed in betrayal of Allah and His Messenger, and betrayal of the trust, since the killers broke the pledge of allegiance (bay'a) to him that was around their necks. May Allah have mercy on Uthman and forgive him.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of the sayings on this matter, and the most likely to be right, is to say: Allah forbade the believers from betraying Him, betraying His Messenger, and betraying His trust. It is possible that it was revealed concerning Abu Lubaba, and it is possible that it was revealed concerning someone else, and we have no report with which we know which of these was the case, such that it would be obligatory to accept it as authentic.

So the meaning of the verse and its interpretation are what we have mentioned.

* *

The people of interpretation said the like of what we have said.

Those who said this:

15926. Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: "O you who believe, do not betray Allah and the Messenger," he said: He forbade you from betraying Allah and the Messenger, as the hypocrites did.

15927. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufadhdhal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "Do not betray Allah and the Messenger," the verse. He said: They used to hear a hadith from the Prophet (ﷺ) and would spread it until it reached the polytheists.

* *

They differed concerning the interpretation of His saying: "and betray your trusts while you know."

Some of them said: "Do not betray Allah and the Messenger, for that is a betrayal of your trust and its destruction."

Those who said this:

15928. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufadhdhal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "O you who believe, do not betray Allah and the Messenger and betray your trusts," meaning: when they betray Allah and the Messenger, they have betrayed their trusts.

15929. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: "O you who believe, do not betray Allah and the Messenger, and betray your trusts while you know," meaning: do not show to Allah of the truth what He is pleased with from you, then oppose Him in secret in favour of another. For that is the destruction of your trusts and a betrayal of your own selves. [[The report 15929: Sira of Ibn Hisham (2/325), and it follows the earlier report numbered 15873.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: On this interpretation, His saying "and betray your trusts" is in a position of accusative (nasb) by way of al-sarf (a grammatical term, here meaning the accusative of the verb being turned from its expected form, in the sense of a verb conjoined to a prohibited one). [[In the printed edition: "on the adverbial accusative (al-zarf)," and in the manuscript: "on the edge (al-taraf)," and the correct form is what I have set. For the meaning of "al-sarf" see the glossary of terms above, and see al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Qur'an, 1:408.]]

As the poet said: [[He is al-Mutawakkil al-Laythi, though it is attributed to others.]]

"Do not forbid a disposition while you yourself do its like; it is a great shame upon you when you do it."

[[This verse passed earlier, with its takhrij (sourcing) at 1:569 and 3:552.]]

It is narrated as: "and you come to its like." [[That is, in other than the accusative case.]]

* *

Others said: Its meaning is: "Do not betray Allah and the Messenger, nor betray your trusts while you know."

Those who said this:

15930. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: "O you who believe, do not betray Allah and the Messenger and betray your trusts," he says: "Do not betray": meaning, do not diminish them.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: On this interpretation: "Do not betray Allah and the Messenger, nor betray your trusts."

The people of interpretation differed about the meaning of "the trust" (al-amana) mentioned by Allah in His saying: "and betray your trusts."

Some said: It is what is hidden from the eyes of people of Allah's obligations.

Those who said this:

15931. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: "and betray your trusts." "The trust" is the deeds over which Allah entrusted His servants, meaning: the obligation. He says: "Do not betray," meaning: do not diminish them.

15932. Ali ibn Dawud narrated to us, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: "O you who believe, do not betray Allah," he says: by abandoning His obligations; "and the Messenger," he says: by abandoning his sunnas and committing his disobedience. He said: He said at another time: "Do not betray Allah and the Messenger and betray your trusts," and "the trust" is the deeds. Then he mentioned something similar to the report of al-Muthanna.

* *

Others said: The meaning of "the trusts" here is the religion.

Those who said this:

15933. Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: "and betray your trusts," your religion; "and you know," he said: The hypocrites did that, and they know that they are disbelievers, displaying faith. And he recited: ﴿And when they stand up to prayer, they stand up lazily﴾ (4:142). He said: These are the hypocrites. Allah and His Messenger entrusted them with His religion, but they betrayed it: they displayed faith and concealed disbelief.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The meaning of the speech, then, is: O you who believe, do not diminish Allah's rights over you in His obligations, nor His Messenger's due of obedience over you. Rather, obey them in what they command you and forbid you, and do not diminish them. "And betray your trusts" by diminishing your religions and the duties of your deeds and what is binding upon you, "while you know" that they are binding upon you and obligatory, by the proofs that Allah has established against you.

Commentary on the interpretation of His words: ﴿And know that your wealth and your children are only a trial, and that with Allah is a great reward﴾ (8:28)

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says to the believers: "And know, O believers, that your wealth which Allah has entrusted to you, and your children whom Allah has granted you, are a test and a trial. He has given them to you in order to test you with them and try you, to see how you will act concerning the fulfilment of Allah's right over you in them, and in submitting to His command and prohibition regarding them." [[See the explanation of "fitnah" (trial, test) above, p. 486, note 1, and the references there.]] As for His words "and that with Allah is a great reward," the meaning is: know that with Allah is goodness and a great reward for your obedience to Him in what He has commanded you and forbidden you, concerning your wealth and children which He has tested you with in this world. Obey Allah in what He has charged you regarding them, and you will obtain from Him abundant reward in your return. [[See the explanation of "ajr" (reward) in the lexical indices above under (a-j-r).]]

15934 - Al-Harith related to me, saying: 'Abd al-'Aziz related to us, saying: al-Mas'udi related to us, from al-Qasim, from 'Abd al-Rahman, from Ibn Mas'ud, regarding His words: "Indeed, your wealth and your children are a trial," he said: "None of you is without being enveloped in a trial. So whoever seeks refuge, let him seek refuge in Allah from misleading trials."
[[Report 15934 – see the earlier report no. 15912 and the commentary on it.]]

15935 - Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: "And know that your wealth and your children are only a trial," he said: "Fitnah" means testing, their being tested. And he recited: ﴿And We test you with evil and with good as a trial, and to Us you will be returned﴾ (21:35).

The commentary on His words, "O you who believe, if you fear God, He will grant you a criterion (furqan) and will remove from you your misdeeds and forgive you. And God is the Possessor of great bounty" (Qur'an 8:29).

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: O you who have affirmed God and His Messenger, if you fear God by obeying Him, performing His obligations, avoiding His disobedience, and abandoning betrayal of Him, of His Messenger, and of your trusts, "He will grant you a criterion (furqan)," meaning: He will grant you a distinction and separation between your right and the falsehood of those among your enemies, the polytheists, who wish you evil, by His giving you victory over them and granting you triumph against them [see the explanation of "al-furqan" above, 1:98-99, 3:448, 6:162-163]. "And will remove from you your misdeeds," meaning: He will erase from you what has passed of your sins between you and Him [see the explanation of "al-takfir" above in the lexical indexes (kafara), and the explanation of "al-sayyi'at" in the indexes (sa'a)]. "And forgive you," meaning: He will cover them over and conceal them, so that He does not hold you to account for them [see the explanation of "al-maghfirah" in the lexical indexes (ghafara)]. "And God is the Possessor of great bounty," meaning: God, who does that for you, has great bounty over you and over others of His creation, by His doing that and doing the like of it. His doing is a recompense from Him to His servant for his obedience to Him, because He is the One who guides His servant to the obedience which he has earned, until he deserves from his Lord the reward which He promised him for it [see the explanation of "al-fadl" above in the lexical indexes (fadala)].

* *

The exegetes have differed in expressing the interpretation of His words, "He will grant you a criterion (furqan)."

Some of them said: a way out (makhraj).

* *

Some of them said: deliverance (najah).

* *

Some of them said: a separation (fasl).

* *

All of these are close in meaning, even though the expressions differ, and I have already shown the soundness of this earlier, in a way that makes repeating it unnecessary [meaning what has passed, 1:98-99].

* *

Those who said its meaning is: a way out.

15936 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid: "If you fear God, He will grant you a criterion (furqan)," he said: a way out.

15937 - ......... He said: My father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Mujahid: "If you fear God, He will grant you a criterion (furqan)," he said: a way out.

15938 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, from Anbasa, from Jabir, from Mujahid: "furqanan," a way out.

15939 - Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, "furqanan," he said: a way out in this world and the next.

15940 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

15941 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Hani' ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from Hajjaj, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "furqanan," he said: "al-furqan" is the way out.

15942 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, his words: "furqanan," meaning: a way out.

15943 - Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: al-Thawri informed us, from Mansur, from Mujahid: "furqanan," a way out.

15944 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abd Allah ibn Raja' al-Basri narrated to us, saying: Za'idah narrated to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, the same.

15945 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: al-Muharibi narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak: "furqanan," he said: a way out.

15946 - I was told on the authority of al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: I heard Ubayd say: I heard al-Dahhak say: "furqanan," a way out.

15947 - Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, the same.

15948 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Humayd narrated to us, from Zuhayr, from Jabir, from Ikrimah, he said: "al-furqan," the way out.

* *

Those who said its meaning is: deliverance.

15949 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, from Anbasa, from Jabir, from Ikrimah: "If you fear God, He will grant you a criterion (furqan)," he said: deliverance.

15950 - Al-Harith narrated to me, saying: Abd al-Aziz narrated to us, saying: Isra'il narrated to us, from a man, from Ikrimah and Mujahid, regarding His words: "He will grant you a criterion (furqan)." Ikrimah said: the way out; and Mujahid said: deliverance.

15951 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "He will grant you a criterion (furqan)," he said: deliverance.

15952 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas: "He will grant you a criterion (furqan)," meaning: He will grant you deliverance.

15953 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: "He will grant you a criterion (furqan)," i.e., deliverance.

* *

Those who said it means a separation (fasl).

15954 - ...................................... "O you who believe, if you fear God, He will grant you a criterion (furqan)," he said: a criterion that distinguishes in their hearts between truth and falsehood, until they recognize it and are guided by that criterion. [Note on the report 15954: the chain of this report is missing in the manuscript, where a blank space roughly a line and a half long was left, and the editor of the printed edition joined the text without indicating that blank. It is evident that it is an independent report, as I have placed it.]

15955 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: "O you who believe, if you fear God, He will grant you a criterion (furqan)," i.e., a separation between truth and falsehood, so that your truth may be manifested by it, and the falsehood of those who oppose you may be hidden by it. [Note on the report 15955: Sirat Ibn Hisham 2:325, and it follows the earlier report numbered 15929. The printed edition had "yazhir" without the initial lam; the manuscript reads it in both ways, and I have adopted the text of the Sirah, with the lam at its beginning.]

The word "al-furqan" in the speech of the Arabs is a verbal noun from their saying: "faraqtu bayn al-shay' wa al-shay' afruqu baynahuma farqan wa furqanan."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 8, verse 30 (part 1 of 2):

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And [remember] when those who disbelieved plotted against you, to restrain you or kill you or expel you. They plot, and Allah plots. And Allah is the best of planners.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is He, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), reminding him of His favours upon him: "And remember, O Muhammad, when those who disbelieved among your people, the polytheists, plotted against you so that they might restrain you." [[See the explanation of "plotting" (al-makr) above, 12:95, 97, 579 and 13:33.]]
* *
The interpreters differed regarding the interpretation of His saying "to restrain you" (liyuthbitūka).

Some said: its meaning is "to bind you."
Those who said this:

15956. Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiya related to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: "And when those who disbelieved plotted against you to restrain you," he means: "to bind you" (liyuthiqūka).

15957. ............ He said: Abu Hudhayfa related to us, saying: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "to restrain you" – "to bind you" (liyuthiqū).

15958. Bishr ibn Mu'adh related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, regarding His saying: "And when those who disbelieved plotted against you to restrain you," the verse: he says, "to bind you in fetters." And they intended by that the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ), who at that time was in Makkah.

15959. Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada and Miqsam, who both said: they said: "Bind him with bonds."

15960. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: "to restrain you" – he said: the restraint is imprisonment and fettering.
* *
Others said: rather, its meaning is imprisonment.
Those who said this:

15961. Al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Juraij, who said: I asked 'Ata' about His saying "to restrain you," and he said: "to imprison you." And 'Abd Allah ibn Kathir said the same.

15962. Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: they said: "Imprison him."

* *
Others said: rather, its meaning is: "to bewitch you."
Those who said this:

15963. Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Basri, known as al-Wasawisi, related to me, saying: 'Abd al-Majid ibn Abi Rawwad related to us, from Ibn Juraij, from 'Ata', from 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr, from al-Muttalib ibn Abi Wada'a: that Abu Talib said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "What is your people conspiring about?" He said: "They want to bewitch me, kill me and expel me!" He said: "Who told you this?" He said: "My Lord!" He said: "Excellent Lord is your Lord! So enjoin well concerning Him!" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I enjoin well concerning Him! Rather, He enjoins well concerning me!" Then it was revealed: "And when those who disbelieved plotted against you to restrain you or kill you or expel you," the verse. [[The report 15963: "Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Basri," known as "al-Wasawisi," a teacher of al-Tabari. I did not find explicit statement that he was called "al-Wasawisi"; what Abu Ja'far narrates from him in his History, in various places, is "Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Daraari," who is "Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Abi Darrar al-Razi," truthful (saduq). He is biographed in al-Tahdhib and Ibn Abi Hatim 3/2/190, and al-Tahdhib mentions that Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Jarir al-Tabari narrated from him, without mentioning that he was known as al-Wasawisi.
Ibn Abi Hatim biographed his brother "Ahmad ibn Isma'il ibn Abi Darrar al-Razi," 1/1/41, and I found in Lubab al-Ansab 2:273: "al-Wasawisi, known by it: Ahmad ibn Isma'il al-Wasawisi al-Basri," which indicates that it is likely that "Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Abi Darrar" was also called "al-Wasawisi."
"'Abd al-Majid ibn Abi Rawwad" is "'Abd al-Majid ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Abi Rawwad al-Azdi," who narrated from Ibn Juraij and others. Ahmad and Ibn Ma'in and others declared him trustworthy. Abu Hatim and Ibn Sa'd declared him weak. Some said he was reliable in his narration from Ibn Juraij, and others said he narrated from Ibn Juraij hadiths not corroborated by others. Biographed in al-Tahdhib and Ibn Abi Hatim 3/1/64.
"'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr ibn Qatada al-Laythi" is trustworthy; he has passed as nos. 9180, 9181, 9189, 15621.
In the manuscript and printed edition it read: "'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr ibn al-Muttalib ibn Abi Wada'a," which is an error beyond doubt.
"al-Muttalib ibn Abi Wada'a al-Sahmi al-Qurashi" had companionship (of the Prophet); he is biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 4/2/7, and Ibn Abi Hatim 4/1/385, and none mentions a narration by 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr from him.
This report was narrated by Ibn Kathir in his Tafsir 4:46, 47, and he said: "The mention of Abu Talib in this is very strange, indeed rejected (munkar), because this verse is Medinan. Moreover, this story, and the gathering of Quraysh in this conspiracy and consultation about restraint, expulsion or killing, was on the night of the Hijra, by all means. That was about three years after the death of Abu Talib, when they became bold against him due to the death of his uncle Abu Talib, who used to protect him, support him and bear his burdens."
If what Ibn Kathir said is correct, this report would be one of the reports that led them to say of "'Abd al-Majid ibn Abi Rawwad" that he narrated from Ibn Juraij hadiths not corroborated by others. Nevertheless, Hajjaj narrated from him the like of 'Abd al-Majid's narration. See the commentary on the following report, for I take a course different from Ibn Kathir's regarding the report. See also no. 15976, for Ibn Juraij will say that this verse is Meccan, not Medinan.]]

15964. Al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, saying: Ibn Juraij said: 'Ata' said: I heard 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr say: When they conspired against the Prophet (ﷺ) to kill him, or restrain him, or expel him, Abu Talib said to him: "Do you know what they have conspired about you?" He said: "Yes!" He said: "Then inform me." He said: "Who told you?" He said: "My Lord!" He said: "Excellent Lord is your Lord; enjoin well concerning Him!" He said: "Shall I enjoin well concerning Him, or does He enjoin well concerning me?" [[The report 15964: see the commentary on the previous report. Ibn Kathir's criticism of this report was mentioned earlier. What led him to say what he said, that it was the night of the Hijra, is what Ibn Jarir narrated in the following report, which he titled: "And it seems that the meaning of the plotting of the people of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) against him was to restrain him, as Muhammad ibn ... related to me," and he related the report of their conspiracy against him on the night of the Hijra.
But it is possible that the two earlier reports concern another matter and another night; indeed I nearly assert that the report narrated by Ibn Juraij has no connection to the matter of the Hijra, and that Ibn Kathir followed al-Tabari in what he merely assumed. Ibn Ishaq and others narrated that the nobles of Quraysh gathered one day in al-Hijr and mentioned the Messenger of Allah, and claimed that they had endured from him a great matter. While they were thus, the Messenger of Allah appeared to them, came walking until he touched the Corner, then passed by them while circumambulating the House, and they made a slighting remark at him. The anger was recognised in his face (ﷺ). When he passed them a second time, they slighted him with the same, then he passed a third time, and they did the same, so he stopped and said: "Hear me, O assembly of Quraysh! By Him in whose hand is my soul, I have brought you slaughter!" They became submissive and soothed him with the best speech, out of fear and hope. When the next day came, they gathered in al-Hijr, and some said to others: "You mentioned what had reached you from him and what reached him from you, until when he confronted you with what you dislike, you left him." While they were thus, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) appeared to them, and they leapt at him as one man, surrounding him, saying: "Are you the one who says such and such?" concerning his criticism of their gods. He said: "Yes, I am the one who says that." Then one of them seized the collar of his garment, and Abu Bakr stood before him, weeping and saying: "Will you kill a man for saying 'My Lord is Allah'?!" (Sirat Ibn Hisham 1:309, 310). See the following report no. 15974 and its commentary.
This was long before the Hijra, during the lifetime of Abu Talib. So this report is likely the one 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr referred to in his narration from al-Muttalib ibn Abi Wada'a as his people's conspiracy against him. If that is correct, there is no basis for what Ibn Kathir said, and this report would be sound because its chain is sound.]] And it seems that the meaning of the plotting of the people of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) against him was to restrain him, as:

15965. Sa'id ibn Yahya al-Umawi related to us, saying: my father related to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq related to us, from 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas – and al-Kalbi related to me, from Zadhan, client of Umm Hani', from Ibn 'Abbas: that a group of men of Quraysh, from the nobles of each tribe, gathered to enter the Dar al-Nadwa, and Iblis confronted them in the form of an aged, noble shaykh. [[In the manuscript: "in the form of a noble man"; above "noble" is the letter (ṭ) indicating an error, and the correct reading is that of the printed edition, matching Sirat Ibn Hisham.]] When they saw him, they said: "Who are you?" He said: "A shaykh from Najd. I heard that you had gathered, so I wished to attend you, and no opinion or counsel will be lacking to you from me." [["Will not be lacking to you," i.e., will not fail or elude you, an opinion and counsel from me.]] They said: "Yes, enter!" So he entered with them and said: "Look at the affair of this man. By God, he will soon rise against you in your affairs by his command." [[In the printed edition: "that he will come to you in your affairs," which has no meaning; I have retained what is in the manuscript, which is unpointed, and the correct reading is what I have given.]] He said: Then one speaker said: "Confine him in fetters, then wait for him the vicissitudes of fate, until he dies as those poets before him died, Zuhayr and al-Nabigha; he is only like one of them!" He said: The enemy of God, the Najdi shaykh, shouted and said: "By God, this is not an opinion for you! By God, his Lord will certainly bring him out of his confinement to his companions, and they will soon rise against him until they take him from your hands and protect him from you, and I am not safe from them expelling you from your lands!" They said: "Then look into something other than this." He said: Then one speaker said: "Expel him from among you, and you will be relieved of him, for when he goes out, whatever he does and wherever he lands will not harm you; when he is absent from you, his harm is gone and you are relieved, and his affair will be among others." The Najdi shaykh said: "By God, this is not an opinion for you. Have you not seen the sweetness of his speech, the eloquence of his tongue, and what he hears from his discourse that captures hearts? By God, if you do so, then he will go to the Arabs, and they will gather against you, then he will surely come upon you until he expels you from your lands and kills your nobles!" They said: "He has spoken truly, by God! Look for an opinion other than this!" He said: Then Abu Jahl said: "By God, I will counsel you with an opinion which I do not think you have yet perceived; I see no other than it!" They said: "And what is it?" He said: "We take from each tribe a young man, a noble and handsome youth, of high lineage, and give each young man a sharp sword, then they strike him as one man. When they have killed him, his blood will be dispersed among all the tribes, and I do not think this clan of Banu Hashim will be able to fight all of Quraysh, for when they see that, they will accept the blood-money, and we will be relieved and cut off his harm from us." The Najdi shaykh said: "This, by God, is the opinion; what the youth has said is the opinion, I see no other!" He said: So they dispersed upon that, resolved against him. He said: Then Gabriel came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and ordered him not to sleep in the bed in which he used to sleep that night, and God permitted him at that time to leave, and He revealed to him after his arrival in Medina "al-Anfal," reminding him of His favours upon him and His trial for him: "And [remember] when those who disbelieved plotted against you, to restrain you or kill you or expel you. They plot, and Allah plots. And Allah is the best of planners," and He revealed concerning their saying: "Wait for him the vicissitudes of fate," until he dies as those poets before him died: "Or do they say, 'A poet, we await for him the vicissitudes of fate'?" [Surah al-Tur: 30]. That day was called "the day of the crowding," because of the opinion they gathered upon. [[The report 15965: Sirat Ibn Hisham 2:124–128, and the chain there is "Ibn Ishaq said: one of our companions whom I do not suspect told me, from 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid ibn Jabr Abu al-Hajjaj, and others whom I do not suspect, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abbas, may God be pleased with them both," then he related the report in different wording.
Among what has been raised as an objection to this report is that the verse of "Surat al-Tur," is a Meccan verse, revealed some time before the Hijra, and Ibn Ishaq's placement of the verse after the report gives the impression that it was revealed on the night of the Hijra, or after the Hijra, and this can hardly be correct.]]
15966. Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada and Miqsam, regarding His saying: "And when those who disbelieved plotted against you to restrain you," they both said: they consulted about it one night while they were in Makkah. Some of them said: "When it is morning, bind him with fetters." Others said: "Rather, kill him." Others said: "Rather, expel him." When they woke in the morning, they saw 'Ali, may God have mercy on him, so God turned back their plot.

15967. Al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: my father informed me, from 'Ikrima, who said: When the Prophet (ﷺ) and Abu Bakr went out to the cave, he ordered 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, and he slept in his bed, and the polytheists spent the night guarding him. When they saw him sleeping, they thought he was the Prophet (ﷺ), so they left him. When they woke in the morning, they rushed at him thinking he was the Prophet (ﷺ), but they found 'Ali, so they said: "Where is your companion?" He said: "I do not know!" They said: So they mounted the hard and the tame camels in search of him. [[" The hard " of camels is the one never ridden, because it does not submit to its rider; its opposite is " the tame," which is easy and submissive. It is a metaphor for mounting every kind of mount in search of what one wants, whether easy or hard.]]

15968. Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ishaq related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq related to us, from Ma'mar, who said: 'Uthman al-Jazari informed me that Miqsam, client of Ibn 'Abbas, informed him, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying: "And when those who disbelieved plotted against you to restrain you," he said: Quraysh consulted one night in Makkah. Some of them said: "When it is morning, bind him with fetters" – meaning the Prophet (ﷺ). Others said: "Rather, kill him." Others said: "Rather, expel him." So God informed His Prophet of that, and he spent that night on the bed of the Prophet (ﷺ), may God have mercy on him, and the Prophet (ﷺ) went out until he reached the cave, and the polytheists spent the night guarding 'Ali, thinking he was the Prophet (ﷺ). When they woke in the morning, they rushed at him, and when they saw 'Ali, may God have mercy on him, God turned back their plot. They said: "Where is your companion?" He said: "I do not know!" So they followed his trail, and when they reached the mountain and passed by the cave, they saw spider webs on its door. They said: "If he had entered here, there would not be webs on its door!" So he remained in it three nights. [[The report 15968: "'Uthman al-Jazari," who is called "'Uthman al-Mashahid." He narrated from Miqsam, and Ma'mar and al-Nu'man ibn Rashid narrated from him. Abu Hatim said: "I know of no one who narrated from him except Ma'mar and al-Nu'man." Ahmad was asked about him and said: "He narrated munkar hadiths; they claim his book was lost." Biographed in Ibn Abi Hatim 3/1/174.
In the printed edition it read: "'Uthman al-Jurayri," while the manuscript, as I have given, is unpointed.
This report was narrated by Ahmad in his Musnad, no. 3251, and my brother said: "There is doubt in its chain, because of 'Uthman al-Jazari, as in the chain 2562," and there it was inferred that "'Uthman al-Jazari" is "'Uthman ibn Sajj," but what Ibn Abi Hatim said suggests that "'Uthman al-Jazari" is other than "'Uthman ibn Sajj."
I have since found in Majma' al-Zawa'id 7:27 this report, in similar form, and then he said: "Ahmad and al-Tabarani narrated it, and in it is 'Uthman ibn 'Amr al-Jazari, whom Ibn Hibban declared trustworthy, and others declared weak, and the rest of its narrators are the narrators of the Sahih."
I still doubt that "'Uthman al-Jazari" is other than "'Uthman ibn 'Amr ibn Sajj."]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 8, verse 30 (part 2 of 2):

15969 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿And when those who disbelieved plotted against you, to confine you, or kill you, or expel you. They plot, and Allah plots, and Allah is the best of plotters﴾. He said: The elders of Quraysh gathered, consulting about the Prophet (ﷺ) after the Ansar had embraced Islam, and they feared that his affair would rise if he found a refuge to which he could retreat. ["Fariqu" (they feared): they were afraid and alarmed.] Then Iblis came in the form of a man from the people of Najd, and he entered with them into the Dar al-Nadwa (the council house). When they did not recognize him, they said: "Who are you? By God, we have not informed everyone of our people about this gathering of ours!" He said: "I am a man from the people of Najd. I listen to your talk and I will advise you!" So they were ashamed and let him be. Then some of them said: "Seize Muhammad when he lies down on his bed." [In the printed edition: "idha isbahaha 'ala firashihi" (when he rises in the morning on his bed), I do not know where this came from!] "Put him in a room and wait for him to suffer the misfortunes of time." [Al-raib is death, and al-manun is time (al-dahr).] Iblis said: "How evil is what you have said! You would put him in a room, and then his companions would come and free him, and there would be fighting between you!" They said: "The elder has spoken truly!" He said: "Expel him from your town!" Iblis said: "How evil is what you have said! You would expel him from your town, and he has corrupted your foolish ones, and then he would go to another town and corrupt its foolish ones, and then he would come to you with horsemen and men!" They said: "The elder has spoken truly!" Abu Jahl said, and he was the first of them in obeying Iblis: "Rather, we shall go to every clan of Quraysh and select one man from them, and we will give them weapons, and they will all rush upon Muhammad and strike him with one blow, as a single man. Then the Banu 'Abd al-Muttalib will not be able to fight all of Quraysh, and they will have nothing but the blood-money!" Iblis said: "He has spoken truly, and this young man is the best of you in opinion!" So they resolved upon that. Allah informed His Messenger (ﷺ), and he slept on the bed, and they set watchers over him. When part of the night came, he and Abu Bakr set out to the cave, and 'Ali ibn Abi Talib slept on the bed. This is when Allah says: ﴿to confine you﴾ or kill you or expel you. ["Al-Ithbat" (confinement) is imprisonment and binding.] And this is His saying: ﴿And indeed, they almost tried to unsettle you from the land to expel you from it, and then they would not remain after you except for a little﴾ [Surah al-Isra, 76]. He says: He will destroy them.

When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) migrated to Medina, 'Umar met him and said: "What did the people do?" He thought that they had been destroyed when the Prophet (ﷺ) left among them, and this is how nations were treated. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Delay the fighting."

15970 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿to confine you or kill you﴾: He said: The disbelievers of Quraysh intended that against Muhammad (ﷺ) before he left Mecca.

15971 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similarly.

15972 - Ibn Wakic narrated to me, saying: Hani ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from Hajjaj, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similarly; except that he said: "They did that to Muhammad."

15973 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿And when those who disbelieved plotted against you, to confine you or kill you﴾, the verse: he is the Prophet (ﷺ), they plotted against him while he was in Mecca.

15974 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿And when those who disbelieved plotted against you, to confine you﴾, to the end of the verse: They gathered and consulted about the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and they said: "Kill this man." Some of them said: "No man will kill him without being killed for it!" They said: "Seize him and imprison him, and put iron on him." They said: "Then his family will not leave you alone!" They said: "Expel him." They said: "Then he will incite the people against you." ["Yastaghwi al-nas" (he incites the people): i.e., he calls them to gather. It is said: "Taghawaw 'alayhi hatta qatalahu" (they gathered against him until they killed him), when they gather and cooperate in evil. What I consider more correct is "yasta'wi" (with the letter 'ayn, unpointed). It is said: "Asta'wa fulan jama'ah" (so-and-so called a group), when he howled at them toward strife. It is also said: "Ta'awa Banu fulan 'ala fulan" and "taghawaw" (with the letter ghayn, pointed), when they gathered against him. And "Asta'wa al-qawm" means they called on them for help. Its origin is from "al-'awa'," the howling of a dog, so the dogs of the tribe answer it.]

He said: Iblis was with them in the form of a man from the people of Najd, and their opinion was unified that when he came to circumambulate the House and touch its corner, they would gather upon him, cover him, and kill him, for his family would not know who killed him, and they would accept the blood-money, so we would kill him and be relieved and pay the blood-money! When he came to circumambulate the House, they gathered upon him and covered him. [In the printed edition and the manuscript: "fa-ya'muhu" with the letter 'ayn, unpointed, which has a weak meaning in my view, and the correct reading is with the letter ghayn: "fa-yaghummuhu." It is said: "Ghamma al-shay' yaghummuhu," when it overtops and covers and conceals a thing so that there is no gap in it. From this is the saying of al-Namir ibn Tawlab, describing the gathering of Arab fighters in war:

"The corners of the enemy struck you, and they became
A rugged and a serpent from the dwelling place of their homes.
As if it were a thicket whose plants are vivid,
Dense plants that cover the astray plants of its valleys."

From this comes the word "ghummah" (distress), and it is said: "a cloud that is aghamm," one with no gap in it. Consider afterward the description of their gathering upon him (ﷺ), may my father and mother be ransomed for him, and that Abu Bakr found no way in, and His saying also: "Then Allah relieved it from him." All of this indicates the correctness of reading it as I have established. This page of the manuscript is nearly all unpointed.]

So his family would not know who killed him. When Abu Bakr came, he was told of that, so he came and found no way in. When he found no way in, he said: ﴿Will you kill a man because he says: My Lord is Allah, and he has brought you clear proofs from your Lord?﴾ [Surah Ghafir, 28]. He said: Then Allah relieved him from them. When the night descended, [In the printed edition: "fa-lamma kana al-layl" (when the night was), different from what is in the manuscript, which has "fa-lamma habata" and the correct reading, God willing, is what I have established. "Hatta al-layl" means it descended and enveloped.] Gabriel, peace be upon him, came to him and said: "Who are your companions?" He said: "So-and-so, so-and-so, and so-and-so." He said: "No, we know them better than you do, O Muhammad, it is a night-gnat!" [In the printed edition and the manuscript: "huwa namus layl," and the context requires what I have established. "Al-namus" is a dusty small creature, the lice of grain, which bites people and stings them. Their saying: "They are a night-gnat" means their insignificance and lowliness.]

He said: Those men were seized from their beds while they were asleep, and they were brought to the Prophet (ﷺ). One of them was presented to Gabriel, who blinded him, then released him. He said: "What is his state, O Gabriel?" He said: "I have taken care of him, O Prophet of Allah!" Then another was presented, and he struck him on the head with a stick, one blow, then released him. He said: "What is his state, O Gabriel?" He said: "I have taken care of him, O Prophet of Allah!" Then another was brought, and he struck him in the knee. He said: "What is his state, O Gabriel?" He said: "I have taken care of him!" Then another was brought, and he gave him a drink of "madhaqah." ["Al-madhaqah" is a portion of milk mixed with water.] He said: "What is his state, O Gabriel?" He said: "I have taken care of him, O Prophet of Allah!" And the fifth was brought. [He did not mention what Gabriel, peace be upon him, did to the fifth, though he mentioned what his affair came to, so I fear that some words have been omitted.]

When he went out of his house, he passed by an archer, and an arrowhead ["mishqas"] caught on his cloak, so he turned, and it cut the "akhal" vein of his leg. ["Al-akhal" is the vein of life, also called "nahr al-badan" (river of the body). It is a vein in the hand and in the middle of the forearm, and in each limb of it there is a branch with its own name. When it is cut, the blood does not stop.] As for the one whose eyes had been blinded, he woke up blind. As for the one who was given the drink, he woke up with his belly swollen with dropsy. As for the one who was struck on his head, the "naqbah" afflicted him. [In the printed edition: "al-naqdah," in both places. As for the manuscript, the first is what it likely reads as "al-naqbah," except that it adds to the head of the "ba" and then wrote "al-naqdah" after it, and I found no sores called "naqdah." "Al-naqbah" (with a vowel on the first letter and sukun on the second) is the first beginning of mange; one sees a patch like the palm on the side of a camel or its hip or its muzzle, then it spreads over it until it fills it all. Perhaps this is what is meant here.] He was afflicted in his head. As for the one who was stabbed in his knee, he woke up and was paralyzed. That is the saying of Allah: ﴿And when those who disbelieved plotted against you, to confine you or kill you or expel you. They plot, and Allah plots, and Allah is the best of plotters﴾.

15975 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, regarding His saying: ﴿They plot, and Allah plots, and Allah is the best of plotters﴾, meaning: "So I plotted against them with My firm scheme, until He delivered you from them." [The report: 15975, Sirat Ibn Hisham 1:325, and it follows the earlier report no. 15955. In the printed edition and the manuscript: "fa-makartu lahum" (I plotted against them), and I have established what is in Sirat Ibn Hisham, which is more correct.]

15976 - al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from 'Ikrimah, regarding His saying: ﴿And when those who disbelieved plotted against you﴾, he said: "This is Meccan." [He said: Ibn Jurayj said: Mujahid said: This is Meccan.] [The report: 15976. See the commentary on the earlier report no. 15964. It seems he means that this verse concerns a matter that concerned the Prophet (ﷺ) while he was in Mecca. Being certain that this verse, or the verses that follow it, were revealed in Mecca is a difficult matter, and one can hardly be confident of its correctness, and objections to it have many aspects, which have no place to be mentioned here.]

Abu Ja'far said: So the meaning of the statement is then: Remember, O Muhammad, My favor upon you, by My plotting against those who tried to plot against you from the polytheists of your people, by confining you, killing you, or expelling you from your homeland, until I rescued you from them and destroyed them. So proceed with My command in fighting whoever fights you from the polytheists, and turn away from answering what I sent you with, of the upright religion. Let the multitude of their number not frighten you, for your Lord is the best of plotters against whoever disbelieves in Him, worships other than Him, and opposes His command and prohibition.

* * *

We have already explained the meaning of "al-makr" (plotting) earlier, in a way that makes repeating it in this place unnecessary. [See the explanation of "al-makr" in what preceded: 12:95, 97, 579 / 13:33, 491.]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 8, verse 31:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And when Our verses are recited to them, they say, "We have heard. If we willed, we could say the like of this. This is not but the tales of the former peoples."﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is He, mentioning: And when the clear verses of the Book of God are recited to these disbelievers, for whom God has expanded the breast to understand them [[See the explanation of "recitation" (al-tilawa) above, p. 385, note 1, and the references there.]] =, they say, out of ignorance on their part and obstinacy against the truth, while they know that they are lying in what they say: "If we willed, we could say the like of this," which is recited to us, "This is not but the tales of the former peoples." That is, they say: this Qur'an that is recited to them is nothing but the tales of the former peoples.

"Asatir" is the plural of "usṭur," and it is a plural of a plural, because the singular of "asṭur" is "saṭr," then "saṭr" is pluralized as "asṭur" and "suṭur," then "asṭur" is pluralized as "asatir" and "asatir." [[See the explanation of "asatir" above, 11:308–310.]]

Some of the grammarians used to say: the singular of "asatir" is "uslūra" (usṭūra).

* *

The polytheists, by their saying, "This is not but the tales of the former peoples," meant: this Qur'an which you recite to us, O Muhammad, is nothing but what the ancients wrote down and inscribed of the reports of the nations! As if they attributed it to having been taken from the sons of Adam, and that God had not revealed it to him.

* *

Those who engage in interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said in agreement with what we have said on this.

Those who said so:

15977 – Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, saying: Ibn Jurayj said regarding His saying: "And when Our verses are recited to them, they say, 'We have heard. If we willed, we could say the like of this'": Al-Nadr ibn al-Harith used to travel as a merchant to Persia, and he would pass by the ʿIbad, who were reciting the Gospel and bowing and prostrating. [[" al-ʿIbad," a people from various tribes among the branches of the Arabs, who gathered upon Christianity before Islam. They disdained to be called "slaves" (ʿabid), so they said, "We are the ʿIbad," and they settled in al-Hira. Thus they were attributed to "al-ʿIbad," and among them was ʿAdi ibn Zayd al-ʿIbadi, the poet.]] Then he came to Mecca and found Muhammad (ﷺ) having had the revelation sent down to him while he was bowing and prostrating, so al-Nadr said: "We have heard. If we willed, we could say the like of this!" – referring to what he had heard from the ʿIbad. Then it was revealed: "And when Our verses are recited to them, they say, 'We have heard. If we willed, we could say the like of this.'" He said: Our Lord then related what they had said in Mecca, and related their saying when they said: "O God, if this is the truth from You," [the verse].

15978 – Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said: al-Nadr ibn al-Harith ibn ʿAlqama, brother of the Banu ʿAbd al-Dar, used to frequent al-Hira, and he would hear the rhymed prose (saj') of its people and their speech. When he came to Mecca and heard the speech of the Prophet (ﷺ) and the Qur'an, he said: "We have heard. If we willed, we could say the like of this. This is not but the tales of the former peoples," meaning: the rhymed utterances of the people of al-Hira. [[" al-asajiʿ," the plural of "usjuʿa," what a soothsayer or other person chants in rhymed phrases. See what has preceded, no. 13157.]]

15979 – Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, saying: Shuʿba narrated to us, from Abu Bishr, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) killed on the day of Badr, by way of sabr (tying and killing in captivity): ʿUqba ibn Abi Muʿayt, Tuʿayma ibn ʿAdi, and al-Nadr ibn al-Harith. al-Miqdad had captured al-Nadr, and when he was ordered to be killed, al-Miqdad said: "O Messenger of God, my captive!" The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "He used to say about the Book of God what he used to say!" So the Prophet (ﷺ) ordered his killing, and al-Miqdad said: "My captive!" The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "O God, enrich al-Miqdad from Your bounty!" Al-Miqdad said: "This is what I wanted!" And this verse was revealed concerning him: "And when Our verses are recited to them," [the verse].

15980 – Yaʿqub narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Abu Bishr informed us, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr: that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) killed on the day of Badr three men of Quraysh by way of sabr: al-Mutʿim ibn ʿAdi, al-Nadr ibn al-Harith, and ʿUqba ibn Abi Muʿayt. He said: When it was ordered to kill al-Nadr, al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad said: "My captive, O Messenger of God!" He said: "He used to say about the Book of God and about His Messenger what he used to say!" He said: He said that twice or thrice, and the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "O God, enrich al-Miqdad from Your bounty!" And al-Miqdad had captured al-Nadr. [[The report 15980: This is how it came in the narration of this report, "al-Mutʿim ibn ʿAdi," in place of "Tuʿayma ibn ʿAdi," and it seems this is not an error by the copyist, because Ibn Kathir in his tafsir (4:51) said: "Thus Hushaym narrated it from Abu Bishr Jaʿfar ibn Abi Wahshiyya, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, that he said: al-Mutʿim ibn ʿAdi, in place of Tuʿayma. And this is an error, because al-Mutʿim ibn ʿAdi was not alive on the day of Badr, and for this reason the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said that day: 'If al-Mutʿim ibn ʿAdi were alive and then asked me about these foul ones, I would have granted them to him!' meaning the captives, because he had given protection to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) on the day he returned from al-Ta'if." See the note on no. 15981.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 8, verse 32:

On the interpretation of His saying: ﴿And when they said, "O Allah, if this is indeed the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky or bring us a painful punishment."﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The Exalted says: And remember, O Muhammad, also what befell those who said, "O Allah, if this is indeed the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky or bring us a painful punishment," when I deceived them (makartu bihim) and brought upon them a painful punishment. [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "makartu lahum" (I plotted for them), which is not correct.]] That punishment was their being killed by the sword on the day of Badr.

* *

It is also mentioned that this verse was revealed concerning al-Nadr ibn al-Harith.

Those who said so:

15981. Yaqub related to me, saying: Hushaym related to us, saying: Abu Bishr related to us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, regarding His saying: "And when they said, 'O Allah, if this is indeed the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky,'" he said: It was revealed concerning al-Nadr ibn al-Harith. [[The report 15981: "Abu Bishr" is Ja'far ibn Iyas, Ja'far ibn Abi Wahshiyyah, who has passed many times. In Ibn Kathir's commentary, which I quoted in the note on the earlier report, it appears as "Ja'far ibn Abi Dahiyyah," which is a pure error.]]

15982. Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: "If this is indeed the truth from You," he said: the statement of al-Nadr ibn al-Harith, or: the son of al-Harith ibn Kaladah. [[The report 15982: In the printed edition: "al-Nadr ibn al-Harith ibn 'Alqamah ibn Kaladah." The correct form is that of the manuscript, since the genealogy varies thus: "al-Nadr ibn al-Harith ibn Kaladah ibn 'Alqamah ibn 'Abd Manaf ibn 'Abd al-Dar," or: "al-Nadr ibn al-Harith ibn 'Alqamah ibn Kaladah ibn 'Abd Manaf ibn 'Abd al-Dar." See Sirat Ibn Hisham 2: 320, 321. The printed edition altered what was in the manuscript without justification or scruple.]]

15983. Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah related to us, saying: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "O Allah, if this is indeed the truth from You," the statement of al-Nadr ibn al-Harith ibn 'Alqamah ibn Kaladah, of the Banu 'Abd al-Dar.

15984. ...... He said: Ishaq informed us, saying: Abdullah informed us, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding His saying: "If this is indeed the truth from You," he said: It is al-Nadr ibn al-Harith ibn Kaladah.

15985. Ahmad ibn Ishaq related to us, saying: Abu Ahmad related to us, saying: Talhah ibn Amr related to us, from 'Ata', who said: A man of the Banu 'Abd al-Dar, called al-Nadr ibn Kaladah, said: "O Allah, if this is indeed the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky or bring us a painful punishment." Then Allah said: ﴿And they say, "Our Lord, hasten to us our share (of punishment) before the Day of Reckoning."﴾ [Surah Sad: 16], and He said: ﴿And you have certainly come to Us alone, as We created you the first time.﴾ [Surah al-An'am: 94], and He said: ﴿A seeker asked for a punishment that will occur, for the disbelievers.﴾ [Surah al-Ma'arij: 1-2]. 'Ata' said: Some ten-odd verses of the Book of Allah were revealed concerning him.

15986. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, who said: So he said, meaning al-Nadr ibn al-Harith: "O Allah, if what Muhammad says is indeed the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky or bring us a painful punishment!" Allah said: ﴿A seeker asked for a punishment that will occur, for the disbelievers.﴾

15987. Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Hakkam related to us, from 'Anbasah, from Layth, from Mujahid regarding His saying: "If this is indeed the truth from You," the verse, he said: ﴿A seeker asked for a punishment that will occur, for the disbelievers.﴾

15988. Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah regarding His saying: "And when they said, 'O Allah, if this is indeed the truth from You,'" the verse, he said: This was said by the fools and ignorant ones of this Ummah. [[In the printed edition: "sufahat hadhihi al-ummah," which departs from the manuscript and is a clear error; the correct form is "sufaha'" (plural of safih, fool), with "sufah" and "sufahah" also attested. The lexicographers say that "sifahah," "sufah," and "sufa'ih" are plurals of "safihah."]] So Allah returned with His kindness and mercy to the fools and ignorant ones of this Ummah. [[The manuscript also reads "sufahah" here, and I have left it as it is. See the earlier note. It seems to follow "juhalah" (ignorant ones), which is a feature of Arabic.]]

15989. Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: Then he mentioned the heedlessness of Quraysh and their seeking victory against themselves, when they said: "O Allah, if this is indeed the truth from You," that is, what Muhammad brought, "then rain down upon us stones from the sky," as You rained them upon the people of Lut, "or bring us a painful punishment," that is, some of what the nations before us were punished with. [[The report 15989 follows the earlier report no. 15975, and is found in Sirat Ibn Hisham 2: 325. In the printed edition: "thumma dhakara ghayrat Quraysh," which has no meaning; the correct reading from the manuscript and Ibn Hisham is "gharrat Quraysh," meaning their deception by their own affairs and their heedlessness of the truth.]]

* *

The scholars of Arabic grammar differed on the function of "huwa" (he/it) in the sentence.

Some of the Basran grammarians said: The accusative case of "al-haqq" (the truth) is because "huwa," God knows best, was transformed into an extra element in the speech, a connective of emphasis (sillat tawkid), like the extra "ma"; it is only added to every verb that does not dispense with a predicate, and it is not an adjective of "hadha" (this), for if you said, "I saw this, he," it would not be a sentence. This implied pronoun is not an adjective of the explicit noun, but it is an adjective of the implied pronoun, as in His saying: ﴿But they were the wrongdoers themselves.﴾ [Surah al-Zukhruf: 76] and ﴿Better and greater in reward, you will find it with Allah.﴾ [Surah al-Muzzammil: 20].

For you say, "I found him, he and me," so "huwa" is an adjective. [[The "adjective" here refers to the separating pronoun (damir al-fasl); see the next note, no. 4.]]

It may also in this sense be not an adjective but an extra element, as it was at first. It may also in all of this function as a noun, so that what follows it is in the nominative case, whether what follows is an explicit or implied noun, in the dialect of Banu Tamim. They say, regarding His saying, "If this is indeed the truth from You," and "But they were the wrongdoers themselves," [[In the printed edition: "al-zalimin," which departs from the manuscript and is incorrect.]] and "You will find it with Allah, he is better and greater in reward" [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "huwa khayran," which has no evidence in it; the correct reading is what I have given.]], just as you say, "their fathers were the wrongdoers," they made this implied pronoun, like "huwa," "huma," and "anta," an extra element in this position, and did not make it the place of an adjective, because it is a separator, intended to show that what follows is not an adjective of what precedes it, and there was no need for this where there is no predicate.

* *

Some of the Kufan grammarians said: "Huwa," which is the support (imad) in speech, is not added except for a sound meaning. He said: It is as if he said, "Zayd is standing," and you said, "Rather, 'Amr is the one standing," so "huwa" is for the known subject, and "al-alif wa-al-lam" (the definite article) is for the known predicate, [[Here "predicate" (al-fi'l) means the predicate.]] [and "al-alif wa-al-lam"] which is a connective in speech [[The text between the brackets has a blank in the manuscript, but the printer joined the words together. I have inserted what is between the brackets as a likely reading, and it is probably correct, God willing. "Connective" (silah) here means extra element; see the explanation of this in earlier passages.]] differing in meaning from "huwa," because its insertion and removal are the same in speech, and "huwa" is not like that. As for what is added as a connective in speech, it is an emphasis similar to their saying, "I found him himself," which you say, and it is not an adjective, like "the witty" or "the intelligent." [[See the discussion of the pronoun of support (damir al-'imad) in al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1: 50–52, 104, 248, 249, 409, 410. The earlier commentary, 2: 312, 313 and 7: 429, 430, and elsewhere, is indexed in the indexes of Arabic grammar and other subjects.]]

**The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And Allah would not punish them while you are among them, nor would Allah punish them while they seek forgiveness (33). And what is [the matter] with them that Allah should not punish them, while they bar [people] from the Sacred Mosque?﴾**

Abu Ja'far [al-Tabari] said: The interpreters (ahl al-ta'wil) differed regarding the interpretation (ta'wil) of this.

Some of them said: Its interpretation is: "And Allah would not punish them while you are among them," meaning: while you are residing among them.
