He said: This was revealed to the Prophet ﷺ while he was residing in Makkah. He said: Then the Prophet ﷺ left from among them, and those Muslims who remained there sought forgiveness, so after his departure, when they sought forgiveness there, it was revealed: "Nor would Allah punish them while they seek forgiveness." He said: Then those remaining Muslims left from among them, and Allah punished the disbelievers.

Mention of those who said this:

15990. Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Ya'qub related to us, from Ja'far ibn Abi al-Mughirah, from Ibn Abza, who said: The Prophet ﷺ was in Makkah, and Allah revealed to him: "And Allah would not punish them while you are among them." He said: Then the Prophet ﷺ went out to Madinah, and Allah revealed: "Nor would Allah punish them while they seek forgiveness." He said: Those remaining Muslims who stayed there were seeking forgiveness, meaning in Makkah. When they left, Allah revealed to him: "And what is [the matter] with them that Allah should not punish them, while they bar [people] from the Sacred Mosque, and they are not its guardians." He said: Then Allah permitted him to conquer Makkah, and that is the punishment He had promised them.

15991. Ya'qub related to me, he said: Hushaym related to us, he said: Husayn informed us, from Abu Malik, regarding His saying: "And Allah would not punish them while you are among them," meaning the Prophet ﷺ; "nor would Allah punish them while they seek forgiveness," meaning: those Muslims who were there; "and what is [the matter] with them that Allah should not punish them," meaning Makkah, and in it are the disbelievers. [[In the printed edition: "wa-fīhā al-kuffār" (and in it are the disbelievers); the manuscript reads: "bi-ghayr Makkah, wa-fīhim al-kuffār" (other than Makkah, and among them are the disbelievers). What is in the printed edition is probably more correct.]]

15992. Al-Muthanna related to me, he said: Amr ibn 'Awn related to us, he said: Hushaym informed us, from Husayn, from Abu Malik, regarding the saying of Allah: "And Allah would not punish them," meaning the people of Makkah; "nor would Allah punish them," while among them are believers who seek forgiveness, so that whoever among them of the Muslims is forgiven.

15993. Ibn Waki' related to us, he said: Ishaq ibn Isma'il al-Razi and Abu Dawud al-Hafri related to us, from Ya'qub, from Ja'far, from Ibn Abza: "Nor would Allah punish them while they seek forgiveness," he said: The remnant of those among them who remained of the Muslims. When they left, He said: "And what is [the matter] with them that Allah should not punish them." [[The report 15993: "Ishaq ibn Isma'il al-Razi" is Habbuwayh Abu Yazid, mentioned several times before, the last of which was number 15311.]]

15994. ...... He said: Imran ibn 'Uyaynah related to us, from Husayn, from Abu Malik: "And Allah would not punish them while you are among them," he said: the people of Makkah.

15995. ...... And my father informed us, from Salamah ibn Nubayt, from al-Dahhak: "Nor would Allah punish them while they seek forgiveness," he said: the believers among the people of Makkah; "And what is [the matter] with them that Allah should not punish them while they bar [people] from the Sacred Mosque," he said: the polytheists among the people of Makkah.

15996. ...... He said: Abu Khalid related to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak: "Nor would Allah punish them while they seek forgiveness," he said: the believers seek forgiveness among themselves.

15997. Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, he said: My father related to me, he said: My paternal uncle related to me, he said: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: "Nor would Allah punish them while they seek forgiveness," meaning: those who believed with you seek forgiveness in Makkah, until He brings you out, and those who believed with you.

15998. al-Qasim related to us, he said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Hajjaj related to me, he said: Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn 'Abbas said: He does not punish a town until the Prophet and those who believe with him have left it, and he has joined the place where he was commanded [to go]. "Nor would Allah punish them while they seek forgiveness," meaning the believers. Then he returned to the polytheists and said: "And what is [the matter] with them that Allah should not punish them."

15999. Yunus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: "And Allah would not punish them while you are among them," he said: meaning the people of Makkah.

* *

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: And Allah would not punish these polytheists of Quraysh in Makkah while you, O Muhammad, are among them, until He brings you out from among them. "Nor would Allah punish them," and these polytheists were saying: "O Lord, [we seek] Your forgiveness!" and what resembles that of the meanings of seeking forgiveness by speech. They said: As for His saying: "And what is [the matter] with them that Allah should not punish them," it refers to the Hereafter.

Mention of those who said this:

16000. Ahmad ibn Mansur al-Ramadi related to us, he said: Abu Hudhayfah related to us, he said: 'Ikrimah related to us, from Abu Zumayl, from Ibn 'Abbas: The polytheists used to circumambulate the House, saying: "Here I am, here I am, You have no partner," and the Prophet ﷺ would say: "Qad, qad!" [[Qad, qad means: "enough for you, do not add [more]." It is said: qadaka, meaning "enough for you," and it is used to express deterrence and reproach.]] So they would say: "Except a partner who is Yours, You own him and what he owns," [[The printed edition added an unnecessary addition, writing: "fa-yaqūlūn: lā sharīka laka, illā sharīkan huwa laka" (so they say: You have no partner, except a partner who is Yours).]] and they would say: "Your forgiveness, Your forgiveness!" So Allah revealed: "And Allah would not punish them while you are among them, nor would Allah punish them while they seek forgiveness." Ibn 'Abbas said: There were two securities among them: the Prophet of Allah and the seeking of forgiveness. He said: The Prophet ﷺ departed, and the seeking of forgiveness remained. "And what is [the matter] with them that Allah should not punish them, while they bar [people] from the Sacred Mosque, and they are not its guardians; its guardians are only the God-fearing," he said: This is the punishment of the Hereafter. He said: And that is the punishment of this world. [[The report 16000: "Abu Zumayl" is Simak ibn al-Walid al-Hanafi al-Yamami, mentioned under numbers 13832 and 15734.]]

16001. al-Harith related to me, he said: 'Abd al-'Aziz related to us, he said: Abu Ma'shar related to us, from Yazid ibn Ruman and Muhammad ibn Qays, who both said: Quraysh said to one another: Muhammad, may Allah honor him, is from among us: "O Allah, if this is the truth from You, then rain down upon us," the verse. When it was evening, they regretted what they had said, and said: "Your forgiveness, O Allah!" So Allah revealed: "And Allah would not punish them while they seek forgiveness," up to His saying: "they do not know."

16002. Ibn Humayd related to me, he said: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: They used to say, meaning the polytheists: By Allah, Allah will not punish us while we seek forgiveness, and He does not punish a nation while its prophet is with them until He removes him from it! This was among their statements, while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was among them. Allah said to His Prophet ﷺ, mentioning to him their ignorance, their delusion, and their seeking victory over themselves when they said: "O Allah, if this is the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky," as You rained them upon the people of Lot. And when He reproached them for their evil deeds, He said: "And Allah would not punish them while you are among them, nor would Allah punish them while they seek forgiveness," meaning: because of their saying: "We seek forgiveness while Muhammad is among us." "And what is [the matter] with them that Allah should not punish them," even though you are among them, and even though they seek forgiveness as they claim, "while they bar [people] from the Sacred Mosque," meaning: those who believe in Allah and worship Him, meaning: you and those who follow you. [[The printed and manuscript texts both read this sentence as: "ay bi-qawlihim, wa-in kānū yastaghfirūn kamā qāla wa-hum yaṣuddūn..." with an omission of what is necessary and a distortion. I have restored the correct wording within parentheses, and the rest of the phrasing is from Ibn Hisham's Sirah.]] [[The report 16003: Sirah of Ibn Hisham 2:325, which continues the earlier report numbered 15989.]]

16003. al-Hasan ibn al-Sabbah al-Bazzar ..................... related to us, he said: Abu Burdah related to us, from Abu Musa, who said: There were two securities before, the saying: "And Allah would not punish them while you are among them, nor would Allah punish them while they seek forgiveness." He said: As for the Prophet ﷺ, he has passed away; as for the seeking of forgiveness, it remains among you until the Day of Resurrection. [[The report 16004: "al-Hasan ibn al-Sabbah al-Bazzar" is a teacher of al-Tabari, mentioned under numbers 4442 and 9857. This chain has many narrators dropped from it, and in the manuscript it reads "Burdah," so the editor made it "Abu Burdah," and he was right without knowing it.
A similar report was also transmitted in raised (marfu') form by al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan, in the commentary on this surah, and its chain is: "Sufyan ibn Waki' related to us, Ibn Numayr related to us, from Isma'il ibn Ibrahim ibn Muhajir, from 'Abbad ibn Yusuf, from Abu Burdah ibn Abi Musa, from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: Allah has revealed to me two securities for my nation: 'And Allah would not punish them while you are among them, nor would Allah punish them while they seek forgiveness.' So when I pass away, I leave among them the seeking of forgiveness until the Day of Resurrection."
Al-Tirmidhi then said: "This is a gharib (rare) hadith, and Isma'il ibn Ibrahim is weak in hadith."
As for the report of al-Tabari, there is no doubt that it is a mawquf (halted) report, attributed to Abu Musa al-Ash'ari.
In the printed edition it reads: "innahu kāna fīkum amānān" (there were among you two securities), differing from the manuscript, and the correct reading is what I have indicated.]]

16004. al-Harith related to me, he said: 'Abd al-'Aziz related to us, he said: Yunus ibn Abi Ishaq related to us, from 'Amir Abu al-Khattab al-Thawri, who said: I heard Abu al-'Ala' say: The nation of Muhammad ﷺ had two securities: one of them has departed and the other remains: "And Allah would not punish them while you are among them," the verse. [[The report 16005: "'Amir, Abu al-Khattab al-Thawri": I have not found any mention of him, and I fear that his name may contain a distortion.]]

* *

Others said: The meaning of that is: "And Allah would not punish them while you are among them," O Muhammad, and Allah would not punish the polytheists while they seek forgiveness, that is: if they had sought forgiveness. They said: But they did not seek forgiveness, so when they did not seek forgiveness, He, may His praise be exalted, said: "And what is [the matter] with them that Allah should not punish them, while they bar [people] from the Sacred Mosque."

Mention of those who said this:

16005. Bishr ibn Mu'adh related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah: "And Allah would not punish them while you are among them, nor would Allah punish them while they seek forgiveness," he said: The people did not seek forgiveness, and if they had sought forgiveness they would not have been punished. Some people of knowledge used to say: There are two securities which Allah revealed: as for one of them, it has passed away, the Prophet of Allah. As for the other, Allah has kept it as a mercy among you, which is seeking forgiveness and repentance.

16006. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to me, he said: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, he said: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, who said: Allah said to His Messenger: "And Allah would not punish them while you are among them, nor would Allah punish them while they seek forgiveness," meaning: I would not punish them while they seek forgiveness, and if they had sought forgiveness and acknowledged their sins, they would have been believers. And how would I not punish them when they do not seek forgiveness? "And what is [the matter] with them that Allah should not punish them, while they bar [people] from Muhammad and from the Sacred Mosque?"

16007. Yunus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: "And Allah would not punish them while you are among them, nor would Allah punish them while they seek forgiveness," he said: He means: if they had sought forgiveness, I would not have punished them.

Others said: The meaning of that is: And Allah would not punish them while they are submitting [to Islam]. They said: And "their seeking forgiveness" in this context means their submission [to Islam].

Mention of those who said this:

16008. Suwwar ibn 'Abd Allah related to us, he said: 'Abd al-Malik ibn al-Sabbah related to us, he said: Imran ibn Hudayr related to us, from 'Ikrimah, regarding His saying: "And Allah would not punish them while you are among them, nor would Allah punish them while they seek forgiveness," he said: They asked for punishment, so He said: He would not punish them while you are among them, and He would not punish them while they are entering Islam.

16009. Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, he said: Abu 'Asim related to us, he said: 'Isa related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: "While you are among them," he said: among them. And His saying: "While they seek forgiveness," he said: they submit.

16010. al-Muthanna related to me, he said: Abu Hudhayfah related to us, he said: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "And Allah would not punish them while you are among them," among them. "Nor would Allah punish them while they seek forgiveness," he said: and they are submitting [[In the manuscript: "wa-hum muslimūn," and the correct reading is what is in the printed edition.]]. "And what is [the matter] with them that Allah should not punish them, while they bar," Quraysh, "from the Sacred Mosque." [[(2) In the printed edition, the verse was given without a break, which is his saying: "Quraysh," which I have included from the manuscript. The manuscript reads: "wa-hum muslimūn yu'adhdhibuhum Allah" (while they are submitting, Allah punishes them), with a blank space between the two statements, and in the margin there is the letter (ṭ) indicating an error.]]

16011. al-Harith related to me, he said: 'Abd al-'Aziz related to us, he said: Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd Allah related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "And Allah would not punish them while you are among them," he said: among them. "Nor would Allah punish them while they seek forgiveness," he said: their entry into Islam.

* *

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: And among them are those for whom Allah has already decreed entry into Islam.

Mention of those who said this:

16012. al-Muthanna related to me, he said: Abu Salih related to us, he said: Mu'awiyah related to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: "And Allah would not punish them while you are among them," he means: Allah, glorified is He, would not punish a people while their prophets are among them until He brings them out. Then He said: "Nor would Allah punish them while they seek forgiveness," he means: and among them are those for whom Allah has already decreed entry into faith, and that is seeking forgiveness. Then He said: "And what is [the matter] with them that Allah should not punish them," so He punished them on the day of Badr by the sword.

* *

Others said: Rather, its meaning is: "Nor would Allah punish them while they pray."

Mention of those who said this:

16013. al-Muthanna related to me, he said: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih related to us, he said: Mu'awiyah related to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: "Nor would Allah punish them while they seek forgiveness," meaning: they pray, meaning by this the people of Makkah.

16014. Musa ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Masruqi related to me, he said: Husayn al-Ju'fi related to us, from Za'idah, from Mansur, from Mujahid, regarding the saying of Allah: "And Allah would not punish them while you are among them, nor would Allah punish them while they seek forgiveness," he said: they pray.

16015. It was related to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd ibn Sulayman related to us, he said: I heard al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim say, regarding His saying: "And Allah would not punish them while you are among them," meaning: the people of Makkah. He says: I would not have punished you while Muhammad is among you. Then He said: "Nor would Allah punish them while they seek forgiveness," meaning: they believe and pray.

16016. Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Jarir related to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: "Nor would Allah punish them while they seek forgiveness," he said: while they pray.

* *

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: And Allah would not punish the polytheists while they seek forgiveness.

They said: Then that was abrogated (naskh) by His saying: "And what is [the matter] with them that Allah should not punish them, while they bar [people] from the Sacred Mosque."

Mention of those who said this:

16017. Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Yahya ibn Wadih related to us, from al-Husayn ibn Waqid, from Yazid al-Nahwi, from 'Ikrimah and al-Hasan al-Basri, who both said, regarding [the sura of] "al-Anfal": "And Allah would not punish them while you are among them, nor would Allah punish them while they seek forgiveness," which was abrogated by the verse that follows it: "And what is [the matter] with them that Allah should not punish them," up to His saying: "So taste the punishment because of what you used to disbelieve." So they were fought in Makkah, and hunger and siege afflicted them there.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of these opinions in my view is the statement of the one who said: Its interpretation is: "And Allah would not punish them while you are among them," O Muhammad, and while you remain residing among them, until He brings you out from among them, because I do not destroy a town while its prophet is in it; "nor would Allah punish them while they seek forgiveness," from their sins and their disbelief, but they do not seek forgiveness from that; rather they persist in it, and so they deserve punishment. This is like saying: "I would not do good to you while you do evil to me," meaning: I do not do good to you when you do evil to me. If you did evil to me, I would not do good to you; rather I do good to you because you do not do evil to me. And likewise that. Then it is said: "And what is [the matter] with them that Allah should not punish them, while they bar [people] from the Sacred Mosque?" meaning: What is their situation, and what prevents them from being punished by Allah, while they do not seek forgiveness from Allah for their disbelief, so that they might believe in Him, and while they bar the believers in Allah and His Messenger from the Sacred Mosque? [[See the explanation of "mālak" (what is with you) in what preceded: 5:301, 302; 9:7.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 8, verses 33–34 (part 2 of 2):

We said, "This view is the most correct of the views on this matter," because the people, meaning the polytheists of Mecca, had sought to hasten the punishment. They said, "O Allah, if this is indeed the truth from You, then rain down on us stones from the sky, or bring us a painful punishment." So Allah said to His Prophet, ﴿And Allah would not punish them while you are among them, nor would Allah punish them while they seek forgiveness. And why should Allah not punish them when they bar access to al-Masjid al-Haram, though they are not its guardians?﴾ Thus He, great is His praise, informed him that those who sought to hasten the punishment would certainly be overtaken by it and would descend upon them, [[In the printed edition: "that those who sought to hasten the punishment will be overtaken by it." In the manuscript it is as I have recorded, except that it was written "ḥāq" in place of "ḥāʾiq," which is an error.]] and He informed them of the moment of its descent upon them, which would come after his expulsion from among them. There is no basis for threatening them with punishment in the Hereafter, when they were seeking it in this world, and there is no doubt that in the Hereafter they will reach the punishment. Rather, Allah's hastening of that punishment for them on the day of Badr is clear evidence that the meaning is what we have stated.

Likewise, there is no basis for the view of those who take the statement ﴿And Allah would not punish them while they seek forgiveness﴾ to refer to the believers, since it is within a report about them and about what Allah will do to them. There is no evidence that the report about them has ended, and the pronoun was used to refer to them. [[In the printed edition: "and that it was about them that it was intended, and there is no disagreement about its interpretation." In the manuscript, as I have recorded, the word "kunniya" [was referred] has dropped out, as I have placed in parentheses. I suspect there is a gap in the text.]]

Abu Ja'far al-Nahhas mentioned this opinion in his book Nasikh wa-l-Mansukh (Abrogating and Abrogated), p. 154, and then said: "He made the two pronouns refer to different groups, and this is a good view, although Muhammad ibn Jarir denied it, because he claimed that there had been no prior mention of the believers that would make a pronoun refer to them. This is a mistake, because the believers have been mentioned in more than one place in the surah.

If it is said: their mention did not precede this place.

The answer: the meaning itself indicates their mention in this place. Those among the disbelievers who said, 'O Allah, if this is the truth from You, then rain down on us stones from the sky,' said that only mockingly and obstinately. Had they sought the truth, they would have said, 'O Allah, if this is the truth from You, then guide us to it.' But they disbelieved and denied that Allah would send a messenger with revelation from Him. That is, [they said]: 'O Allah, if this is the truth from You, then destroy the group of disbelievers and Muslims.' This is the meaning of the mention of the Muslims, so the meaning becomes: How could Allah destroy the Muslims? This is the sense of ﴿Allah would not punish them while they seek forgiveness﴾, meaning the believers, and ﴿Why should Allah not punish them?﴾, meaning the disbelievers."

And there is no disagreement among the people of interpretation (ta'wil, meaning the explanation of what a verse signifies) about this.

Likewise, there is no basis for the view of those who say that this verse is abrogated by ﴿And why should Allah not punish them when they bar access to al-Masjid al-Haram﴾, and the verse that follows, because His statement, great is His praise, ﴿And Allah would not punish them while they seek forgiveness﴾ is a report, and a report cannot contain abrogation. Abrogation (naskh, the cancelling of a previous ruling by a later one) applies only to commands and prohibitions.

* *

The grammarians differed concerning the reason for the particle "an" (that) entering the statement ﴿And why should Allah not punish them﴾.

Some grammarians of Basra said: it is superfluous here, and it has operated as "lā" (not) operates, though "lā" is also superfluous. There appears in poetry (this is by al-Farazdaq):

"Had Ghatafan had no grievances (dhunub) against me, the nobles of its lineages would have blamed 'Umar."

[[The line has already been cited and its sources given at 5:302–303, where its wording is: "then the nobles of its lineages would have blamed [him]," and I explained it there, and claimed that "dhunub" with a fatha on the dhal means a share or portion of honor, lineage and manliness. The wording of the line as it appears here and in the Diwan requires that "dhunub" be the plural of "dhanb" (grievance). This is the difference between the two readings and the two meanings.]]

Some grammarians denied this view and said: "an" is not introduced except for a correct meaning, because the meaning of ﴿And what is with them﴾ is: what prevents them from being punished? So "an" entered for this meaning, and it is taken out with "lā" so that it is known that the sense is negation, since prevention is a negation. He said: "lā" in the line is correct in meaning, because when negation is applied to something, it becomes an affirmation. [[By "affirmation" he means an assertion.]]

He said: Do you not see your saying, "Zayd is not not standing," which affirms the standing? He said: Likewise "lā" in this line. [[See Ma'ani al-Qur'an by al-Farra' 1:163–166, and the earlier exegesis at 5:300–305.]]

* *

The interpretation of His statement: ﴿And they were not its guardians. Its guardians are only the God-fearing, but most of them do not know.﴾ (34)

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: And these polytheists have no reason that Allah should not punish them while they bar access to al-Masjid al-Haram, and they were not the guardians of Allah. ﴿Its guardians are only﴾ means: the guardians of Allah are only ﴿the God-fearing﴾, meaning those who fear Allah by performing His obligations and avoiding His prohibitions. ﴿But most of them do not know﴾ means: but most of the polytheists do not know that the guardians of Allah are the God-fearing; rather, they assume that they themselves are the guardians of Allah.

* *

The people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said.

Those who said this:

16018 – Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿And they were not its guardians. Its guardians are only the God-fearing﴾: they are the companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

16019 – Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning Allah's words: ﴿Its guardians are only the God-fearing﴾: whoever they may be, and wherever they may be.

16020 – al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similarly.

16021 – Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: ﴿And they were not its guardians. Its guardians are only the God-fearing﴾, those who honor its sanctity [[In the printed and manuscript editions the phrase reads "yakhrujūna minhu" (they leave it) in place of "yuḥarrimūna ḥurmatahu" (they honor its sanctity). This is one of the strange distortions that comes from abridgement. The correct reading is from Sirat Ibn Hisham.]] and establish the prayer there, meaning: you, that is the Prophet (ﷺ), and those who believed in you. ﴿But most of them do not know.﴾ [[The report 16021 is in Sirat Ibn Hisham 2:325–326, and it continues the earlier report numbered 16003.]]

**The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And Allah would not punish them while you are among them, nor would Allah punish them while they seek forgiveness (33). And what is [the matter] with them that Allah should not punish them, while they bar [people] from the Sacred Mosque?﴾**

Abu Ja'far [al-Tabari] said: The interpreters (ahl al-ta'wil) differed regarding the interpretation (ta'wil) of this.

Some of them said: Its interpretation is: "And Allah would not punish them while you are among them," meaning: while you are residing among them. He said: This was revealed to the Prophet ﷺ while he was residing in Makkah. He said: Then the Prophet ﷺ left from among them, and those Muslims who remained there sought forgiveness, so after his departure, when they sought forgiveness there, it was revealed: "Nor would Allah punish them while they seek forgiveness." He said: Then those remaining Muslims left from among them, and Allah punished the disbelievers.

Mention of those who said this:

15990. Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Ya'qub related to us, from Ja'far ibn Abi al-Mughirah, from Ibn Abza, who said: The Prophet ﷺ was in Makkah, and Allah revealed to him: "And Allah would not punish them while you are among them." He said: Then the Prophet ﷺ went out to Madinah, and Allah revealed: "Nor would Allah punish them while they seek forgiveness." He said: Those remaining Muslims who stayed there were seeking forgiveness, meaning in Makkah. When they left, Allah revealed to him: "And what is [the matter] with them that Allah should not punish them, while they bar [people] from the Sacred Mosque, and they are not its guardians." He said: Then Allah permitted him to conquer Makkah, and that is the punishment He had promised them.

15991. Ya'qub related to me, he said: Hushaym related to us, he said: Husayn informed us, from Abu Malik, regarding His saying: "And Allah would not punish them while you are among them," meaning the Prophet ﷺ; "nor would Allah punish them while they seek forgiveness," meaning: those Muslims who were there; "and what is [the matter] with them that Allah should not punish them," meaning Makkah, and in it are the disbelievers. [[In the printed edition: "wa-fīhā al-kuffār" (and in it are the disbelievers); the manuscript reads: "bi-ghayr Makkah, wa-fīhim al-kuffār" (other than Makkah, and among them are the disbelievers). What is in the printed edition is probably more correct.]]

15992. Al-Muthanna related to me, he said: Amr ibn 'Awn related to us, he said: Hushaym informed us, from Husayn, from Abu Malik, regarding the saying of Allah: "And Allah would not punish them," meaning the people of Makkah; "nor would Allah punish them," while among them are believers who seek forgiveness, so that whoever among them of the Muslims is forgiven.

15993. Ibn Waki' related to us, he said: Ishaq ibn Isma'il al-Razi and Abu Dawud al-Hafri related to us, from Ya'qub, from Ja'far, from Ibn Abza: "Nor would Allah punish them while they seek forgiveness," he said: The remnant of those among them who remained of the Muslims. When they left, He said: "And what is [the matter] with them that Allah should not punish them." [[The report 15993: "Ishaq ibn Isma'il al-Razi" is Habbuwayh Abu Yazid, mentioned several times before, the last of which was number 15311.]]

15994. ...... He said: Imran ibn 'Uyaynah related to us, from Husayn, from Abu Malik: "And Allah would not punish them while you are among them," he said: the people of Makkah.

15995. ...... And my father informed us, from Salamah ibn Nubayt, from al-Dahhak: "Nor would Allah punish them while they seek forgiveness," he said: the believers among the people of Makkah; "And what is [the matter] with them that Allah should not punish them while they bar [people] from the Sacred Mosque," he said: the polytheists among the people of Makkah.

15996. ...... He said: Abu Khalid related to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak: "Nor would Allah punish them while they seek forgiveness," he said: the believers seek forgiveness among themselves.

15997. Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, he said: My father related to me, he said: My paternal uncle related to me, he said: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: "Nor would Allah punish them while they seek forgiveness," meaning: those who believed with you seek forgiveness in Makkah, until He brings you out, and those who believed with you.

15998. al-Qasim related to us, he said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Hajjaj related to me, he said: Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn 'Abbas said: He does not punish a town until the Prophet and those who believe with him have left it, and he has joined the place where he was commanded [to go]. "Nor would Allah punish them while they seek forgiveness," meaning the believers. Then he returned to the polytheists and said: "And what is [the matter] with them that Allah should not punish them."

15999. Yunus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: "And Allah would not punish them while you are among them," he said: meaning the people of Makkah.

* *

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: And Allah would not punish these polytheists of Quraysh in Makkah while you, O Muhammad, are among them, until He brings you out from among them. "Nor would Allah punish them," and these polytheists were saying: "O Lord, [we seek] Your forgiveness!" and what resembles that of the meanings of seeking forgiveness by speech. They said: As for His saying: "And what is [the matter] with them that Allah should not punish them," it refers to the Hereafter.

Mention of those who said this:

16000. Ahmad ibn Mansur al-Ramadi related to us, he said: Abu Hudhayfah related to us, he said: 'Ikrimah related to us, from Abu Zumayl, from Ibn 'Abbas: The polytheists used to circumambulate the House, saying: "Here I am, here I am, You have no partner," and the Prophet ﷺ would say: "Qad, qad!" [[Qad, qad means: "enough for you, do not add [more]." It is said: qadaka, meaning "enough for you," and it is used to express deterrence and reproach.]] So they would say: "Except a partner who is Yours, You own him and what he owns," [[The printed edition added an unnecessary addition, writing: "fa-yaqūlūn: lā sharīka laka, illā sharīkan huwa laka" (so they say: You have no partner, except a partner who is Yours).]] and they would say: "Your forgiveness, Your forgiveness!" So Allah revealed: "And Allah would not punish them while you are among them, nor would Allah punish them while they seek forgiveness." Ibn 'Abbas said: There were two securities among them: the Prophet of Allah and the seeking of forgiveness. He said: The Prophet ﷺ departed, and the seeking of forgiveness remained. "And what is [the matter] with them that Allah should not punish them, while they bar [people] from the Sacred Mosque, and they are not its guardians; its guardians are only the God-fearing," he said: This is the punishment of the Hereafter. He said: And that is the punishment of this world. [[The report 16000: "Abu Zumayl" is Simak ibn al-Walid al-Hanafi al-Yamami, mentioned under numbers 13832 and 15734.]]

16001. al-Harith related to me, he said: 'Abd al-'Aziz related to us, he said: Abu Ma'shar related to us, from Yazid ibn Ruman and Muhammad ibn Qays, who both said: Quraysh said to one another: Muhammad, may Allah honor him, is from among us: "O Allah, if this is the truth from You, then rain down upon us," the verse. When it was evening, they regretted what they had said, and said: "Your forgiveness, O Allah!" So Allah revealed: "And Allah would not punish them while they seek forgiveness," up to His saying: "they do not know."

16002. Ibn Humayd related to me, he said: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: They used to say, meaning the polytheists: By Allah, Allah will not punish us while we seek forgiveness, and He does not punish a nation while its prophet is with them until He removes him from it! This was among their statements, while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was among them. Allah said to His Prophet ﷺ, mentioning to him their ignorance, their delusion, and their seeking victory over themselves when they said: "O Allah, if this is the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky," as You rained them upon the people of Lot. And when He reproached them for their evil deeds, He said: "And Allah would not punish them while you are among them, nor would Allah punish them while they seek forgiveness," meaning: because of their saying: "We seek forgiveness while Muhammad is among us." "And what is [the matter] with them that Allah should not punish them," even though you are among them, and even though they seek forgiveness as they claim, "while they bar [people] from the Sacred Mosque," meaning: those who believe in Allah and worship Him, meaning: you and those who follow you. [[The printed and manuscript texts both read this sentence as: "ay bi-qawlihim, wa-in kānū yastaghfirūn kamā qāla wa-hum yaṣuddūn..." with an omission of what is necessary and a distortion. I have restored the correct wording within parentheses, and the rest of the phrasing is from Ibn Hisham's Sirah.]] [[The report 16003: Sirah of Ibn Hisham 2:325, which continues the earlier report numbered 15989.]]

16003. al-Hasan ibn al-Sabbah al-Bazzar ..................... related to us, he said: Abu Burdah related to us, from Abu Musa, who said: There were two securities before, the saying: "And Allah would not punish them while you are among them, nor would Allah punish them while they seek forgiveness." He said: As for the Prophet ﷺ, he has passed away; as for the seeking of forgiveness, it remains among you until the Day of Resurrection. [[The report 16004: "al-Hasan ibn al-Sabbah al-Bazzar" is a teacher of al-Tabari, mentioned under numbers 4442 and 9857. This chain has many narrators dropped from it, and in the manuscript it reads "Burdah," so the editor made it "Abu Burdah," and he was right without knowing it.
A similar report was also transmitted in raised (marfu') form by al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan, in the commentary on this surah, and its chain is: "Sufyan ibn Waki' related to us, Ibn Numayr related to us, from Isma'il ibn Ibrahim ibn Muhajir, from 'Abbad ibn Yusuf, from Abu Burdah ibn Abi Musa, from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: Allah has revealed to me two securities for my nation: 'And Allah would not punish them while you are among them, nor would Allah punish them while they seek forgiveness.' So when I pass away, I leave among them the seeking of forgiveness until the Day of Resurrection."
Al-Tirmidhi then said: "This is a gharib (rare) hadith, and Isma'il ibn Ibrahim is weak in hadith."
As for the report of al-Tabari, there is no doubt that it is a mawquf (halted) report, attributed to Abu Musa al-Ash'ari.
In the printed edition it reads: "innahu kāna fīkum amānān" (there were among you two securities), differing from the manuscript, and the correct reading is what I have indicated.]]

16004. al-Harith related to me, he said: 'Abd al-'Aziz related to us, he said: Yunus ibn Abi Ishaq related to us, from 'Amir Abu al-Khattab al-Thawri, who said: I heard Abu al-'Ala' say: The nation of Muhammad ﷺ had two securities: one of them has departed and the other remains: "And Allah would not punish them while you are among them," the verse. [[The report 16005: "'Amir, Abu al-Khattab al-Thawri": I have not found any mention of him, and I fear that his name may contain a distortion.]]

* *

Others said: The meaning of that is: "And Allah would not punish them while you are among them," O Muhammad, and Allah would not punish the polytheists while they seek forgiveness, that is: if they had sought forgiveness. They said: But they did not seek forgiveness, so when they did not seek forgiveness, He, may His praise be exalted, said: "And what is [the matter] with them that Allah should not punish them, while they bar [people] from the Sacred Mosque."

Mention of those who said this:

16005. Bishr ibn Mu'adh related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah: "And Allah would not punish them while you are among them, nor would Allah punish them while they seek forgiveness," he said: The people did not seek forgiveness, and if they had sought forgiveness they would not have been punished. Some people of knowledge used to say: There are two securities which Allah revealed: as for one of them, it has passed away, the Prophet of Allah. As for the other, Allah has kept it as a mercy among you, which is seeking forgiveness and repentance.

16006. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to me, he said: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, he said: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, who said: Allah said to His Messenger: "And Allah would not punish them while you are among them, nor would Allah punish them while they seek forgiveness," meaning: I would not punish them while they seek forgiveness, and if they had sought forgiveness and acknowledged their sins, they would have been believers. And how would I not punish them when they do not seek forgiveness? "And what is [the matter] with them that Allah should not punish them, while they bar [people] from Muhammad and from the Sacred Mosque?"

16007. Yunus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: "And Allah would not punish them while you are among them, nor would Allah punish them while they seek forgiveness," he said: He means: if they had sought forgiveness, I would not have punished them.

Others said: The meaning of that is: And Allah would not punish them while they are submitting [to Islam]. They said: And "their seeking forgiveness" in this context means their submission [to Islam].

Mention of those who said this:

16008. Suwwar ibn 'Abd Allah related to us, he said: 'Abd al-Malik ibn al-Sabbah related to us, he said: Imran ibn Hudayr related to us, from 'Ikrimah, regarding His saying: "And Allah would not punish them while you are among them, nor would Allah punish them while they seek forgiveness," he said: They asked for punishment, so He said: He would not punish them while you are among them, and He would not punish them while they are entering Islam.

16009. Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, he said: Abu 'Asim related to us, he said: 'Isa related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: "While you are among them," he said: among them. And His saying: "While they seek forgiveness," he said: they submit.

16010. al-Muthanna related to me, he said: Abu Hudhayfah related to us, he said: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "And Allah would not punish them while you are among them," among them. "Nor would Allah punish them while they seek forgiveness," he said: and they are submitting [[In the manuscript: "wa-hum muslimūn," and the correct reading is what is in the printed edition.]]. "And what is [the matter] with them that Allah should not punish them, while they bar," Quraysh, "from the Sacred Mosque." [[(2) In the printed edition, the verse was given without a break, which is his saying: "Quraysh," which I have included from the manuscript. The manuscript reads: "wa-hum muslimūn yu'adhdhibuhum Allah" (while they are submitting, Allah punishes them), with a blank space between the two statements, and in the margin there is the letter (ṭ) indicating an error.]]

16011. al-Harith related to me, he said: 'Abd al-'Aziz related to us, he said: Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd Allah related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "And Allah would not punish them while you are among them," he said: among them. "Nor would Allah punish them while they seek forgiveness," he said: their entry into Islam.

* *

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: And among them are those for whom Allah has already decreed entry into Islam.

Mention of those who said this:

16012. al-Muthanna related to me, he said: Abu Salih related to us, he said: Mu'awiyah related to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: "And Allah would not punish them while you are among them," he means: Allah, glorified is He, would not punish a people while their prophets are among them until He brings them out. Then He said: "Nor would Allah punish them while they seek forgiveness," he means: and among them are those for whom Allah has already decreed entry into faith, and that is seeking forgiveness. Then He said: "And what is [the matter] with them that Allah should not punish them," so He punished them on the day of Badr by the sword.

* *

Others said: Rather, its meaning is: "Nor would Allah punish them while they pray."

Mention of those who said this:

16013. al-Muthanna related to me, he said: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih related to us, he said: Mu'awiyah related to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: "Nor would Allah punish them while they seek forgiveness," meaning: they pray, meaning by this the people of Makkah.

16014. Musa ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Masruqi related to me, he said: Husayn al-Ju'fi related to us, from Za'idah, from Mansur, from Mujahid, regarding the saying of Allah: "And Allah would not punish them while you are among them, nor would Allah punish them while they seek forgiveness," he said: they pray.

16015. It was related to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd ibn Sulayman related to us, he said: I heard al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim say, regarding His saying: "And Allah would not punish them while you are among them," meaning: the people of Makkah. He says: I would not have punished you while Muhammad is among you. Then He said: "Nor would Allah punish them while they seek forgiveness," meaning: they believe and pray.

16016. Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Jarir related to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: "Nor would Allah punish them while they seek forgiveness," he said: while they pray.

* *

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: And Allah would not punish the polytheists while they seek forgiveness.

They said: Then that was abrogated (naskh) by His saying: "And what is [the matter] with them that Allah should not punish them, while they bar [people] from the Sacred Mosque."

Mention of those who said this:

16017. Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Yahya ibn Wadih related to us, from al-Husayn ibn Waqid, from Yazid al-Nahwi, from 'Ikrimah and al-Hasan al-Basri, who both said, regarding [the sura of] "al-Anfal": "And Allah would not punish them while you are among them, nor would Allah punish them while they seek forgiveness," which was abrogated by the verse that follows it: "And what is [the matter] with them that Allah should not punish them," up to His saying: "So taste the punishment because of what you used to disbelieve." So they were fought in Makkah, and hunger and siege afflicted them there.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of these opinions in my view is the statement of the one who said: Its interpretation is: "And Allah would not punish them while you are among them," O Muhammad, and while you remain residing among them, until He brings you out from among them, because I do not destroy a town while its prophet is in it; "nor would Allah punish them while they seek forgiveness," from their sins and their disbelief, but they do not seek forgiveness from that; rather they persist in it, and so they deserve punishment. This is like saying: "I would not do good to you while you do evil to me," meaning: I do not do good to you when you do evil to me. If you did evil to me, I would not do good to you; rather I do good to you because you do not do evil to me. And likewise that. Then it is said: "And what is [the matter] with them that Allah should not punish them, while they bar [people] from the Sacred Mosque?" meaning: What is their situation, and what prevents them from being punished by Allah, while they do not seek forgiveness from Allah for their disbelief, so that they might believe in Him, and while they bar the believers in Allah and His Messenger from the Sacred Mosque? [[See the explanation of "mālak" (what is with you) in what preceded: 5:301, 302; 9:7.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 8, verses 33–34 (part 2 of 2):

We said, "This view is the most correct of the views on this matter," because the people, meaning the polytheists of Mecca, had sought to hasten the punishment. They said, "O Allah, if this is indeed the truth from You, then rain down on us stones from the sky, or bring us a painful punishment." So Allah said to His Prophet, ﴿And Allah would not punish them while you are among them, nor would Allah punish them while they seek forgiveness. And why should Allah not punish them when they bar access to al-Masjid al-Haram, though they are not its guardians?﴾ Thus He, great is His praise, informed him that those who sought to hasten the punishment would certainly be overtaken by it and would descend upon them, [[In the printed edition: "that those who sought to hasten the punishment will be overtaken by it." In the manuscript it is as I have recorded, except that it was written "ḥāq" in place of "ḥāʾiq," which is an error.]] and He informed them of the moment of its descent upon them, which would come after his expulsion from among them. There is no basis for threatening them with punishment in the Hereafter, when they were seeking it in this world, and there is no doubt that in the Hereafter they will reach the punishment. Rather, Allah's hastening of that punishment for them on the day of Badr is clear evidence that the meaning is what we have stated.

Likewise, there is no basis for the view of those who take the statement ﴿And Allah would not punish them while they seek forgiveness﴾ to refer to the believers, since it is within a report about them and about what Allah will do to them. There is no evidence that the report about them has ended, and the pronoun was used to refer to them. [[In the printed edition: "and that it was about them that it was intended, and there is no disagreement about its interpretation." In the manuscript, as I have recorded, the word "kunniya" [was referred] has dropped out, as I have placed in parentheses. I suspect there is a gap in the text.]]

Abu Ja'far al-Nahhas mentioned this opinion in his book Nasikh wa-l-Mansukh (Abrogating and Abrogated), p. 154, and then said: "He made the two pronouns refer to different groups, and this is a good view, although Muhammad ibn Jarir denied it, because he claimed that there had been no prior mention of the believers that would make a pronoun refer to them. This is a mistake, because the believers have been mentioned in more than one place in the surah.

If it is said: their mention did not precede this place.

The answer: the meaning itself indicates their mention in this place. Those among the disbelievers who said, 'O Allah, if this is the truth from You, then rain down on us stones from the sky,' said that only mockingly and obstinately. Had they sought the truth, they would have said, 'O Allah, if this is the truth from You, then guide us to it.' But they disbelieved and denied that Allah would send a messenger with revelation from Him. That is, [they said]: 'O Allah, if this is the truth from You, then destroy the group of disbelievers and Muslims.' This is the meaning of the mention of the Muslims, so the meaning becomes: How could Allah destroy the Muslims? This is the sense of ﴿Allah would not punish them while they seek forgiveness﴾, meaning the believers, and ﴿Why should Allah not punish them?﴾, meaning the disbelievers."

And there is no disagreement among the people of interpretation (ta'wil, meaning the explanation of what a verse signifies) about this.

Likewise, there is no basis for the view of those who say that this verse is abrogated by ﴿And why should Allah not punish them when they bar access to al-Masjid al-Haram﴾, and the verse that follows, because His statement, great is His praise, ﴿And Allah would not punish them while they seek forgiveness﴾ is a report, and a report cannot contain abrogation. Abrogation (naskh, the cancelling of a previous ruling by a later one) applies only to commands and prohibitions.

* *

The grammarians differed concerning the reason for the particle "an" (that) entering the statement ﴿And why should Allah not punish them﴾.

Some grammarians of Basra said: it is superfluous here, and it has operated as "lā" (not) operates, though "lā" is also superfluous. There appears in poetry (this is by al-Farazdaq):

"Had Ghatafan had no grievances (dhunub) against me, the nobles of its lineages would have blamed 'Umar."

[[The line has already been cited and its sources given at 5:302–303, where its wording is: "then the nobles of its lineages would have blamed [him]," and I explained it there, and claimed that "dhunub" with a fatha on the dhal means a share or portion of honor, lineage and manliness. The wording of the line as it appears here and in the Diwan requires that "dhunub" be the plural of "dhanb" (grievance). This is the difference between the two readings and the two meanings.]]

Some grammarians denied this view and said: "an" is not introduced except for a correct meaning, because the meaning of ﴿And what is with them﴾ is: what prevents them from being punished? So "an" entered for this meaning, and it is taken out with "lā" so that it is known that the sense is negation, since prevention is a negation. He said: "lā" in the line is correct in meaning, because when negation is applied to something, it becomes an affirmation. [[By "affirmation" he means an assertion.]]

He said: Do you not see your saying, "Zayd is not not standing," which affirms the standing? He said: Likewise "lā" in this line. [[See Ma'ani al-Qur'an by al-Farra' 1:163–166, and the earlier exegesis at 5:300–305.]]

* *

The interpretation of His statement: ﴿And they were not its guardians. Its guardians are only the God-fearing, but most of them do not know.﴾ (34)

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: And these polytheists have no reason that Allah should not punish them while they bar access to al-Masjid al-Haram, and they were not the guardians of Allah. ﴿Its guardians are only﴾ means: the guardians of Allah are only ﴿the God-fearing﴾, meaning those who fear Allah by performing His obligations and avoiding His prohibitions. ﴿But most of them do not know﴾ means: but most of the polytheists do not know that the guardians of Allah are the God-fearing; rather, they assume that they themselves are the guardians of Allah.

* *

The people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said.

Those who said this:

16018 – Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿And they were not its guardians. Its guardians are only the God-fearing﴾: they are the companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

16019 – Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning Allah's words: ﴿Its guardians are only the God-fearing﴾: whoever they may be, and wherever they may be.

16020 – al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similarly.

16021 – Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: ﴿And they were not its guardians. Its guardians are only the God-fearing﴾, those who honor its sanctity [[In the printed and manuscript editions the phrase reads "yakhrujūna minhu" (they leave it) in place of "yuḥarrimūna ḥurmatahu" (they honor its sanctity). This is one of the strange distortions that comes from abridgement. The correct reading is from Sirat Ibn Hisham.]] and establish the prayer there, meaning: you, that is the Prophet (ﷺ), and those who believed in you. ﴿But most of them do not know.﴾ [[The report 16021 is in Sirat Ibn Hisham 2:325–326, and it continues the earlier report numbered 16003.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 8, verse 35:

The explanation of His words: ﴿And their prayer at the House was nothing but whistling and clapping. So taste the punishment for what you used to disbelieve.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: May He be exalted and remembered, says: What is the matter with these polytheists, that Allah should not punish them, when they bar [people] from the Sacred Mosque, in which they pray to Allah and worship Him, and they were not His allies? Rather, His allies are those who bar them from the Sacred Mosque, and they do not pray in the Sacred Mosque. ﴿And their prayer at the House﴾, meaning: the House of Allah, the Ancient House. ﴿was nothing but mukā'﴾, and it is whistling.

It is said from it: "makā yamkū makwan and mukā'an." It has also been said that al-Makw (mukā') is that a man joins his two hands, then puts them into his mouth, then shouts. It is said from it: "makat ist al-dābba mukā'" when it breathes out wind. And it is said: "He does not whistle except an uncovered backside (ist)," and for this reason the backside is called "al-makwa," being named thus [[and the completion of its context is that he says: "It was named thus for its whistling."]] And from this is the saying of 'Antarah:

"And the husband of a beautiful woman, I left him felled, his artery whistles like the mouth of a split-lipped camel." [[From his famous mu'allaqa. Sirat Ibn Hisham 2: 326, al-Ma'ani al-Kabir: 981, and al-Lisan (mkw), and after the verse: "My two hands preceded to him with a swift thrust, and a spray of piercing blood the color of the 'andam."

"Al-halil" is the husband; "al-ghaniyya" is the woman brilliant in beauty and loveliness, who has no need to adorn herself because of her beauty. "Mujdalan" means prostrate on the jadala, which is the ground. "Al-farisa" is the flesh at the base of the shoulder blade, in the middle of the side, at the place where the heart beats; there are two of them, and it is what trembles at fright, so it is said of one in fear: "his farisas trembled." Striking the farisa is fatal. "Al-a'lam" is the camel whose upper lip is split. This slain man came out, relying on his strength and youth, desiring to win the admiration of his beautiful beloved by killing 'Antarah, but he had scarcely begun when 'Antarah struck him with the thrust whose width the poet described as the mouth of the split-lipped camel.]]

And the saying of al-Tirimmah: "So he turned aside for its first part with a thrust of one enraged, whose sides whistle from the widening." [[His Diwan 149, al-Ma'ani al-Kabir: 983. It is a line from a poem in praise of Khalid ibn 'Abd Allah al-Qasri, but this line stands alone with no connection to what precedes it; the poem is undoubtedly incomplete. Ibn Qutaybah explained it, saying: "Nahā" means deviated; "al-mihfaz" means angered; "tamkū" means whistles, and that is when it flows. "Al-inhār" means the width of the thrust, and from it is the saying of Qays ibn al-Khatim describing a thrust: "I thrust Ibn 'Abd al-Qays a thrust of one seeking vengeance, through which there is a passage, were it not for the light it would have illuminated... I held it in my hand and widened its opening, so that one standing beyond it can see what lies behind it."]]

means: it makes a sound.

As for "al-tasdiyah," it is clapping; it is said from it: "sadda yusaddi tasdiyatan," and "saffaqa" and "saffaha" have the same meaning.

* *

It has also been said regarding "al-taṣdiyah" that it is "barring from the House of Allah, the Sacred." That is a view without basis, because "al-taṣdiyah" is a verbal noun from the saying of the speaker: "sadday tasdiyah." As for "al-sadd," one does not say from it "sadday"; rather one says from it "sadadtu," and if one doubles the dal to indicate repetition of the action, one says "saddadta tasdidan." [[In the printed and manuscript editions: "sadadt tasdiyah," which is an obvious error; the correct form is what is established here.]] Unless the proponent of this view took "al-taṣdiyah" to derive from "saddadtu," then one of its two dals was changed to a yā', as one says "tazannaytu" from "zanantu," and as the rajaz poet said: [[He is al-'Ajjaj.]]

"Tiqaddiya al-bazi idha al-bazi kasar" — the falcon's swoop when the falcon has broken [its prey].

meaning "taqaddud al-bazi," so one of its two dads was changed to a yā', and this is a possible direction to take.

As for His words: "So taste the punishment for what you used to disbelieve," it means the punishment He had promised them by the sword on the day of Badr. It says to the polytheists who said: "O Allah, if this is the truth from You, then rain down on us stones from the sky," the verse, when He brought upon them what they had sought hastily as punishment. "Taste" means: feel, and it is not tasting by the mouth, but tasting by sensation, and the existence of the taste of its pain in the hearts. [[See the explanation of "al-dhawq" above, p. 434, note 1, and the references there.]] It says to them: taste the punishment for what you used to deny, that Allah would punish you with it for your rejection of the Oneness of your Lord and the message of your Prophet ﷺ.

**The discussion of the interpretation of His words:** ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve spend their wealth to avert [people] from the way of Allah. They will spend it; then it will be to them a [source of] regret; then they will be overcome. And those who disbelieve will be gathered unto Hell﴾ [8:36].

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: Allah, dhikruhu, says: Indeed, those who disbelieve in Allah and His Messenger spend their wealth [[See the explanation of "spending" (infaq) in earlier lexical indices, under (n-f-q).]] by giving it to their likes among the polytheists, so that they may strengthen themselves with it in fighting the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the believers in him, in order to turn the believers in Allah and His Messenger away from faith in Allah and His Messenger. [[See the explanation of "turning away" (sadd) in earlier volumes, 12:559, note 2, and the references there.]] They will spend their wealth in that, and then that expenditure will become for them "a [source of] regret," meaning it will turn into remorse for them, [[See the explanation of "regret" (hasrah) in earlier volumes, 3:295; 7:335; 11:325.]] because their wealth will be lost, and they will not attain what they hope for and desire, namely the extinguishing of the light of Allah and the elevation of the word of disbelief over the word of Allah. For Allah elevates His word and makes the word of disbelief the lowest. Then the believers will overcome them, and Allah will gather those who disbelieved in Him and His Messenger into Hell, where they will be punished. [[See the explanation of "gathering" (hashr) in earlier volumes, p. 472, note 2, and the references there.]] How great, then, will be the regret and remorse for those among them who survive and for those who perish! As for the living, his wealth is plundered, it goes in vain without any benefit, and he returns defeated, subdued, plundered and despoiled of his wealth. [[In the printed edition: "mahzunan maslubán" (grieved and despoiled), but the context requires what has been adopted: "mahrubán" (plundered), "maslubán" (despoiled of wealth).]] As for the one who perishes, he is killed and despoiled, and he is hastened to the Fire of Allah, where he will abide forever. We seek refuge with Allah from His wrath.

It was reported that the one who undertook the expenditure mentioned by Allah in this verse was Abu Sufyan.

[[The Ahabish are the Banu al-Harith ibn Abd Manat ibn Kinanah, 'Adal, al-Dayish from the Banu al-Hun ibn Khuzaymah, al-Mutalliq and al-Hiya from Khuza'ah. They were called "al-Ahabish" because they gathered and united in an alliance with Quraysh in fighting the Banu Layth ibn Bakr ibn Abd Manat ibn Kinanah. (See al-Muhabbar: 246, 267, and Nasab Quraysh: 9.)]] He fought the Prophet (ﷺ) with them, and they are the ones about whom Ka'b ibn Malik said:

"We came to a surging sea of men in its midst, the Ahabish, among them the bare-headed and the helmeted,
three thousand, and we are a chosen force, three hundred if they are many, and four..." [[Sirat Ibn Hisham 3:141; Tabaqat Fuhul al-Shu'ara: 183; Nasab Quraysh: 9, and others.

By his words "we came to a surging [mawj]," he means the army of the disbelievers on the Day of Uhud, which surged. The number of the polytheists at Uhud was three thousand. "Al-hasir" is one who has no coat of mail and no helmet on his head. "Al-muqannaʿ" is one armored who has put on his weapons and placed a helmet on his head.]]

"...three thousand, and we are a chosen force [nasiyyah], three hundred if they are many, and four." [["Nasiyyah" means the choice nobles, people of strength and battle; it is said "intanaa al-shay'," meaning he chose its best part, i.e., the most noble of it. The manuscript reading is: "in kathurna fa-arba'," as if he means that they were three hundred, and if they increased, four hundred. This is not correct, because the number of Muslims at Uhud was seven hundred. The correct reading is what Ibn Ishaq and Ibn Sallam recited: "in kathurna wa-arba'."]]

He hired two thousand on the Day of Uhud to fight the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), besides those he recruited from the Arabs. ["Istajsha" means he requested an army from him and gathered it against his enemy.]

16063. Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: Muhammad ibn Muslim ibn Ubaydullah ibn Shihab al-Zuhri related to us, and Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Hibban, and Asim ibn Umar ibn Qatadah, and al-Husayn ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Amr ibn Sa'd ibn Mu'adh, [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "al-Husayn ibn Abd al-Rahman wa-Amr ibn Sa'd ibn Mu'adh," which is an error, as has occurred repeatedly before. The correct form is from Ibn Hisham's Sirah.]] [and others among our scholars, all of whom narrated part of the report about the Day of Uhud. Their reports have been combined in what I have related of the account of the Day of Uhud. They said, or whoever among them said: When there were slain among the disbelieving Quraysh on the Day of Badr, those from the well [ashab al-qalib], [[This addition in parentheses is from Ibn Hisham's Sirah. I did this because the printed edition differs from the manuscript through an error. The printed edition reads: "qalu: amma asabat al-Muslimin yawm Badr..." while the manuscript reads: "qalu: lamma usibat Quraysh, aw man qalahu minhum, yawm Badr," which is not sound. The phrase "aw man qala minhum" shows that the copyist hastened in copying the rest of the isnad and garbled the speech, so it became confused. Therefore I have given it in its text from the Sirah.]] and their remnant returned to Makkah. [["Al-fall" (with a fatha on the fa') means the defeated, those returning from an army that has been routed.] Abu Sufyan returned with his caravan. Abdullah ibn Abi Rabi'ah, [[In the printed edition: "Abdullah ibn Rabi'ah," which is a plain error.]] Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl and Safwan ibn Umayyah walked, along with men of Quraysh whose fathers, sons and brothers had been struck down at Badr, and they spoke to Abu Sufyan ibn Harb and to those among Quraysh who had trade in that caravan, saying: "O assembly of Quraysh, Muhammad has avenged himself upon you and killed your best men. [["Watara al-qawm" means he inflicted an injury upon them by killing or otherwise. The "mawtur" is one for whom a slain person was killed without his blood being avenged.] So help us with this wealth against his war, that perhaps we may exact vengeance from him for those among us who were struck down!" They did so. He said: Concerning them, as was reported from Ibn Abbas, [[In Ibn Hisham's Sirah it reads: "Ibn Ishaq said: concerning them, as some of the scholars related to me," without attributing the statement to Ibn Abbas.]] Allah revealed: "Indeed, those who disbelieve spend their wealth..." to His words: "...and those who disbelieve will be gathered unto Hell." [[Report 16063: Sirah Ibn Hisham 3:64.]]

16064. Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Ishaq: "Indeed, those who disbelieve spend their wealth to avert [people] from the way of Allah," to His words: "...will be gathered," meaning the group who went to Abu Sufyan and to those among Quraysh who had wealth in that trade, and asked them to strengthen them against fighting the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). [[In the printed edition: "an yu'iniihum" (to help them), while in Ibn Hisham's Sirah: "yaqwwuhum biha" (to strengthen them with it), with an addition.]] And they did so. [[Report 16064: Sirah Ibn Hisham 2:327, a continuation of the earlier report no. 16053.]]

16065. Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Sa'id ibn Abi Ayyub informed me, from Ata' ibn Dinar, regarding the words of Allah: "Indeed, those who disbelieve spend their wealth," the verse; it was revealed concerning Abu Sufyan ibn Harb. [[Report 16065: "Sa'id ibn Abi Ayyub Miqlas al-Misri," which has occurred repeatedly, the last time as no. 13178. In the manuscript it reads "Sa'id ibn Ayyub," and the editor of the printed edition corrected it.

"Ata' ibn Dinar al-Hudhali al-Misri," also occurred earlier as no. 160 and 13178, with the same isnad.]]

\* \*

Some said: It was meant as the polytheists of Badr.

Those who said this:

16066. It was related to me on the authority of al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman related to us, who said: I heard al-Dahhak say, regarding the words: "Indeed, those who disbelieve spend their wealth to avert [people] from the way of Allah," the verse: They are the people of Badr.

\* \*

Abu Ja'far said: The correct view on this matter, in my judgment, is what we have said: namely, that Allah informed us concerning those who disbelieved in Him among the polytheists of Quraysh, that they spend their wealth to avert [people] from the way of Allah. He did not tell us which of them He meant, except that He addressed "those who disbelieved" in general terms. It is permissible that He meant those who spent their wealth to fight the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his companions at Uhud; it is permissible that He meant those among them who spent for that at Badr; and it is permissible that He meant both groups. Since that is the case, the correct view is that it be understood in general, just as He, majestic is His praise, generalized the words "those who disbelieved" to include Quraysh.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 8, verse 37:

The interpretation of His words: ﴿That Allah may distinguish the wicked from the good, and place the wicked some of them upon others, heap them all together, and put them into Hell. Those are the losers.﴾ (8:37)

Abu Ja'far said: May He be exalted in remembrance, says: Allah will gather those who disbelieved in their Lord and spend their wealth to bar from the way of Allah, to Hell, in order to separate them— and they are the people of wickedness (al-khabith), as He said, and He named them "the wicked" (al-khabith)— from the believers in Allah and His Messenger, who are "the good" (al-tayyibun), as He, may His praise be great, named them. So He, may His praise be great, distinguished between them by settling the people of faith in Him and His Messenger in His gardens, and sending the people of disbelief to His Fire. [See the explanation of "al-khabith" above, p. 165, notes 3, 4, and the references there.

And the explanation of "al-tayyib" is in the lexical indices above (under ṭ-y-b).]

* *

And in accordance with what we have said on this, the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have spoken.

Mention of those who said this:

16067 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: "That Allah may distinguish the wicked from the good": He distinguished the people of happiness from the people of wretchedness.

16068 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, who said: Then He mentioned the polytheists and what will be done with them on the Day of Resurrection, and said: "That Allah may distinguish the wicked from the good," meaning: He distinguishes the believer from the disbeliever, and places the wicked some of them upon others.

* *

By His words, may His praise be great, "and place the wicked some of them upon others," He means: the disbelievers will be piled on top of one another. "Heap them all together" means: He will make them a heap (rukam), which is to gather some of them to others until they become many, just as He, may His praise be great, said in describing the clouds: ﴿Then He joins them together, then makes them a heaped mass⁠﴾ (24:43), meaning a gathered, dense mass. And as the following:

16069 - Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: "heap them all together," he said: He gathers them all together, some upon others.

* *

As for His words: "and put them into Hell," meaning: He will put the wicked, all of them, into Hell. He made the report about them singular to match His words "That Allah may distinguish the wicked," then He said: "Those are the losers," in the plural, and did not say "that is the loser," returning it to the beginning of the report.

By "those," He means the disbelievers; its meaning: these who spend their wealth to bar from the way of Allah "are the losers." By His words "the losers" He means those whose transaction was defrauded and whose trade was ruined. [See the explanation of "khasara" above, 12:579, note 2, and the references there.] That is because they sold their wealth for the punishment of Allah in the Hereafter, and hastened, by spending it on fighting the Prophet of Allah and the believers in him, to acquire disgrace and humiliation.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 8, verse 38:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Say to those who disbelieve: If they desist, what is past will be forgiven them; but if they return [to hostility], then the precedent of the former peoples has already passed.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is He, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): "Say", O Muhammad, "to those who disbelieve", from among your people the polytheists, "If they desist" [[See the discussion of "desisting" (intiha') above: 455, footnote 1, and the references there.]] from what they persist in, of their disbelief in Allah and His Messenger, and of fighting you and the believers, and turn in repentance to faith, then Allah will forgive them what has already passed and gone by of their sins before their faith and their turning to the obedience of Allah and the obedience of His Messenger through their faith and repentance. [[See the discussion of "salafa" (passed) above: 6:14; 8:138, 150; 11:48.]] "But if they return", meaning: if these polytheists return to fighting you after the battle that you inflicted upon them on the day of Badr, then the precedent of My way has already passed concerning the former ones among them at Badr, and among others from the earlier generations, [[See the discussion of "sunna" (precedent, way) above: 7:228; 8:209.]] when they transgressed and denied My messengers and did not accept their counsel, through the swift descent of vengeance upon them. So the same will be inflicted upon these people if they return to war and fighting against you, as I inflicted upon them. [[In the printed edition: "allatheena ahlaltu bihim" (those upon whom I inflicted); in the manuscript, which is poorly written, the correct reading is what has been adopted.]]

* *

Those interpreting the verse have said things similar to what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:

16070- Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His saying: "then the precedent of the former peoples has already passed", regarding Quraysh on the day of Badr, and other nations before that.

16071- Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

16072- Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abdullah narrated to us, from Warqa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

16074- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said concerning His saying: "Say to those who disbelieve: If they desist, what is past will be forgiven them; but if they return" to fight you, "then the precedent of the former peoples has already passed", meaning: those of them who were killed on the day of Badr. [[The report: 16074 — Ibn Hisham's Sira 2:327, and it continues the earlier report no. 16064.]]

16075- Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "But if they return", to fight you, "then the precedent of the former peoples has already passed", from the people of Badr.

The Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 8, verse 39:

The interpretation (ta'wil) of His saying: ﴿And fight them until there is no more fitnah (trial and disorder, here meaning shirk) and religion is entirely for Allah. But if they cease, then indeed Allah is Seeing of what they do.﴾ (8:39)

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says to the believers in Him and His Messenger: "If these people return to fight you, you have already seen My way (sunnah) with those among them who fought you on the day of Badr, and I shall return with its like against those among them who wage war upon you. So fight them until there is no shirk, and none is worshipped except Allah alone, without partner, and the affliction is lifted from the servants of Allah on earth." = And this is "fitnah" [[See the explanation of "fitnah" above: 486, note 1, and the references there.]] = "and religion is entirely for Allah," meaning: until obedience and worship are entirely for Allah, sincerely, to the exclusion of anyone else. [[The explanation of "religion" (din) above: 1:155, 156; 6:273-275, and elsewhere in the indices of language under (dīn).]]
