In agreement with what we have said on this, the people of ta'wil said:

Among those who said this:

16076. Al-Muthanna related to me, he said: Abu Salih related to us, he said: Mu'awiya related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: "And fight them until there is no fitnah," he meant: until there is no shirk.

16077. Al-Muthanna related to me, he said: Amr ibn Awn related to us, he said: Hushaym informed us, from Yunus, from al-Hasan regarding His saying: "And fight them until there is no fitnah," he said: "The fitnah" is shirk.

16078. Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada regarding His saying: "And fight them until there is no fitnah," he says: Fight them until there is no shirk = "and religion is entirely for Allah," until it is said: "There is no god but Allah," for which the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) fought and to which he called.

16079. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to me, he said: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, he said: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: "And fight them until there is no fitnah," he said: until there is no shirk.

16080. Al-Harith related to me, he said: Abd al-Aziz related to us, he said: Mubarak ibn Fudala related to us, from al-Hasan regarding His saying: "And fight them until there is no fitnah," he said: until there is no affliction (bala').

16081. Al-Qasim related to us, he said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Hajjaj related to me, he said: Ibn Juraij said: "And fight them until there is no fitnah and religion is entirely for Allah," i.e., no believer is tried away from his religion, and the tawhid is for Allah sincerely, with no shirk in it, and what is other than Him of rivals is cast off. [[The report 16081: This is the text of Ibn Hisham in his Sira, from his transmission from Ibn Ishaq. I almost decide that this report is compiled from two reports: the first is this first chain, whose report text has fallen out. The other is Abu Ja'far's chain to Ibn Ishaq, which is this: "Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Salama related to us, from Ibn Ishaq regarding His saying: ..." Then this context which is here, and it is the text of what is in Ibn Hisham.

See Ibn Hisham's Sira 2:327, which follows the earlier report numbered 12074.]]

16082. Yunus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: "And fight them until there is no fitnah," he said: until there is no kufr = "and religion is entirely for Allah," there will be no kufr alongside your religion.

16083. Abd al-Warith ibn Abd al-Samad related to me, he said: My father related to us, he said: Aban al-Attar related to us, he said: Hisham ibn Urwa related to us, from his father: that Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan wrote to him asking him about several matters, and Urwa wrote back: "Peace be upon you. I praise Allah to you, there is no god but He. To proceed: you wrote to me asking about the departure of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) from Makkah, and I shall inform you of it, and there is no power nor strength except through Allah. The matter of the departure of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) from Makkah was that Allah gave him prophethood, so what a Prophet! What a master! What a clan! May Allah reward him with good, and make us know his face in Paradise, and keep us alive upon his creed, cause us to die upon it, and raise us upon it. When he called his people to the guidance and the light that Allah had sent to him, sent down upon him, they did not shun him at the first thing he called them to, [[In the printed edition: "did not flee from him," differing from the manuscript, and it agrees with the History.]] and they nearly listened to him, until he mentioned their idols. Some people of Quraysh came from Ta'if, who had wealth, and some people denied this and were harsh against him, [[In the printed edition: "some people denied this against him," adding "against him"; in the History: "they denied this against him," without "some people."]] and disliked what he said, and incited against him whoever obeyed them, and the general mass of people turned away from him and left him, [[In the printed edition: "then turned away from him," differing from the manuscript without reason; and it agrees with the History. "Insafaqa 'anhu al-nas" means they returned and dispersed; "insafaqu 'alayhi" means they closed in and gathered; it is from "al-safqa," which is gathering around a thing. What changed the meaning is the use of the preposition: in the first, "anhu," and in the second, "alayhi." This is one of the beauties of Arabic.]] except those whom Allah protected among them, and they were few. So he remained thus as long as Allah decreed he should remain. Then their leaders plotted to put to trial those who followed him away from the religion of Allah, among their sons, brothers and tribes, and it was a severe ordeal of trembling, [[In the manuscript: "shadudat al-zilzal," which is an error by the copyist.]] so whoever was tried was tried, and Allah protected whomever He willed of them. When this was done to the Muslims, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ordered them to go out to the land of Abyssinia. In Abyssinia there was a righteous king called "al-Najashi," no one is wronged in his land, [[In the manuscript: "no one is wronged in his land," and the editor corrected it, and his correction agrees with the History.]] and he was praised besides that for [righteousness], [[The addition between brackets is from Tarikh al-Tabari.]] and the land of Abyssinia was a trading place for Quraysh, where they traded, and dwelling places for their merchants, [[The phrase "and dwelling places for their merchants" is not in the History. In the printed edition: "li-tijaratihim," which is an error; the correct form is from the manuscript and Ibn Kathir.]] where they found abundant sustenance, security and a good market, [[In the printed edition: "ratha'an min al-rizq," which contradicts the manuscript, since it is unpointed, and it agrees with the History. "Al-rafagh" is the verbal noun of "rafaga" (with fatha then damma), which is the analogy in Arabic, but what is in the dictionaries is "rafagha." It is said: "innahu lafi rafagha min al-'aysh," and "rafaghiya" (on the pattern of "thamaniya"): a breadth of living, goodness and fertility. And "'aysh rafigh."]] so the Prophet (ﷺ) commanded them to go there, and most of them went there when they were subdued in Makkah, and he feared trials for them. [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "and they feared trials for them," and what I have established from the History is better.]] He himself remained and did not leave. So he remained thus for years, and they were harsh against those among them who became Muslim. [[In the History: "So he remained thus for years," which is better.]] Then Islam spread there, and men of their nobles and protectors entered it. [[Up to this point, what Abu Ja'far narrated in his History is finished, 2:220, 221, except that he did not mention at the end of the sentence "wa-mana'atihim."

And his saying "wa-mana'atihim" (with fathas), is the plural of "mani'," like "kafir" and "kafara," and they are those who protect whoever they ruin from harm.

And see the takhrij of the report at the end of this report.]] When they saw that, they relaxed their hold on the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his Companions. [["al-istirkha'" means ease and facility. "Istarkhu 'anhum" means they loosened the severity of the torment and the trial from them.]] The first trial was what drove out those among the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) who left toward the land of Abyssinia, fearing it, and fleeing from the trials and trembling they were in. When they were relieved, and those among them who had entered Islam did so, their relaxing was discussed. [[In the printed edition: "their relaxation was discussed," and in the manuscript it reads: "tahaddadu istirkha'ahum 'anhum," and I have established the correct reading from Ibn Kathir's Tafsir.]] This reached those among the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) who were in the land of Abyssinia: that they had relaxed their hold on those among them in Makkah, and that they would not be tried. So they returned to Makkah, and nearly felt safe there, and they began to increase and multiply. And many men of the Ansar in Madinah became Muslim, and Islam spread in Madinah, and the people of Madinah began to come to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in Makkah. When Quraysh saw that, they incited each other to try them and to be harsh against them, [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "they conspired to try them," and I have established what is in the History. As for Ibn Kathir in his Tafsir, he quoted: "they conspired to try them." And in the printed edition alone: "wa-yashudu 'alayhim," and I have established what is in the History and Ibn Kathir.

"Tadhamara al-qawm" means some of them urged others on and spurred them to fight or other things. "Dhamara hizbahu tadhmiran" means he encouraged and urged him, with blame and impatience.]] so they seized them, and were eager to try them, and a severe hardship befell them. And this was the final trial. So there were two trials: a trial that drove out those among them who left toward the land of Abyssinia, when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ordered them to go there and permitted them to leave for it; and a trial when they returned and saw those who came to them from the people of Madinah. Then seventy leaders (naqib) came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) from Madinah, the chiefs of those who had become Muslim, and they met him during the Hajj, and they pledged allegiance to him at al-'Aqaba, and gave him their covenants that "we are with you and you are with us, and whoever among your companions comes to us or you come to us, we will protect you from what we protect ourselves from." [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "and they gave him upon that, that we are from you..." The word "covenants" fell out of the speech; I have restored it from the History. In Ibn Kathir's Tafsir: "and they gave him their covenants and their pacts."]] Quraysh became harsh against them at that. So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ordered his Companions to go out to Madinah, and this is the final trial in which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent his Companions out, and he himself went out. And this is what Allah revealed concerning: "And fight them until there is no fitnah and religion is entirely for Allah." [[The report 16083: "Aban al-Attar" is Aban ibn Yazid al-Attar, and the explanation of this chain was previously given: 15719, 15821, and others; it is a sound chain.

Urwa's letter to Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan was narrated by Abu Ja'far in fragments in his Tafsir and in his History. What he narrated in his Tafsir just now, numbers 15719, 15821. As for his History, he narrated it in fragments in several places, these being 2:220, 221, 240, 241, 245, 267-269; then 3:117, 125, 132. Perhaps I may be able to gather the scattered parts of this book from the Tafsir and the History, so that I may bring out Urwa's letter to Abd al-Malik complete, for it is among the earliest books written on the Sira of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

This same report is also dispersed in two places in the History 2:220, 221, as I pointed out on p. 443 note 1; then 2:240, 241.

Ibn Kathir quoted it from this place of the Tafsir in his Tafsir 4:61, 62.

Then see the commentary on the following report.]]

16084. Yunus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi al-Zinad informed me, from his father, from Urwa ibn al-Zubayr: that he wrote to al-Walid: "To proceed: you wrote to me asking about the departure of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) from Makkah, and with me, praise be to Allah, is knowledge of everything you asked me about, and I shall inform you, if Allah wills, and there is no power nor strength except through Allah," then he mentioned something similar. [[The report 16084: "Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi al-Zinad" is "Abd al-Rahman ibn Abd Allah ibn Dhakwan," mentioned under number 1695, 9225, and my brother al-Sayyid Ahmad said he is trustworthy, though some imams spoke about him. Then he said: al-Tirmidhi also declared him trustworthy and authenticated several of his hadiths, indeed he said in his Sunan 3:59: "He is trustworthy and a memorizer."

Among those who weakened "Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi al-Zinad" is Ibn Ma'in, who said: "He is not among those whom the people of hadith rely upon; he is nothing." And Ahmad said: "Unstable in his hadith." Ibn al-Madini said: "He was weak according to our companions." And Ibn al-Madini said: "What he narrated in Madina is sound, and what he narrated in Baghdad, the Baghdadis spoiled." Ibn Sa'd said: "He narrated much, and he was weakened for his narration from his father."

His father "Abd Allah ibn Dhakwan," Abu al-Zinad, is trustworthy, and the group narrated from him.

And it was narrated by "Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi al-Zinad" that the one to whom Urwa wrote was "al-Walid ibn Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan," while the earlier chain is more sound and more reliable, that he wrote to "Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan." So I fear this report may be among those whose narration from Ibn Abi al-Zinad, from his father, has been confused.]]

16085. Ahmad ibn Ishaq related to us, he said: Abu Ahmad related to us, he said: Qays related to us, from al-A'mash, from Mujahid: "And fight them until there is no fitnah," he said: "Yusaf" and "Na'ila," two idols that were worshipped. [["Isaf" (with kasra or fatha on the alif) and "Yusaf" (with kasra or fatha on the ya') are one. This was already mentioned in the report 10433 and its commentary 9:208, note 1.

In the manuscript here it reads: "Saf wa-Nafila," which is pure error.]]

* *

As for His saying: "But if they cease," its meaning is: if they cease from fitnah, which is shirk with Allah, and turn to the true religion with you = "then indeed Allah is Seeing of what they do," meaning: indeed Allah is not hidden from what they do of abandoning kufr and entering the religion of Islam, because He sees you and sees your deeds, and all things are manifest to Him, nothing is hidden from Him, and not an atom's weight in the heavens or in the earth escapes Him, nor anything smaller or greater than that, except that it is in a clear Book. [[See the explanation of "cease" (intaha) above: 536, note 1, and the references there.]] [[See the explanation of "seeing" (basir) above in the indices of language under (basara).]]

* *

Some of them said: the meaning of that is: if they cease from fighting.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: What we have said on this is more correct, because even if the polytheists cease from fighting, it was an obligation upon the believers to fight them until they submit to Islam.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 8, verse 40:

The discussion of His saying: ﴿And if they turn away, then know that Allah is your Protector; excellent is the Protector and excellent is the Helper﴾ (40)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: May His remembrance be exalted, He says: And if these polytheists turn their backs on what you, O believers, have called them to, of faith in Allah and His Messenger, and of abandoning fighting you on account of their disbelief, and they refuse anything but persistence in disbelief and fighting you, then fight them, and be certain that Allah is your helper against them and your supporter [[See the explanation of "al-tawalli" (turning away) above (9:141), commentary: ..., and the references there.]] = "excellent is the Protector" (mawla), He is for you; that is, excellent is the one who aids you and His allies [[See the explanation of "al-mawla" above in the language indices (w-l-y).]] = "and excellent is the Helper" (nasir), who is the one who gives victory. [[See the explanation of "al-nasir" above at 10:481, commentary: 5, and the references there.]]

* *

16086 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, who said: Salama narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: "And if they turn away" from your command to what they are upon of their disbelief. Indeed Allah is your Protector, who honoured you and gave you victory over them on the day of Badr, despite their great number and your small number = "excellent is the Protector and excellent is the Helper." [[The report: 18086 - Sirat Ibn Hisham 2:327, with slight variation in its context; it follows the two preceding reports: 16074 and 16081. See the commentary on this last report and what I have inferred there.]]

**The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And know that whatever you obtain as spoils of war﴾**

Abu Ja'far said: This is an instruction from God, mighty and majestic, to the believers concerning the division of their spoils when they take them.

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: Know, O believers, that whatever booty (*ghanīma*) you obtain.

* * *

The scholars differed concerning the meaning of *al-ghanīma* (spoils taken by force in battle) and *al-fay'* (property gained without fighting).

Some of them said: Each of the two terms has its own meaning, distinct from the other.

Those who said this:

16087. Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Ḥumayd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, from al-Ḥasan ibn Ṣāliḥ, who said: I asked ʿAṭā' ibn al-Sā'ib about this verse, "And know that whatever you obtain as spoils of war, then for God is one-fifth of it," and this verse: ﴿What God has restored to His Messenger from the people of the townships﴾ [Surah al-Ḥashr: 7]. I said: What is *al-fay'*, and what is *al-ghanīma*? He said: When the Muslims prevail over the polytheists and over their land and seize them by force, then whatever property they take over which they prevailed is *ghanīma*. As for the land, in our region it is *fay'*. [[In the printed edition: "fa-hiya fī sawādinā" (so it is in our region). I have retained what is in the manuscript, which is sound.]]

* * *

Others said: *al-ghanīma* is what is taken by force, and *al-fay'* is what is obtained by treaty.

Those who said this:

16088. Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Sufyān al-Thawrī, who said: *Al-ghanīma* is what the Muslims obtain by force through fighting; from it one-fifth is due, and the remaining four-fifths belong to those who were present. *Al-fay'* is what they reach agreement upon without fighting; from it there is no one-fifth, and it belongs to those whom God named.

* * *

Others said: *al-ghanīma* and *al-fay'* have the same meaning. They said: this verse in Surat al-Anfāl abrogates His saying: ﴿What God has restored to His Messenger from the people of the townships, then it is for God and for the Messenger﴾, [and so on, to the end of the verse] [Surah al-Ḥashr: 7].

Those who said this:

16089. Ibn Bashshār narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-A'lā narrated to us, saying: Saʿīd narrated to us, from Qatādah, concerning His saying: ﴿What God has restored to His Messenger from the people of the townships, then it is for God and for the Messenger, and for the near of kin, the orphans, the needy, and the wayfarer﴾. He said: *al-fay'* was for these; then this was abrogated in Surat al-Anfāl, where He said: "And know that whatever you obtain as spoils of war, then for God is one-fifth of it, and for the Messenger, and for the near of kin, the orphans, the needy, and the wayfarer." So this abrogated what preceded it in Surat al-Anfāl, [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "mā kāna qablahā fī sūrat al-Ḥashr" (what preceded it in Surat al-Ḥashr). The correct reading, as will come in the commentary on Surat al-Ḥashr at 28:25 (Bulaq edition), is in Surat al-Anfāl. He means that it abrogated His saying at the beginning of Surat al-Anfāl: "They ask you about the spoils".]] and the one-fifth was assigned to those who were entitled to *fay'* in Surat al-Ḥashr, while all the rest belongs to those who fought for it. [[The report 16089 will come at greater length in the commentary on Surat al-Ḥashr at 28:25–26 (Bulaq edition).]]

* * *

We have already explained *al-ghanīma* in the earlier part of this work: it is the property that is reached from the property which God has entrusted to the people of His religion, by overpowering it and subduing it through fighting. [[See the explanation of *al-ghanīma* earlier, in the commentary on *al-nafl*, pp. 361–385.]]

As for *al-fay'*, it is what God restores to the Muslims from the property of the people of polytheism, namely what is returned to them by agreement, without horses or riders being driven against them. It may also be that what their swords, spears, and other weapons restore to them is called *fay'*, because *al-fay'* is a verbal noun from the saying of the speaker: "*fā' al-shay' yafī'u fay'an*," when it returns; and "*afāhu Allāh*," when He restores it. [[See the explanation of *fā'a* earlier, vol. 4, pp. 465–466.]]

However, what God's ruling concerning *fay'* restores, according to His ruling in Surat al-Ḥashr, [[In the printed edition: "... alladhī warada ḥukm Allāh fīhi min al-fay' yaḥkīhi fī sūrat al-Ḥashr" — which differs from the manuscript and utterly corrupts the sense.]] is only what I have described as *fay'*, excluding what was gained from it by horses and riders. This is for reasons I have explained in my book *Kitāb laṭīf al-qawl fī aḥkām sharā'i' al-dīn* ("The Book of Refined Speech on the Rulings of the Religious Laws"). We will also explain it in the commentary on Surat al-Ḥashr, when we reach it, God willing. [[See what will come at 28:24–27 (Bulaq edition).]]

* * *

As for the statement of the one who said: the verse in Surat al-Anfāl abrogates the verse in Surat al-Ḥashr, it has no meaning, since neither of the two verses negates the ruling of the other. We have already explained the meaning of *naskh* (abrogation), which is the cancellation of a ruling that was established by a ruling contrary to it, in more than one place, which suffices and makes repetition here unnecessary. [[See his discussion of *naskh* in the indices of grammar and Arabic and elsewhere, and in places in this book where references to all of that are given.]]

* * *

As for His saying "from anything" (*min shay'*), it is meant to include everything to which the term "thing" applies, of the property which God entrusted to the believers from the property of the polytheists whose wealth they overpowered, in which division takes place, even a thread and a needle [[*al-mikhyat*: the needle, which is that with which something is sewn.]], as:

16090. Muḥammad ibn Bashshār narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, saying: Sufyān narrated to us, from Layth, from Mujāhid, concerning His saying: "And know that whatever you obtain as spoils of war," he said: "*al-mikhyat*" is included in "*al-shay'*" (thing).

16091. Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Sufyān, from Layth, from Mujāhid, with the same.

16092. Al-Muthannā narrated to me, saying: Abū Nuʿaym al-Faḍl narrated to us, saying: Sufyān narrated to us, from Layth, from Mujāhid, the same.

* * *

**The interpretation of His saying: ﴿then for God is one-fifth of it, and for the Messenger, and for the near of kin, the orphans, the needy, and the wayfarer﴾**

Abu Ja'far said: The exegetes differed in their interpretation of this.

Some of them said: His saying "then for God is one-fifth of it" is an opening of speech [[meaning it is an opening with the mention of God, exalted is His remembrance. See what has passed at 6:272, note 5.]], for to God belong this world and the next and what is in them; and the meaning of the statement is: "then for the Messenger is one-fifth of it."

Those who said this:

16093. Ibn Bashshār narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, saying: Sufyān narrated to us, from Qays ibn Muslim, who said: I asked al-Ḥasan about the saying of God: "And know that whatever you obtain as spoils of war, then for God is one-fifth of it, and for the Messenger," and he said: This is an opening of speech; to God belong this world and the next.

16094. Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Sufyān, from Qays ibn Muslim, who said: I asked al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad about His saying: "And know that whatever you obtain as spoils of war, then for God is one-fifth of it," and he said: This is an opening of speech; to God belong this world and the next. [[The two reports 16093 and 16094: "al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad" is al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, who is al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥanafiyya, and he is the one from whom Qays ibn Muslim narrates. He is not al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī. This report was transmitted by Abū ʿUbayd al-Qāsim ibn Sallām in Kitāb al-Amwāl, pp. 14, 326, 330, nos. 39, 836, 846, and it will come at greater length as no. 16121.]]

16095. Abū Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Aḥmad ibn Yūnus narrated to us, saying: Abū Shihāb narrated to us, from Warqāʾ, from Nahshal, from al-Ḍaḥḥāk, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: When the Messenger of God (ﷺ) dispatched a detachment and they took spoils, he would divide the spoils into five, then multiply that fifth by five. Then he recited: "And know that whatever you obtain as spoils of war, then for God is one-fifth of it, and for the Messenger." He said: And His saying "then for God is one-fifth of it" is an opening of speech; to God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. So God made the share of God and the share of the Messenger one share. [[The report 16095: Aḥmad ibn Yūnus is Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yūnus al-Tamīmī, who has passed at nos. 2144, 2362, 5080. Abū Shihāb is ʿAbd Rabbih ibn Nāfiʿ al-Kinānī, al-Ḥannāṭ, a trustworthy transmitter, whose biography is in al-Tahdhīb and Ibn Abī Ḥātim, 3/1/42. Warqāʾ is Warqāʾ ibn ʿAmr al-Yashkurī, who has passed at no. 6534. Nahshal is Nahshal ibn Saʿīd ibn Wardān al-Nīsābūrī, who is not trustworthy; Abū Ḥātim said: "not strong, abandoned in narration, weak in narration"; Ibn Ḥibbān said: "he narrates from the trustworthy things that are not from their hadiths; it is not lawful to write down his hadith except in wonder." al-Bukhārī said: "His hadiths are rejected. Isḥāq ibn Ibrāhīm said: Nahshal was a liar." His biography is in al-Tahdhīb, al-Kabīr 4/2/115, Ibn Abī Ḥātim 4/1/496, and Mīzān al-iʿtidāl 3/243. See report 16120. In the printed edition it reads "fa-jaʿala sahm Allāh" (so he made the share of God), which differs from the manuscript and omits a word; I have adopted the manuscript's reading.]]

16096. Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Jarīr narrated to us, from Mughīra, from Ibrāhīm: "then for God is one-fifth of it," he said: To God belongs everything.

16097. Al-Muthannā narrated to us, saying: ʿAmr ibn ʿAwn narrated to us, saying: Hushaym informed us, from Mughīra, from Ibrāhīm, concerning His saying: "And know that whatever you obtain as spoils of war, then for God is one-fifth of it." He said: To God belongs everything, and one-fifth is for God and His Messenger, and the rest is divided into four shares.

16098. Ibn Bashshār narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-A'lā narrated to us, saying: Saʿīd narrated to us, from Qatādah, who said: The spoils used to be divided into five-fifths: four-fifths for those who fought for them, and the remaining fifth was divided into five-fifths; one fifth for God and the Messenger.

16099. ʿImrān ibn Mūsā narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Wārith narrated to us, saying: Abān narrated to us, from al-Ḥasan, who said: Abū Bakr (may God have mercy on him) bequeathed one-fifth of his wealth, and said: Am I not content with my wealth what God has been content with for Himself?

16100. Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad ibn Fuḍayl narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Malik, from ʿAṭā': "And know that whatever you obtain as spoils of war, then for God is one-fifth of it, and for the Messenger," he said: The fifth of God and the fifth of His Messenger is one. The Prophet (ﷺ) would take from it and place in it what he wished. [[In the printed edition: "wa-yaṣnaʿu fīhi" (and he would do with it); I have retained the manuscript's reading. I have read in Kitāb al-Amwāl by Abū ʿUbayd al-Qāsim ibn Sallām, in another report: "yaḥmilu minhu wa-yuʿṭī, wa-yaḍaʿuhu ḥaythu shāʾ, wa-yaṣnaʿu bihi mā shāʾ" (he takes from it and gives, places it wherever he wishes, and does with it what he wishes), p. 14, 326, nos. 40, 837.]]

16101. Al-Muthannā narrated to me, saying: al-Ḥajjāj narrated to us, saying: Abū ʿAwāna narrated to us, from al-Mughīra, from his companions, from Ibrāhīm: "And know that whatever you obtain as spoils of war, then for God is one-fifth of it," he said: Everything belongs to God; the fifth is for the Messenger, and for the near of kin, the orphans, the needy, and the wayfarer.

* * *

Others said: the meaning of that is: "then for the House of God is one-fifth of it, and for the Messenger."

Those who said this:

16102. Abū Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Wakīʿ ibn al-Jarrāḥ narrated to us, from Abū Jaʿfar al-Rāzī, from al-Rabīʿ ibn Anas, from Abū al-ʿĀliya al-Riyāḥī, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) would be brought the spoils, and he would divide them into five: four-fifths for those who were present, and then he would take the fifth and place his hand in it, and take from it what his hand grasped, and make it for the Kaʿba, and it is the share of God. Then he would divide what remained into five shares: one share for the Messenger, one share for the near of kin, one share for the orphans, one share for the needy, and one share for the wayfarer.

16103. Aḥmad ibn Isḥāq narrated to us, saying: Abū Jaʿfar al-Rāzī narrated to us, from al-Rabīʿ ibn Anas, from Abū al-ʿĀliya: "And know that whatever you obtain as spoils of war, then for God is one-fifth of it," to the end of the verse. He said: The spoils used to be brought and placed, and the Messenger of God (ﷺ) would divide them into five shares, making four shares among the people, and taking one share. Then he would place his hand over all of that share, and whatever he grasped of it he made for the Kaʿba, and that is what is named "for God." He would say: "Do not make a portion for God, for to God belong this world and the next." Then he would divide the rest into five shares: a share for the Prophet (ﷺ), a share for the near of kin, a share for the orphans, a share for the needy, and a share for the wayfarer. [[The reports 16102 and 16103: Abū ʿUbayd al-Qāsim ibn Sallām transmitted them in Kitāb al-Amwāl, through the chain of Ḥajjāj, from Abū Jaʿfar al-Rāzī, with wording like the first. Kitāb al-Amwāl: 14, 325, nos. 400, 835.]]

* * *

Others said: what is named for the Messenger of God (ﷺ) from that is only meant as his kin, and neither God nor His Messenger has any share of it.

Those who said this:

16104. Al-Muthannā narrated to me, saying: Abū Ṣāliḥ narrated to us, saying: Muʿāwiya narrated to us, from ʿAlī, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The spoils were divided into five-fifths: four of them for those who fought for them, and one fifth divided into four: a quarter for God and the Messenger and the near of kin — meaning the kin of the Prophet (ﷺ) — so what belonged to God and the Messenger belonged to the kin of the Prophet (ﷺ), and the Prophet (ﷺ) took nothing from the fifth. The second quarter is for the orphans, the third quarter for the needy, and the fourth quarter for the wayfarer. [[The report 16104: Abū ʿUbayd al-Qāsim ibn Sallām transmitted it with this same chain and wording in Kitāb al-Amwāl, pp. 13, 325, nos. 37, 834, and at its end he explains "the wayfarer" as: "the weak, poor person who arrives among the Muslims." See what will come at nos. 16124 and 16129.]]

* * *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of these sayings is the statement of the one who said: His saying "then for God is one-fifth of it" is an "opening of speech," because the consensus of the proof-bearing scholars is that the fifth may not be divided into six shares; and if God had a share in it, as Abū al-ʿĀliya said, it would be necessary that the fifth of the spoils be divided into six shares. The scholars have differed only concerning its division into five or fewer; as for more than that, we know of no one who has said it except the report from Abū al-ʿĀliya that we mentioned. In the consensus of those I have named is clear evidence for the soundness of what we have chosen.

* * *

As for the one who said: "the Messenger's share is for the near of kin," he has assigned a share to the Messenger, even though he (ﷺ) directed it to his near kin; it did not cease to be a division into five shares. And:

16105. Bishr ibn Muʿādh narrated to us, saying: Yazīd narrated to us, saying: Saʿīd narrated to us, from Qatādah, concerning His saying: "And know that whatever you obtain as spoils of war, then for God is one-fifth of it," the verse. He said: When the Prophet of God (ﷺ) took spoils, they were made into fifths, and one fifth was for God and His Messenger, and the Muslims would divide what remained. And the fifth that was assigned to God and His Messenger was for His Messenger, and for the near of kin, the orphans, the needy, and the wayfarer. [[The manuscript has an error here, omitting the second "li-rasūlihi" (for His Messenger), which the sense requires as in the printed edition; in the margin of the manuscript there is a letter "alif" with three dots over it, indicating the place of the omission.]] So this fifth was five-fifths: one fifth for God and His Messenger, one fifth for the near of kin, one fifth for the orphans, one fifth for the needy, and one fifth for the wayfarer.

16106. Ibn Bashshār narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, saying: Sufyān narrated to us, from Mūsā ibn Abī ʿĀʾisha, who said: I asked Yaḥyā ibn al-Jazzār about the share of the Prophet (ﷺ), and he said: It is a fifth of the fifth. [[The report 16106: Mūsā ibn Abī ʿĀʾisha al-Makhzūmī, from whom the whole group narrates, has passed at no. 11408. Yaḥyā ibn al-Jazzār al-ʿAranī is trustworthy, passed at no. 5425. In the manuscript it reads "Yaḥyā al-Jazzār," and the printed edition's reading is correct, but it comes correctly in the next report in the manuscript. Abū ʿUbayd transmitted it in al-Amwāl, pp. 13, nos. 34, 35, and pp. 324, nos. 831, 832.]]

16107. Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Ibn ʿUyayna and Jarīr narrated to us, from Mūsā ibn Abī ʿĀʾisha, from Yaḥyā ibn al-Jazzār, the same.

16108. Aḥmad ibn Isḥāq narrated to us, saying: Abū Aḥmad narrated to us, saying: Sufyān narrated to us, from Mūsā ibn Abī ʿĀʾisha, from Yaḥyā ibn al-Jazzār, the same.

16109. al-Qāsim narrated to us, saying: al-Ḥusayn narrated to us, saying: Ḥajjāj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj: "then for God is one-fifth of it," he said: Four-fifths are for those who attended the battle, and the remaining fifth is for God and the Messenger: one fifth he places wherever he sees fit, one fifth is for the near of kin, one fifth for the orphans, one fifth for the needy, and one fifth for the wayfarer.

* * *

As for His saying "and for the near of kin," the exegetes differed concerning who they are.

Some of them said: They are the kin of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) from the Banū Hāshim.

Those who said this:

16110. Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to me, from Sharīk, from Khuṣayf, from Mujāhid, who said: The family of Muḥammad (ﷺ) were not permitted to take charity, so they were given one-fifth of the fifth.

16111. Aḥmad ibn Isḥāq narrated to us, saying: Abū Aḥmad narrated to us, saying: Sharīk narrated to us, from Khuṣayf, from Mujāhid, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) and his household did not eat charity, so they were given one-fifth of the fifth.

16112. Aḥmad narrated to us, saying: Abū Aḥmad narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Salām narrated to us, from Khuṣayf, from Mujāhid, who said: God knows that among the Banū Hāshim there are the poor, so He assigned to them the fifth in place of charity.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 8, verse 41 (part 2 of 3):

16113 - Muhammad ibn 'Umarah narrated to me, saying: Isma'il ibn Aban narrated to us, saying: al-Sabbah ibn Yahya al-Muzani narrated to us, from al-Suddi, from Abu al-Dailam, who said: 'Ali ibn al-Husain, may Allah have mercy on him, said to a man from the people of Syria: "Have you not read in 'al-Anfal': ﴿And know that whatever you acquire of booty, a fifth of it is for Allah and for the Messenger﴾, to the end of the verse?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Then you are indeed those (who are meant)?" He said: "Yes."

[Editor's note: Isma'il ibn Aban al-Warraq al-Azdi is trustworthy (thiqah) and truthful in narration. Al-Bazzar said: "His defect was only his strong Shi'ism; it was not that he was altered in what he heard." As for Isma'il ibn Aban al-Ghanawi, he is a liar. Isma'il al-Warraq has passed under no. 14550. As for al-Sabbah ibn Yahya al-Muzani, he is also a Shi'i, abandoned (matruk), rather accused (muttaham), so said al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar and al-Dhahabi. Al-Bukhari mentioned him and said: "There is something to consider in him (fihi nazar)," and Abu Hatim said: "a shaykh." He is biographed in Lisan al-Mizan 3:160, al-Kabir 2/2/315, Ibn Abi Hatim 2/1/442, and Mizan al-I'tidal 1:462. As for Abu al-Dailam, I do not know who he is; this is how I found it in the manuscript, while in the printed edition it reads: "from Ibn al-Dailami," meaning 'Abdullah ibn Fairuz al-Dailami, the trustworthy Successor (tabi'i). I do not think he narrates from 'Ali ibn al-Husain ibn 'Ali ibn Abi Talib. This chain is ruined (halik), as you see.]

16114 - al-Harith narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-'Aziz narrated to us, saying: Isra'il narrated to us, from Khusaif, from Mujahid, who said: "These are the relatives of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to whom charity is not lawful."

16115 - al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husain narrated to us, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from Hajjaj, from 'Ata', from Ibn 'Abbas: that Najdah wrote to him asking him about the kinsfolk (dhawi al-qurba). So he wrote to him a letter: "We maintain that we are they, but our people refused this for us."

[Editor's note: Najdah ibn 'Uwaymir al-Haruri, one of the leaders of the Kharijites. Ibn 'Abbas's letter to Najdah was transmitted by Abu 'Ubaydah in Kitab al-Amwal, through several chains, pp. 332–335, nos. 850–852. See what follows, no. 16117.]

16116 - ... He said: al-Husain narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding "a fifth of it is for Allah": Four-fifths are for those who attended the battle, and the remaining fifth is for Allah and for the Messenger; he places his fifth wherever he sees fit, and a fifth is for the kinsfolk, a fifth for the orphans, a fifth for the needy, and a fifth for the wayfarer.

* *

Others said: Rather, they are all of Quraysh.

Those who said this:

16117 - Yunus ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to me, saying: 'Abdullah ibn Nafi' informed me, from Abu Ma'shar, from Sa'id al-Maqbari, who said: Najdah wrote to Ibn 'Abbas asking him about the kinsman (dhi al-qurba). He said: Ibn 'Abbas wrote to him: "We used to say that we are they, but our people refused this for us, and said: all of Quraysh are kinsfolk (dhawu qurba)."

[Editor's note: See the earlier commentary, by way of Abu Ma'shar. Abu 'Ubayd narrated it in no. 850, at length, similar in meaning.]

* *

Others said: The share of the kinsfolk belonged to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and after him it passed to the ruler of affairs (wali al-amr) after him.

Those who said this:

16118 - Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: that he was asked about the share of the kinsfolk, and he said: It was a provision (tu'mah) for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ as long as he lived. ["Tu'mah" (with the ta' vowelled with a damma): provision and sustenance; he means by it the fay' (spoils acquired without fighting).] When he died, it was assigned to the ruler of affairs after him.

* *

Others said: Rather, the share of the kinsfolk belonged specifically to the Banu Hashim and the Banu al-Muttalib.

Among those who said this was al-Shafi'i, and his reason for that was:

16119 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Yunus ibn Bukayr narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: al-Zuhri narrated to me, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, from Jubayr ibn Mut'im, who said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ divided the share of the kinsfolk from Khaybar between the Banu Hashim and the Banu al-Muttalib, I and 'Uthman ibn 'Affan, may Allah have mercy on him, walked and said: "O Messenger of Allah, these are your brothers, the Banu Hashim; we do not deny their merit, because of your standing by which Allah has placed you among them. But what of our brothers, the Banu al-Muttalib? You gave to them and left us out, though we and they stand in the same position relative to you." He said: "They never separated from us, in the Jahiliyyah or in Islam. The Banu Hashim and the Banu al-Muttalib are one thing!" Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ interlaced his fingers, one of his hands with the other.

[Editor's note: al-Shafi'i narrated it in al-Umm through several chains, including the chain of Muhammad ibn Ishaq; see al-Umm 4:71. Abu Dawud narrated it in his Sunan 3:201, no. 2980, and Abu 'Ubayd al-Qasim ibn Sallam in al-Amwal: 331, no. 842.]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of the statements in this matter, in my view, is the statement of the one who said: "The share of the kinsfolk was for the relatives of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ from the Banu Hashim and their allies from the Banu al-Muttalib," because the ally of a people is one of them, and because of the soundness of the report we have mentioned on this from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

* *

The people of knowledge differed regarding the ruling on these two shares, meaning the share of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the share of the kinsfolk, after the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

Some of them said: They are to be spent on supporting Islam and its people.

Those who said this:

16120 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Yunus narrated to us, saying: Abu Shihab narrated to us, from Waqa', from Nahshal, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The share of Allah and the share of the Messenger were made one, and for the kinsfolk; these two shares were placed in horses and weapons. The share of the orphans, the needy and the wayfarer was made so that it is not given to anyone else."

[Editor's note: This is the extended form of the earlier report, and its abridged form is no. 16095, and I explained its chain there.]

16121 - Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Qays ibn Muslim, who said: I asked al-Hasan regarding the saying of Allah: "And know that whatever you acquire of booty, a fifth of it is for Allah and for the Messenger and for the kinsfolk," and he said: "This is the key to the speech: to Allah belong this world and the Hereafter." Then the people differed regarding these two shares after the death of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Some said: the share of the Prophet ﷺ is for the relatives of the Prophet ﷺ. Others said: the share of the kinsfolk is for the relatives of the caliph. They agreed that these two shares be placed in horses and the equipment of war in the way of Allah, and they remained so during the caliphate of Abu Bakr and 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both.

16122 - Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Qays ibn Muslim, who said: I asked al-Hasan ibn Muhammad, and he mentioned something similar.

[Editor's note: The two reports 16121 and 16122: "al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah." The chain of this report was explained earlier, and it was given in abridged form earlier as nos. 16093 and 16094.]

16123 - Ibn WakI' narrated to us, saying: 'Umar ibn 'Ubayd narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, who said: Abu Bakr and 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, used to place the share of the Prophet ﷺ in the kura' and the weapons. ["Al-kura'" (with the kaf vowelled with a damma): a term that encompasses horses and weapons.] I said to Ibrahim: "What did 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, say about it?" He said: "'Ali was the strictest of them concerning it."

16124 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: 'Abdullah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, his statement: "And know that whatever you acquire of booty, a fifth of it is for Allah and for the Messenger and for the kinsfolk, and the orphans, and the needy," to the end of the verse. When Allah took His Messenger ﷺ, Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, returned the share of the relatives to the Muslims, and it was spent on carrying (equipment) in the way of Allah, because the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "We are not inherited from; what we leave is charity."

[Editor's note: This report was passed earlier before its beginning, no. 16104, and its takhrij was given there; see also its continuation, no. 16129.]

When he died, Abu Bakr and 'Umar used it to carry (equipment) in the way of Allah, as charity for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

[Editor's note: See what passed earlier, no. 16118, and what follows, 16127.]

* *

Others said: The share of the kinsfolk after the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, along with the share of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, goes to the ruler of the Muslims.

Those who said this:

16126 - Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: 'Amr ibn Thabit narrated to us, from 'Imran ibn Zabyan, from Hukayym ibn Sa'd, from 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: Every person is given his share of the fifth, and the Imam takes charge of the share of Allah and His Messenger.

[Editor's note: "'Imran ibn Zabyan al-Hanafi," concerning whom there is something to consider; he inclined toward Shi'ism, and al-'Uqayli and Ibn 'Adi declared him weak. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, and Ibn Abi Hatim 3/1/300; it passed under no. 12100.
And "Hukayim ibn Sa'd al-Hanafi," Abu Tuhayy, whose standing is truthfulness. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 2/1/87, and Ibn Abi Hatim 1/2/286.
"Hukaym," with the ha' vowelled with a damma, a diminutive. "Tuhayy," with the ta' vowelled with a kasra.]

16127 - Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: that he was asked about the share of the kinsfolk, and he said: It was a provision for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ as long as he lived. When he died, it was assigned to the ruler after him.

[Editor's note: It passed in its wording, no. 16118; see also what passed earlier: 16125.]

* *

Others said: The share of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is returned into the fifth, and the fifth is divided into three shares: for the orphans, the needy, and the wayfarer. This is the statement of a group of the people of Iraq.

Others said: The entire fifth belongs to the relatives of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

Those who said this:

16128 - al-Harith narrated to me, saying: 'Abd al-'Aziz narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Ghaffar narrated to us, saying: al-Minhal ibn 'Amr narrated to us, who said: I asked 'Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn 'Ali and 'Ali ibn al-Husain about the fifth, and they both said: "It is ours." I said to 'Ali: "Allah says: 'and the orphans, and the needy, and the wayfarer.'" They said: "Our orphans and our needy."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct statement on this matter, in our view, is that the share of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is returned into the fifth, and the fifth is divided into four shares, according to what is reported from Ibn 'Abbas: one share for the kinsfolk, one share for the orphans, one share for the needy, and one share for the wayfarer. This is because Allah made the fifth obligatory for groups of people described by attributes, just as He made the other four-fifths obligatory. They have agreed that the right to the four-fifths belongs only to those who deserve it, and likewise the right of the people of the fifth belongs only to them. It is not permissible to transfer it from them to others, just as it is not permissible to divert some of the shares that Allah made for those He named in His Book, due to the absence of some of those who deserve them, to people other than the people of the (other) shares.

* *

As for the "orphans" (al-yatama), they are the children of the Muslims whose fathers have died. [See the explanation of "orphans" in the earlier volume 7:541, note 2, and the references there.]

And the "needy" (al-masakin) are the people of poverty and need among the Muslims. [See the explanation of "the needy" in the earlier volume 10:544, note 2, and the references there.]

And the "wayfarer" (ibn al-sabil) is one who passes through on a journey and has been cut off, [See the explanation of "wayfarer" in the earlier volume 8:346, 347, note 1, and the references there. His statement "cut off" (inqata'a bihi) is in the passive form, and it means one who is unable to continue his journey due to lost provisions, or his mount has perished, or his provisions have run out.] as follows:

16129 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: 'Abdullah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The fifth's quarter is for the wayfarer, who is the poor guest who arrives among the Muslims."

[Editor's note: See what passed earlier, nos. 16104 and 16124, and the notes on them.]

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿If you have believed in Allah and in what We sent down to Our servant on the Day of Criterion, the day the two armies met. And Allah is over all things competent﴾ (8:41).

Abu Ja'far said: He, may He be exalted, says: O believers, be certain that whatever you acquire of booty, its division is as I have explained, and affirm it, if you have acknowledged the oneness of Allah and what Allah sent down to His servant Muhammad ﷺ on the day He separated truth from falsehood at Badr. [See the explanation of "al-Furqan" (the Criterion) in the earlier pages, p. 487, note 2, and the references there.] He made manifest the victory of the believers and their dominance over their enemy. That is "the day the two armies met": the army of the believers and the army of the polytheists. "And Allah is over" the destruction of the people of disbelief and their humiliation at the hands of the believers, and over other things that He wills, "competent," no matter that He wills is withheld from Him. [See the explanation of "competent" in the earlier lexical indices under (q-d-r).]

* *

The commentators (ahl al-ta'wil) gave a statement similar to what we have said on this.

The Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ were three hundred and some ten men, and the polytheists were between one thousand and nine hundred. [Editor's note: "Yahya ibn Ya'qub ibn Mudrak al-Ansari," Abu Talib al-Qass (the storyteller), biographed in al-Kabir 4/2/312, Ibn Abi Hatim 4/2/198, Lisan al-Mizan 6:282, and Mizan al-I'tidal 3:306. ١٦١٣٧ - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, regarding ﴿And that which We sent down upon Our servant on the Day of the Criterion, the day the two hosts met﴾: i.e., the day I separated truth from falsehood by My power, [[In the printed edition: "i.e., the day He separated truth from falsehood at Badr, i.e., the day the two hosts met." This has played with what is in the manuscript, playing fast and loose, and it has done wrong and fallen short of trust. **The Interpretation of His Words (Exalted is He): ﴿When you were on the near side of the valley, and they were on the far side, and the caravan was lower than you.﴾**

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is He, says: Be certain, O believers, and know that the division of the spoils is as your Lord has explained it to you, if you truly believed in Allah and in what He sent down to His servant on the day of Badr, when He distinguished between truth and falsehood, by the support of His Messenger. ﴿When you were﴾, at that time, ﴿on the near side of the valley﴾, meaning: on the edge (*shafir*) of the valley nearest to Madina [[*Shafir al-wadi*: the side of its upper part, its boundary and its edge.]] ﴿and they were on the far side﴾, meaning: your enemy from among the polytheists was descending on the edge of the far valley, toward Makka. ﴿And the caravan was lower than you﴾, meaning: the caravan, in which was Abu Sufyan and his companions, was in a place lower than you, toward the seashore.

* *

Those who engage in *ta'wil* (interpretation) have said something similar to what we have said.

**Those who said this:**

16139. Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada: ﴿When you were on the near side of the valley﴾, he said: the edge of the nearer valley, and they were on the edge of the farther valley. ﴿And the caravan was lower than you﴾, he said: Abu Sufyan and his companions, lower than them.

16140. Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, regarding His words: ﴿When you were on the near side of the valley and they were on the far side﴾, and they were the edges of the valley. The Prophet of Allah was at the upper part of the valley, and the polytheists were at its lower part. ﴿And the caravan was lower than you﴾, meaning Abu Sufyan, [who descended with the caravan to its place (*hawzatihi*)], [[The printed edition wrote this phrase between brackets, and I do not know what it is. In the manuscript it reads: "*infakhada bil-'ir 'ala hawarma*," and I could not find a reading of it that I am satisfied with, nor did I find the report elsewhere.]] until he arrived with it at Makka.

16141. Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salama related to us, from Ibn Ishaq: ﴿When you were on the near side of the valley and they were on the far side﴾, from the valley toward Makka. ﴿And the caravan was lower than you﴾, that is: the caravan of Abu Sufyan, which you went out to seize, and they went out to protect, without an appointment between you and them. [[The report: 16141, Sira of Ibn Hisham 2:328, and it follows the earlier report no. 16137.]]

16142. Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿And the caravan was lower than you﴾, he said: Abu Sufyan and his companions, coming from Syria as merchants, who had not become aware of the companions of Badr, and Muhammad ﷺ had not become aware of the unbelievers of Quraysh, nor the unbelievers of Quraysh of Muhammad and his companions, until they met at the water of Badr, whoever was drawing water for them all. [[(3) In the printed edition: "*hatta iltaqa*" (dual), and I have kept what is in the manuscript.]] Then they fought, [[*Faqatalu* (they fought) is repeated twice in the manuscript, and I am doubtful about this whole sentence.]] and the companions of Muhammad ﷺ overcame them and took them captive.

16143. Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Huthayfa related to us, saying: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similarly.

16144. Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ishaq related to us, saying: 'Abd Allah related to us, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

16145. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, who said: He mentioned the positions of the people and the caravan, and said: ﴿When you were on the near side of the valley and they were on the far side﴾, and the caravan: it was Abu Sufyan ﴿lower than you﴾, on the shore of the sea. [[In the printed edition: "Abu Sufyan wa 'ayruhu" (Abu Sufyan and his caravan), which adds what is not in the manuscript.]]

* *

The readers differed regarding the recitation of His words: "*idh antum bil-'adwa*."

The majority of the readers of Madina and Kufa recited it: ﴿bil-'udwa﴾, with a *damma* on the *'ayn*.

Some of the readers of Makka and Basra recited it: ﴿bil-'idwa﴾, with a *kasra* on the *'ayn*.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: They are two well-known dialects with the same meaning, so whichever of them the reciter reads is correct. The verse of al-Ra'i is recited:

"And two eyes, red at their corners, as a gazelle calf looks at the *'idwa*."

With a *kasra* on the 'ayn of "*al-'adwa*." Likewise, the verse of Aws ibn Hajar is recited:

"And a horseman, if horses were to alight at his *'idwa*, they would turn away swiftly, and they would not intend to advance."

[[From his ode lamenting Fudala ibn Kalada al-Asadi. The verse is in *Muntaha al-Talab*, and not in his *Diwan*. Before it he says: "Am li-'adiyatin tardi mulamlamatin... ka-annaha 'aridun fi hadb awal" ... "Lama ra'awka 'ala nahdin maraakiluhu... yas'a bi-bizzi kamiyyin ghayri mi'zal"; and "Wa faris la yahullu al-qawm 'udwatahu..." Its reading is better than his reading "*law tahullu*," for the negation here is the correct sense of the statement.]]

* *

**The Interpretation of His Words: ﴿Even if you had made an appointment, you would have differed about the appointment; but Allah might accomplish a matter that was to be done.﴾**

Abu Ja'far said: He, Exalted is His remembrance, means: Even if your gathering at the place where you gathered, you, O believers, and your enemy from the polytheists, had been by a mutual appointment between you and them, ﴿you would have differed about the appointment﴾, because of the greatness of your enemy's number and the smallness of yours. But Allah gathered you without any appointment between you and them. [[See the explanation of "*al-mi'ad*" (appointment) above, 6:222.]] ﴿But Allah might accomplish a matter that was to be done﴾. That decree from Allah was His support of His allies from among the believers in Allah and His Messenger, and the destruction of His enemies and their enemies at Badr by killing and capture, as follows:

16146. Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salama related to us, from Ibn Ishaq: ﴿Even if you had made an appointment, you would have differed about the appointment﴾: even if that had been by an appointment between you and them, and then the greatness of their number and the smallness of yours had reached you, you would not have met them. ﴿But Allah might accomplish a matter that was to be done﴾, meaning: that Allah might accomplish what He willed by His power, of the exaltation of Islam and its people and the humiliation of polytheism and its people, not by a deliberate plan (*mala'*) from you, [[In the printed edition: "*'an ghayri bala'*" (without trial), and in the Sira of Ibn Hisham, in the original printed edition, the same, which is extremely corrupt speech. In the manuscript of al-Tabari and the manuscripts of Ibn Hisham and the European printed edition: "*'an ghayri mala'*," as I have written.

It is said: "*Ma kana hadha al-amr 'an mala' minna*," meaning: it was not by consultation and gathering. In the hadith of 'Umar when he was stabbed: "*Akana hadha 'an mala' minkum?*" meaning: was this by consultation with your nobles and your community?

Then the editor of the printed edition changed the following word, writing "*fa'ala*" in place of "*fa-fa'ala*." All of this is pointless meddling and a lack of scruple.]] and He did what He willed of that by His kindness. [[The report: 16146, Sira of Ibn Hisham 2:328, and it follows the earlier report no. 16141.]]

16147. Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: Yunus ibn Shihab informed me, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Ka'b ibn Malik informed me, that 'Abd Allah ibn Ka'b said: I heard Ka'b ibn Malik say regarding the battle of Badr: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the Muslims only set out seeking the caravan of Quraysh, until Allah brought them together with their enemy without an appointment. [[The report: "'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Ka'b ibn Malik al-Ansari," trustworthy, who related from his father. Al-Zuhri related from him. He was the most knowledgeable and retentive of his people. Biographed in *al-Tahdhib* and Ibn Abi Hatim 2/2/249.

And "'Abd Allah ibn Ka'b ibn Malik al-Ansari," trustworthy, who was the guide of his father when he became blind, and related from his father. He related. His son 'Abd al-Rahman related from him, and al-Zuhri related from him. Biographed in *al-Tahdhib* and Ibn Abi Hatim 2/2/142.

In the manuscript it reads: "*Innama yakhruju Rasul Allah*," which is good Arabic, but in the references it is "*Innama kharaja*," so I have kept it as in the printed edition.

This report is part of the lengthy report of Ka'b ibn Malik concerning the expedition of Tabuk, and what happened in his staying behind until Allah accepted his repentance.

It was narrated by Ahmad in his *Musnad* 3:456, 457, 459 and 6:387.

It was narrated by al-Bukhari in his *Sahih* (*al-Fath* 8:86).

It was narrated by Muslim in his *Sahih* by this route 17:87.]]

16148. Ya'qub related to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayya related to us, from Ibn 'Awn, from 'Umayr ibn Ishaq, who said: Abu Sufyan came with the caravan from Syria, and Abu Jahl went out to prevent him from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his companions. They met at Badr, and neither group was aware of the other, until the water-carriers met. He said: And the people charged (*nahada*) at one another. [[The report: 16148, "Ibn 'Awn" is "'Abd Allah ibn 'Awn al-Muzani," who has passed several times.

And "'Umayr ibn Ishaq al-Qurashi," from whom none related except Ibn 'Awn, and he is spoken of with criticism. It passed as no. 7776.

In the printed edition it was "'Umar ibn Ishaq," which shows that the editor did not read the manuscript well.

As for His words, "*nahada al-nas ba'duhum li-ba'd*": they rose to fight. It is said: "*Nahada al-qawm ila 'aduwwihim wa li-'aduwwihim*," meaning: they stood firm against him and began fighting him. And "*nahadu yas'aluhu*" means: they began and rose up.

It seems the editor of the printed edition did not understand it or did not read it well, so he wrote in place of "*nahada*": "*nazara al-nas*" (the people looked), and this is from his long meddling with this noble text, until he became accustomed to meddling and grew to enjoy it.]]

* *

**The Interpretation of His Words: ﴿That whoever perishes might perish upon clear evidence, and whoever lives might live upon clear evidence. Indeed, Allah is Hearing and Knowing.﴾ (42)**

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is His remembrance, says: But Allah gathered them there, that He might accomplish a matter that was to be done, ﴿that whoever perishes might perish upon clear evidence﴾.

And this "*li*" (lam) in His words "*liyahlika*" (that he might perish) is repeated on the "*lam*" in His words "*liyaqdiya*" (that He might accomplish), as if He had said: But that whoever perishes might perish upon clear evidence, He gathered you.

By His words "*liyahlika man halaka 'an bayyina*," He means: that whoever among His creatures dies might die after a proof from Allah has been established against him and his excuse cut off, and a lesson which he has witnessed and seen [[See the explanation of "*halaka*" (perish) above, p. 149, note 1, and the references there.]]. ﴿And whoever lives might live upon clear evidence﴾, He says: and that whoever lives among them might live after a proof from Allah has been established for him and has become manifest to his eye, so that he knows it, by Our gathering you and your enemy there. [[See the explanation of "*bayyina*" (clear evidence) above in the lexical indexes under (*bayn*).]]

* *

Ibn Ishaq said regarding this:

16149. Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salama related to us, from Ibn Ishaq: ﴿that whoever perishes might perish upon clear evidence﴾, [meaning: that whoever disbelieves after the proof might disbelieve,] [[This addition between the brackets is necessary; I have added it from the Sira of Ibn Hisham.]] because of what he saw of the sign and the lesson, ﴿and whoever believes might believe upon the same﴾. [[In the printed edition: "*min al-ayati wal-'ibar*" (of the signs and lessons), and in the manuscript: "*min al-ayati wal-'ibarati*" (of the sign and the lesson). I have kept the correct reading from the Sira of Ibn Hisham.]] [[The report: 16149, Sira of Ibn Hisham 2:328, and it follows the earlier report no. 16146.]]

* *

As for His words, ﴿And indeed Allah is Hearing and Knowing﴾, its meaning is: ﴿And indeed Allah﴾, O believers, ﴿is Hearing﴾ of your words and the words of others, when Allah showed His Prophet in his dream and showed you your enemy as few in your eyes, though they were many, and showed your enemy you as few in their eyes; ﴿Knowing﴾ of what your souls conceal and what your hearts hold within them, at that time and in every state.

[[See the explanation of "*sami'*" (Hearing) and "*'alim*" (Knowing) above in the lexical indexes under (*sami'a*) and (*'alima*).]]

He, may His praise be exalted, says to them and to His servants: So fear your Lord, O people, in your speech, that you do not speak without right, and in your hearts, that you do not hold within them anything other than right guidance, for indeed Allah is not hidden from any hidden thing, whether apparent or concealed.

**The interpretation of His words:** ﴿When Allah showed them to you in your sleep as few; and had He shown them to you as many, you would have lost heart and disputed about the matter, but Allah saved you. Indeed, He is Knowing of what is in the breasts﴾ [8:43].

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is He, says: Indeed Allah, O Muhammad, hears what your companions say and knows what they conceal, when Allah shows you your enemy and their enemy ﴿in your sleep as few﴾, meaning: He shows them to you in your sleep as few, so that you inform them of that, until their hearts were strengthened and they grew bold to fight their enemy. ﴿And had your Lord shown you your enemy and their enemy as many, your companions would have lost heart, become cowardly and hesitant﴾ [[In the printed edition: "became cowardly and feared", which differs from the manuscript. It is said "khāma fī al-qitāl" (he hesitated in battle) when he becomes cowardly, so he retreats, recoils and turns back.]] ﴿and would not have been able to fight the people﴾ [[See the explanation of "fashal" (loss of heart) above, 7:168, 289.]] ﴿and would have disputed about it﴾ [[See the explanation of "tanāzu'" (dispute) above, 7:289; 8:504.]] ﴿but Allah saved them from that by what He showed you in your sleep of the vision. Indeed, He is Knowing of what the breasts conceal﴾ [[In the printed edition: "what the breasts hide", which differs from the manuscript to no purpose, and both have the same meaning.]] nothing that the hearts conceal is hidden from Him. [[See the explanation of "dhāt al-ṣudūr" (what is in the breasts) above, 7:155, 325; 10:94.]]

* *

Some have claimed that the meaning of His words ﴿when Allah shows them to you in your sleep as few﴾ is: "in your eye with which you sleep," so that "al-manām" (sleep) is taken to mean the eye, as though he intended: when Allah shows them to you in your eye as few. [[This is Abu 'Ubayda in Majāz al-Qur'ān 1:247.]]

* *

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) said things similar to what we have said on this matter.

Those who said that:

16150. Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿when Allah showed them to you in your sleep as few﴾: He said: Allah showed them to him in his sleep as few, so the Prophet ﷺ informed his companions of that, and it was a reassurance for them.

16151. Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa related to us, saying: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similarly.

16152. ...And he said: Ishaq related to us, saying: 'Abd Allah related to us, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

16153. Ibn Humayd related to me, saying: Salama related to us, from Ibn Ishaq: ﴿when Allah showed them to you in your sleep as few﴾, the verse. The first of what He showed him of that was a blessing of His upon them, with which He encouraged them against their enemy, and with which He warded off what they had feared for their weakness, because He knew what was in them. [[The report: 16153 — Sirat Ibn Hisham 2:328; it follows the earlier report no. 16149.]] [[In the printed edition: "and He warded off for them what they feared ...", whereas in the manuscript: "and He restrained from them what was feared", which breaks the sentence; I have adopted the text of Ibn Hisham. Al-Khushani vocalized it in the passive voice.

In the Sira, after the completion of the sentence, it reads: "Ibn Hisham said: '(takhawwuf) is a substitution for a word that Ibn Ishaq mentioned, but I did not mention it.'" Abu Dhar al-Khushani, in his commentary on the Sira, then said: "The word is said to be (takhawwuf), with a fatḥa on the tā', khā' and wāw; and it is said that it was (takhawwafat), and Ibn Hisham corrected that because of the ugliness of the expression with regard to Allah, Mighty and Majestic."

This cannot be accepted, because Ibn Hisham explicitly states that he forgot it and did not mention it, so he substituted another word for it; he changed it only because of the reason of forgetfulness.]]

* *

The people of interpretation differed regarding the interpretation of His words: ﴿but Allah saved﴾.

Some of them said: Its meaning is: but Allah secured their affair for the believers, until He made them victorious over their enemy.

Those who said that:

16154. Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: My father related to me, saying: My paternal uncle related to me, saying: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His words ﴿but Allah saved﴾: He says: Allah secured their affair for them until He made them victorious over their enemy.

* *

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: but Allah secured His command concerning them.

Those who said that:

16155. Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr related to us, saying: Ma'mar related to us, from Qatada: ﴿but Allah saved﴾: He said: He secured His command concerning them.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of the two opinions in my view is what Ibn 'Abbas said, namely that Allah saved the people, through what He showed His Prophet ﷺ in his sleep, from the loss of heart and dispute, until their hearts were strengthened and they grew bold to fight their enemy. That is because His words ﴿but Allah saved﴾ come directly after His words ﴿and had He shown them to you as many, you would have lost heart and disputed about the matter﴾; so the more appropriate thing to report about it is that He, exalted is His praise, saved them from what they had feared, had He not shown His Prophet ﷺ the fewness of the people in his sleep.

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And when He showed them to you as few when you met them, and made you appear few in their eyes, that Allah might accomplish a matter already decreed. And to Allah are all matters returned.﴾ (8:44)

Abu Ja'far said: He, exalted is His remembrance, says: "Indeed Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing" — when Allah showed His Prophet the polytheists as few in his dream, and when Allah showed them the believers as few in their eyes when they met them, though their number was great, and made the believers appear few in their eyes, so that they would abandon preparation against them, and thus the might of the believers would seem insignificant to them, as related:

16156 - Ibn Bazi' al-Baghdadi narrated to me, saying: Ishaq ibn Mansur narrated to us, from Isra'il, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu Ubaydah, from Abdullah, who said: "They were made to appear few in our eyes on the Day of Badr, so that I said to a man beside me: Do you think they are seventy?" He said: "I think they are a hundred." Then we took a man of them captive and we said: "How many are they?" He said: "A thousand." [[Report 16156: Ibn Bazi' al-Baghdadi is Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Bazi' al-Baghdadi, one of the shaykhs of Muslim; it has passed as nos. 2451, 3130, 10239. In the printed edition it read "kunna alfan" ("we were a thousand"), adding "kunna"; I have kept what is in the manuscript, which is entirely correct.]]

16157 - Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Isra'il narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu Ubaydah, from Abdullah, with similar wording.

16158 - al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding His saying: "And when He showed them to you as few when you met them, and made you appear few in their eyes." He said: Ibn Mas'ud said: "They were made to appear few in our eyes, until I said to a man: Do you think they are a hundred?"

16159 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said: Some people of the polytheists said: "The caravan has departed, so return." Abu Jahl said: "Now that Muhammad and his companions have come out against you! Do not return until you have wiped them out." And he said: "O people, do not kill them with weapons, but take them captive, and bind them with ropes!" — he said this out of self-assurance.

* *

As for His saying: "that Allah might accomplish a matter already decreed," He, exalted is His praise, says: I made you, O believers, appear few in the eyes of the polytheists, and I showed them to you as few in your eyes, so that Allah might decide between you what He decreed of fighting among yourselves, and your victory, O believers, over your enemies among the polytheists, and your triumph over them, so that the word of Allah would be the highest and the word of those who disbelieved the lowest. That is a matter which Allah was to do, and He carried out His command in it, as related:

16160 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: "that Allah might accomplish a matter already decreed," meaning: that He might bring them together for war, for vengeance upon whomever He willed to take vengeance against, and for the bestowal of favor upon those whom He willed to complete His blessing upon, from among the people of His guardianship. [[Report 16160: Sirat Ibn Hisham 2:328; it follows the preceding report no. 16153.]]

* *

= "And to Allah are all matters returned": He, exalted is His praise, says: the final outcome of all matters returns to Him in the Hereafter, and He will recompense their people according to their deserving, the doer of good with His goodness, and the doer of evil with his evil.

**The exposition of His words: ﴿O you who have believed, when you encounter a company [of disbelievers], stand firm and remember Allah much, that you may be successful﴾ [Qur'an 8:45]**

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: This is an instruction from Allah, may His praise be exalted, to the people of faith in Him, concerning the conduct in fighting His enemies from among the people of disbelief in Him, and the actions through which they may hope, by practicing them when they meet the enemy, to be granted victory over them and to prevail against them. Then He, may His praise be exalted, says to them: "O you who have believed," (affirm that you believe in Allah and His Messenger), "when you encounter a company of those who disbelieve in Allah in battle and combat," [[See the explanation of "fi'ah" (company) above, p. 455, note 2, and the references there.]] "then stand firm for their fighting, and do not flee from them or turn your backs in retreat, except one who swerves to [another position for] fighting or joins a company of your own," "and remember Allah much," meaning: call upon Allah for victory over them and for prevailing against them, and let your hearts and tongues be mindful of Him. "That you may be successful" means: so that you may succeed and prevail over your enemy, and Allah may grant you victory and triumph over them. [[See the explanation of "al-falah" (success) above, p. 169, note 2, and the references there.]] As related:

1616 (1). Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning His words: "O you who have believed, when you encounter a company, stand firm and remember Allah much, that you may be successful." He said: Allah has enjoined His remembrance at the time you are most preoccupied, at the clashing of swords.

1616 (2). Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: "O you who have believed, when you encounter a company," who fight you in the way of Allah, "then stand firm and remember Allah much," remember Allah, to whom you have given your souls, and fulfil what you pledged to Him in your allegiance, "that you may be successful." [[The report 1616(2) is in Sirah Ibn Hisham 2:329, and it follows the earlier report numbered 1616.]]

The interpretation of His words: ﴿And obey Allah and His Messenger, and do not dispute with one another, lest you lose courage and your strength depart. And be patient. Indeed, Allah is with the patient.﴾ (46)

Abu Ja'far said: He, exalted is His remembrance, says to the believers in Him: Obey, O believers, your Lord and His Messenger in what He has commanded you and forbidden you, and do not oppose them in anything. "And do not dispute with one another, lest you lose courage" means: do not differ, lest you split apart and your hearts diverge. [[See the explanation of "tanazu'" (dispute) above, p. 569, note 5, and the references there.]] "Lest you lose courage" means: lest you become weak and cowardly. [[See the explanation of "fashal" (losing courage) p. 569, note 4, and the references there.]] "And your strength depart."

* *

This is a figure of speech. A man is said, when fortune is turned toward him and he is pleased by what he loves, to have "the wind (rih) favorable to him." By this is meant what he loves. Among the poetry on this is the verse of 'Ubayd ibn al-Abras:

*As We protected you on the day of al-Na'f from Shatab, and the superiority of the people lies in wind and numbers.*

[[From his Diwan, p. 49, from verses preceding it, where he says: "He called out to his people, but their ears were stopped. Alas for my soul, if only he had called to Banu Asad.

They do not call out when the warriors turn back, nor when the swords are in the hands of the people like flaming embers.

Had they been your protectors in the protected place, they would have protected you, and you would not have been left on a day that set the people in distress.

As We protected you..."

The second verse of these lines appears in the Diwan manuscript as: "They do not call when the warriors turn back, nor when..." The editor, the orientalist, corrected it to: "Let them call, the protector of the warriors, not out of laziness," which produces an entirely insipid half-line. So it should be corrected as I have recorded it. By his words "they do not call when the warriors turn back" he means they do not summon one another to abandon flight; "khama" means to recoil, as another poet said: "They called to one another: O family of 'Amr, do not flee! So we said: No flight and no turning away."

"Al-Na'f" is what slopes down from the rough ground of a mountain. "Shatab" is a mountain in the lands of Banu Asad.]] That is, of strength and multitude.

* *

What is meant in this place is: your power and might will depart, so you become weak, and weakness and disorder will enter you.

* *

"And be patient," means: be patient alongside the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when you meet your enemy, and do not flee from him or abandon him. "Indeed, Allah is with the patient," means: be patient, for I am with you. [[See the explanation of "ma'" (with) above, p. 455, note 4, and the references there.]]
