Those who engaged in ta'wil (interpretation) said the same as what we have said on this matter.

Those who said this:

16163. Muhammad ibn 'Amr told me, he said: Abu 'Asim told us, he said: 'Isa told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding His words "and your strength depart," he said: your victory. He said: The strength of the companions of Muhammad ﷺ departed when they disputed with him on the day of Uhud.

16164. Ibn Numayr told us, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "and your strength depart," and he mentioned something similar.

16165. al-Qasim told us, he said: al-Husayn told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, similar, except that he said: the strength of the companions of Muhammad departed when they abandoned him on the day of Uhud.

16166. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told me, he said: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, he said: Asbat told us, from al-Suddi: "And do not dispute, lest you lose courage and your strength depart," he said: your vigor (hadd) and your zeal (jidd). [[In the printed edition: "your war and your zeal," but the manuscript is nearly readable as he read it, though the writing shows he meant "hadd-kum." "Al-hadd" is a man's valor and the thrust of his courage. One says "so-and-so has hadd," meaning valor and courage. Had it been read "wahdatakum" (your unity), it would have been correct; "al-hadd" and "al-hidda" (with a kasra on the ha') are the same. See the following note.]]

16167. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah: "and your strength depart," he said: the strength of war.

16168. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words "and your strength depart," he said: "al-rih" is victory. Victory never came except by a wind that Allah sends, striking the faces of the enemy. When that wind departs, they have no standing.

16169. Ibn Humayd told us, he said: Salamah told us, from Ibn Ishaq: "And do not dispute, lest you lose courage," that is: do not differ, so your affair will be divided. "And your strength depart," so your vigor (hadd) departs. "And be patient, indeed Allah is with the patient," that is: I am with you if you do that. [[The report: 16169, Sirat Ibn Hisham 2:329, which continues the previous report numbered 16162.]]

16170. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words "And do not dispute, lest you lose courage," he said: "al-fashal" is weakness in striving against one's enemy and yielding to them. That is "fashal."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 8, verse 47:

On the interpretation of His words: ﴿And be not like those who went forth from their homes insolently and to be seen of men, and who bar from the way of Allah; and Allah encompasses what they do.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: This is an admonition from Allah, may His praise be great, to the believers in Him and His Messenger, that they should not do any deed except for Allah alone, seeking what is with Him, not to be seen by people, just as the polytheists did on their march to Badr, seeking to be seen by people. That is because they were informed that the caravan had escaped the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his companions, [[In the manuscript: "near the caravan", and the correct reading is what is in the printed edition.]] and it was said to them: "Turn back, for the caravan you came to support has been saved!" But they refused and said: "We will go to Badr and drink wine there, and female singers will play for us, and the Arabs will speak of us there," [[In the printed edition: "and the Arabs will speak of us for our standing there," which adds what is not in the manuscript.]] so they were given the cups of death in place of wine, as-

161171 - Abd al-Warith ibn Abd al-Samad narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: Aban narrated to us, saying: Hisham ibn Urwah narrated to us, from Urwah, who said: Before the Prophet ﷺ met them on the Day of Badr, Quraysh had been approached by a rider from Abu Sufyan and the company with him: "We have let the people pass, so turn back." [[In the printed edition: "so turn back", and I have kept what is in the manuscript, which agrees with what is in the History.]] Then the company that Abu Sufyan had sent, who were ordering Quraysh to return, came to al-Juhfah, and they said: "By Allah, we will not return until we reach Badr, and remain there three nights, and those of the Hijaz who have gathered around us will see us, for no Arab will see us and what we have gathered and then fight us." These are the ones of whom Allah said: "those who went forth from their homes insolently and to be seen of men." They met the Prophet ﷺ, and Allah granted victory to His Messenger, humbled the leaders of disbelief, and healed the hearts of the believers from them. [[Report 16171: this is from the letter of Urwah ibn al-Zubayr to Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan, which I previously took out from the History of al-Tabari in compiled form under no. 16083. This section is in the History of al-Tabari 2: 269.]]

161172 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, saying: Ibn Ishaq narrated to me, in a report he mentioned, saying: Muhammad ibn Muslim, Asim ibn Umar, [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "Asim ibn Amr", which is an error; it is "Asim ibn Umar ibn Qatadah", which has been mentioned many times before; see the Sirah of Ibn Hisham 2: 257.]] Abd Allah ibn Abi Bakr, and Yazid ibn Ruman narrated to me, from Urwah ibn al-Zubayr and others of our scholars, from Ibn Abbas, who said: When Abu Sufyan saw that he had secured his caravan, he sent to Quraysh: "You only went out to protect your caravan, your men and your wealth, and Allah has saved them, so turn back!" Abu Jahl ibn Hisham said: "By Allah, we will not return until we reach Badr," - and Badr was a seasonal gathering of the Arabs, where a market gathered for them every year - "and we will remain there three days, slaughter camels, feed the people, serve wine, female singers will play for us, and the Arabs will hear of us, and they will continue to fear us forever. So proceed." [[Report 16172: Sirah of Ibn Hisham 2: 270, and the History of al-Tabari 2: 276, from a long report.]]

161173 - Ibn Humayd said: Salamah narrated to us, saying: Ibn Ishaq said: "And be not like those who went forth from their homes insolently and to be seen of men," meaning: Do not be like Abu Jahl and his companions who said: "We will not return until we reach Badr, slaughter camels, serve wine with them, female singers will play for us, and the Arabs will hear of us, and they will continue to fear us." That is, let your affair not be for show or reputation, nor seeking what people have; make your intention and reckoning sincerely for Allah in supporting your religion and aiding your Prophet; that is, do not act except for Allah, and seek nothing else. [[Report 16173: Sirah of Ibn Hisham 2: 329, and it follows the earlier report no. 16169. The wording differs slightly.]]

161174 - Muhammad ibn Umarah al-Asadi narrated to me, saying: Ubayd Allah ibn Musa narrated to us, saying: Israil informed us; and Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Israil narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "Those who went forth from their homes insolently and to be seen of men," he said: the companions of Badr.

161175 - Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: "insolently and to be seen of men," he said: Abu Jahl and his companions on the Day of Badr.

161176 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, the like of it. Ibn Juraij said: Abd Allah ibn Kathir said: They are the polytheists of Quraysh, and that was their going out to Badr.

161177 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas: "And be not like those who went forth from their homes insolently and to be seen of men," meaning: the polytheists who fought the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the Day of Badr.

161178 - Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: "went forth from their homes insolently and to be seen of men," he said: They are Quraysh, Abu Jahl and his companions, who went forth on the Day of Badr.

161179 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: "And be not like those who went forth from their homes insolently and to be seen of men, and who bar from the way of Allah; and Allah encompasses what they do," he said: The polytheists of Quraysh who fought the Prophet of Allah on the Day of Badr went forth with arrogance and pride. It was said to them that day: "Turn back, for your caravan has departed, and you have been victorious." They said: "No, by Allah, until the people of the Hijaz speak of our march and our number!" He said: It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of Allah ﷺ said that day: "O Allah, Quraysh has come with its pride and vanity to oppose You and Your Messenger!"

161180 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said: He mentioned the polytheists and what they fed at the watering places, and said: "And be not like those who went forth from their homes insolently and to be seen of men, and who bar from the way of Allah."

161181 - It was narrated to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh al-Fadl ibn Khalid say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words: "those who went forth from their homes insolently," he said: They are the polytheists, who went forth to Badr in haughtiness and insolence.

161182 - Al-Harith narrated to me, saying: Abd al-Aziz narrated to us, saying: Abu Ma'shar narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, who said: When Quraysh went out from Makkah to Badr, they went out with female singers and tambourines, so Allah revealed: "And be not like those who went forth from their homes insolently and to be seen of men, and who bar from the way of Allah; and Allah encompasses what they do."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The meaning of the speech, then, is: And be not, O believers in Allah and His Messenger, in acting for show and reputation, and abandoning sincerity of deed to Allah and seeking reward for it, like the army of the people of disbelief in Allah and His Messenger, who went forth from their dwellings insolently and to be seen of people by their finery, their wealth, the abundance of their numbers, and the strength of their supporters [[See the explanation of "ri'a'" above: 5: 521, 522; 8: 356; 9: 331.]] = "and who bar from the way of Allah," meaning: and who prevent people from the religion of Allah and from entering Islam, by fighting them and torturing those among the believers in Allah whom they could overpower [[See the explanation of "sadd" above, p. 529, note 2, and the references there. And the explanation of "way of Allah" above in the indexes of language (sabl).]] = "and Allah encompasses what they do," meaning: from showing off and barring from the way of Allah, and other of their deeds = "encompasses," meaning: He knows all of that, nothing of it is hidden from Him, for all things are manifest to Him, and nothing of them escapes Him; so He will requite them for it and punish them for it. [[See the explanation of "muhit" above: 9: 252, note 3, and the references there.]]

**The interpretation of His words: ﴿And when Satan made their deeds seem attractive to them and said, "No one among the people can overcome you today, and I am your protector." But when the two hosts came into view, he turned on his heels and said, "I am free of you. I see what you do not see. I fear Allah, and Allah is severe in punishment."﴾ (8:48)**

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, means by His words: ﴿And when Satan made their deeds seem attractive to them﴾, and when Satan made their deeds seem attractive to them, and his making them attractive was [as follows]. [[See the explanation of "zayyana" (made attractive) in earlier volume 12, p. 136, note 1, and the references there.]] As related:

16183. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abdullah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talha, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Iblis came on the day of Badr with an army of devils, carrying his banner, in the form of a man from Banu Mudlij, and the Satan in the form of Suraqa ibn Malik ibn Ju'shum. [[In the printed edition, the phrase "and the Satan" has been omitted, and the account has been run as a single continuous passage.]] Then Satan said to the polytheists: ﴿No one among the people can overcome you today, and I am your protector.﴾ When the people lined up, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took a handful of dust and threw it into the faces of the polytheists, and they turned their backs in flight. Gabriel approached Iblis, and when he saw him, Iblis's hand was in the hand of one of the polytheists; so he withdrew his hand and fled, he and his followers. The man said: "O Suraqa, do you claim you are our protector?" He said: ﴿I see what you do not see. I fear Allah, and Allah is severe in punishment.﴾ This was when he saw the angels.

16184. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said: Iblis came to the polytheists in the form of Suraqa ibn Malik ibn Ju'shum al-Kinani the poet, then al-Mudlaji. He came on a horse and said to the polytheists: ﴿No one among the people can overcome you today!﴾ They said: "And who are you?" He said: "I am your protector, Suraqa. These are the Kinana, who have come to you!"

16185. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, saying: Ibn Ishaq said: Yazid ibn Ruman narrated to me, from Urwa ibn al-Zubayr, who said: When Quraysh resolved to march out, they recalled the enmity between them and Banu Bakr — meaning the war — and that nearly deterred them. Then Iblis appeared to them in the form of Suraqa [ibn Malik] ibn Ju'shum al-Mudlaji, who was one of the nobles of Banu Kinana, and said: "I am your protector against Kinana coming to you from behind with something you dislike!" So they set out quickly. [[The report 16185: Ibn Hisham's Sira 2:263; the words in parentheses are taken from it.]]

16186. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, saying: Ibn Ishaq said, concerning His words: ﴿And when Satan made their deeds seem attractive to them and said, "No one among the people can overcome you today, and I am your protector"﴾, he mentioned Iblis's enticing of them and his impersonation of Suraqa ibn Malik ibn Ju'shum to them, [[In the printed edition, "to them" has been omitted; it is present in the manuscript and in Ibn Hisham's Sira.]] when they mentioned what lay between them and Banu Bakr ibn Abd Manat ibn Kinana in the war that had been between them. [[In the printed edition: "from the war"; this differs from the manuscript and matches Ibn Hisham's Sira. The editor, as you know and see, frequently tampers with the words of the scholars.]] Allah says: ﴿But when the two hosts came into view﴾, and the enemy of Allah looked at the armies of Allah from the angels, with whom Allah had strengthened His Messenger and the believers against their enemy, ﴿he turned on his heels and said, "I am free of you. I see what you do not see"﴾ — and the enemy of Allah spoke truly, for he did see what they did not see — and said: ﴿I fear Allah, and Allah is severe in punishment﴾. So he led them astray and then abandoned them.

He said: It was related to me that they used to see him at every stopping place in the form of Suraqa ibn Malik ibn Ju'shum, and they did not deny him, until the day of Badr, when the two hosts met. The one who saw him when he turned back was either "al-Harith ibn Hisham" or "Umayr ibn Wahb al-Jumahi." One of them was mentioned, and he said: "Where, O Suraqa!" [[This sentence and the one that follows are completely altered by the editor, who wrote: "He said, 'Where is Suraqa! We have been betrayed by the enemy of Allah, and he has gone.'" The text in the manuscript matches Ibn Hisham's Sira. The phrase "mathal" here means he stood up and rose.]] And the enemy of Allah stood up and departed. [[The report 16186: Ibn Hisham's Sira 2:318, 319. He moved the opening of the report to its end. This report is not narrated by Ibn Hisham in the context of the interpretation of these verses in his Sira 2:329, following the earlier report no. 16173; rather, he mentioned the verse and then said: "The interpretation of this verse has already passed."]]

16187. Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, concerning His words: ﴿And when Satan made their deeds seem attractive to them﴾ up to His words: ﴿Severe in punishment﴾. He said: It was related to us that he saw Gabriel descending with the angels accompanying him, so the enemy of Allah claimed that he had no power against the angels, and said: ﴿I see what you do not see. I fear Allah﴾. The enemy of Allah lied, by Allah; there was no fear of Allah in him, but he knew that he had no strength and no protection. That is the habit of the enemy of Allah toward whoever obeys him and submits to him, until, when truth and falsehood meet, he hands them over to the worst fate, [[In the printed edition: "and sought refuge in him", differing from the manuscript, which reads "with his bad trustworthiness and opinion". "Istaqada lahu" means he submitted to him and obeyed him.]] and disowns them at that moment. ["Muslam" (with a u, then a sukun, then a fatha) is a verbal noun, meaning "surrender/submission".]

16188. Al-Qasim narrated to me, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn Abbas said: ﴿And when Satan made their deeds seem attractive to them﴾, the verse. He said: When the day of Badr came, Iblis marched with his banner and his armies alongside the polytheists, and he cast into the hearts of the polytheists: "No one will defeat you, and I am your protector!" When they met, and Satan saw the reinforcements of the angels, he turned on his heels — that is, he turned back fleeing — and said: ﴿I see what you do not see﴾, the verse.

16189. Ahmad ibn al-Faraj narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Malik ibn Abd al-Aziz ibn al-Majishun narrated to us, saying: Malik narrated to us, from Ibrahim ibn Abi Ablah, from Talha ibn Ubayd Allah ibn Kurayz, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Iblis has never been seen on a day more humiliated, more abased, more repelled, or more enraged than on the day of Arafa, and that is because of what he sees of the descent of mercy and the pardoning of sins — except what he saw on the day of Badr!" They said: "O Messenger of Allah, what did he see on the day of Badr?" He said: "He saw Gabriel marshaling the angels. [[Report 16189: Malik related it in the Muwatta, p. 422, in nearly this wording. See also Ibn Abd al-Barr's al-Taqassi, pp. 12, 13.

Ahmad ibn al-Faraj ibn Sulayman al-Himsi is the teacher of al-Tabari; he was mentioned earlier under nos. 6899 and 15377. Abd al-Malik ibn Abd al-Aziz ibn al-Majishun al-Taymi was a jurist and mufti of Medina in his time; he was the son of a jurist, and he was weak in hadith. He is described in al-Tahdhib and in Ibn Abi Hatim, 2/2/358.

Ibrahim ibn Abi Ablah al-Ramli was mentioned earlier under no. 11014.

Talha ibn Ubayd Allah ibn Kurayz ibn Jabir al-Ka'bi was of few narrations, and was mentioned earlier under no. 15585.

This is a mursal report.

His words "yaza' al-malaika" mean: he arranges them, levels them, and draws them up in rows for battle, as though he restrains them from scattering and dispersing. The "wazi'" is the one who goes before the army, entrusted with the rows and the management of their affairs and their arrangement in fighting the enemy. From their saying: "wazzahu," meaning he restrained him and held him back from some action or other.]]

16190. Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sulayman ibn al-Mughira narrated to us, from Humayd ibn Hilal, from al-Hasan, concerning His words: ﴿I see what you do not see﴾, who said: He saw Gabriel wearing a turban with a cloak [[The "i'tijar" is wrapping the turban around the head in a circle, without passing it under the chin; passing it under the chin is called "talahhi" (with a doubled ha).]] walking before the Prophet (ﷺ), and in his hand was the bridle, which he rode.

16191. Ibn Wakic narrated to us, saying: Hashim ibn al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Sulayman ibn al-Mughira narrated to us, from Humayd ibn Hilal, who said: Al-Hasan said, reciting this verse: ﴿And when Satan made their deeds seem attractive to them﴾, the verse. He said: Iblis marched with the polytheists at Badr with his banner and his armies, and he cast into the hearts of the polytheists that no one would defeat them, "while you are fighting for the religion of your fathers, and you will not be defeated by numbers!" When the two hosts met, he turned on his heels — he means he turned back fleeing — and said: ﴿I am free of you. I see what you do not see﴾, meaning the angels. [[In the printed edition: "lan yaghlibakum," but I have kept what is in the manuscript.]]

16192. Al-Harith narrated to me, saying: Abd al-Aziz narrated to us, saying: Abu Ma'shar narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b, who said: When Quraysh resolved to march, they said: "We only fear Banu Bakr!" So Iblis, in the form of Suraqa ibn Malik ibn Ju'shum, said to them: "I am your protector against Banu Bakr, and no one among the people can overcome you today."

* * *

Abu Ja'far said: So the meaning of the statement is: ﴿And Allah is Hearing, Knowing﴾ — in these circumstances [and when Satan made attractive to them their going out against you, O believers, to fight and to war against you, and beautified that for them and urged them against you, and said to them: "No one among the sons of Adam can overcome you today, so be at ease and take heart"] — ﴿and I am your protector﴾ against Kinana, that they might come upon you from behind, so I will protect you, [[In the printed edition: "fayughayyirukum" (will change you), and the manuscript has the same unpointed form; this is the correct reading after correcting its corruption.]] I will protect you and defend you from them, so do not fear them, and direct your edge and your might against Muhammad and his companions. [[In the printed edition: "jaddakum" with a jim; see what was said earlier in vol. 13, p. 577, note 1.]] ﴿But when the two hosts came into view﴾, he means: when the hosts of Allah from the believers and the hosts of Satan from the polytheists came into contact with each other, and some of them looked at others: ﴿he turned on his heels﴾, he means: he turned back retreating on his back, fleeing. [[See the explanation of "al-aqib" (heel) earlier, vol. 3, p. 163, and vol. 11, p. 450.]]

* * *

It is said of this: "Nakasa yankusu wa yankisu nukusan," and from it is the saying of Zuhayr:

They strike the keen edges of the helmets when they clash;
they do not turn back when they are drawn into the battle, and they defend themselves. [[His Diwan, p. 159, from his poem in praise of Harim ibn Sinan, which is among the finest of his poetry. "Hubuk al-bid" means the ridges of the iron. "Al-bid" is the plural of "bayda," the helmet of the warrior's armor, shaped like an ostrich egg, worn by the rider on his head to protect him from the blows of swords and spears. "Istulhima al-rajul" (in the passive) means: when a man was caught in the thick of the battle and found no escape. His words "wa hammu" come from their saying: "hamiya min al-shay' hamiyatan wa mahmiyatan," meaning when his soul boiled and seethed, and he refused to accept the injustice that was intended for him; from this is "anf hamiya" (a zealous pride).]]

And he said to the polytheists: ﴿I am free of you. I see what you do not see﴾, meaning that he sees the angels whom Allah sent as reinforcements to the believers, while the polytheists do not see them [[See the explanation of "bari'" earlier in the lexical indexes under (b-r-a').]] — ﴿I fear the punishment of Allah,﴾ and the enemy of Allah lied — ﴿and Allah is severe in punishment.﴾ [[See the explanation of "shadid al-iqab" earlier in the lexical indexes under (`-q-b).]]

**The interpretation of His words:** ﴿When the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is a disease say, "These people's religion has deluded them." But whoever relies upon Allah, indeed Allah is Mighty and Wise﴾ (8:49).

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The Exalted One says, ﴿And indeed Allah is Hearing and Knowing﴾ of these circumstances, ﴿when the hypocrites say﴾. He repeated ﴿when the hypocrites say﴾ in connection with His words ﴿when Allah showed them to you in your dream as few﴾ (8:43). ﴿And those in whose hearts is a disease﴾ means doubt about Islam; their certainty was not sound, and their hearts had not been opened to faith. [[See the explanation of "marad" (disease) above, vol. 1, pp. 278–281, and vol. 10, p. 404.]] ﴿These people's religion has deluded them﴾ means: these people, who fight the polytheists among the companions of Muhammad ﷺ, have been deluded by their own religion, which is Islam. [[See the explanation of "al-ghurur" (delusion) above, vol. 12, p. 475, note 1, and the references there.]]

* *

It is mentioned that those who said this were a group of Meccan polytheists of the Quraysh who had professed Islam verbally, but Islam had not taken firm root in their hearts.

Those who said this:

16193. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Dawud related to us, from Amir, concerning this verse, ﴿When the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is a disease say, "These people's religion has deluded them"﴾. He said: Some people from Mecca had professed Islam, then went out with the polytheists on the day of Badr. When they saw the small number of the Muslims, they said, ﴿"These people's religion has deluded them"﴾.

16194. Ishaq ibn Shahin related to me, saying: Khalid related to us, from Dawud, from Amir, the like of it. [[Report 16194: "Ishaq ibn Shahin al-Wasiti" is a teacher of al-Tabari, mentioned under nos. 7211 and 9788. In the manuscript it reads "Abu Ishaq ibn Shahin," which is an error; the correct reading is what is in the printed edition. His kunya is "Abu Bishr."]]

16195. al-Harith related to me, saying: 'Abd al-'Aziz related to us, saying: Yahya ibn Zakariyya related to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, concerning His words, ﴿When the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is a disease say, "These people's religion has deluded them"﴾. He said: A group from the Quraysh: Abu Qays ibn al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, [[In the manuscript, the place of "Abu Qays ibn" is blank, and above the blank is the letter (ṭ) indicating an error. After it is "al-Walid ibn al-Mughira," and the editor of the printed edition wrote "Qays ibn al-Walid ibn al-Mughira," which is an error. It is in fact "Abu Qays ibn al-Walid," who witnessed Badr and was killed by Hamza ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib. So I have affirmed it. It appears that the blank is intended for only what I have affirmed, with nothing added to it.]] Abu Qays ibn al-Fakih ibn al-Mughira, al-Harith ibn Zam'a ibn al-Aswad ibn al-Muttalib, 'Ali ibn Umayya ibn Khalaf, and al-'As ibn Munabbih ibn al-Hajjaj. They went out with the Quraysh from Mecca while they were in doubt, and their doubt held them back. When they saw the small number of the companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, they said, ﴿"These people's religion has deluded them"﴾, until they arrived at what they arrived at, despite their small number and the great number of their enemy. Thereby He made an example of them to those behind them. [[In the printed edition, "Thereby He made an example of them to those behind them" is omitted; it is present in the manuscript.]]

16196. Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Hasan, concerning ﴿When the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is a disease say, "These people's religion has deluded them"﴾. He said: They were a people who did not witness the fighting at Badr, so they were named "hypocrites." Ma'mar said: Some of them said: They were a people who had acknowledged Islam while in Mecca, then went out with the polytheists on the day of Badr. When they saw the small number of the Muslims, they said, ﴿"These people's religion has deluded them"﴾.

16197. Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, concerning His words, ﴿When the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is a disease say﴾ up to His words ﴿indeed Allah is Mighty and Wise﴾. He said: They saw a band of believers who had been dispersed for the sake of Allah's command. [[In the printed edition: "tashaddadat" (were hardened); in the manuscript: "tasaradat." It seems the correct reading is what I have given: "tasharrada fi al-ard" means to flee and disperse. It seems he means their emigration to Allah and His Messenger. This is what I have worked out, and Allah knows best.]] It was also mentioned to us that Abu Jahl, the enemy of Allah, when he came upon Muhammad ﷺ and his companions, said, "By Allah, Allah will not be worshipped after today!" out of harshness and arrogance.

16198. al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, saying: Ibn Jurayj said, concerning His words, ﴿When the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is a disease say﴾, He said: They were people among the hypocrites in Mecca who said it on the day of Badr, and they were, on that day, three hundred and some ten men.

16199. ... He said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, concerning His words, ﴿When the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is a disease say﴾. He said: When the two groups drew near to one another, Allah made the Muslims appear few in the eyes of the polytheists, and made the polytheists appear few in the eyes of the Muslims. So the polytheists said, ﴿"These people's religion has deluded them"﴾. They only said that because of their smallness in their eyes, and they assumed they would defeat them, having no doubt about it. Then Allah said, ﴿But whoever relies upon Allah, indeed Allah is Mighty and Wise﴾.

* *

As for His words, ﴿But whoever relies upon Allah﴾, its meaning is: whoever entrusts his affair to Allah, trusts in Him, and is content with His decree, Allah is his guardian and helper. [[See the explanation of "tawakkul" (trust in God) above, vol. 13, p. 385, note 3, and the references there.]] ﴿For He is "Mighty"﴾, nothing overpowers Him and no one subdues Him; so whoever He protects is secure, and whoever relies upon Him is sufficed. [[In the printed edition: "... 'alayhi yakfihi" (upon Him, He will suffice him), which differs from the manuscript and is entirely correct.]]

This is a command from Allah, may His praise be exalted, to the believers in Him among the companions of the Messenger of Allah and others, that they entrust their affair to Him and submit to His decree, so that He may suffice them against their enemies, and that those who oppose them may not humiliate them. For He is "Mighty," not overcome, so the one He protects is not subdued. "Wise" means: He is wise in what He manages of the affairs of His creation; no flaw enters His management. [[See the explanation of "'azīz" and "ḥakīm" above in the language indexes under the roots (ʿ-z-z) and (ḥ-k-m).]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 8, verse 50:

The interpretation of His words: ﴿And if you could see when the angels take the lives of those who disbelieve, striking their faces and their backs, [saying], "Taste the punishment of the burning."﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): And if you could witness, O Muhammad, when the angels take the souls of the disbelievers, pulling them out of their bodies, striking their faces and their rears (asta'ahum), and saying to them: "Taste the punishment of the Fire that burns you on the day you are brought down to Hell." [[See the explanation of "tawaffi" (taking/receiving in full) above, vol. 13, p. 35, footnote 5, and the references there.

And the explanation of "adbar" (backs/rears) above, vol. 13, p. 435, footnote 2, and the references there.

And the explanation of "dhawq" (tasting) above, vol. 13, p. 528, footnote 2, and the references there.

And the explanation of "harīq" (burning) above, vol. 7, pp. 446–447.]]

* *

Similarly to what we have said regarding this, the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said.

Mention of those who said that:

16200 - Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿when those who disbelieve are taken by the angels, striking their faces and their backs﴾, he said: On the day of Badr.

16201 - Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Sulaym narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn Kathir, from Mujahid: ﴿striking their faces and their backs﴾, he said: and their rears (asta'ahum), but Allah is Generous and uses euphemism. [[The report 16201: "Yahya ibn Sulaym al-Ta'ifi", trustworthy, already mentioned under no. 4894 and 9788; in the printed edition it read "Yahya ibn Aslam", which is a clear error, and the manuscript writing is confused. "Isma'il ibn Kathir al-Hijazi", trustworthy, already mentioned under no. 8929.]]

16202 - Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Hashim, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿striking their faces and their backs﴾, he said: and their rears (asta'ahum), but He is Generous and uses euphemism. [[In the printed edition: "but Allah", and I have retained what is in the manuscript.]]

16203 - Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Wahb ibn Jarir narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah informed us, from Ya'la ibn Muslim, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr regarding His words: ﴿striking their faces and their backs﴾, he said: Indeed Allah uses euphemism; had He willed, He would have said "asta'ahum", but He meant by "adbarahum" their rears (asta'ahum).

16204 - al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, who said: their rears (asta'ahum) on the day of Badr. Ibn Juraij said: Ibn 'Abbas said: When the polytheists advanced with their faces toward the Muslims, they were struck on their faces with swords; and when they turned their backs, the angels overtook them and struck their backs.

16205 - Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: 'Abbad ibn Rashid narrated to us, from al-Hasan, who said: A man said: O Messenger of Allah, I saw on the back of Abu Jahl something like a shirak! [[The "shirak" is the strip of the sandal that lies over its top.]] He said: What is that? He said: The striking of the angels.

16206 - Muhammad narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Isra'il narrated to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid: that a man said to the Prophet (ﷺ): I charged at a man from the polytheists and went to strike him, [[See what I have previously mentioned in the explanation of "dhahaba yafʿalu" above, vol. 11, p. 128, footnote 1, then vol. 11, pp. 250–251, and p. 250, footnote 1.]] and his head fell off? [["Nadara al-shay'" means it fell. It is said: "he struck his hand with the sword and severed it," i.e., cut it off so that it fell.]] He said: The angel had already got to him before you.

16207 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Harmalah narrated to me that he heard 'Umar, the mawla of Ghafirah, say: When you hear Allah say: ﴿striking their faces and their backs﴾, He only means: their rears (asta'ahum). [[The report 16207: "Harmalah ibn Imran al-Tujibi", trustworthy, already mentioned under nos. 6890 and 13240. "'Umar, the mawla of Ghafirah", is "'Umar ibn 'Abd Allah al-Madani", Abu Hafs, who is not unreliable; he was a transmitter of mursal reports and of narrations on asceticism. He is biographically recorded in al-Tahdhib and Ibn Abi Hatim, 3/1/119.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: In the speech there is an omitted element, the omission being permitted by what the outward wording indicates, namely His words "they say," [implied in] ﴿Taste the punishment of the burning﴾. The word "they say" has been omitted, just as it is omitted in His words: ﴿And if you could see when the criminals bow their heads before their Lord, [saying], "Our Lord, we have seen and heard"﴾ [Surah as-Sajdah: 12], meaning: they say, "Our Lord, we have seen." [[See the Ma'ani al-Qur'an of al-Farra' 1/413.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 8, verse 51:

The interpretation of His words: ﴿That is for what your hands have put forward, and that Allah is not ever unjust to the servants﴾ (8:51)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says, informing about what the angels say to these polytheists who were killed at Badr, that they will say to them while they strike their faces and their backs: "Taste the punishment of Allah which burns you." This punishment is for you, ﴿for what your hands have put forward﴾, that is, for what your hands have earned of sins and burdens, and what you committed of disobedience to Allah during the days of your lives. [[See the explanation of "qadamat aydikum" (what your hands have put forward) above: 2:368 / 7:447 / 8:514 / 10:497.]] So taste the punishment today, and in your return, the punishment of the Burning. That is for you because Allah ﴿is not ever unjust to the servants﴾; He does not punish any of His creatures except for a crime that he has committed, and He does not chastise him except for his disobedience to Him, because injustice cannot be attributed to Him.

As for the vowelling of "anna" in His words ﴿and that Allah﴾, there are two grammatical possibilities:

The first: the accusative (naṣb), which is in coordination with "mā" in His words ﴿for what﴾, meaning: ﴿That is for what your hands have put forward, and that Allah is not ever unjust to the servants﴾. This is according to the view of some of them. And the genitive (khafḍ), according to the view of others.

The second: the nominative (raf'), on the basis of ﴿That is for what [your hands have put forward]﴾, and that Allah... [[See Ma'ani al-Qur'an by al-Farra' 1:413.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 8, verse 52:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿As was the habit of the people of Pharaoh and those before them, who denied the signs of Allah, so Allah seized them for their sins. Indeed Allah is Powerful, Severe in punishment﴾ (8:52).

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: He, exalted is His mention, says: The conduct of these polytheists of Quraysh who were killed at Badr is like the habit of the people of Pharaoh, their practice, their deeds, and the deeds of those among the earlier nations who denied the proofs of Allah and His messengers before them. [[See the explanation of "Al" (ali, "family/people of") earlier: 2:37 \ 6:326.]] So We dealt with them as We dealt with those.

We have already explained earlier that "al-da'b" (habit, custom, way of behaviour) means the affair and the custom, which is sufficient so that it need not be repeated here. [[See the explanation of "al-da'b" earlier: 6:223–225.]]

* *

16208. Al-Harith narrated to me, saying: 'Abd al-'Aziz narrated to me, saying: Shayban narrated to us, from Jabir, from 'Amir, Mujahid and 'Ata', regarding ﴿As was the habit of the people of Pharaoh﴾: like the conduct of the people of Pharaoh, like the ways of the people of Pharaoh.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿So Allah seized them for their sins﴾, He means: Allah punished them for their denial of His proofs and His messengers, and their disobedience to their Lord, just as He punished their likes and the nations before them. ﴿Indeed Allah is Powerful﴾: none overcomes Him, and none turns back His decree; He carries out His command and executes His judgment upon His creation. ﴿Severe in punishment﴾ for those who disbelieve in His signs and deny His proofs.

The Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 8, verse 53:

On the interpretation of His words: ﴿That is because Allah never changes a favour He has bestowed upon a people until they change what is in themselves, and indeed Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing﴾ (8:53).

Abu Ja'far said: He, exalted is His remembrance, says: We seized these who disbelieved in Our signs, from the polytheists of Quraysh, at Badr, for their sins, [[See the explanation of "al-akhdh" (seizing) in the preceding lexical indexes, under (akhadha).]] and We did that to them because they changed what Allah had bestowed upon them by sending His Messenger among them and in their midst, by their expelling him from among them, their denying him, and their waging war against him. So We changed Our favour upon them by destroying them, just as We had done with those before them who transgressed against Us and disobeyed Our command.

* *

And in accordance with what we have said on this, the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said.

Mention of those who said that:

16209. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, he said: Ahmad ibn al-Mufadddal narrated to us, he said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿That is because Allah never changes a favour He has bestowed upon a people until they change what is in themselves﴾, he says: "The favour of Allah" is Muhammad (ﷺ), whom He bestowed upon Quraysh, and they disbelieved, so He transferred it to the Ansar.

* *

As for His words: ﴿And indeed Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing﴾, He says: Nothing of the speech of His creatures is hidden from Him; He hears the speech of every speaker among them, whether it is good speech or evil speech, ﴿All-Knowing﴾, of what their breasts conceal, and He will recompense and reward them for what they say and do: if good, then good, and if evil, then evil. [[See the explanation of "sami'" (All-Hearing) and "alim" (All-Knowing) in the preceding lexical indexes, under (sami'a) and (alima).]]

Discourse on the interpretation of His words: ﴿Like the habit of the people of Pharaoh and those before them, who denied the signs of their Lord, so We destroyed them for their sins and drowned the people of Pharaoh; and all of them were wrongdoers﴾ (8:54).

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Those polytheists who were slain at Badr have changed the blessing of their Lord that He had bestowed upon them, by sending Muhammad (ﷺ) among them and in their midst, calling them to guidance, by their denial of him and their fighting against him. ﴿Like the habit of the people of Pharaoh﴾, like the custom, practice and conduct of the people of Pharaoh toward Moses, the Prophet of Allah [[See the explanation of "al-da'b" (habit) above, p. 19, footnote 1, and the references there.

And the explanation of "al" (people/household) above, p. 18, footnote 3, and the references there.]] in their denial of him and their intention to fight him, and the custom of those before them of the denying nations toward their messengers and their deeds. ﴿So We destroyed them for their sins﴾: some by the quake, some by the sinking into the earth, and some by the wind. ﴿And We drowned the people of Pharaoh﴾ in the sea. ﴿And all of them were wrongdoers﴾: he says, all these nations that We destroyed were doing what was not theirs to do, by denying the messengers of Allah and rejecting His signs. Likewise, We destroyed these whom We destroyed at Badr, when they changed the blessing of Allah that was among them, by killing with the sword, and We humbled some of them by captivity and taking them as prisoners.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 8, verse 55–56:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Indeed, the worst of living creatures in the sight of Allah are those who disbelieve, so they will not believe﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, exalted is His mention, says: Indeed, the worst of what crawls upon the earth in the sight of Allah [[See the explanation of "al-Dabba" (living creature) above: 3:274, 275 \ 11:344 \ 13:459.]] are those who disbelieve in their Lord, who deny His oneness and worship other than Him. ﴿So they will not believe﴾ means: they do not confirm the messengers of Allah, nor acknowledge His revelation and His sending down.

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Those with whom you made a covenant, then they break their covenant every time, and they do not fear Allah﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, exalted is His mention, says: ﴿Indeed, the worst of living creatures in the sight of Allah are those who disbelieve﴾, ﴿those with whom you made a covenant﴾, O Muhammad, meaning: you took their pledges and covenants that they would not fight against you, nor would they back anyone against you in war, like Qurayza and their counterparts, those who had a treaty and agreement with you [[See the explanation of "al-'ahd" (covenant) above: 13:72, footnote 2, and the references there.]]. ﴿Then they break [their covenant]﴾, their pledges and covenants, every time they make a covenant and pledge with you: they fight against you and back others against you [[See the explanation of "al-naqd" (breaking) above: 9:363 \ 10:125.]]. ﴿And they do not fear Allah﴾, and in doing that they do not fear that a calamity will befall them that would destroy and annihilate them, as in the following:

16210 - Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿Those with whom you made a covenant, then they break their covenant﴾, he said: Qurayza aided Muhammad's enemies against him on the Day of the Trench.

16211 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, similarly.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 8, verse 55–56:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Indeed, the worst of living creatures in the sight of Allah are those who disbelieve, so they will not believe﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, exalted is His mention, says: Indeed, the worst of what crawls upon the earth in the sight of Allah [[See the explanation of "al-Dabba" (living creature) above: 3:274, 275 \ 11:344 \ 13:459.]] are those who disbelieve in their Lord, who deny His oneness and worship other than Him. ﴿So they will not believe﴾ means: they do not confirm the messengers of Allah, nor acknowledge His revelation and His sending down.

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Those with whom you made a covenant, then they break their covenant every time, and they do not fear Allah﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, exalted is His mention, says: ﴿Indeed, the worst of living creatures in the sight of Allah are those who disbelieve﴾, ﴿those with whom you made a covenant﴾, O Muhammad, meaning: you took their pledges and covenants that they would not fight against you, nor would they back anyone against you in war, like Qurayza and their counterparts, those who had a treaty and agreement with you [[See the explanation of "al-'ahd" (covenant) above: 13:72, footnote 2, and the references there.]]. ﴿Then they break [their covenant]﴾, their pledges and covenants, every time they make a covenant and pledge with you: they fight against you and back others against you [[See the explanation of "al-naqd" (breaking) above: 9:363 \ 10:125.]]. ﴿And they do not fear Allah﴾, and in doing that they do not fear that a calamity will befall them that would destroy and annihilate them, as in the following:

16210 - Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿Those with whom you made a covenant, then they break their covenant﴾, he said: Qurayza aided Muhammad's enemies against him on the Day of the Trench.

16211 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, similarly.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 8, verse 57:

The exegesis of His saying: ﴿So if you gain the upper hand over them in war, then scatter those behind them, that they may remember﴾ (57)

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): If you encounter in war those with whom you have made a covenant, who have broken your covenant time and again, from the tribe of Qurayza, and you take them captive, ﴿then scatter those behind them﴾ — that is, do to them a deed that will scatter those who are behind them of their counterparts, those between you and whom there is a pact and a treaty. [[See the explanation of "thaqafa" above, 3:564 and 7:110.]]

* *

And "tashrid" (scattering) means driving away, dispersing and dividing.

* *

The Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) was only commanded to do this to those who break the covenant between him and them, when he gains power over them, a deed that will be a terror to those behind them, of those who had a covenant with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so that they will not dare to do the like of what these people dared, those whose attribute Allah described in this verse, of breaking the covenant.

* *

The people of interpretation have said what is similar to what we have said.

Those who said this:

16212. Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abdullah ibn Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiya ibn Salih related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿So if you gain the upper hand over them in war, then scatter those behind them﴾, he means: punish those after them severely.

16213. Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: My father related to me, saying: My paternal uncle related to me, saying: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿then scatter those behind them﴾, he says: punish severely those who are behind them.

16214. Bishr ibn Mu'adh related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada regarding His saying: ﴿So if you gain the upper hand over them in war, then scatter those behind them﴾, he says: make an example of them to others among people.

16215. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿So if you gain the upper hand over them in war, then scatter those behind them﴾, he says: punish severely those behind them, those after them of the enemy, so that they may fear to break faith, lest you do to them the like.

16216. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Ayyub, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: ﴿then scatter those behind them﴾, he said: warn those behind them through them.

16217. Al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ata' al-Khurasani, from Ibn Abbas, who said: punish severely those behind them, those after them. Ibn Jurayj said: Abdullah ibn Kathir said: punish severely those who are behind them.

16218. Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salama related to us, from Ibn Ishaq: ﴿So if you gain the upper hand over them in war, then scatter those behind them, that they may remember﴾, i.e., punish severely those behind them, that they may understand.

16219. I was told on the authority of al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman related to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim say regarding His saying: ﴿then scatter those behind them﴾: punish severely those after them.

16220. Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding the saying of Allah: ﴿So if you gain the upper hand over them in war, then scatter those behind them﴾, he said: frighten them by what you do to these. And he recited: ﴿And others besides them whom you do not know; Allah knows them﴾ [[Report 16220: see the following report no. 16242 and the comment on it.]] [al-Anfal: 60]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿that they may remember﴾, its meaning is: so that they may take warning from what I did to those whose description I have given, and so that they beware of breaking the covenant between you and them, fearing that what befell these people if they broke it may befall them from you.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 8, verse 58:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And if you fear treachery from a people, then throw back to them [their treaty] on equal terms. Indeed, Allah does not love the treacherous﴾ [8:58].

Abu Ja'far said: His saying, exalted is He, ﴿And if you fear﴾, O Muhammad, ﴿from a people [who have a treaty with you] a breach﴾, meaning: from an enemy with whom you have a treaty and a covenant, that he will break the pact and violate his agreement and betray you, and that is "treachery" (khiyanah) and deceit [see the explanation of "khiyanah" above, 13:480, note 1, and the references there] ﴿then throw back to them on equal terms﴾, meaning: fight them, and inform them before your war against them that you have annulled the treaty between you and them, because of the signs of deceit and treachery that have appeared from them [see the explanation of "nabdh" (throwing back) above, 2:401, 402; 7:459. In the printed edition: "athar al-ghadr" (traces of deceit), and I have kept what is in the manuscript; "al-amar" and "al-amarah" mean a sign, and it is said "amar" as the plural of "amarah"], until you and they are on equal terms in knowledge that you are at war with them, so that they may take up the weapons of war, and you may be free of treachery. ﴿Indeed, Allah does not love the treacherous﴾, those who betray one who is under their protection and in a covenant with them, by attacking him in war before informing him that there is war between them and that the contract is annulled.

* *

If someone says: How is it permissible to break a covenant out of fear of treachery, when "fear" is mere supposition, not certainty? [see the explanation of "khawf" above, 11:373, note 5, and the references there]

It is said: The matter is contrary to what you have supposed. Its meaning is: when signs of treachery appear from your enemy, and you fear that they will attack you, then cast to them the reins of peace and notify them of war. [In the manuscript: "wa-ad", followed by a blank; its correct form is what is in the printed edition.] This is like what occurred with the Banu Qurayzah when they answered Abu Sufyan and those with him of the polytheists to support them against the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and to fight alongside them, after the covenant they had made with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for peace, and that they would not fight the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. [In the printed edition: "wa-muharabatihim maAhu"; I have kept what is in the manuscript.] Their acceptance of that was a reason for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to fear betrayal of him and his companions by them. Likewise, the ruling for every people who have a truce with the believers is that, if the leader of the Muslims sees from them signs of treachery like those that appeared to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his companions from Qurayzah, it is incumbent upon the leader of the Muslims to throw back to them on equal terms and inform them of war.

* *

The meaning of His saying: ﴿on equal terms﴾ is: until your knowledge and theirs is equal that each party is at war with the other, not at peace.

* *

It was said: the verse was revealed concerning Qurayzah.

Those who said this:

16221 - Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿then throw back to them on equal terms﴾, he said: Qurayzah.

* *

Some of them said: "al-sawa'" in this place means a respite.

Those who said this:

16222 - Ali ibn Sahl narrated to me, saying: al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us, saying: It has become clear to us that His saying ﴿then throw back to them on equal terms﴾ means: with a respite, as Bukayr narrated to us, from Muqatil ibn Hayyan, concerning the saying of Allah: (A declaration of freedom from Allah and His Messenger to those of the polytheists with whom you made a treaty: so travel freely in the land for four months) [al-Tawbah: 1-2].

* *

As for the scholars of the Arabic language, they differ concerning its meaning.

Some of them said: its meaning is: then throw back to them on justice, meaning: until your knowledge and theirs becomes balanced regarding what each of you has over the other of war. They cited for their saying the verse of a rajiz (poet of rajaz verse), [the reciter is unknown]:

"Strike the faces of the treacherous enemies until they answer you with equality"

meaning: to justice. [In the printed edition it read "al-ghadr lil-a'da'", which is an error; the correct reading is from the manuscript, and "al-ghudur" (with two dammas), plural of "ghadur", like "sabur", is one who is treacherous and habitually treacherous.]

* *

Others said: its meaning is: the middle, from the verse of Hassan:

"Woe to the helpers of the Messenger and his kin, after his concealment in the middle of the niche"

meaning: in the middle of the burial niche. [The verse was previously cited and its takhrij and explanation given above, 2:496, note 2.]

* *

These meanings are close to one another, for "justice" is a middle that does not rise above the truth nor fall short of it, and likewise "the middle" is justice, and the equality of knowledge of both parties regarding what each holds against the other after the truce is justice, from the root of the verb and of the middle. As for what al-Walid ibn Muslim said, that its meaning is "respite," I know of no basis for it in the speech of the Arabs.

The Interpretation of His Words: ﴿And let not those who disbelieve suppose that they have gotten away; indeed, they cannot escape﴾ (59)

Abu Ja'far said: The readers differed concerning the recitation of this.

The majority of the readers of Hijaz and Iraq recited it: "Wa-la taḥsabanna alladhina kafaru sabaqu innahum" with the alif of "innahum" pronounced with a kasra, and with the taa' in "taḥsabanna", meaning: "And let not you, O Muhammad, suppose that those who disbelieved outran us and escaped us by themselves. Then the report begins concerning God's power over them: indeed, these disbelievers cannot escape their Lord when He seeks them and wishes to punish and destroy them, by themselves, so that they could elude Him by it."

* *

Some readers of Madina and Kufa recited it: ﴿Wa-la yaḥsabanna alladhina kafaru﴾, with the yaa' in "yaḥsabanna", and the kasra of the alif in ﴿innahum﴾.

* *

This is a disliked recitation, for two reasons. [[This recitation which Abu Ja'far rejected is the one we recite today.]] One is that it departs from the recitation of the readers and is anomalous compared with them. The other is that it is distant from the eloquent speech of the Arabs. That is because "yaḥsib" in the speech of the Arabs requires an object and its predicate, as in the saying: "Abdullah thinks your brother standing" and "stands" and "stood". So the reciter of this reading made "yaḥsib" a predicate for an unmentioned subject. Its meaning, in my opinion: [[In the printed edition: "and its meaning was buti wa-la yaḥsabanna", which gives a meaningless expression. Al-Tabari's words "ẓanni" say, as we say today: "in my opinion".]] "And let not those who disbelieved suppose that they outran us, indeed they cannot escape us." He did not consider the correctness of the structure of the speech and its defect, and in his recitation he used what appeared to him as the meaning of the speech. I suppose that what led him to this was consideration of the recitation of Abdullah. For it is mentioned in the codex of Abdullah: ﴿Wa-la yaḥsabanna alladhina kafaru annahum sabaqu innahum la yu'jizun﴾. This is eloquent and sound, when "annahum" is introduced into the speech, because "yaḥsabanna" governs "annahum"; and when "annahum" is not in the speech, the verb is left without a noun on which to act.

For the one who recited thus among the readers, there are two possibilities in the speech of the Arabs, although both are remote from their eloquent usage:

First: that it is meant as: "And let not those who disbelieved suppose that they outran," or "that they outran", and then "an" and "annahum" were omitted, as He, exalted is His praise, said: ﴿And among His signs is that He shows you the lightning, as fear and as hope﴾ [Al-Rum: 24], meaning: "that He shows you." A line of verse is recited in a similar case, by Dhu al-Rumma:

"I suppose that Ibn Tarthuth, Utaybah, is going off with my well of 'Adiyya, his deceit and his bribes" [[From his Diwan, p. 473, from a poem in which he mentioned "al-Muhajir ibn Abdullah al-Kilabi", governor of al-Yamama. Al-Muhajir had a collector among the tax-gatherers in the desert called "Rumi". Dhu al-Rumma and Utaybah ibn Tarthuth disputed over an old well, and Dhu al-Rumma brought the dispute before Rumi, who, before the case was decided, ruled for Ibn Tarthuth and wrote him a deed. Dhu al-Rumma said in that poem, according to the version of his Diwan: "I say to myself, I do not blame anyone but her, and the man of intellect, whatever happens, speaks to his own soul." "Perhaps Ibn Tarthuth, Utaybah, is going off..." "In a valley which we prevented him from for eighty years and some more, its thickets and its watercourses are ours." Then he mentioned al-Muhajir with fine praise and said: "O son of Abdullah, whoever you support is made strong, and the Merciful does not support whoever you forsake." "When my heart fears the oppression of a collector and his injustice, I remember you, and my anxious thoughts are calmed." "You see that God, nothing hidden from Him of a servant's secret, nor the means of any affair one seeks to achieve." "Rumi has drawn for Utaybah a line which his joints have not fitted to, without a clear writ from al-Muhajir, nor from a seated man, with me disputing against an opponent." This is a living story. The printed edition had "Uyayna", and the correct form is from the Diwan, as is indicated by the preceding verse which names him "Utaybah", then diminutive. "Al-'adiyya" is the old well, as if from the time of 'Ad. "Al-tukdhab" is a verbal noun like "al-kadhb". "Al-ja'a'il" is the bribe given to the agent who takes bribes.]] Meaning: "Do I suppose that Ibn Tarthuth will take away my well by his deceit and his bribes?" Likewise the recitation of whoever recited it with the yaa' directs "sabaqu" toward "sabiqin" on this meaning. [[See this in al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1: 414-416.]]

The second possibility is that it is meant to supply an object governed by "yaḥsib", as if he said: "And let not those who disbelieved suppose that they outran," then "annahum" was omitted and implied.

[[In the printed edition: "then the hamza was omitted and implied", which is a statement that a sound mind would not produce. The correct reading of the manuscript is "annahum" as I have recorded it, and it is very clear.]]

Some have explained the meaning of His words: ﴿It is only Satan who frightens his allies﴾ [Al Imran: 175] as: "It is only Satan who frightens the believer from his allies", and that the mention of the believer is implied in "yukhawwif" (frightens), since Satan in their view does not frighten his allies. [[See what preceded, 7: 417, the interpretation of this verse.]]

* *

Some people of al-Sham recited it: "Wa-la taḥsabanna alladhina kafaru" with the taa' in "taḥsabanna" = ﴿sabaqu annahum la yu'jizun﴾, with the alif of "annahum" pronounced with a fatha, meaning: "And let not those who disbelieved suppose that they cannot be overtaken."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: There is no intelligible meaning for this recitation, unless the reciter intended by the "la" in "yu'jizun" the "la" which enters speech as filler and connective, [[The "sila" is the addition, as mentioned many times before; see the index of terms above.]] so the meaning of the speech then would be: "And let not those who disbelieved suppose that they outran that they are unable." There is no justification for placing a letter of the Book of God into lengthening [[The "tatwil" is also addition. See what preceded 1: 118, 224, 405, 406, 440, 441, where it reads "tatawwul".]] without an argument which must be accepted, and it has a sound explanation.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct recitation in this matter in my view is the recitation of the one who recited: ﴿La taḥsabanna﴾ with the taa', ﴿alladhina kafaru sabaqu innahum﴾ with the kasra of the alif in "innahum", ﴿la yu'jizun﴾, meaning: "And let not you, O Muhammad, suppose that those who denied the proofs of God and called them lies outran us by themselves and escaped us, indeed they cannot escape us" — that is, they cannot elude us by themselves, nor are they able to flee from us. [[See the explanation of "a'jaza" in what preceded 12: 128.]] As:

16223 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told me, he said: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, he said: Asbat told us, from al-Suddi, concerning: ﴿And let not those who disbelieve suppose that they have outrun; indeed, they cannot escape﴾, he says: they will not elude.

**The interpretation of His words: ﴿And prepare against them whatever force you can muster, and horses stationed at the frontier, to terrify thereby the enemy of Allah and your enemy﴾ (60)**

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: ﴿And prepare﴾ against those who disbelieve in their Lord, with whom you have a covenant, when you fear their treachery and deceit, O believers in Allah and His Messenger, ﴿whatever force you can muster﴾. That is, whatever you are able to provide them with of the instruments that will be a strength for you against them, [[See the explanation of "al-istita'ah" (ability, capacity) above, 4:315 and 9:284.]] such as weapons and horses. ﴿To terrify thereby the enemy of Allah and your enemy﴾: that is, you frighten the enemy of Allah and your enemy among the polytheists by your preparation of that.

* *

Scholars of ta'wil (interpretation, the explanation of the meaning and the ultimate reality of a verse) have said the same as what we have said about this.

Those who said that:

16224. Abu Kurayb narrated to us, who said: Ibn Idris narrated to us, who said: I heard Usama ibn Zayd, from Salih ibn Kaysan, from a man of Juhayna, who traced the report back to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): ﴿And prepare against them whatever force you can muster﴾. Indeed, archery is the force; indeed, archery is the force. [[The report 16224: "Ibn Idris" is ʿAbd Allah ibn Idris al-Awdi, the imam, who has been mentioned many times before. In the printed edition and the manuscript it reads "Abu Idris", which is a plain error. "Usama ibn Zayd al-Laythi" is trustworthy (thiqah); he has been mentioned before under nos. 2867 and 3354. "Salih ibn Kaysan al-Madani": the whole group (al-jama'ah, i.e., the six canonical collections) narrated from him; he has been mentioned before under nos. 1020 and 5321. This report will come through other chains, nos. 16226–16228, and I will mention them at each one; see the takhrij (tracing of sources) of the following report.]]

16225. Abu Kurayb narrated to us, who said: Sa'id ibn Sharahbil narrated to us, who said: Ibn Lahi'a narrated to us, from Yazid ibn Abi Habib and ʿAbd al-Karim ibn al-Harith, from Abu ʿAli al-Hamdani: that he heard ʿUqba ibn ʿAmir on the pulpit saying: Allah said: ﴿And prepare against them whatever force you can muster and horses stationed at the frontier﴾. Indeed, I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say on the pulpit: Allah said: ﴿And prepare against them whatever force you can muster﴾. Indeed, the force is archery; indeed, the force is archery, three times. [[The report 16225: "Sa'id ibn Sharahbil al-Kindi": al-Bukhari narrated from him, and al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah narrated from him through an intermediary. He is trustworthy. He is mentioned in al-Tahdhib, in al-Kabir (2/1/442), and in Ibn Abi Hatim (2/1/33). "Ibn Lahi'a": he has been mentioned many times before, and the discussion of his reliability has been given. "Yazid ibn Abi Habib al-Azdi al-Misri": trustworthy; the whole group narrated from him; he has been mentioned many times, the last under no. 11871. "ʿAbd al-Karim ibn al-Harith ibn Yazid al-Hadrami al-Misri": trustworthy; mentioned in al-Tahdhib and in Ibn Abi Hatim (3/1/60). "Abu ʿAli al-Hamdani" is Thumama ibn Shafi al-Hamdani al-Misri, trustworthy; mentioned in al-Tahdhib, in al-Kabir (1/2/177), and in Ibn Abi Hatim (1/1/466). This chain is weak because of whoever is weak among the narrators, namely Ibn Lahi'a, and al-Tabari himself will say in p. 37, note 2, that it is a chain with weakness (wahn). However, this report has been transmitted through very sound routes: Muslim narrated it in his Sahih (13:64), through Harun ibn Maʿruf, from Ibn Wahb, from ʿAmr ibn al-Harith, from Abu ʿAli Thumama ibn Shafi, with the same wording. Abu Dawud narrated it in his Sunan (3:20, no. 2514), through Sa'id ibn Mansur, from Ibn Wahb, with the same wording. Ibn Majah narrated it in his Sunan (p. 940, no. 2813), through Yunus ibn ʿAbd al-A'la, from Ibn Wahb, with the same wording. al-Hakim narrated it in al-Mustadrak (2:328), through Sa'id ibn Abi Ayyub, from Yazid ibn Abi Habib, from Abu al-Khayr, from ʿUqba, and he said: "This is a sound hadith according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim), but [al-Bukhari] did not narrate it, because Salih ibn Kaysan halted it (at a companion)." al-Dhahabi agreed with him.]]

16226. Abu Kurayb narrated to us, who said: Mahbub, Ja'far ibn ʿAwn, Waki', Abu Usama, and Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, from Usama ibn Zayd, from Salih ibn Kaysan, from a man, from ʿUqba ibn ʿAmir al-Juhani, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited on the pulpit: ﴿And prepare against them whatever force you can muster and horses stationed at the frontier﴾, and he said: "Indeed, the force is archery; indeed, the force is archery," three times. [[The report 16226: "Mahbub" is Mahbub ibn Muhriz al-Qawariri; Ibn Hibban declared him trustworthy and al-Daraqutni declared him weak. He is mentioned in al-Tahdhib and in Ibn Abi Hatim (4/1/388). "Ja'far ibn ʿAwn al-Makhzumi": trustworthy; the whole group narrated from him; mentioned before under no. 9506. This report was narrated by al-Tirmidhi through Waki' from Usama ibn Zayd, and then he said: "Some of them have narrated this hadith from Usama ibn Zayd, from Salih ibn Kaysan, from ʿUqba ibn ʿAmir, but the hadith of Waki' is more sound, and Salih ibn Kaysan did not meet ʿUqba ibn ʿAmir, though he met Ibn ʿUmar." See report no. 16228.]]

16227. Ibn Waki' narrated to us, who said: My father narrated to us, from Usama ibn Zayd, from Salih ibn Kaysan, from a man, from ʿUqba ibn ʿAmir: that the Prophet (ﷺ) recited this verse on the pulpit, and he mentioned something similar. [[The report 16227: it is a repetition of the preceding report. See its takhrij; al-Tirmidhi narrated it in his Sunan through this route, as has been mentioned.]]

16228. Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, who said: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, who said: Usama ibn Zayd narrated to us, from Salih ibn Kaysan, from ʿUqba ibn ʿAmir, from the Prophet (ﷺ), something similar. [[The report 16228: this is the hadith to which al-Tirmidhi referred, and of which he said: "Salih ibn Kaysan did not meet ʿUqba ibn ʿAmir." See what preceded at 16226.]]

16229. Ahmad ibn Humayd narrated to us, who said: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, who said: Musa ibn ʿUbayda narrated to us, from his brother Muhammad ibn ʿUbayda, from his brother ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUbayda, from ʿUqba ibn ʿAmir, from the Prophet (ﷺ), concerning His words: ﴿And prepare against them whatever force you can muster﴾: "Indeed, the force is archery." [[The report 16229: "Musa ibn ʿUbayda ibn Nashit al-Rabadhi" is extremely weak; it is not permissible to narrate from him. He has been mentioned many times before, the last under nos. 11811 and 14045. He narrated from his two brothers, "ʿAbd Allah" and "Muhammad." His brother "Muhammad ibn ʿUbayda ibn Nashit al-Rabadhi": I have not found a biography of him, but he is mentioned in the biography of his brother Musa and in the biography of his brother ʿAbd Allah, as one who narrated from him. He was eighty years older than his brother Musa. His brother "ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUbayda ibn Nashit al-Rabadhi" narrated from a group of Companions; some declared him trustworthy and others declared him weak. Ahmad said: "Musa ibn ʿUbayda and his brother are not to be occupied with." He is mentioned in al-Tahdhib and in Ibn Abi Hatim (2/2/101).]]

16230. Ibn Waki' narrated to us, who said: My father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Shuʿba ibn Dinar, from ʿIkrima, concerning His words: ﴿And prepare against them whatever force you can muster﴾, he said: "The fortresses." ﴿And horses stationed at the frontier﴾, he said: "The females." [[The report 16230: "Shuʿba ibn Dinar al-Kufi": he narrated from ʿIkrima and Abu Burda ibn Abi Musa al-Ash'ari; he is trustworthy. He is mentioned in al-Tahdhib, in al-Kabir (2/2/245), and in Ibn Abi Hatim (2/1/368).]]

16231. ʿAli ibn Sahl narrated to us, who said: Damra ibn Rabi'a narrated to us, from Raja' ibn Abi Salama, who said: A man met Mujahid in Mecca, and with Mujahid was a jawaliq, [[The "jawaliq" (with a dammah on the jim, and a fathah or kasrah on the lam) is a kind of container among containers; it is what we today in Egypt call, in a distorted form, the "shawal" (a sack).]] and he said: Then Mujahid said: "This is from the force!" And Mujahid was preparing for a raid.

16232. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, who said: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, who said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿And prepare against them whatever force you can muster﴾, [meaning] from weapons.

* *

As for His words: ﴿To terrify thereby the enemy of Allah and your enemy﴾:

Ibn Waki' said:

16233. My father narrated to us, from Isra'il, from ʿUthman ibn al-Mughira al-Thaqafi, from Mujahid, from Ibn ʿAbbas: ﴿To terrify thereby the enemy of Allah and your enemy﴾, he said: "To humiliate (takhzuna) thereby the enemy of Allah and your enemy."

16234. Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, who said: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, who said: Isra'il narrated to us, from ʿUthman, from Mujahid, from Ibn ʿAbbas, something similar.

16235. al-Harith narrated to me, who said: ʿAbd al-ʿAziz narrated to us, who said: Isra'il narrated to us, from Khusayf, from ʿIkrima and Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbas: (To terrify thereby the enemy of Allah and your enemy), he said: "To humiliate thereby the enemy of Allah and your enemy." And thus he used to recite it: ﴿Tukhzunna﴾ (you humiliate). [[In the printed edition and the manuscript it reads: "And thus he used to recite it: terrify (turhibuna)." The correct reading, about which there is no doubt here, is "takhzun", as I have written it. Ibn Khalawayh mentioned this reading of Ibn ʿAbbas in al-Qira'at al-Shadhdha (p. 50). (In the printed edition there is an error: it has "yajurrun bihi", and the correct reading is what I have written.) Abu Hayyan said in his tafsir (4:512): "Ibn ʿAbbas, ʿIkrima, and Mujahid recited 'takhzunna bihi' in place of 'turhibuna bihi'." Al-Tabari mentioned it as an explanation, not as a reading, and this is what is proper, because it contradicts the consonantal text of the Mushaf. I say: I have since seen that al-Tabari also mentioned it as a reading, and his text cannot be correct except with what I have written.]]

16237. al-Harith narrated to me, who said: ʿAbd al-ʿAziz narrated to us, who said: Isra'il narrated to us, from ʿUthman ibn al-Mughira, and Khusayf, from Mujahid, from Ibn ʿAbbas: ﴿Turhibuna bihi﴾ (you terrify therewith): "takhzun bihi" (you humiliate therewith). [[A number was dropped from the numbering: 16236, by mistake.]]

16238. Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, who said: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, who said: Isra'il narrated to us, from Khusayf, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbas, something similar.

* *

It is said from this: "Arhabtu al-ʿaduww" and "rahhabtuhu" (I terrified the enemy), so I terrify him (arhabu) and make him terrified (urhibu), terrifying (irhab) and making terrified (tarhib), and it is "al-rahab" and "al-ruhb" (fear). From it is the saying of Tufayl al-Ghanawi:

Woe to the mother of a tribe, you pushed into their throats the Banu Kilab on the morning of terror and fear.

[[His Diwan, p. 56; Majaz al-Qur'an of Abu ʿUbayda, 1:249. He praises with it the Banu Ja'far ibn Kilab, from three verses, isolated.]]

* *

The interpretation of His words: ﴿And others besides them, whom you do not know; Allah knows them﴾.

Abu Ja'far said: The scholars of ta'wil have differed about these "others": who are they, and what are they?

Some of them said: They are the Banu Qurayza.

Those who said that:

16239. It was reported to me on the authority of ʿAmmar ibn al-Hasan, who said: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿And others besides them﴾, meaning: from the Banu Qurayza.

16240. Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, who said: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, who said: ʿIsa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿And others besides them﴾, he said: "Qurayza."

* *

Others said: They are from Persia.

Those who said that:

16241. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, who said: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, who said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿And others besides them, whom you do not know; Allah knows them﴾, these are the people of Persia.

* *

Others said: They are every enemy of the Muslims, other than the ones whom the Prophet (ﷺ) was ordered to scatter those behind them by. They said: And they are the hypocrites.

Those who said that:

16242. Yunus narrated to me, who said: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said, concerning the saying of Allah: ﴿So if you overcome them in war, scatter those behind them﴾, he said: "Lighten them by them (akhifhum bihim), for what you do with these." And he recited: ﴿And others besides them, whom you do not know; Allah knows them﴾. [[The report 16242: this is a repetition of the report that preceded, no. 16220, and I do not know why he brought it here singly. The report he meant is the one following it, and it seems to be an error by al-Tabari himself in the transmission. The wording of this report differs slightly from the preceding report.]]

16243. Yunus narrated to me, who said: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words: ﴿And others besides them, whom you do not know; Allah knows them﴾, he said: "These are the hypocrites. You do not know them, because they are with you; they say: There is no god but Allah, and they fight with you."

* *

Others said: They are a group of the jinn.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct position on this matter is to say that Allah commanded the believers to prepare for jihad and the implements of war, and whatever they might strengthen themselves with in the jihad against His enemy and their enemy among the polytheists, such as weapons, archery, and other things, and the stationing of horses. There is no basis for saying that "force" refers to one meaning rather than another of the meanings of "force," since Allah has generalized the command to it.
