If someone says: But the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) has made clear that this is specifically meant, by his saying: "Indeed, the force is archery"?

It is said to him: Even though the report has come with that, there is nothing in the report that indicates that archery alone is meant by it, to the exclusion of all other meanings of force against them. Archery is one of the meanings of force, for it was only said in the report: "Indeed, the force is archery," and it was not said: "to the exclusion of others." Among "force" are also the sword, the spear, and the lance, and everything that is a help in fighting the polytheists, such as the help of archery or more effective than archery against them and in wounding them. This is in addition to the weakness of the chain of that report from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). [[Here again the manuscript's writing differs: it reads "wahha" (weakness), as I have written it, and the printed edition had "wahiya". See what I wrote before at 9:531, note 2. Then see what I wrote in the takhrij of the earlier report, no. 16225, and what I mentioned of the sound route for the transmission of this report.]]

* *

As for His words: ﴿And others besides them, whom you do not know﴾, the saying of the one who said that it refers to the jinn is closer to the truth and more fitting, because He, may His praise be exalted, has included, by His words: ﴿And of the stationing of horses, you terrify thereby the enemy of Allah and your enemy﴾, the command to station horses to terrify every enemy of Allah and of the believers whom they know. There is no doubt that the believers were aware of the enmity of Qurayza and Persia toward them, because they knew that they were polytheists and that they were at war with them. There is no sense in saying: "And they know them as enemies to them": ﴿And others besides them, whom you do not know﴾. Rather, the meaning of that, if Allah wills, is: you terrify by your stationing of horses, O believers, the enemy of Allah and your enemies from among the children of Adam, whose enmity to you you have known, because of their disbelief in Allah and His Messenger, and you terrify by that another kind other than the children of Adam, whose places and conditions you do not know, Allah knows them apart from you, because the children of Adam do not see them. It has been said that the neighing of horses terrifies the jinn, and that the jinn do not approach a house in which there is a horse. [[Ibn Kathir mentioned in his tafsir two reports. One of them was narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim from Zayd ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿArib, from his father, from his grandfather, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "They are the jinn," in this verse; then he said: "al-Tabarani narrated it, and added: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'No house in which there is a noble horse is struck with insanity (yukhbal).'" (See al-Isaba, entry on ʿArib.) Then Ibn Kathir said: "This hadith is munkar (rejected); its chain is not sound, nor its text." See also al-Qurtubi 8:38. What al-Tabari said has been rejected by scholars, and rightly so. Ibn Kathir and Abu Hayyan (4:513) preferred that the meaning is the hypocrites, and that is the position which Abu Ja'far rejects below, and Abu Ja'far's rejection is a firm rejection. If it is for us to choose, then I choose that what is meant is those among the polytheists whose affair was hidden from the believers, like the Christians of Syria and others, whose hostility the believers had not yet observed, and which is coming, and they will see it with their own eyes shortly. There is in the discussion surplus of inquiry that is not this place for it, and the verse is general; I do not know how Abu Ja'far would particularize it with a report that contains no proof.]]

* *

If someone says: The believers did not know what the hypocrites were upon, so what prevents you from saying that the hypocrites are meant by that?

It is said: The hypocrites were not frightened by the horses of the Muslims or by their weapons. What frightened them was that the Muslims would discover their hidden secrets, which they concealed from disbelief. The believers were only commanded to prepare force to terrify the enemy. As for one whom that does not terrify, he is not included in the meaning of those for whom the believers were commanded to prepare that. It has been said: "Lā taʿlamūnahum" (you do not know them): the verb "to know" is satisfied with one object in this place, because what is intended is: "You do not recognize them," as the poet said: [[He is al-Nimr ibn Tawlab al-ʿUklī.]]

Indeed Allah knows me and Wahb,
and that we both will meet Him.

[[al-Iqtidab, p. 303; al-Mufassal of al-Zamakhshari, p. 88. Al-Nimr ibn Tawlab was disputing with a man of his tribe called "Wahb" over a well called "al-Duhul" (with an unpointed ḥāʾ), in the land of ʿAkl, Numayra's water. He says in these verses:

But al-Duhul, when one comes to it,
lean in wealth, it leaves him fat.

Al-Nimr had given him water from it, but he was not grateful to him, and he betrayed the trust, and disputed with him over it. So he said:

Wahb wants to betray me, while I hope
from Allah for innocence and security.

Indeed Allah knows me and Wahb,
and knows that we both shall meet.]]

إنَّ بَنِي رَبِيعَةَ بَعْدَ وَهْبٍ ... كَرَاعِي البَيْتِ يَحْفَظُهُ فخانَا

Indeed, the Banu Rabi'ah after Wahb are like the keeper of the house who guards it, yet betrays it [us].

وكان البيت في المطبوعة والمخطوطة: فإن اللهَ يعلمني ... وأَنا سوف يلقاهُ كلانا]]

In the printed edition and the manuscript, the line reads: "For God knows me... and I shall meet Him, both of us [[..."

* *

القول في تأويل قوله: ﴿وَمَا تُنْفِقُوا مِنْ شَيْءٍ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ يُوَفَّ إِلَيْكُمْ وَأَنْتُمْ لا تُظْلَمُونَ (٦٠) ﴾

On the interpretation (ta'wil, the explanation of the meaning) of His saying: ﴿And whatever you spend in the way of God, it will be repaid to you, and you will not be wronged﴾ (60).

Abu Ja'far said: His mention, exalted is He, means: Whatever you, O believers, spend of expenditure in purchasing the instruments of war, such as weapons, spears, horses or other expenses, [[See the explanation of "nafaqah" (expenditure) in the earlier language indices under (nafaqa).]] in fighting the enemies of God among the polytheists, God will replace it for you in this world, and He will store up your rewards for that with Him, until He repays them to you on the Day of Resurrection. [[See the explanation of "wafa" (fulfilment) in the earlier discussion, 12:224, note 3, and the references there.]] ﴿And you will not be wronged﴾ means: your Lord deals with you in this way, so He does not waste your rewards with Him.

* *

Similar to what we have said on this matter is what the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said.

Mention of those who said this:

16244. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, who said: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, regarding ﴿And whatever you spend in the way of God, it will be repaid to you, and you will not be wronged﴾: that is, their reward will not be lost to you with God in the Hereafter, nor will its swift replacement in this world be lost. [[The report 16244 is in Sirat Ibn Hisham 2: 329, 330, and it follows the earlier report No. 16218.]]

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And if they incline to peace, then incline to it, and put your trust in Allah. Indeed, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾ (8:61)

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): And if you fear treachery and betrayal from a people, then throw back to them [their covenant] on equal terms, and inform them of war. ﴿And if they incline to peace, then incline to it﴾: that is, if they lean toward making peace with you and abandoning war, whether by entering Islam, or by paying the jizyah (poll tax), or by a truce, and the like of the causes of peace and reconciliation [[See the explanation of "peace" (al-salm) earlier, 4:251–255.]]. ﴿Then incline to it﴾ means: turn toward it, and grant them what they have inclined to and asked of you.

* *

It is said of this verb: "jana'a al-rajul ila kadha yajnahu ilayhi junuhan" (the man inclined toward such-and-such), and it is reported of the tribes of Tamim and Qays that they say "yajnuh" with a damma on the nun, while others say "yajnih" with a kasra on the nun; this means he inclined. From it is the verse of Al-Nabigha of Banu Dhubyan:

Jawanih qad ayqan anna qabilahu / idha ma iltaqa al-jam'an awwalu ghalib
[[From his Diwan, p. 43, from his well-known poem about Amr ibn al-Harith al-A'raj, when he fled to Syria from al-Nu'man ibn al-Mundhir, in the story of al-Mutajarrida. Before it, he mentions the raid of his army and the vultures that follow the army: "When they campaigned with the army, there hovered above them / flocks of birds guided by flocks [of other birds]; / they accompany them until they raid their camp / from the striking ones stained with blood, the swirling. / You see them behind the people, their eyes sidelong, / sitting like elders in the garments of the grave-diggers. / Jawanih, who was certain..." This is among the finest and purest poetry.]]

Jawanih: inclining (mawa'il).

* *

The people of interpretation have said what we have said in this matter.

Those who said so:

16245. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿And if they incline to peace﴾, he said: to reconciliation. And it was abrogated by His saying: ﴿So kill the polytheists wherever you find them﴾ [Surah al-Tawbah: 5].

16246. Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿And if they incline to peace﴾, to reconciliation, ﴿then incline to it﴾. He said: This was before "Bara'ah" (Surah al-Tawbah), and the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) would make a truce with the people until a term; then either they would embrace Islam, or he would fight them. Then this was later abrogated in "Bara'ah" when He said: ﴿So kill the polytheists wherever you find them﴾, and He said: ﴿Fight the polytheists all together﴾ [Surah al-Tawbah: 36], and he renounced to every party with a covenant its covenant, and commanded him to fight them until they say "There is no god but Allah" and embrace Islam, and that nothing be accepted from them except that. Every covenant that was in this surah and in others, and every reconciliation by which the Muslims made peace with the polytheists and truced with them, "Bara'ah" came with its abrogation; so he was commanded to fight them in every case until they say: "There is no god but Allah."

16247. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, from al-Husayn, from Yazid, from Ikrimah and al-Hasan al-Basri, who both said: ﴿And if they incline to peace, then incline to it﴾ was abrogated by the verse in "Bara'ah": His saying: ﴿Fight those who do not believe in Allah nor in the Last Day﴾, up to His saying: ﴿and they are humbled﴾ [Surah al-Tawbah: 29].

16248. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿And if they incline to peace, then incline to it﴾, he said: If they desire reconciliation, then grant it.

16249. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: ﴿And if they incline to peace, then incline to it﴾, i.e., if they call you to peace, to Islam, then make peace with them upon it. [[The report 16249: Sirah Ibn Hisham 2:330, a continuation of the earlier report no. 16244.]]

16250. Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying: ﴿And if they incline to peace, then incline to it﴾: He said: So make peace with them. He said: This was abrogated by jihad.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: As for what Qatadah and whoever said like his saying said, that this verse is abrogated, it is a statement for which there is no evidence from the Book, nor the Sunnah, nor sound reason.

We have shown in more than one place in this book of ours and others that abrogation (naskh) occurs only when the abrogating ruling negates the ruling of the abrogated in every respect. As for what is otherwise, it does not constitute abrogation. [[See his view on "abrogation" (naskh) earlier, 11:209 and what follows and precedes it, in the indexes of the book, and in the indexes of Arabic, grammar and other works.]]

Allah's saying in Bara'ah: ﴿So kill the polytheists wherever you find them﴾ does not negate the ruling of His saying: ﴿And if they incline to peace, then incline to it﴾, because His saying: ﴿And if they incline to peace﴾ refers only to the Banu Qurayza, who were Jews, People of the Book, and Allah, may His praise be exalted, has permitted the believers to make peace with the People of the Book and to truce with them in war, in exchange for taking the jizyah from them.

As for His saying: ﴿So kill the polytheists wherever you find them﴾, it refers only to the polytheists of the Arabs, the idol-worshippers, from whom accepting the jizyah is not permitted. So there is no negation of the ruling of one verse by the other in either of them; rather each of them is firmly established regarding what it was revealed about.

16251. Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿And if they incline to peace﴾, he said: Qurayza.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And put your trust in Allah﴾, it means: entrust your affair, O Muhammad, to Allah, and seek His sufficiency, certain that He will suffice you, as in:

16252. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: ﴿And put your trust in Allah﴾, indeed Allah is sufficient for you. [[The report 16252: Sirah Ibn Hisham 2:330, a continuation of the earlier report no. 16249.]]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Indeed, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾, it means by that: indeed Allah, in whom you put your trust, is "All-Hearing" of what you and those with whom you make peace and truce in war among the enemies of Allah and your enemies say when concluding the peace between you and them, and what conditions each party stipulates upon the other [[In the printed edition: "wa yashrit kull fariq..." ; in the manuscript: "wa yashtarit..."; the correct reading between them is what has been adopted.]]; and "All-Knowing" of what each party among you conceals for the other party regarding fulfilling what it has contracted to, and of what is concealed in the heart of one of you and harbored contrary to his companion. [[See the explanation of "All-Hearing" (samee') and "All-Knowing" (aleem) earlier in the lexical indexes (sami'a), ('alima).]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 8, verse 62:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And if they intend to deceive you, then sufficient for you is Allah. It is He who supported you with His help and with the believers﴾ (62)

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is He, the One who is mentioned, says: And if they intend, O Muhammad, those whom I commanded you to throw back their treaty on equal terms (inbadh ilayhim 'ala sawa', i.e., to openly announce the end of the treaty) if you fear treachery from them, and [to make peace with them] if they incline to peace, to deceive you and to plot against you [[See the explanation of "deception" (al-khada') in what has preceded: 1:273–277, 302; 9:329.]] = ﴿then sufficient for you is Allah﴾, meaning: then Allah is sufficient for you against them and sufficient for you against their deception of you, [[See the explanation of "sufficient" (hasbuka) in what has preceded: 11:137, note 2, and the references there.]] because He has undertaken to make your religion prevail over all religions, and has guaranteed that He will make His word the highest and the word of His enemies the lowest = ﴿It is He who supported you with His help﴾, meaning: Allah is the One who strengthened you with His help against His enemies [[See the explanation of "supported" (ayyada) in what has preceded: 13:377, note 3, and the references there.]] = ﴿and with the believers﴾, meaning: with the Helpers (al-Ansar).

* *

And the people of interpretation have said things similar to what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said this:

16253- Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, he said: Abu 'Asim related to us, he said: 'Isa related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿And if they intend to deceive you﴾, he said: Qurayzah.

16254- Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Ishaq: ﴿And if they intend to deceive you, then sufficient for you is Allah﴾, he is behind that. [[The report 16254: Sirat Ibn Hisham, 2:331, and it continues the previous report no. 16252.]]

16255- Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to me, he said: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, he said: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿It is He who supported you with His help﴾, he said: With the Helpers (al-Ansar).

**The Interpretation of His Words: ﴿And He joined their hearts. Had you spent everything on earth, you could not have joined their hearts, but God joined them. Indeed, He is Mighty and Wise﴾ (8:63)**

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: By His words ﴿And He joined their hearts﴾, may His praise be exalted, God means that He gathered together the hearts of the believers from the Aws and the Khazraj after their dispersal and division, upon His true religion. He made them one through it after they had been scattered, and brothers after they had been enemies.

As for His words ﴿Had you spent everything on earth, you could not have joined their hearts﴾, God, may His remembrance be exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Even if you, O Muhammad, were to spend everything on earth of gold, silver and goods, you would not have joined their hearts by your own strength [[The word "حيل" (ḥayl, pronounced with a fatha and then a sukun) means strength, like "حول" (ḥawl). One says, "He is very strong (innahu la-shadid al-ḥayl)." In a hadith: "O God, Lord of mighty strength (dha al-ḥayl al-shadid)." This usage still survives in the colloquial Arabic of Egypt.]], but God joined them upon guidance, so they came together and were united, as a strengthening from God for you, a support from Him and an aid against your enemy. He, may His praise be exalted, says: The One who did this and brought it about for you, so that they became your helpers and supporters and one hand against whoever desires you harm, is the One who, if an enemy aims at you, will suffice you against his plotting and grant you victory over him. So trust in Him, proceed according to His command, and rely upon Him.

* *

What we have said on this matter is also what the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) [[Ahl al-ta'wil: the exegetes, the scholars of Qur'anic interpretation.]] have said.

Those who said so:

He joined their hearts after war that had been between them."[[The space between "من بعد حرب" (after war) and "فيما كان بينهم" (what had been between them) is blank in the manuscript and is enclosed in red brackets. I do not know whether it is a blank left by an omission or a mistake by the copyist, which he filled with red.]]

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Bashir ibn Thabit, a man from the Ansar, that he said about this verse ﴿Had you spent everything on earth, you could not have joined their hearts﴾: "He means the Ansar."[[Report 16257: Bashir ibn Thabit al-Ansari, client (mawla) of al-Nu'man ibn Bashir. Ibn Hibban mentioned him in al-Thiqat (the trustworthy). Shu'bah narrated from him. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir (1/2/97), and Ibn Abi Hatim (1/1/372).]]

It continues the preceding report no. 16254.]]

16260. Abd al-Karim ibn Abi Umayr narrated to me: al-Walid narrated to me, from Abu Amr, who said: Abdah ibn Abi Lubabah narrated to me, from Mujahid, and I met him, and he took my hand and said: "When two loving ones for God's sake see each other,[[Tara'a al-rajulan: the two men saw one another.]] and one of them takes the hand of his companion and smiles at him, their sins fall away as the leaves of a tree fall away."[[Tahatt warq al-shajar: it fell from its branch when it withered, and then scattered.]] Abdah said: I said to him: "Surely this is a small matter!" 16261. Muhammad ibn Khalaf narrated to me: Ubayd Allah ibn Musa narrated to us: Fudayl ibn Ghazwan narrated to us, who said: "I came to Abu Ishaq, greeted him, and said [[In al-Mustadrak: "I met Abu Ishaq after his sight had gone."]]: 'Do you know me?' Fudayl said: 'Yes! If not for my shame before you, I would have kissed you.'" He said: Abu al-Ahwas narrated to me, from Abd Allah, who said: This verse was revealed about those who love one another for God's sake: ﴿Had you spent everything on earth, you could not have joined their hearts﴾.[[Report 16261: "Abu Ishaq" is al-Sabi'i. 16263. Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Hakam narrated to me: Ayyub ibn Suwayd narrated to us, from al-Awza'i, who said: Abdah ibn Abi Lubabah narrated to me, from Mujahid — then he mentioned something like the hadith of Abd al-Karim, from al-Walid.[[Report 16263: See what preceded at no. 16260, and the note on it.]]

16264. Ibn Wakic narrated to us: Abu Usamah, Ibn Numayr, and Hafs ibn Ghiyath narrated to us, from Fudayl ibn Ghazwan, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu al-Ahwas, who said: "I heard Abd Allah say: ﴿Had you spent everything on earth, you could not have joined their hearts﴾, to the end of the verse," and he said: "They are those who love one another for God's sake."[[Report 16264: Another route for the report preceding at no. 16261.]]

* *

His words ﴿Indeed, He is Mighty and Wise﴾ mean: Indeed, God, who joined the hearts of the Aws and the Khazraj after their word had been scattered and they had been hostile, and made them helpers for you — ﴿Mighty﴾: nothing overpowers Him, and no one turns back His decree, but He executes His judgment upon His creation. That is, so rely upon Him and trust in Him — ﴿Wise﴾: in the management of His creation.[[For the explanation of "عزيز" (Mighty) and "حكيم" (Wise), see the earlier glossaries of vocabulary under the roots (عزز) and (حكم).]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 8, verse 64:

The explanation of His saying: ﴿O Prophet, Allah is sufficient for you and for those believers who follow you﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The Exalted, may His remembrance be glorified, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿O Prophet, Allah is sufficient for you﴾, and Allah is sufficient for you and for those believers who follow you. He, may His praise be exalted, says to them: Press on against your enemy, for Allah is sufficient for you against them, and let the multitude of their number and the paucity of your number not dismay you, for Allah supports you with His victory. [[See the explanation of "hasb" (sufficiency) earlier, p. 44, note 2, and the references there.]]

* *

Those who engaged in interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) said things similar to what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:

16265- Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Mu'ammil ibn Isma'il narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Shawdhab Abu Mu'adh, from al-Sha'bi, regarding His saying: ﴿O Prophet, Allah is sufficient for you and for those believers who follow you﴾, he said: Allah is sufficient for you, and Allah is sufficient for those believers who follow you. [[The report 16265: "Shawdhab, Abu Mu'adh", also said to be "Abu Uthman", the client of al-Bara' ibn 'Azib. Sufyan said, from Shawdhab: "I was a stallion-keeper, and al-Bara' ibn 'Azib forbade me from the stud-fee of the stallion." Narrated from him by Sufyan al-Thawri and Shu'ba. Biographed in al-Kabir 2/2/261 and Ibn Abi Hatim 2/1/377. In the printed edition it read "Shawdhab ibn Mu'adh," which is an error; the correct form is in the manuscript.

The two following chains will come.]]

16266- Ahmad ibn Uthman ibn Hakim al-Awdi narrated to me, saying: 'Ubayd Allah ibn Musa narrated to us, saying: Sufyan informed us, from Shawdhab, from al-Sha'bi, regarding His saying: ﴿O Prophet, Allah is sufficient for you and for those believers who follow you﴾, he said: Allah is sufficient for you, and for those who are with you.

16267- Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: 'Ubayd Allah narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Shawdhab, from 'Amir, similarly, except that he said: Allah is sufficient for you, and for those who witnessed (the battle) with you.

16268- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, from Ibn Zayd, regarding His saying: ﴿O Prophet, Allah is sufficient for you and for those believers who follow you﴾, he said: O Prophet, Allah is sufficient for you, and for those believers who follow you; indeed your sufficiency is you and they, and Allah.

* *

As for "man" in His saying ﴿and for those believers who follow you﴾, on this interpretation that we have mentioned from al-Sha'bi, it is in the accusative case, being conjoined to the meaning of the "ka" (you) in His saying ﴿Allah is sufficient for you﴾, not to its apparent wording, since the apparent position is genitive while the meaning is accusative. The sense of the statement is: Allah suffices you, and suffices the believers who follow you.

* *

Some of the grammarians (ahl al-'arabiyya) said that "man" is in the nominative case, conjoined to the subject "Allah", as if he said: Allah is sufficient for you, and those who follow you in striving against the enemy from among the believers, apart from those among them who stay behind from you. They cited as evidence for the soundness of this view His saying: ﴿Urge the believers to fighting﴾. [[This is al-Farra' in Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1:417.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 8, verses 65–66:

The interpretation of His words: ﴿O Prophet, urge the believers to fight. If there are twenty of you who are steadfast, they will overcome two hundred; and if there are a hundred of you, they will overcome a thousand of those who disbelieve, because they are a people who do not understand.﴾ (65) ﴿Now Allah has lightened your burden, for He knows that there is weakness in you. So if there are a hundred of you who are steadfast, they will overcome two hundred; and if there are a thousand of you, they will overcome two thousand, by Allah's leave. And Allah is with the steadfast.﴾ (66)

Abu Ja'far said: May His remembrance be exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: ﴿O Prophet, urge the believers to fight.﴾ Urge those who follow you and believe you regarding what you have brought them of truth, to fight those polytheists who have turned their backs and turned away from the truth [[See the explanation of "tahrid" (urging) above, 8:579.]] = ﴿If there are twenty of you﴾ men = ﴿who are steadfast﴾ when meeting the enemy, seeking reward (from Allah) and holding firm against their enemy = ﴿they will overcome two hundred﴾ of their enemy and subdue them = ﴿And if there are a hundred of you﴾ at that time = ﴿they will overcome﴾ of them = ﴿a thousand﴾ = ﴿because they are a people who do not understand﴾. He says: because the polytheists are a people who fight without hope of reward and without seeking recompense or seeking the reward of God, for they did not understand that Allah makes obligatory (reward) for whoever fights seeking reward and seeks what Allah has promised in the promise, what He promised to those who strive in His way; so they do not stand firm when they meet in battle, for fear of being killed and thereby losing their worldly life. [[See the explanation of "fiqh" (understanding) above, 13:278, note 1, and the references there.]] Then He, may His remembrance be exalted, lightened (the burden) for the believers, knowing their weakness, and said to them: ﴿Now Allah has lightened your burden, for He knows that there is weakness in you.﴾ That is: in each one of them, in facing ten of their enemy, there is weakness = ﴿So if there are a hundred of you who are steadfast﴾ when they meet them, to stand firm against them = ﴿they will overcome two hundred﴾ of them = ﴿and if there are a thousand of you, they will overcome two thousand﴾ of them = ﴿by Allah's leave﴾, that is: by Allah's permitting them to overcome, and His help to them = ﴿And Allah is with the steadfast﴾, against their enemy and the enemy of Allah, seeking reward in their steadfastness and seeking abundant reward from their Lord, with His aid to them and victory over them.

* *

Ahl al-ta'wil (the people of interpretation) said things similar to what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said this:

16269. Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Muhabbab narrated to us, he said: Sufyan narrated to us, from Layth, from ʿAta' regarding His words: ﴿If there are twenty of you who are steadfast, they will overcome two hundred﴾, he said: One man was (required) for ten, then it was made one man for two; he should not flee from them. [[The report 16269: Muhammad ibn Muhabbab ibn Ishaq al-Qurashi, trustworthy, previously mentioned under no. 6320.]]

16270. Sa'id ibn Yahya narrated to us, he said: My father narrated to us, he said: Ibn Juraij narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Dinar, from Ibn ʿAbbas who said: It was made obligatory on the Muslims that one man should face ten of the disbelievers. Then He said: ﴿If there are twenty of you who are steadfast, they will overcome two hundred﴾, and that lightened it for them, so it was made one man against two men. Ibn ʿAbbas said: I do not like that people should know of the lightening of this for them.

16271. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Salamah narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: ʿAbd Allah ibn Abi Najih al-Makki narrated to me, from ʿAta' ibn Abi Rabah, from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAbbas, who said: When this verse was revealed, it weighed heavily on the Muslims, and they considered it great that twenty should fight two hundred, and a hundred fight a thousand. So Allah lightened it for them, and abrogated it with the other verse: ﴿Now Allah has lightened your burden, for He knows that there is weakness in you. So if there are a hundred of you who are steadfast, they will overcome two hundred; and if there are a thousand of you, they will overcome two thousand﴾. He said: When they were on half of their enemy's number, it was not fitting for them to flee from them; and if they were fewer than that, it was not obligatory for them to fight, and it was permissible for them to withdraw from them. [[The report 16271: Sirat Ibn Hisham 2:331. It follows the next report, no. 16285; Tabari placed it earlier and delayed it here, so the order of its transmission differs from Ibn Ishaq's tafsir in his biography.]]

16272. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, he said: ʿAbd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, he said: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding His words: ﴿If there are twenty of you who are steadfast, they will overcome two hundred﴾, he said: Each man among the Muslims had (the obligation against) ten, and he should not flee from them. They remained so until Allah revealed: ﴿Now Allah has lightened your burden, for He knows that there is weakness in you. So if there are a hundred of you who are steadfast, they will overcome two hundred﴾, and He arranged for each Muslim man two polytheists. So the first command was abrogated. He said again regarding His words: ﴿If there are twenty of you who are steadfast, they will overcome two hundred﴾: Allah commanded the believing man to fight ten of the disbelievers, and that was difficult for the believers, and Allah had mercy on them, so He said: ﴿If there are a hundred of you who are steadfast, they will overcome two hundred; and if there are a thousand of you, they will overcome two thousand, by Allah's leave; and Allah is with the steadfast﴾. So Allah commanded the believing man to fight two of the disbelievers.

16273. Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, he said: My father narrated to me, he said: My paternal uncle narrated to me, he said: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding His words: ﴿O Prophet, urge the believers to fight﴾, up to His words: ﴿because they are a people who do not understand﴾. That was because he had made it obligatory on each Muslim man to face ten of the enemy, taunting them — that is, inciting them [[The word "ta'shib" means inciting people against one another with evil; similarly "ta'shib" means inciting against the enemy. See what preceded in the note on no. 16059, vol. 13:531, note 2. The lexicons are deficient in explaining the meaning of this Arabic term.]] with that, so that they would prepare themselves for the raid, and that Allah would help them against the enemy. It was not a command that Allah resolved upon them or made obligatory, but it was urging and a charge that Allah commanded His Prophet with. Then He lightened it for them, saying: ﴿Now Allah has lightened your burden, for He knows that there is weakness in you﴾, so He made it two men for each man after that, as a lightening, so that the believers would know that Allah is merciful to them. So they relied on Allah, were steadfast and were truthful. Had it been obligatory upon them, they would have been unbelievers... each Muslim man [nakal] from those of the disbelievers they met when they were more numerous than them, and they did not fight them. [[In the printed edition: "had it been obligatory upon them the raid, when each Muslim man was distanced from those of the disbelievers he met," a sentence with no meaning. In the manuscript: "had it been obligatory upon them, they would have disbelieved, when each Muslim man was lax (kull) about those of the disbelievers he met," and the correct reading is what I have given, but the copyist omitted, God knows best, the word [nakal] placed between brackets. "Nakala 'an 'aduwwihi" means he shrank back from his enemy.]] So let not the words of men deceive you! For I have heard men say: It is not right for a Muslim man to fight until there are two men against each man, and until there are four against each two, and calculate by that, and they claim that they disobey Allah if they fight until they reach that number, and that there is no sin on them if they do not fight until they reach the number that there be two men against each man and four against each two. Allah has said: ﴿And among mankind is he who sells himself seeking the pleasure of Allah, and Allah is Kind to the servants﴾ [Surah al-Baqarah: 207], and Allah has said: ﴿So fight in the way of Allah; you are not charged except with yourself, and urge the believers﴾ [Surah al-Nisa': 84]. This is the urging that Allah revealed to them in "al-Anfal", so do not weaken; fight, for you have been placed among a people as Allah willed them to be. [[In the printed edition: "so let not the enemy overwhelm you, for he has fallen," which has no meaning; the correct reading is what is in the manuscript, as I have given, and it is unpointed there, which is the correct reading. His words "fa-la ta'jizanna" mean: do not sit back from fighting out of weakness, but fight, for you have come among a number of the enemy, as Allah willed their number to be, few or many.]]

16274. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, from al-Husayn, from Zayd, from ʿIkrimah and al-Hasan, who both said: He said in "Surat al-Anfal": ﴿If there are twenty of you who are steadfast, they will overcome two hundred; and if there are a hundred of you, they will overcome a thousand of those who disbelieve, because they are a people who do not understand﴾. Then it was abrogated, and He said: ﴿Now Allah has lightened your burden, for He knows that there is weakness in you﴾, up to His words: ﴿And Allah is with the steadfast﴾.

16275. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Jarir narrated to us, from Mughirah, from ʿIkrimah, regarding His words: ﴿If there are twenty of you who are steadfast﴾, he said: One man of the Muslims against ten of the polytheists. Then He lightened it for them, making it obligatory that not one man flee from two.

16276. As for His words: ﴿because they are a people who do not understand﴾, we have already explained its interpretation. [[See what preceded, p. 51.]]

Ibn Ishaq used to say concerning this:

16285. [[The report 16285: Sirat Ibn Hisham 2:331. It follows the earlier report no. 16257, and Abu Ja'far delayed it from its place to this point, and placed before it the report no. 16271, which in Ibn Hisham's biography is the subsequent report on the revelation of the surah. In the printed edition: "and no knowledge of what is good," and I have kept what is in the manuscript and the biography.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: This verse — I mean His words: ﴿If there are twenty of you who are steadfast, they will overcome two hundred﴾ — although its form is that of a report, its meaning is a command. This is indicated by His words: ﴿Now Allah has lightened your burden﴾, for the lightening was only after the burdening. Had the holding firm of ten of them against a hundred of their enemy been something not obligatory upon them before the lightening, but a recommendation, there would have been no point in the lightening, because the lightening is only a permission to abandon the holding firm of one Muslim against ten of the enemy. When the burdening had not preceded it, there was no point to the permission, since what is understood from permission is only after burdening. Since that is so, it is known that the ruling of His words: ﴿Now Allah has lightened your burden, for He knows that there is weakness in you﴾ abrogates the ruling of His words: ﴿If there are twenty of you who are steadfast, they will overcome two hundred; and if there are a hundred of you, they will overcome a thousand of those who disbelieve﴾. The readers differed regarding the recitation of His words: ﴿and He knows that there is weakness in you﴾.

Some Medinan and some Basran readers recited it: ﴿وَعَلِمَ أَنَّ فِيكُمْ ضُعْفًا﴾, with a "dammah" on the "ḍād" throughout the Qur'an, and with tanwin on "ḍu'f", as a verbal noun of "ḍa'ufa al-rajul ḍu'fan" (the man became weak).

* *

The majority of the Kufan readers recited it: ﴿وَعَلِمَ أَنَّ فِيكُمْ ضَعْفًا﴾, with a "fathah" on the "ḍād", also as a verbal noun of "ḍa'ufa".

* *

Some Medinan readers recited: ﴿ضُعَفَاء﴾, as a form of "fu'ala" (the plural of "ḍa'if" as "ḍu'afa'"), just as "al-sharik" is pluralized as "shuraka'" and "al-rahim" as "ruhama'".

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of the readings in this matter is the reading of the one who recites it: (وَعَلِمَ أَنَّ فِيكُمْ ضَعْفًا) and ﴿ضُعْفًا﴾, with a fathah or dammah on the "ḍād", because these are the two well-known readings, and they are two famous dialects in the speech of the Arabs, eloquent and with one meaning. So whichever of the two the reciter recites, he is correct in the right.

* *

As for the reading of the one who recites it: "ḍu'afa'", it is irregular (shādh) among the readings, and although it has a valid basis in soundness, I do not like a reader to recite it.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 8, verses 65–66:

The interpretation of His words: ﴿O Prophet, urge the believers to fight. If there are twenty of you who are steadfast, they will overcome two hundred; and if there are a hundred of you, they will overcome a thousand of those who disbelieve, because they are a people who do not understand.﴾ (65) ﴿Now Allah has lightened your burden, for He knows that there is weakness in you. So if there are a hundred of you who are steadfast, they will overcome two hundred; and if there are a thousand of you, they will overcome two thousand, by Allah's leave. And Allah is with the steadfast.﴾ (66)

Abu Ja'far said: May His remembrance be exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: ﴿O Prophet, urge the believers to fight.﴾ Urge those who follow you and believe you regarding what you have brought them of truth, to fight those polytheists who have turned their backs and turned away from the truth [[See the explanation of "tahrid" (urging) above, 8:579.]] = ﴿If there are twenty of you﴾ men = ﴿who are steadfast﴾ when meeting the enemy, seeking reward (from Allah) and holding firm against their enemy = ﴿they will overcome two hundred﴾ of their enemy and subdue them = ﴿And if there are a hundred of you﴾ at that time = ﴿they will overcome﴾ of them = ﴿a thousand﴾ = ﴿because they are a people who do not understand﴾. He says: because the polytheists are a people who fight without hope of reward and without seeking recompense or seeking the reward of God, for they did not understand that Allah makes obligatory (reward) for whoever fights seeking reward and seeks what Allah has promised in the promise, what He promised to those who strive in His way; so they do not stand firm when they meet in battle, for fear of being killed and thereby losing their worldly life. [[See the explanation of "fiqh" (understanding) above, 13:278, note 1, and the references there.]] Then He, may His remembrance be exalted, lightened (the burden) for the believers, knowing their weakness, and said to them: ﴿Now Allah has lightened your burden, for He knows that there is weakness in you.﴾ That is: in each one of them, in facing ten of their enemy, there is weakness = ﴿So if there are a hundred of you who are steadfast﴾ when they meet them, to stand firm against them = ﴿they will overcome two hundred﴾ of them = ﴿and if there are a thousand of you, they will overcome two thousand﴾ of them = ﴿by Allah's leave﴾, that is: by Allah's permitting them to overcome, and His help to them = ﴿And Allah is with the steadfast﴾, against their enemy and the enemy of Allah, seeking reward in their steadfastness and seeking abundant reward from their Lord, with His aid to them and victory over them.

* *

Ahl al-ta'wil (the people of interpretation) said things similar to what we have said on this matter.

**The interpretation of His saying: ﴿It is not for a Prophet to have captives until he has inflicted a heavy slaughter in the land. You desire the goods of this world, but Allah desires the Hereafter. And Allah is Mighty and Wise﴾ (8:67)**

Abu Ja'far said: May His remembrance be exalted, He says: It was not for a Prophet to hold in custody an unbeliever over whom he had power and who came into his hand, from among the worshippers of idols, in exchange for ransom or for a free release.

* *

In the speech of the Arabs, "al-asr" (captivity) means confinement. From it one says "ma'sur," meaning "confined." It is also heard from them: "abalahu Allah asran" (may Allah afflict him with urinary retention).

[[See the explanation of "al-asir" (the captive) above, 2:311-312.

As for his saying "abalahu Allah asran": "al-asr," with a damma on the alif and a sukun on the sin, is the retention of urine; one says "akhadhahu al-asr" (retention seized him). This phrase in the manuscript reads "abi Allah asran," while in Lisan al-Arab, as in the printed edition, it reads "analahu bil-nun" ("analahu" with a nun). In Asas al-Balagha it reads: "And in their supplications: abi laka Allah asran."

What is in the manuscript and in Asas al-Balagha supports the correctness of what I read with the ba'.]]

* *

Allah, exalted is His praise, said that to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) to inform him that killing the polytheists whom he (ﷺ) took captive at the Battle of Badr and then ransomed for money was more fitting than taking ransom from them and releasing them.

* *

His saying ﴿until he has inflicted a heavy slaughter in the land﴾ means: until he has thoroughly killed the polytheists in it and subdued them by force and compulsion.

* *

From this one says: "athkhana fulan fi hadha al-amr" (so-and-so went to excess in this matter, i.e., he exerted himself thoroughly in it). It is also related: "athkhantuhu ma'rifatan," meaning: I killed him for certain (or: I thoroughly killed him).

* *

[The next clause:] ﴿You desire﴾ addresses the believers among the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): ﴿You desire,﴾ O believers, ﴿the goods of this world,﴾ by taking your captives from the polytheists. The "'aradh" (goods) is what presents itself to a person of wealth and goods [of this world]. [[See the explanation of "al-'aradh" above, 9:71 and 13:211.]] He means: by your taking ransom from the polytheists you desire the enjoyment and the sweetness of worldly goods. ﴿But Allah desires the Hereafter,﴾ He means: and Allah desires for you the splendor of the Hereafter and what He has prepared for the believers and the people of His friendship in His gardens, through your killing them and your inflicting a heavy slaughter in the land. He says to them: Seek what Allah desires for you and act for Him, not what the desires of your souls call you to, namely the longing for this world and its causes. ﴿And Allah is Mighty﴾ means: if you desire the Hereafter, no enemy of yours will overcome you, for Allah is Mighty, not subdued or defeated. And He is ﴿Wise﴾ [[See the explanation of "'Aziz" and "Hakim" above in the lexical indexes under ('-z-z) and (h-k-m).]] in His management of the affairs of His creation.

* *

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said the same as what we have said about this.

Those who said so:

16286. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿It is not for a Prophet to have captives until he has inflicted a heavy slaughter in the land﴾. This was on the day of Badr, when the Muslims were few. Then, when they increased and their authority grew strong, Allah, blessed and exalted, revealed after this concerning the captives: ﴿Then either free them as a favor or ransom them﴾ [Surah Muhammad: 4]. So Allah made the Prophet and the believers free to choose concerning the matter of the captives: if they wished they could kill them, if they wished they could enslave them, and if they wished they could ransom them.

16287. Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His saying: ﴿It is not for a Prophet to have captives until he has inflicted a heavy slaughter in the land; you desire the goods of this world﴾, the verse. He said: The Companions of the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) on the day of Badr desired ransom, so they ransomed them at four thousand each, four thousand each. [[In the printed edition the second "four thousand" has been omitted, as if he disliked it—may Allah forgive him!!]] By my life, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had not inflicted a heavy slaughter on that day! And it was the first battle that he fought against the polytheists.

16288. Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from Habib ibn Abi 'Amra, from Mujahid, who said: "al-Ikhtkhan" is killing.

[[Report 16288: Habib ibn Abi 'Amra, the butcher or the seller of meat, Abu 'Abd Allah al-Hammani, is trustworthy but narrates little; he was mentioned above under no. 10224.]]

16289. Al-Harith narrated to me, saying: 'Abd al-'Aziz narrated to us, saying: Shurayk narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr regarding His saying: ﴿It is not for a Prophet to have captives until he has inflicted a heavy slaughter in the land﴾. He said: If you take them captive, do not ransom them until you have inflicted a heavy slaughter of killing on them.

16290. ... He said: 'Abd al-'Aziz narrated to us, saying: Isra'il narrated to us, from Khasif, from Mujahid: ﴿It is not for a Prophet to have captives﴾, the verse. The concession was revealed afterward: if you wish, then show favor; and if you wish, then ransom.

16291. It was related to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying: ﴿It is not for a Prophet to have captives until he has inflicted a heavy slaughter in the land﴾: he means those who were taken captive at Badr.

16292. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: ﴿It is not for a Prophet to have captives﴾, from among his enemy, ﴿until he has inflicted a heavy slaughter in the land﴾, that is, until he has inflicted a heavy slaughter on his enemy until he has expelled them from the land. ﴿You desire the goods of this world﴾, that is, the enjoyment and the ransom by taking the men. ﴿But Allah desires the Hereafter﴾, by their killing, for the victory of the religion which they desire to extinguish, through which the Hereafter is attained.

[[Report 16292: Ibn Hisham's Sira 2:332. It continues the report preceding it, no. 16271. The wording of Ibn Hisham's Sira differs somewhat, and I am uncertain about his saying there: "that is, their killing for the victory of the religion which he desires to make manifest, and by which the Hereafter is attained."]]

16293. Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to me, saying: Abu Mu'awiya narrated to us, saying: al-A'mash narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn Murra, from Abu 'Ubayda, from 'Abd Allah, who said: When the day of Badr came and the captives were brought, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: What do you say about these captives? Abu Bakr said: O Messenger of Allah, they are your people and your family; spare them and give them respite, [[In the printed edition it reads "wa-ista'na bihim" ("and give them respite"), which is the wording of the report in Musnad Ahmad and others, from "al-anah" (patience). One says "ista'na bil-shay'," meaning: he treated it gently, delayed it, and waited for it, and awaited it. The author of Asas al-Balagha reports: "wa-ista'naytu fulanan": I did not hasten him. He cited Ibn Muqbil: "And a people in whose hands are Radaynah spears, flowing, seeking blood or fleeing." He said: "wait for it or hasten it."

The wording "wa-ista'nahum" is the established reading in the History of Abu Ja'far in the transmission of this report.]] perhaps Allah will turn to them in mercy. Then 'Umar said: O Messenger of Allah, they denied you and expelled you; bring them forward and strike off their necks! 'Abd Allah ibn Rawaha said: O Messenger of Allah, look for a valley with much firewood, bring them into it, then set fire to it upon them. He said: Then al-'Abbas said to him: May your kinship be severed! He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was silent and did not answer them, then he entered [his dwelling]. Some people said: He will take the saying of Abu Bakr. Some people said: He will take the saying of 'Umar. Some people said: He will take the saying of 'Abd Allah ibn Rawaha. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came out to them and said: "Indeed Allah softens the hearts of some men until they are softer than milk, and indeed Allah hardens the hearts of some men until they are harder than stones! And your likeness, O Abu Bakr, is the likeness of Abraham, when he said: ﴿Whoever follows me, then he is of me, and whoever disobeys me, then You are Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [Surah Ibrahim: 36], and your likeness, O Abu Bakr, is the likeness of Jesus, when he said: ﴿If You punish them, then they are Your servants﴾, the verse [Surah al-Ma'ida: 118]. And your likeness, O 'Umar, is the likeness of Noah, when he said: ﴿My Lord, do not leave upon the earth from among the disbelievers a single dweller﴾ [Surah Nuh: 26], and your likeness is like the likeness of Moses, when he said: [[In the printed edition: "And your likeness, O son of Abi Rawaha, is the likeness of Moses," which adds from his own mind what is not in the manuscript. This is an ugly presumption without knowledge, for the report contains no such addition, and the saying in it is directed to 'Umar; no mention is made in it of Ibn Rawaha as a likeness, as in all the sources. Rather, in some of them: "And your likeness, O 'Umar, is like the likeness of Moses." This addition is therefore not permissible for anyone.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) only left off giving a likeness to 'Abd Allah ibn Rawaha, and Allah knows best, because of the severe punishment in his counsel, for none punishes with the Fire except the Lord of the Fire, glorified and exalted; and may He protect us from the punishment of Hell by His grace, mercy, and bounty, for every disobedient one of His servants.]] ﴿Our Lord, obliterate their wealth and harden their hearts, so that they will not believe until they see the painful punishment﴾ [Surah Yunus: 88]. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: You are today in want, [["'ala" means the poor who are in need, plural of "'a'il." And "'ala al-rajul" means he was in need and became poor.]] so none of them shall escape except by ransom or by striking off his neck. 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud said: Except Suhayl ibn Bayda', for I heard him mention Islam! So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was silent, and I have never seen myself on a day more afraid that stones would fall upon me from the sky than I was on that day, until the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Except Suhayl ibn Bayda'." He said: Then Allah revealed: ﴿It is not for a Prophet to have captives until he has inflicted a heavy slaughter in the land﴾, to the end of the three verses.

[[Report 16293: its chain is interrupted, because "Abu 'Ubayda ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud" did not hear from his father.

Ahmad narrated this report in his Musnad through this very same route, nos. 3632–3634.

Al-Hakim narrated it in al-Mustadrak 3:21–22, through the route of Jarir ibn 'Abd al-Hamid, from al-A'mash, and said: "This is a hadith with a sound chain, though they did not include it." Al-Dhahabi said: "Sound; Jarir ibn 'Abd al-Hamid heard it."

Al-Tabari narrated it in his History 2:259, with its wording and chain.

Al-Haythami narrated it in Majma' al-Zawa'id 6:86–87 and discussed it at length, saying: "Ahmad narrated it... al-Tabarani narrated it, and in it is Abu 'Ubayda, who did not hear from his father, but its narrators are trustworthy."

Al-Wahidi narrated it in Asbab al-Nuzul: 178.

As for his saying "illa Suhayl ibn Bayda'," it is an error by some of the transmitters; it should be "Suhayl ibn Bayda'" [i.e., Sahl ibn Bayda'], the brother of "Suhayl" through the same father and mother. Ibn Sa'd said: "He embraced Islam in Mecca and concealed his Islam, so Quraysh brought him out with them in the levy of Badr, and he witnessed Badr with the polytheists, and he was taken captive that day. Ibn Mas'ud testified that he saw him praying in Mecca, so he was released. The one who related the story about Suhayl ibn Bayda' has erred: Suhayl ibn Bayda' embraced Islam before 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, and his Islam was not concealed; he emigrated to Medina and witnessed Badr with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) as a Muslim, without doubt. Thus the transmitter of that hadith confused what was between him and his brother, for Suhayl was more famous than his brother Sahl, and the story is about Sahl." Ibn Sa'd 4/1/156.]]

16294. Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: [Umar ibn Yunus al-Yamami narrated to us] saying: 'Ikrima ibn 'Ammar narrated to us, saying: Abu Zumayl narrated to us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abbas narrated to me, saying: When they took the captives, that is, on the day of Badr, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: Where are Abu Bakr, 'Umar, and 'Ali? The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: What do you think, O son of al-Khattab? [a tree near the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)]. It is a sound hadith, known only through the route of 'Ikrima ibn 'Ammar, as already stated.

Ibn Kathir cited it in his Tafsir 4:18–19.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 8, verse 68:

The interpretation of His words: ﴿Had there not been a decree from Allah that preceded, a great punishment would have touched you for what you took﴾

Abu Ja'far said: May His remembrance be exalted, says to the people of Badr who acquired spoils and took ransom from the captives: ﴿Had there not been a decree from Allah that preceded﴾, meaning: had there not been a decree from Allah that preceded for you, the people of Badr, in the Preserved Tablet (al-lawh al-mahfuz), that Allah makes the spoils lawful for you, and that Allah has decreed, among what He decreed, that He does not send astray a people after He has guided them until He makes clear to them what they should guard against [see the explanation of "kitab" in the earlier index of linguistic terms, root k-t-b], and that He does not punish anyone who witnessed the battle you witnessed at Badr with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, supporting the religion of Allah — a great punishment would have touched you from Allah for your taking of the spoils and the ransom. [See the explanation of "mass" (touching) in the earlier volume 13, p. 333, note 2, and the references there.]

* *

Those who interpreted it said the same as what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:

16295. Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Adi narrated to us, saying: Awf narrated to us, from al-Hasan, regarding His words: ﴿Had there not been a decree from Allah that preceded﴾ — the verse. He said: Allah had made the spoils lawful to this nation, but they took the ransom from the captives of Badr before they were commanded to do so. He said: So Allah reproached them for that, then made it lawful for them.

16296. Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Bazi' narrated to us, saying: Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, from Awf, from al-Hasan, regarding the saying of Allah: ﴿Had there not been a decree from Allah that preceded﴾ — the verse. That was on the day of Badr, and the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ took the spoils and the captives before they were commanded to do so. Allah, blessed and exalted, had written in the Mother of the Book: "The spoils and the captives are lawful for Muhammad and his community," and He had not made it lawful for any nation before them. They took the spoils and took the captives before it was revealed to them concerning that. Allah said: ﴿Had there not been a decree from Allah that preceded﴾, meaning in the first Book: that the spoils and the captives are lawful for you = ﴿a great punishment would have touched you for what you took﴾.

16297. Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿Had there not been a decree from Allah that preceded﴾ — the verse. The spoils, before the Prophet ﷺ was sent to the nations, when they obtained spoils they would set them aside as an offering, and Allah forbade them to eat from them, little or much. This was forbidden for every prophet and his community, so they did not eat from it, nor did they embezzle from it, nor did they take from it, little or much, without Allah punishing them for it. Allah had forbidden it to them with a severe prohibition, and He did not make it lawful for any prophet except Muhammad ﷺ. It had preceded from Allah in His decree that the spoils were lawful for him and his community. That is His saying on the day of Badr, concerning the taking of ransom from the captives: ﴿Had there not been a decree from Allah that preceded, a great punishment would have touched you for what you took﴾.

16298. Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Abu Usama narrated to us, from Urwa, from al-Hasan: ﴿Had there not been a decree from Allah that preceded﴾. He said: Allah had given the spoils to this nation, but they did what they did before the spoils were made lawful.

16299. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, who said: al-A'mash said regarding His words: ﴿Had there not been a decree from Allah that preceded﴾: a decree from Allah had preceded that He would make the spoils lawful for them.

16300. Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla narrated to us, from Bashir ibn Maymun, who said: I heard Sa'id narrate, from Abu Hurayra, who said: He recited this verse: ﴿Had there not been a decree from Allah that preceded, a great punishment would have touched you for what you took﴾, and said: meaning: had it not been that it had preceded in My knowledge that I would make the spoils lawful, a great punishment would have touched you for what you took of the captives. [Report 16300: Bashir ibn Maymun al-Khurasani al-Wasiti, Abu Sayfi, weak, rejected in narration, accused of fabrication. Abu Hatim said: "Weak in hadith, and most of his narrations are unfamiliar." 16301. Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Jabir ibn Nuh narrated to us, and Abu Mu'awiya, with similar wording, from al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: The spoils were not made lawful for any black-headed person before you; fire would descend from the sky and consume them, until the day of Badr, when the people fell upon the spoils, so Allah revealed: ﴿Had there not been a decree from Allah that preceded, a great punishment would have touched you﴾, until His words: ﴿lawful and good﴾. [Reports 16301, 16302: a hadith with a sound chain, except for Jabir ibn Nuh al-Hammani, whose hadith is worth nothing; he is weak. Biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 1/2/210, Ibn Abi Hatim 1/1/500, and Mizan al-I'tidal 1:176. Abu Kurayb narrated it from Jabir and from Abu Mu'awiya, so the hadith of Abu Mu'awiya is the sound one. This report was transmitted by al-Tirmidhi in the Book of Tafsir through 'Abd ibn Humayd, from Mu'awiya ibn Amr, from Za'ida, from al-A'mash, and he said: "This is a hasan sahih hadith." It was also transmitted by al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan 6:290, through Muhadir from al-A'mash, and through Abu Mu'awiya from al-A'mash. al-Suyuti cited it in al-Durr al-Manthur 3:203, adding its attribution to al-Nasa'i, Ibn Abi Shayba in al-Musannaf, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh, and Ibn Mardawayh.]

16302. Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Abu Mu'awiya narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayra, from the Prophet ﷺ, similar to it = he said: When it was the day of Badr, the people hastened to the spoils. [See the preceding note.]

16303. Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from Ash'ath ibn Sawwar, from Ibn Sirin, from Ubayda, who said: The Muslims captured seventy of the polytheists and killed seventy. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: Choose whether you will take ransom from them, to strengthen yourselves against your enemy, and if you accept it, seventy of you will be killed = or you kill them! They said: Rather, we will take the ransom from them, and seventy of them were killed. Ubayda said: They chose both options. ["Al-khiyara" (with a kasra on the kha and sukun on the ya', or fatha on the ya') is what is chosen and preferred of good.]

16304. Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from Ash'ath, from Ubayda, who said: The ransom of the captives of Badr was a hundred uqiyya, and the "uqiyya" is forty dirhams, and from the dinars six dinars. Abu Kurayb and Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, both saying: Ibn Ulayya narrated to us, saying: Ibn Awn narrated to us, from Ibn Sirin, from Ubayda, that he said concerning the captives of Badr: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: If you wish, kill them; and if you wish, ransom them, and a number equal to them of you will be martyred! Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Tusi narrated to me, saying: Abd al-Samad ibn Abd al-Warith narrated to us, saying: Hammam ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib narrated to us, from Abu Wa'il, from Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, who said: Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, ordered the killing of the captives, so Allah revealed: ﴿Had there not been a decree from Allah that preceded, a great punishment would have touched you for what you took﴾. And it had preceded in Allah's decree and knowledge that the spoils would be made lawful for this nation, to eat in their bellies.
