Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Ata' regarding the saying of Allah: ﴿Had there not been a decree from Allah that preceded, a great punishment would have touched you﴾, he said: It was in Allah's knowledge that the spoils would be made lawful for them, so He said: ﴿Had there not been a decree from Allah that preceded﴾, that He had made the spoils lawful for you = ﴿a great punishment would have touched you for what you took﴾.

* *

Others said: The meaning of that is: Had there not been a decree from Allah that preceded for the people of Badr, that He would not punish them, a great punishment would have touched them.

Mention of those who said that:

16309. Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri narrated to us, from Sharik, from Salim, from Sa'id: ﴿Had there not been a decree from Allah that preceded﴾, he said: for the people of Badr, from felicity.

16310. Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Ibn Numayr narrated to us, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿Had there not been a decree from Allah that preceded﴾, for the people of Badr and their standing (in that battle).

16311. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Hasan: ﴿Had there not been a decree from Allah that preceded﴾, he said: a good decree from Allah preceded for the people of Badr.

16312. Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada regarding His words: ﴿Had there not been a decree from Allah that preceded, a great punishment would have touched you for what you took﴾: a good decree from Allah had preceded for them, and He made the spoils lawful for them.

16313. al-Harith narrated to me, saying: Abd al-Aziz narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Warith ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from Amr ibn Ubayd, from al-Hasan: ﴿Had there not been a decree from Allah that preceded﴾, he said: "preceded" — that no one from the people of Badr would be punished.

16314. Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to us, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿Had there not been a decree from Allah that preceded﴾, for the people of Badr, and their standing in it.

16315. Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed me, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words: ﴿Had there not been a decree from Allah that preceded, a great punishment would have touched you for what you took﴾: it would have touched you for what you took of the spoils on the day of Badr before I made them lawful for you. He said: A decree from Allah had preceded of pardon for them and mercy toward them; it preceded that He would not punish the believers, because He does not punish His Messenger and those who believed in him, emigrated with him, and supported him.

* *

Others said: The meaning of that is: ﴿Had there not been a decree from Allah that preceded﴾, that He would not take anyone to account for an act committed in ignorance = ﴿a great punishment would have touched you for what you took﴾.

Mention of those who said that:

16316. al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid regarding His words: ﴿Had there not been a decree from Allah that preceded﴾, for the people of Badr and their standing in it, he said: a decree that preceded for His saying: ﴿And Allah would never send astray a people after He has guided them until He makes clear to them what they should guard against﴾ [Surat al-Tawba: 115]; that preceded, and it preceded that He would not take a people to account for something they did in ignorance = ﴿a great punishment would have touched you for what you took﴾. Ibn Juraij said: Ibn Abbas said: "for what you took" — of what you captured. Then He said afterward: ﴿So eat of what you have gained﴾.

16317. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: He rebuked him concerning the captives and the taking of the spoils, and no prophet before him had eaten spoils from an enemy of his.

[Report 16317: Sirat Ibn Hisham 2:331; it precedes report no. 16292 in the order of the Sira.]

16318. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, from Muhammad, who said: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib narrated to me, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: I was helped with terror; the earth was made for me a place of prostration and purification; I was given comprehensive speech; the spoils were made lawful for me, which were not lawful for any prophet before me; and I was given intercession. Five things that no prophet before me was given = Muhammad said [the "Muhammad" here means Muhammad ibn Ishaq, not Muhammad ibn Ali] — then He said: ﴿It is not for a prophet to have captives﴾, to His words: ﴿Had there not been a decree from Allah that preceded, a great punishment would have touched you for what you took﴾, meaning of the captives and the spoils = ﴿a great punishment﴾, meaning: had it not been that it preceded from Me that I would not punish except after a prohibition, and I had not forbidden you, I would have punished you for what you did. Then He made it lawful for him and for them, as mercy, favor, and a gift from the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. [Sirat Ibn Hisham 2:332; its opening follows report 16317 and precedes report 16292, and then he narrated the opening of report 16292 and followed it with what comes after it in the Sira.]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of the sayings concerning this is what we have already explained. That is because His words: ﴿Had there not been a decree from Allah that preceded﴾ are a general statement, not restricted to one meaning over another, and all these meanings that I have mentioned from those I cited are such that it has preceded in the Book of Allah that this nation is not held to account for any of them: what they did in ignorance, the making lawful of the spoils, and the forgiveness for the people of Badr, and all of that was written for them. Since that is so, there is no basis for restricting it to one meaning over another, and Allah has made the statement general in all of that, without any indication requiring the validity of a restricted reading.

16319. Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: None of the believers who were helped failed to love the spoils, except Umar ibn al-Khattab, who would not meet a captive without striking his neck, and he said: O Messenger of Allah, what have we to do with the spoils? We are a people who strive in the religion of Allah until Allah is worshipped! The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "If we were punished for this matter, O Umar, none would be saved but you!" Allah said: Do not return to making lawful what I have not yet made lawful for you.

16320. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, saying: Ibn Ishaq said: When there was revealed: ﴿Had there not been a decree from Allah that preceded﴾, the verse, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "If a punishment had descended from the sky, none would have been saved from it except Sa'd ibn Mu'adh, for his words: O Prophet of Allah, intensive slaughter in killing was dearer to me than sparing the men." [Report 16320: I have not found this report in Sirat Ibn Hisham, as far as I can determine.]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 8, verse 69:

The interpretation of His words: ﴿So eat of what you have taken as spoils, lawful and good, and fear Allah. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [Qur'an 8:69].

Abu Ja'far said: He, may He be exalted and remembered, says to the believers from among the people of Badr: ﴿So eat﴾, O believers, ﴿of what you have taken as spoils﴾, from the wealth of the polytheists, ﴿lawful﴾, by His making it lawful for you, ﴿and good. And fear Allah﴾, meaning: fear Allah lest you return, lest you do anything in your religion after this which has not been enjoined upon you beforehand, as you did in taking ransom and eating the spoils, and taking both before they were made lawful for you; ﴿indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾. [[See the explanation of the words of the verse in the preceding indexes of linguistic terms.]]

* *

This is one of the instances of the delayed (mu'akhkhar) which has the meaning of the advanced (muqaddam), and the meaning of the speech is: ﴿So eat of what you have taken as spoils, lawful and good﴾, ﴿Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾, ﴿and fear Allah﴾.

* *

By His words ﴿Indeed, Allah is Forgiving﴾, He means: forgiving the sins of the people of faith among His servants; ﴿and Merciful﴾, toward them, by not punishing them after their repentance from them.

The commentary of Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari), Jami' al-Bayan, on Surah 8, verse 70:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿O Prophet, say to those in your hands of the captives: If Allah knows any good in your hearts, He will give you better than what was taken from you, and He will forgive you, and Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ (8:70)

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is He, says to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: O Prophet, say to those in your hands, and in the hands of your companions, of the captives of the polytheists from whom ransom was taken, whatever was taken: ﴿If Allah knows any good in your hearts﴾, meaning: if Allah knows Islam in your hearts, ﴿He will give you better than what was taken from you﴾, meaning from the ransom, ﴿and He will forgive you﴾, meaning: He will pardon you for the punishment of the crime you committed by fighting the Prophet of Allah and his companions and by disbelieving in Allah, ﴿and Allah is Forgiving﴾ of the sins of His servants when they repent, ﴿Merciful﴾ toward them, in not punishing them for them after repentance. [[See the explanation of the words of this verse in the earlier linguistic indexes.]]

* *

It is also mentioned that al-Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib used to say: This verse was revealed concerning me.

Those who said so:

16321. Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Ibn Idris narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Al-Abbas said: It was revealed concerning me: ﴿It is not for a Prophet to have captives until he has inflicted a massacre in the land﴾. So I informed the Prophet ﷺ of my Islam, and asked him to reckon with me for the twenty uqiyyas that were taken from me, but he refused. So Allah replaced them for me with twenty slaves, all of them merchants, whose wealth is in their hands. [[Narration 16321: In the printed edition it reads "Abi Ishaq," and the correct reading, from the manuscript, is as given; see the following note.]]

* *

And also:

16322. Ibn Humayd narrated to us this report, saying: Salamah narrated to us, saying: Muhammad said: al-Kalbi narrated to me, from Abu Salih, from Ibn Abbas, from Jabir ibn Abd Allah ibn Ri'ab, who said: Al-Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib used to say: By Allah, it was revealed concerning me, when I mentioned my Islam to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Then he mentioned something similar to the report of Ibn Waki'. [[Narration 16322: Al-Haythami mentioned this report and the previous one in Majma' al-Zawa'id (7:8), in a fuller form, and said: "Al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Awsat and al-Kabir in abridged form, and the men of al-Awsat are men of the Sahih, except Ibn Ishaq, who did state hearing (from his source)."

It is evident that he means a chain other than these two chains, since the first does not state hearing explicitly, and the second contains "al-Kalbi."

Al-Wahidi mentioned it in Asbab al-Nuzul, from al-Kalbi, in a longer form (pp. 180–181).

In the printed edition and the manuscript it reads "Jabir ibn Abd Allah ibn Rabab," which is an error; the correct form is what has been recorded here.]]

16323. Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning his saying: ﴿Say to those in your hands of the captives﴾, to the end of the verse. He said: It was reported to us that when the wealth of Bahrain, eighty thousand, came to the Prophet of Allah ﷺ, he had performed ablution for the noon prayer. He gave that day to no one who complained, and refused no one who asked, and he did not pray that day until he had distributed it. He ordered al-Abbas to take from it and fill his garment, and he took. He said: Al-Abbas used to say: This is better than what was taken from us, and I hope for forgiveness.

16324. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, concerning his saying: ﴿O Prophet, say to those in your hands of the captives﴾, to the end of the verse. Al-Abbas had been taken captive on the day of Badr, and he ransomed himself with forty uqiyyas of gold. When this verse was revealed, al-Abbas said: Allah has given me two qualities, and I would not want the world in exchange for them: I was taken captive on the day of Badr and ransomed myself for forty uqiyyas, and He gave me forty slaves; and I hope for the forgiveness that Allah has promised us.

16325. Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, concerning his saying: ﴿O Prophet, say to those in your hands of the captives﴾, to His saying: ﴿And Allah is Forgiving, Merciful﴾. He means by this: those taken captive on the day of Badr. He says: If you act in obedience to Me and give sincere counsel to My Messenger, I will give you better than what was taken from you, and I will forgive you.

16326. Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ata' al-Khurasani, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿O Prophet, say to those in your hands of the captives﴾: (this was said of) Abbas and his companions. He said: They said to the Prophet ﷺ: We believe in what you have brought, and we testify that you are the Messenger of Allah, and we will surely give you sincere counsel regarding our people. So it was revealed: ﴿If Allah knows any good in your hearts, He will give you better than what was taken from you﴾, meaning faith and affirmation; He will replace for you something better than what was taken from you. ﴿And He will forgive you﴾, meaning the polytheism you were upon. He said: Al-Abbas used to say: I would not like this verse not to have been revealed concerning us, even if I had the world. He said: ﴿He will give you better than what was taken from you﴾, and He has given me better than what was taken from me a hundredfold. And He said: ﴿And He will forgive you﴾, and I hope that I have been forgiven.

16327. I was told, from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say, concerning his saying: ﴿O Prophet, say to those in your hands of the captives﴾, to the end of the verse: he means al-Abbas and his companions, who were taken captive on the day of Badr. Allah says: If you act in obedience to Me and give sincere counsel to Me and to My Messenger, I will give you better than what was taken from you, and I will forgive you. Al-Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib used to say: Allah has given us two qualities, neither of which is better: twenty slaves. As for the second, we are awaiting, in the promise of the Truthful, forgiveness from Allah, glorified is He.

The Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 8, Verse 71:

On the interpretation (*ta'wil*) of His saying: ﴿And if they intend treachery against you, they have already betrayed God before, so He gave you power over them. And God is Knowing and Wise.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: God, may His remembrance be exalted, says to His Prophet: "And if these captives who are in your hands intend to betray you," ﴿khiyanataka﴾, meaning, to deceive you, to plot against you, and to cheat you, by showing you with their words the opposite of what is in their hearts [[See the explanation of "khiyana" (betrayal) above, p. 25, note 1, and the references there.]]. ﴿Then they have already betrayed God before﴾ means: they had already opposed God's command before the battle of Badr, and He gave the believers power over them at Badr [[See the explanation of "amkana" (to give power over) above, vol. 11, p. 263, and vol. 12, p. 315.]]. ﴿And God is Knowing﴾ of what they say with their tongues and conceal in their souls, ﴿Wise﴾ in His management of them and of the affairs of His creation besides them [[See the explanation of "'alim" (knowing) and "hakim" (wise) above in the language indices under the roots ('-l-m) and (h-k-m).]].

* *

Those who engage in interpretation said the same as what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said this:

16328. Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ata al-Khurasani, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿And if they intend treachery against you﴾, meaning: al-Abbas and his companions, in their saying: "We believe in what you have brought, and we testify that you are the Messenger of God, and we will surely counsel you concerning our people." He says: if their saying was treachery, ﴿then they have already betrayed God before, so He gave you power over them﴾, meaning: they disbelieved and fought you, and God gave you power over them.

16329. Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His saying: ﴿And if they intend treachery against you﴾, the verse. He said: It was mentioned to us that a man wrote for the Prophet of God (ﷺ), then he deliberately acted hypocritically, and joined the polytheists in Mecca, then said: "Muhammad only wrote what you willed!" When a man of the Ansar heard that, he vowed that if God gave him power over him, he would surely strike him with the sword. When the day of the Conquest came, the Messenger of God (ﷺ) granted safety to the people except for Abd Allah ibn Sa'd ibn Abi Sarh, Miqyas ibn Subabah, [[In the printed edition: "Ibn Dubabah," which is a plain error.]] Ibn Khatal, and a woman who used to curse the Prophet (ﷺ) every morning. Uthman came with Ibn Abi Sarh, who was his foster-brother, or his brother by nursing, and said: "O Messenger of God, this is so-and-so, who has come repentant and regretful!" The Prophet of God (ﷺ) turned away. When the Ansari heard of him, he came with his sword slung on him, circling around him, and kept looking at the Messenger of God (ﷺ), hoping he would gesture to him. Then the Messenger of God (ﷺ) extended his hand and accepted his pledge. He said: "By God, I had delayed you in this matter so that you might fulfil your vow!" [[" Talawwama fi al-amr" and "talawwama bihi" mean to wait, linger, and be patient, and the transitive use of such a verb is pure Arabic.]] He said: "O Prophet of God, I was in awe of you, so why did you not signal to me?" He said: "It is not fitting for a Prophet to signal." [[" Awmada ilayhi" means to indicate with a subtle gesture, from "iymad al-barq," when lightning flashes faintly and then disappears.]] [[The report 16329: see Musnad Ahmad, vol. 3, p. 151, a hadith of Anas, though not with this wording.]]

16330. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding: ﴿And if they intend treachery against you, they have already betrayed God before, so He gave you power over them﴾. He says: They disbelieved in God and broke His covenant, so He gave you power over them at Badr.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 8, verse 72:

The interpretation of His words: ﴿Indeed, those who believed and emigrated and strove with their wealth and their lives in the cause of Allah, and those who gave shelter and helped – those are allies of one another.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: His saying, may His remembrance be exalted, means: Indeed, those who affirmed Allah and His Messenger = "and emigrated," meaning they forsook their people, their tribe and their homes; that is, they left them and departed from them, and their people and tribe forsook them [[See the explanation of "al-muhajara" (emigration) above in 4:317-318, 7:490, 9:100, 122.]] = ﴿and strove in the cause of Allah﴾, meaning: they exerted themselves to the utmost, wearying and exhausting their souls in fighting the enemies of Allah from among the disbelievers [[See the explanation of "al-mujahada" (striving) above in 4:318, 10:292, 423.]] = ﴿in the cause of Allah﴾, meaning: in the religion of Allah, which He made a path to His mercy and salvation from His punishment [[See the explanation of "sabil Allah" (the way of Allah) above in the language indices (s-b-l).]] = ﴿and those who gave shelter and helped﴾, meaning: those who sheltered the Messenger of Allah and the emigrants with him, that is, they made for them a refuge to which they could resort, which is the abode and dwelling; he means they lodged them and made for them dwellings from their own homes when their people drove them out from their homes [[See the explanation of "awa" and "al-ma'wa" above in 13:477, note 2, and the references there.]] = ﴿and helped﴾, meaning: they helped them against their enemies and the enemies of Allah from among the polytheists = ﴿those are allies of one another﴾, meaning: these two groups, namely the emigrants and the Helpers, are helpers of one another and aides against all others among the polytheists, and their hand is one against whoever disbelieves in Allah, and some of them are brothers to others to the exclusion of their disbelieving relatives. [[See the explanation of "al-wali" (ally) above in the language indices (w-l-y).]]

* *

It has been said: By this He meant only that some of them have greater right to the inheritance of others, and that Allah made some of them inherit from others by emigration and support, to the exclusion of kinship and blood ties, and that Allah afterwards abrogated this by His saying: ﴿And those of blood relationship are more entitled to one another in the Book of Allah﴾ [Surah al-Anfal: 75 and Surah al-Ahzab: 6].

Those who said this:

16331 – Al-Muthanna related to me, he said: Abu Salih related to us, he said: Mu'awiya related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who believed and emigrated and strove with their wealth and their lives in the cause of Allah, and those who gave shelter and helped – those are allies of one another﴾, meaning: concerning inheritance; inheritance was given to the emigrants and the Helpers to the exclusion of those of blood relationship. Allah said: ﴿And those who believed but did not emigrate – you have no obligation of protection towards them until they emigrate﴾, meaning: you have no share in their inheritance at all. And they acted upon this until Allah sent down this verse: ﴿And those of blood relationship are more entitled to one another in the Book of Allah﴾ [Surah al-Anfal: 75], concerning inheritance. So the earlier ruling was abrogated, and inheritance passed to those of blood relationship.

16332 – Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, he said: My father related to me, he said: My paternal uncle related to me, he said: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who believed and emigrated and strove with their wealth and their lives in the cause of Allah﴾, he said: There is no emigration after the Conquest; there is only martyrdom after that. ﴿And those who gave shelter and helped, those are allies of one another﴾, up to His saying: ﴿until they emigrate﴾. That is because the believers, in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, were in three situations: among them was the believer who emigrated, separated from his people in emigration, going out to a people who were believers in their dwellings, their estates and their wealth; and [those who] "gave shelter and helped" – and in the printed edition: "and in His saying: gave shelter and helped" [the manuscript has an addition not in the printed edition] – and who declared what the people of emigration declared, and drew swords against whoever denied and rejected. These two are believers, whom Allah made allies of one another, so they inherited from each other: when a believing emigrant died, the Helper inherited from him by the bond of religious allegiance. And the one who believed but did not emigrate did not inherit, because he had not emigrated nor given help. So Allah absolved the emigrant believers of their inheritance, which is the allegiance about which Allah said: ﴿You have no obligation of protection towards them until they emigrate﴾. And it was binding upon the believers who gave shelter and helped, when they sought their help in religion, that they help them if they fought, except if they sought help against a people with whom the Prophet ﷺ had a covenant; then there was no help for them against those, except against enemies with whom there was no covenant. Then Allah afterwards sent down that every person of kinship should be joined to his kin among the believers who emigrated and the believers who did not emigrate. He thus made for every believer a prescribed share, by His saying: ﴿And those of blood relationship are more entitled to one another in the Book of Allah; indeed Allah is Knowing of all things﴾ [Surah al-Anfal: 75], and by His saying: ﴿And the believing men and believing women are allies of one another﴾ [Surah al-Tawbah: 71].

16333 – Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, he said: Abu Asim related to us, he said: Isa related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: The three verses are the closing verses of al-Anfal; in them is mentioned what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had established between the emigrant Muslims and the Helpers concerning inheritance. Then the last of them abrogated that: ﴿And those of blood relationship are more entitled to one another in the Book of Allah; indeed Allah is Knowing of all things﴾.

16334 – Al-Qasim related to us, he said: Al-Husayn related to us, he said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Abdullah ibn Kathir regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who believed and emigrated and strove﴾, up to His saying: ﴿Seeing of what you do﴾, he said: We have been informed that it concerned inheritance: the believers who emigrated did not inherit from the believers who did not emigrate. He said: Then after that was revealed: ﴿And those of blood relationship are more entitled to one another in the Book of Allah; indeed Allah is Knowing of all things﴾, so they inherited, even though they had not emigrated. Ibn Juraij said: Mujahid said: The closing three verses of "al-Anfal" – in them is mentioned what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had established between the emigrant Muslims and the Helpers concerning inheritance – then the last of them abrogated that: ﴿And those of blood relationship are more entitled to one another in the Book of Allah﴾.

16335 – Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah: ﴿And those who emigrated and strove in the cause of Allah, and those who gave shelter and helped﴾, up to His saying: ﴿You have no obligation of protection towards them until they emigrate﴾. He said: The Muslims remained for a time inheriting by emigration, and the Muslim Bedouin did not inherit anything from the emigrant. Then that was abrogated afterwards, and Allah joined: ﴿And those of blood relationship are more entitled to one another in the Book of Allah, than the believers and the emigrants, except that you do kindness to your allies﴾ [Surah al-Ahzab: 6], meaning: from among the people of polytheism. So bequest was permitted, and there is no inheritance for them; inheritance became by religious communities, and Muslims inherit from one another, both emigrants and believers, and the people of two religions do not inherit from each other.

16336 – Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Yahya ibn Wadih related to us, from al-Hasan, from Yazid, from Ikrimah and al-Hasan, who both said: ﴿Indeed, those who believed and emigrated and strove in the cause of Allah﴾, up to His saying: ﴿You have no obligation of protection towards them until they emigrate﴾. The Bedouin did not inherit from the emigrant, nor did the emigrant inherit from him. Then He abrogated it, saying: ﴿And those of blood relationship are more entitled to one another in the Book of Allah; indeed Allah is Knowing of all things﴾.

16337 – Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to me, he said: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, he said: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿Indeed, those who believed and emigrated and strove with their wealth and their lives in the cause of Allah, and those who gave shelter and helped – those are allies of one another﴾, concerning inheritance. ﴿And those who believed but did not emigrate﴾, these are the Bedouins. ﴿You have no obligation of protection towards them﴾, concerning inheritance. ﴿And if they seek your help in religion﴾, meaning: because they are Muslims. ﴿Then you must help, except against a people between you and whom there is a covenant; and those who disbelieved are allies of one another﴾, concerning inheritance. ﴿And those who believed afterwards and emigrated and strove with you, they are of you﴾. Then the prescriptions and inheritance abrogated them. "And those of blood relationship" – those who inherited by emigration – ﴿are more entitled to one another in the Book of Allah﴾, so the Bedouins and the emigrants inherited.

* *

The interpretation of His words: ﴿And those who believed but did not emigrate – you have no obligation of protection towards them until they emigrate; and if they seek your help in religion, then you must help, except against a people between you and them is a covenant; and Allah is Seeing of what you do﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: ﴿And those who believed﴾, those who affirmed Allah and His Messenger = ﴿but did not emigrate﴾, from their disbelieving people, and did not leave the abode of disbelief for the abode of Islam = ﴿you have no﴾, O believers in Allah and His Messenger – the emigrants from their polytheist people and the land of war [[See the explanation of "al-hijra" (emigration) above, p. 77, note, and the references there.]] = ﴿obligation of protection towards them﴾, meaning: of support and inheritance.

* *

I have mentioned the statement of some who said: "The meaning of wilaya here is inheritance," and I will mention, God willing, what I recall of it later.

* *

= ﴿of anything until they emigrate﴾, leaving their people and their homes from the abode of war to the abode of Islam = ﴿And if they seek your help in religion﴾, meaning: if these who believed but did not emigrate seek your help = ﴿in religion﴾, meaning: because they are of your religion, against your enemies and their enemies from among the polytheists, "then you must", O believers from the emigrants and the Helpers, ﴿help﴾ = ﴿except﴾ if they seek your help = ﴿against a people between you and them is a covenant﴾, meaning: a pact by which some of you have bound yourselves to others not to fight them [[See the explanation of "al-mithaq" (covenant) above, 13, 315, note, and the references there.]] = ﴿and Allah is Seeing of what you do﴾, meaning: Allah is aware of what you do in respect of the allegiance you owe one another, O emigrants and Helpers, and abandoning allegiance to those who believed but did not emigrate, and your help for them when they seek your help in religion, and other obligations of Allah which He has imposed upon you = ﴿Seeing﴾, who sees and perceives it, so nothing of that or of anything else is hidden from Him. [[See the explanation of "basir" (seeing) above in the language indices (b-s-r).]]

16338 – Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿You have no obligation of protection towards them of anything until they emigrate﴾, he said: The Muslims used to inherit by emigration, and the Prophet ﷺ made brotherhood among them, so they inherited by Islam and emigration. A man would embrace Islam without emigrating, and would not inherit from his brother. Then that was abrogated by His saying: ﴿And those of blood relationship are more entitled to one another in the Book of Allah, than the believers and the emigrants﴾ [Surah al-Ahzab: 6].

16339 – Muhammad related to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri: that the Prophet ﷺ took a pledge from a man who entered Islam, saying: You shall establish prayer, give zakat, perform the pilgrimage to the House, fast Ramadan, and that you will not see the fire of a polytheist without being at war [with him]. [[That is, that his dwelling be far from the dwelling of the polytheist, "so that he does not see his fire"; this was a prohibition by him ﷺ against neighbouring a polytheist.]]

16340 – Al-Muthanna related to me, he said: Abu Salih related to us, he said: Mu'awiya related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿And if they seek your help in religion﴾, meaning: if the Muslim Bedouins seek your help, O emigrants and Helpers, against their enemy, then you must help them, except against a people between you and them is a covenant.

16341 – Al-Qasim related to us, he said: Al-Husayn related to us, he said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Juraij, who said: Ibn Abbas said: The Prophet ﷺ left the people on the day he died in four stations: the believing emigrant, the Helpers, and the believing Bedouin who did not emigrate – if the Prophet ﷺ sought his help, he helped him; if he left him, that was his leave; and if the Prophet ﷺ sought his help in religion, it was binding upon him to help him; this is His saying: ﴿And if they seek your help in religion, then you must help﴾. And the fourth: the Followers in excellence.

16342 – I was told on the authority of al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman related to us, he said: I heard al-Dahhak say, regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who believed and emigrated﴾, to the end of the surah: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ died and left the people in four stations: the believing emigrant; the Muslim Bedouin; those who gave shelter and helped; and the Followers in excellence.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 8, verse 73:

The interpretation of His words: ﴿And those who disbelieve, some of them are allies of others. Unless you do so, there will be fitnah (turmoil) on earth and great corruption﴾ (8:73).

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is He, says: ﴿And those who disbelieve﴾ in God and His Messenger, ﴿some of them are allies of others﴾, meaning: some of them are helpers and supporters of others, and more deserving of that than the believers in God and His Messenger. [See the explanation of "wali" (ally) in the indexes of language earlier in this work, under (w-l-y).]

* *

We have already mentioned the view of those who said: "It means that some of them are more deserving of the inheritance of others among their relatives, over the believers," [In the printed edition: "meaning the clarification that some of them," which is a corrupt context. In the manuscript: "meaning the clarification of some of them," undotted, likewise disordered and corrupt. The correct reading is what has been established.] and we will mention the rest of those whose statements we have been present for.

16343 - Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-Suddi, from Abu Malik, who said: A man said: "Shall we inherit from our relatives among the polytheists?" Then it was revealed: ﴿And those who disbelieve, some of them are allies of others﴾, the verse.

16344 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas regarding His words: ﴿And those who disbelieve, some of them are allies of others. Unless you do so, there will be fitnah on earth and great corruption﴾, that it was revealed concerning the inheritances of the polytheists of the covenant people.

16345 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words: ﴿And those who believed but did not emigrate, you have no guardianship over them until they emigrate﴾, up to His words: ﴿and great corruption﴾, he said: The believer who emigrated and the believer who did not emigrate did not inherit from each other, even if they were two believing brothers. He said: That was because this religion was few in this land until the day of the Conquest. When the day of the Conquest came, and emigration ceased, they inherited from one another by kinship wherever they were. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "There is no emigration after the Conquest," and he recited: ﴿And those of blood relationship are more entitled to one another in the Book of God﴾.

* *

Others said: The meaning of that is: The disbelievers are supporters of one another, and that one who remains in the abode of war without emigrating is not a believer. [In the printed edition: "and" with an added waw.]

Those who said this:

1634 6 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah regarding His words: ﴿And those who disbelieve, some of them are allies of others﴾, he said: A man would dwell between the Muslims and the polytheists, saying: "If these prevail, I will be with them, and if those prevail, I will be with them!" So God forbade them that, and God revealed concerning that: "The fire of a Muslim and the fire of a polytheist shall not see each other," [The phrase "shall not see each other" attributes seeing to the fire, as a metaphor for proximity; see the earlier note on p. 83, no. 1.] except for one who pays the jizyah and submits to the kharaj.

1634 7 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: God urged the believers to mutual connection, and made the Emigrants and the Helpers people of wilayah (allegiance) in religion, to the exclusion of others, and made the disbelievers allies of one another. [The report: 16347 - Sirah of Ibn Hisham 2:332, which follows the earlier report no. 16318.]

* *

As for His words: ﴿Unless you do so, there will be fitnah on earth and great corruption﴾, the people of interpretation differed in its interpretation.

Some of them said: Its meaning: Unless you do, O believers, what you were commanded regarding inheriting among the Emigrants, some from others by emigration, and the Helpers by faith, to the exclusion of their relatives among the Bedouin Muslims and to the exclusion of the disbelievers, ﴿there will be fitnah﴾, meaning: a trial will occur on earth because of that, ﴿and great corruption﴾, meaning: and disobedience to God. [See the explanation of "fasad" (corruption) earlier in vol. 13, p. 36, note 3, and the references there.]

Those who said that:

1634 8 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words: ﴿Unless you do so, there will be fitnah on earth and great corruption﴾: Unless you do this, you would leave them inheriting as they used to inherit, ﴿there will be fitnah on earth and great corruption﴾. He said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) would not accept faith except with emigration, and they would not count them among themselves except with emigration. [In the manuscript: "and they do not make them muqim," the correct reading is that of the printed edition.]

1634 9 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿And those who disbelieve, some of them are allies of others﴾, meaning in inheritance. ﴿Unless you do so﴾, meaning: unless you take up inheritance according to what I commanded you. ﴿there will be fitnah on earth and great corruption﴾.

* *

Others said: The meaning of that is: Unless you, O believers, help one another in religion, there will be fitnah on earth and great corruption.

Those who said that:

1635 0 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: He made the Emigrants and the Helpers people of wilayah in religion, to the exclusion of others, and made the disbelievers allies of one another, then He said: ﴿Unless you do so, there will be fitnah on earth and great corruption﴾, meaning: unless the believer allies with the believer rather than the disbeliever, even if he is a relative of his, ﴿there will be fitnah on earth and great corruption﴾, that is: confusion between truth and falsehood, and the appearance of corruption on earth, through a believer's allegiance to a disbeliever rather than to a believer. [The printed edition had after "great corruption" the words: "if the believer allies with the disbeliever rather than the believer, then returns inheritances to relatives," and the manuscript is similar but with "if he allies." This is disordered speech, caused by "the believer" being mentioned several times, so the text between "the believer" in "unless the believer allies with the believer" and the later "allegiance of the believer to the disbeliever" was dropped; the disorder was corrected from Sirah of Ibn Hisham.] Then he returned inheritances to relatives. [The report: 16350 - Sirah of Ibn Hisham 2:332, 333, which follows the earlier report no. 16347, and part of it is in it.]

1635 1 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, saying: Ibn Jurayj said regarding His words: ﴿Unless you do so, there will be fitnah on earth and great corruption﴾, he said: Unless you cooperate and support one another in religion, ﴿there will be fitnah on earth and great corruption﴾.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The more correct of the two interpretations of His words: ﴿And those who disbelieve, some of them are allies of others﴾ is the view of those who said: Its meaning is that some of them are supporters of others to the exclusion of the believers, and that it is an indication of God's prohibition upon the believer to remain in the abode of war and to abandon emigration, because the known usage in Arabic speech for the meaning of "wali" is the supporter and helper, or the cousin and kinsman. [See the explanation of "wali" earlier in the language indexes under (w-l-y).] As for the heir, that meaning is not known for it, except in the sense that he takes charge of his inheritance after him. That is a distant meaning, although the speech may bear it. Directing the meaning of God's speech to the most apparent and well-known meaning is more appropriate than directing it to something else.

Given that this is so, it is clear that the more correct of the two interpretations of His words: ﴿Unless you do so, there will be fitnah on earth and great corruption﴾ is the interpretation of those who said: Unless you do what you were commanded of cooperation and support in religion, there will be fitnah on earth, since the beginning of the verse, His words: ﴿Indeed, those who believed and emigrated and struggled with their wealth and their selves in the way of God﴾, came with urging allegiance in religion and mutual support, so likewise it is necessary that its conclusion be with that.

**The interpretation of His saying:** ﴿And those who believed and emigrated and strove in the way of Allah, and those who sheltered and helped, those are the believers truly. For them is forgiveness and an honorable provision﴾ (8:74)

Abu Ja'far said: May His remembrance be exalted, He says: ﴿And those who believed and emigrated and strove in the way of Allah, and those who sheltered and helped﴾, meaning they sheltered the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the emigrants with him and helped them, and helped the religion of Allah. ﴿Those are the people of faith in Allah and His Messenger truly﴾, not those who believed but did not emigrate from the abode of polytheism and remained among the polytheists, and did not fight alongside the Muslims against their enemy.[[See the explanation of "hajara" (emigrated), "jahada" (strove), and "awa" (sheltered) above, pp. 77, notes 1–4, and the references there.]] ﴿For them is forgiveness﴾, meaning: for them is a covering from Allah over their sins, through His pardon of them.[[See the explanation of "al-maghfirah" (forgiveness) in the earlier lexical indexes under the root "ghafara".]] ﴿And an honorable provision﴾, meaning: for them in Paradise is food and drink that is wholesome and noble,[[See the explanation of "rizq karim" above. In the printed edition here it reads "ta'm wa-mashrab" (food and drink), and the correct reading, from the manuscript, is as given.]] which does not change in their bellies into waste,[["Najw" is what exits from the belly.]] but turns into sweat like the sweat of musk.[[Muslim and Abu Dawud related from the hadith of Jabir: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The people of Paradise eat and drink therein, and they do not spit, nor urinate, nor defecate, nor blow their noses." It was said: "Then what of the food?" He said: "Belching and sweat like the sweat of musk; they are inspired to glorify and praise Allah as you are inspired to breathe." (Sahih Muslim 17:173).]]

* *

This verse indicates the soundness of what we have said: that the meaning of Allah's saying ﴿some of them are allies of others﴾ in this verse, and His saying ﴿you have no allegiance with them at all﴾, is only support and assistance, not inheritance. For He, may His praise be exalted, followed that with praise of the emigrants and the Helpers and information about what they have with Him, excluding those who did not emigrate, by saying: ﴿And those who believed and emigrated and strove in the way of Allah, and those who sheltered and helped﴾, to the end of the verse. Had the intent of the preceding verses been to establish the ruling on their inheritance, nothing following it would have been but an exhortation to carry out the inheritance as commanded.[[In the printed edition it reads "al-hathth 'ala mada'" (the exhortation to proceed), while the manuscript reads "'ala amda" (to carry out); the correct reading is what is given here.]] And the clear evidence for the soundness of this interpretation is that there is no abrogating (nasikh) or abrogated (mansukh) element in these verses.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 8, verse 75:

The interpretation of His words: ﴿And those who believed afterwards and emigrated and strove alongside you — they are of you﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, exalted is His remembrance, says: "And those who believed" in God and His Messenger after My clarifying what I have clarified concerning the mutual guardianship (wilaya) of the emigrants and the Helpers, and the severing of their guardianship from whoever believed but did not emigrate until he emigrates — ﴿and emigrated﴾ from the abode of disbelief to the abode of Islam — ﴿and strove alongside you﴾, O believers — ﴿they are of you﴾ in guardianship; it is incumbent upon you toward them to have the same rights, support in religion, and inheritance as is incumbent upon them toward you and upon some of you toward others [[See the explanation of "hajara" (emigrated) and "jahada" (strove) earlier, p. 88, note 1, and the references there.]] as:

16352 – Ibn Humayd related to us, who said: Salama related to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: "Then He returned the inheritances to the kinship ties among those who embraced Islam after the guardianship, from the emigrants and the Helpers, excluding them, to the kinship ties that are between them." [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "Then the inheritances to the kinship ties that are between them." The completion of the statement, which I have recorded from the Sirah of Ibn Hisham, has dropped out; the cause of this, as occurred in no. 16350, is the mention of "al-arham" (kinship ties) twice, so his sight became confused and he transmitted what he transmitted.]] Then He said: ﴿And those who believed afterwards and emigrated and strove alongside you — they are of you. And blood relatives are closer to one another in the Book of God﴾, i.e., in inheritance [[In the printed edition: "i.e., in the inheritance," which is an error; the correct reading is in the manuscript and the Sirah.]] — ﴿Indeed, God is Knowing of all things﴾. [[The report: 16352 – Sirah of Ibn Hisham 2:333, which follows the earlier report no. 16350.]]

* *

The interpretation of His words: ﴿And blood relatives are closer to one another in the Book of God. Indeed, God is Knowing of all things﴾ (75)

Abu Ja'far said: He, exalted is His remembrance, says: Those related by kinship ties — ﴿are closer to one another﴾ in inheritance, when they are among those for whom God has ordained a share and portion of it, rather than the ally by oath or the protector — ﴿in the Book of God﴾, meaning: in the judgment of God that He has written in the Preserved Tablet and in the prior decree. [[See the explanation of "kitab" (book) earlier, p. 64, note 1, and the references there.]] — ﴿Indeed, God is Knowing of all things﴾, meaning: Indeed God knows what suits His servants in His making some of them inherit from others by kinship and lineage rather than by covenant of alliance, and by other matters entirely, nothing of which is hidden from Him. [[See the explanation of "alim" (knowing) earlier in the language indices (ʿ-l-m).]]

* *

Those who expounded the interpretation said the same as what we have said on this.

Those who said so:

16353 – Ahmad ibn al-Miqdam related to us, who said: al-Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman related to us, who said: my father related to us, who said: Qatada related to us that he said: "The Bedouin did not inherit from the emigrant until God sent down: ﴿And blood relatives are closer to one another in the Book of God.﴾"

16354 – Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna related to us, who said: Mu'adh ibn Mu'adh related to us, who said: Ibn Awn related to us, from Isa ibn al-Harith: that his brother Shurayh ibn al-Harith had a concubine who bore him a girl. When the girl grew up she was married and bore a boy. Then the concubine died, and Shurayh ibn al-Harith and the boy disputed her inheritance before Shurayh the judge. Shurayh ibn al-Harith kept saying: "He has no inheritance in the Book of God!" He said: So Shurayh ruled the inheritance for the boy. He said: ﴿And blood relatives are closer to one another in the Book of God﴾. So Maysara ibn Yazid rode to Ibn al-Zubayr and informed him of Shurayh's ruling and his statement. Ibn al-Zubayr wrote to Shurayh: "Maysara informed me that you ruled thus and thus, and you said: ﴿And blood relatives are closer to one another in the Book of God﴾, and it is not so. This verse was only revealed because a man would make a covenant with another man, saying: 'You inherit from me and I inherit from you.' So it was revealed: ﴿And blood relatives are closer to one another in the Book of God.﴾" He brought the letter to Shurayh, and Shurayh said: "Let her unborn child be freed!" [[In the printed edition: "janin" (fetus), differing from the manuscript. In Akhbar al-Qudat of Waki' it is "janan batnaha," and what is here, and in Akhbar al-Qudat, is problematic, so I have recorded it until I know its correct form or someone else does.]] And he refused to retract his ruling. [[The reports: 16354, 16355 – Waki' related it in Akhbar al-Qudat 2:320, 321, by way of Amr ibn Bishr, from Hasan ibn Isa, from Abd Allah, from Ibn Awn, in similar wording.]]

16355 – Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim related to me, who said: Ibn Ulayya related to us, from Ibn Awn, who said: Isa ibn al-Harith related to me, who said: Shurayh ibn al-Harith had a concubine, and he mentioned something similar, except that in his report it says: "A man would make a covenant with another man, saying: 'You inherit from me and I inherit from you,' and when it was revealed, that was abandoned." [[The report: 16354, 16355 – Waki' related it in Akhbar al-Qudat 2:320, 321, by way of Amr ibn Bishr, from Hasan ibn Isa, from Abd Allah, from Ibn Awn, in similar wording.]]

End of the commentary on "Surat al-Anfal."

Praise be to God alone, and may God bless our master Muhammad and his family.
